## ETEGRec

- Page: pages/papers/etegrec.md
- Venue: SIGIR’25
- Problem: III. SID–Model Alignment
- Stage: Training
- Representation: CF; Tokenization: Learn. RQ; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Altern.; Objective: NTP + Ctr.; Inference: Beam
- TL;DR: ETEGRec trains the item tokenizer and the generator in alternation with sequence-item and preference-semantic alignment losses, instead of building the tokenizer separately before generator training.
- [Code](https://github.com/RUCAIBox/ETEGRec)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 4

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon 2023 Reviews (May 1996-September 2023): Musical Instruments, Industrial and Scientific, Video Games; 5-core filtering of users and items; sequences capped at 50 items. Sizes (users / items / interactions): Instrument 57,439 / 24,587 / 511,836; Scientific 50,985 / 25,848 / 412,947; Game 94,762 / 25,612 / 814,586.
  - Source: Amazon 2023 subsets, 5-core filter, sequence length 50: https://arxiv.org/html/2409.05546v3#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1; statistics: https://arxiv.org/html/2409.05546v3#S4.T2.
- **Split**: Per-user leave-one-out: latest interaction for test, second most recent for validation, the rest for training. Separate generalization study on Instrument and Scientific: the 5% of users with the least history are removed from training and evaluated as unseen users.
  - Source: Leave-one-out allocation: https://arxiv.org/html/2409.05546v3#S4.SS1.SSS3.p1; unseen-user experiment: https://arxiv.org/html/2409.05546v3#S4.SS4.SSS1.p1.
- **Candidates**: full catalog
  - Source: Full ranking over the entire item set: https://arxiv.org/html/2409.05546v3#S4.SS1.SSS3.p1.
- **Visibility**: Main: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. The generalization study holds out users, not items: test users are unseen by both tokenizer and generator training, while item visibility is unchanged.
  - Source: Main protocol and unseen-user study: https://arxiv.org/html/2409.05546v3#S4.SS1.SSS3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2409.05546v3#S4.SS4.SSS1.p1.
- **SID**: 3-level RQ-VAE x 256 codewords (dimension 128) over 256-dimensional SASRec collaborative embeddings; following TIGER, an extra token is appended to make IDs unique. The tokenizer is trained jointly with the generator by alternating optimization.
  - Source: 3 codebooks x 256, dimension 128, extra uniqueness token: https://arxiv.org/html/2409.05546v3#S4.SS1.SSS4.p1; SASRec embeddings as input: https://arxiv.org/html/2409.05546v3#S4.SS1.SSS4.p1.
- **Inference budget**: Beam size 20 for all generative models; T5 with 6 encoder and 6 decoder layers. Recall and NDCG at K=5 and 10. Hardware, inference batch size, and latency: not reported (Section 3.5 gives asymptotic complexity only).
  - Source: Beam size 20 for all generative models: https://arxiv.org/html/2409.05546v3#S4.SS1.SSS3.p1; backbone: https://arxiv.org/html/2409.05546v3#S4.SS1.SSS5.p1; complexity analysis only: https://arxiv.org/html/2409.05546v3#S3.SS5.SSS2.p1.
- **Results from**: Table 3 (Instrument, Scientific, Game; paired t-tests); Table 4 (alignment-loss and alternating-training ablations); Figure 2 (seen versus unseen users); Figure 4 (alignment coefficients).
  - Source: Main: https://arxiv.org/html/2409.05546v3#S4.T3; ablation: https://arxiv.org/html/2409.05546v3#S4.T4; seen/unseen users: https://arxiv.org/html/2409.05546v3#S4.F2; coefficients: https://arxiv.org/html/2409.05546v3#S4.F4.

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: competitor; note: TIGER trains the RQ-VAE tokenizer once and freezes it; ETEGRec optimizes tokenizer and generator alternately with sequence-item and preference-semantic alignment losses.; where: ETEGRec v3, baselines and implementation: https://arxiv.org/html/2409.05546v3#S4.SS1.SSS2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2409.05546v3#S4.SS1.SSS5.p2; Table 3: https://arxiv.org/html/2409.05546v3#S4.T3; unseen-user comparison in Figure 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2409.05546v3#S4.SS4.SSS1.p1.
- id: letter; relation: competitor; note: LETTER regularizes the tokenizer before generator training; ETEGRec couples the two end to end during training.; where: ETEGRec v3, Table 1 comparison of methods: https://arxiv.org/html/2409.05546v3#S3.T1; baselines with official implementation: https://arxiv.org/html/2409.05546v3#S4.SS1.SSS5.p2; Table 3: https://arxiv.org/html/2409.05546v3#S4.T3.
- id: cid; relation: competitor; note: CID and SID (Hua et al., 2023) are fixed indexing schemes for P5-style models; ETEGRec learns the tokenizer jointly with the recommender.; where: ETEGRec v3, Table 1: https://arxiv.org/html/2409.05546v3#S3.T1; baselines CID and SID with official implementations: https://arxiv.org/html/2409.05546v3#S4.SS1.SSS5.p2; Table 3: https://arxiv.org/html/2409.05546v3#S4.T3.
- id: adasid; relation: alternative; note: AdaSID keeps a pre-trained tokenizer and adapts collision repulsion, contrasting with ETEGRec's end-to-end downstream supervision of the tokenizer.; where: Evidence is from the later AdaSID paper, Section 2.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.23522v1#S2.SS2.p1.

### Notes

## 旧卡片说明

迁自 `d61aa6c:papers/etegrec.md`。保留方法说明、实验叙述与局限；本轮只对照现有记录处理明确冲突，未重新逐句核查原论文。分类和规格以页面上方由记录生成的表格为准。

### ETEGRec：端到端可学习物品分词生成推荐

> ETEGRec 将物品分词器与生成推荐器联合优化，让物品标识同时保留语义信息并适应推荐偏好。

### 研究动机与问题定义

固定或独立训练的物品 tokenizer 可能与推荐目标不一致，导致语义标识虽可解释却不利于生成。ETEGRec 研究 tokenizer 与推荐器的端到端协同学习。

### TL;DR（核心摘要）

`物品交互表示 → RQ-VAE分词器 → 语义/偏好对齐 → 生成推荐器 → SID对应物品`

物品编码器和残差量化器产生离散 token，生成推荐器根据用户历史预测 token 序列。序列-物品对齐和偏好-语义对齐损失共同更新两部分，使标识学习受到推荐任务反向约束。

### 输入与使用场景

| 方面 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| 使用信息 | 物品交互表示、用户历史和交互偏好 |
| 信息融入位置 | tokenizer 表示、生成输入和对齐目标 |
| 语义标识结构 | 多级离散序列 |
| 适用场景 | 常规生成式序列推荐 |

### 方法设计

#### 3.1 问题定义与双编码器-解码器结构
ETEGRec 同时包含物品 tokenizer 和生成推荐器。物品交互表示经过编码器和 RQ-VAE 得到离散表示，用户历史中的物品表示则由生成推荐器编码并用于预测下一物品 token。

#### 3.2 物品 tokenizer
tokenizer 通过残差量化逐层编码语义向量，并由解码器重构物品表示。量化损失和重构损失保证离散标识仍保留语义信息；相比固定 tokenizer，它可以在推荐训练中继续接受任务反馈。

#### 3.3 推荐导向对齐
序列-物品对齐让生成器学习历史与目标物品之间的关系，偏好-语义对齐则约束推荐偏好表示和重构语义表示的一致性。两个目标共同推动 tokenizer 从“语义可重构”转向“推荐可生成”。

#### 3.4 交替优化
论文在 tokenizer 和生成推荐器之间进行交替更新，避免离散 code 变化导致推荐器训练不稳定。推理时生成完整 item token 序列，并映射到目标物品。

### 实验结论

- 端到端可学习 tokenizer 在已见和未见用户设置下均有收益。
- 序列-物品与偏好-语义两类对齐目标均有效。

### 局限性与研究定位

#### 局限性
- 交替优化增加训练复杂度和稳定性要求。
- 动态新增物品、低延迟解码和开放目录场景仍未充分验证。

#### 研究定位
ETEGRec 的关键贡献是让 SID 学习直接接受推荐目标的反馈，适合放在“端到端物品标识学习”章节。

### 相关资源

- [论文原文](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.05546)

### 标签

`端到端学习` · `物品分词` · `语义-偏好对齐` · `生成式推荐`

*图源：原论文，图1。图片使用许可待核实。*

## Evo-Rec

- Page: pages/papers/evo-rec.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: III. SID–Model Alignment
- Stage: Training
- Representation: Text; Tokenization: RQ-VAE; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP → RL; Inference: CoT+C-Beam
- TL;DR: Evo-Rec aligns Semantic IDs with text and behavior, fine-tunes on sampled reasoning traces that improve target prediction, and then refines reasoning with catalog-constrained reinforcement learning.
- [Code](https://github.com/mengdanzhu/evo-rec)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Video Games, Office Products, Industrial and Scientific; 5-core filtering.
  - Source: Section 4.1.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2609.29973v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1
- **Split**: Per-user chronological 80%/10%/10% training/validation/test; sliding histories capped at 10.
  - Source: Section 4.1.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2609.29973v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1
- **Candidates**: full catalog
  - Source: Section 4.1.1 explicitly ranks against the entire item catalog: https://arxiv.org/html/2609.29973v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p2
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Item-level visibility to RQ-VAE and SID-language alignment: not reported.
  - Source: Sections 3.2 and 4.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2609.29973v1#S3.SS2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2609.29973v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1
- **SID**: Three RQ-VAE semantic tokens; codebook sizes and collision handling not reported.
  - Source: Sections 3.2 and 4.1.3: https://arxiv.org/html/2609.29973v1#S3.SS2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2609.29973v1#S4.SS1.SSS3.p1
- **Inference budget**: Reasoning followed by catalog-trie beam search, beam 10; inference hardware, batch size, reasoning cap, and latency not reported.
  - Source: Section 4.1.3 separates training rollout settings from inference: https://arxiv.org/html/2609.29973v1#S4.SS1.SSS3.p1
- **Results from**: Original Table 2; baseline numbers quoted from SIDReasoner, with Evo-Rec evaluated on the same split/protocol.
  - Source: Section 4.1.2 and Table 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2609.29973v1#S4.SS1.SSS2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2609.29973v1#S4.T2

### Related

- id: sidreasoner; relation: competitor; note: Evo-Rec compares against SIDReasoner and adds utility-selected reasoning plus ranking-aware RL.; where: Evo-Rec v1, Sections 2.2/4.1.2 and Table 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2609.29973v1#S2.SS2.p1; https://arxiv.org/html/2609.29973v1#S4.SS1.SSS2.p1; https://arxiv.org/html/2609.29973v1#S4.T2.
- id: lc-rec; relation: predecessor; note: The SID-language alignment stage explicitly follows LC-Rec before adding reasoning optimization.; where: Evo-Rec v1, Section 3.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2609.29973v1#S3.SS2.p1.
- id: tiger; relation: competitor; note: TIGER directly generates SIDs; Evo-Rec generates and optimizes an intermediate reasoning sequence.; where: Evo-Rec v1, Sections 2.1/3.1 and Table 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2609.29973v1#S2.SS1; https://arxiv.org/html/2609.29973v1#S3.SS1.p1; https://arxiv.org/html/2609.29973v1#S4.T2.

## FedCGR

- Page: pages/papers/fedcgr.md
- Venue: CIKM’26
- Problem: VI. Generalization
- Stage: Backbone
- Representation: Text; Tokenization: RQ-VAE; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP + Aux.; Inference: C-Beam
- TL;DR: FedCGR performs federated cross-domain recommendation over shared Semantic IDs from public metadata, injects local collaborative evidence, and aggregates parameters by domain relatedness, without exchanging private interactions.
- [Code](https://github.com/ZhuodLiu/FedCGR)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Review: Grocery, Beauty, Sports, Food, Kitchen; six cross-domain scenarios FK/GB/GS/FKB/GBS/GKBS; per-domain 5-core filtering.
  - Source: Section 4.1.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2608.10929v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2608.10929v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p3
- **Split**: Per-user leave-one-out: last item test, second-to-last validation, remaining interactions training.
  - Source: Section 4.1.3: https://arxiv.org/html/2608.10929v1#S4.SS1.SSS3.p1
- **Candidates**: full catalog; additionally sampled: 999 random negatives per user, fixed once and shared across methods (seed42). Negative-sampling distribution beyond random and history-item exclusion: not reported.
  - Source: Section 4.1.3: https://arxiv.org/html/2608.10929v1#S4.SS1.SSS3.p1
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Cold-start analysis groups users by training-history length (<=7, 8-15, >=16), not unseen items. SID metadata pretraining excludes private interactions; local CF uses client interaction sequences. Item-level generator/tokenizer/CF exposure: not reported.
  - Source: Sections 3.1 and 4.4: https://arxiv.org/html/2608.10929v1#S3.SS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2608.10929v1#S4.SS4.p1
- **SID**: Frozen metadata RQ-VAE: 3 levels x 256 codes; colliding items share SID scores, ties broken by validation-set item popularity.
  - Source: Sections 3.2 and 4.1.4: https://arxiv.org/html/2608.10929v1#S3.SS2.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2608.10929v1#S4.SS1.SSS4.p1
- **Inference budget**: Target-domain trie-constrained beam 50; H/NDCG@10; experiments on RTX 4090 GPUs. Inference batch size and latency: not reported.
  - Source: Sections 3.4 and 4.1.4: https://arxiv.org/html/2608.10929v1#S3.SS4.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2608.10929v1#S4.SS1.SSS4.p1
- **Results from**: Original Tables 3/4: full-ranking/sampled comparisons; Table 5: ablation; Table 6: diagnostics; Figures 3-5: user activity, sensitivity, communication efficiency.
  - Source: Tables 3-6 and Figures 3-5: https://arxiv.org/html/2608.10929v1#S4.T3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2608.10929v1#S4.T4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2608.10929v1#S4.T5 and https://arxiv.org/html/2608.10929v1#S4.T6 and https://arxiv.org/html/2608.10929v1#S4.F3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2608.10929v1#S4.F4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2608.10929v1#S4.F5

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: competitor; note: TIGER and its FedAvg/FedProx variants are full-ranking baselines.; where: FedCGR v1, Section 4.1.2 and Table 3: https://arxiv.org/html/2608.10929v1#S4.SS1.SSS2.p2; https://arxiv.org/html/2608.10929v1#S4.T3.
- id: gencdr; relation: alternative; note: GenCDR uses centralized semantic CDR; FedCGR keeps interactions local.; where: FedCGR v1, Section 5: https://arxiv.org/html/2608.10929v1#S5.p1; https://arxiv.org/html/2608.10929v1#S5.p2.
- id: vq-rec; relation: predecessor; note: Related work identifies VQ-Rec as an earlier transferable quantized-item representation method.; where: FedCGR v1, Section 5: https://arxiv.org/html/2608.10929v1#S5.p2.

## FLASH

- Page: pages/papers/flash.md
- Venue: NeurIPS’26
- Problem: III. SID–Model Alignment
- Stage: Backbone
- Representation: Text; Tokenization: SimHash; Backbone: Non-AR; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: MTP + Aux.; Inference: Scoring
- TL;DR: FLASH pairs training-free SimHash Semantic IDs with parallel decoding and explicit semantic alignment, attributing the weakness of hashing to autoregressive decoding and rigid discretization rather than hashing itself.
- [Code](https://github.com/KevinC2015/Flash)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 4

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Beauty, Toys and Games, Sports and Outdoors, CDs and Vinyl; users/items with fewer than 5 interactions removed.
  - Source: Sections 3.1 and A.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.07402v1#S3.SS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.07402v1#A1.SS1.p1
- **Split**: Per-user chronological leave-last-out: last item test, penultimate validation, earlier interactions training.
  - Source: Appendix A.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.07402v1#A1.SS1.p1
- **Candidates**: not reported
  - Source: Section 2.3 ranks all candidate items but evaluation sampling is unspecified: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.07402v1#S2.SS3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.07402v1#S3.SS1.p3
- **Visibility**: Warm main protocol; cold-start targets unseen by generator only: randomly select 5% of test-target items and remove all their training interactions. Tokenizer fitting n/a: fixed SimHash on precomputed text embeddings.
  - Source: Sections 2.1, 3.5 and A.4: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.07402v1#S2.SS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.07402v1#S3.SS5.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.07402v1#A1.SS4.p1
- **SID**: SimHash: Beauty 32x256, Toys/Sports 64x256, CDs 64x512; collision counts analyzed, collision disambiguation not reported.
  - Source: Section 2.1, Table 4 and collision analysis: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.07402v1#S2.SS1.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.07402v1#A1.T4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.07402v1#S3.SS3.SSS1.p3
- **Inference budget**: Parallel per-position probabilities cached, then candidate scores gathered/summed; K=5/10; beam n/a. Single NVIDIA A100 80GB for experiments; inference batch size and latency not reported.
  - Source: Sections 2.3, 3.1 and A.3: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.07402v1#S2.SS3.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.07402v1#S3.SS1.p3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.07402v1#A1.SS3.p4
- **Results from**: Original Table 1 overall results; Figure 6 cold-start. Most baseline results copied from TIGER/RPG; remaining baselines implemented from public code.
  - Source: Sections 3.1/3.2 and Figure 6: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.07402v1#S3.SS1.p4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.07402v1#S3.T1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.07402v1#S3.F6

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: predecessor; note: FLASH revisits TIGER's SimHash ablation with parallel decoding and semantic alignment.; where: FLASH v1, Introduction and Table 1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.07402v1#S1.p2; https://arxiv.org/html/2610.07402v1#S1.p3; https://arxiv.org/html/2610.07402v1#S3.T1.
- id: rpg; relation: predecessor; note: FLASH follows RPG's cached-logit scoring, replacing learned OPQ codes with training-free SimHash.; where: FLASH v1, Sections 2.3 and A.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.07402v1#S2.SS3.p2; https://arxiv.org/html/2610.07402v1#A1.SS2.p4.
- id: letter; relation: competitor; note: LETTER learns regularized residual codes; FLASH uses fixed hashing with parallel prediction and alignment.; where: FLASH v1, Section A.2 and Table 1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.07402v1#A1.SS2.p3; https://arxiv.org/html/2610.07402v1#S3.T1.
- id: diger; relation: competitor; note: DIGER jointly learns residual quantization and recommendation; FLASH uses a fixed tokenizer.; where: FLASH v1, Section A.2 and Table 1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.07402v1#A1.SS2.p3; https://arxiv.org/html/2610.07402v1#S3.T1.

## FlexCode

- Page: pages/papers/flexcode.md
- Venue: arXiv’25
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text+CF; Tokenization: Dual RQ-VAE; Backbone: –; Tokenizer: Joint; Objective: NTP; Inference: –
- TL;DR: FlexCode splits a fixed token budget between a collaborative codebook and a semantic codebook according to item popularity through a lightweight MoE, instead of one uniform codebook for all items.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon-Beauty, Amazon-Sports and Outdoors, KuaiRand-1K; 5-core filtering; proprietary industrial interactions.
  - Source: Sections 4.1.1 and Public Benchmarks: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.20673v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2511.20673v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.Px1.p1
- **Split**: Public: chronological last item test, penultimate validation; industrial: last logged day evaluation, validation not reported.
  - Source: Section 4.1.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.20673v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2511.20673v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.Px2.p1
- **Candidates**: not reported
  - Source: Candidate protocol absent from Section 4.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.20673v1#S4.SS1
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Head/tail evaluation concerns popularity; tokenizer and collaborative-encoder item exposure: not reported.
  - Source: Sections 4.1.1 and 4.3.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.20673v1#S4.SS1.SSS1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2511.20673v1#S4.SS3.SSS2.p1
- **SID**: Dual RQ-VAE; total token budgets 3/4/5/6, popularity-dependent allocation; base K=512. Main-experiment depth and collision handling not reported.
  - Source: Sections 3.1/3.3 and Tables 4-5: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.20673v1#S3.SS1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2511.20673v1#S3.SS3.p3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2511.20673v1#S5.T4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2511.20673v1#S5.T5
- **Inference budget**: Recall/NDCG@5/10; beam width, hardware, inference batch size, latency not reported.
  - Source: Sections 3.4 and 4.1.3: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.20673v1#S3.SS4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2511.20673v1#S4.SS1.SSS3.p1
- **Results from**: Original Table 1: public benchmarks; Figure 2: industrial overall and head/tail results.
  - Source: Table 1 and Figure 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.20673v1#S4.T1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2511.20673v1#S4.F2

## FORGE

- Page: pages/papers/forge.md
- Venue: KDD’26
- Problem: Paradigms, Systems and Benchmarks
- Stage: No single stage
- Representation: Text+Img; Tokenization: RQ-VAE; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP; Inference: Dyn. Beam
- TL;DR: FORGE is a benchmark and industrial dataset, not a new recommender: it compares Semantic ID construction strategies, adds metrics that assess IDs without generator training, and releases Taobao data.
- [Code](https://github.com/selous123/al_sid)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon 2023 Clothing (2,524,981 users / 714,957 items / 12,530,806 interactions; filtering not reported) and AL-GR, released from Taobao (131M users / 251M items / 14B interactions): 40 million behavior records sampled per day over ten consecutive days, sequences truncated to 100 items, with multimodal item embeddings and i2i relations.
  - Source: Datasets: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.20904v3#S3.SS3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2509.20904v3#S3.T1; AL-GR construction and truncation: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.20904v3#S3.SS3.SSS1.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2509.20904v3#S3.SS3.SSS1.p3.
- **Split**: AL-GR: temporal stages S1 (4 days), S2 (3 days), S3 (3 days); 100,000 samples from the day after each stage are used for evaluation; training uses the first clicked item as target, evaluation uses all interacted items on the page view. Amazon split: not reported.
  - Source: Stage split and next-day evaluation: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.20904v3#S3.SS3.SSS1.p2; targets: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.20904v3#S3.SS3.SSS1.p3; Amazon split not found in Sections 3-4.
- **Candidates**: Beam search generates 1,200 candidate SIDs (3 x 8192 example), mapped back to items; top-K items by score are checked against the page-view targets (HR@20 to HR@1000). Full catalog versus sampled candidates is not otherwise stated.
  - Source: 1,200 candidate SIDs from beam search mapped back to items: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.20904v3#S3.SS4.p1.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Evaluation uses the next day after each training stage.
  - Source: Next-day temporal evaluation; unseen-item generalization is cited, not tested: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.20904v3#S3.SS3.SSS1.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2509.20904v3#S2.SS2.p1.
- **SID**: Benchmark of configurations: main 3 levels x 8,192 codewords (also 2 x 32,768), RQ-VAE with 64-dimensional codebook over CN-CLIP multimodal features. Collisions are handled by optional post-processing that caps items per SID: KNN-based reassignment (thresholds 25, 10, 5) or Random-5 random assignment of the last codeword; a no-collision-handling variant (noco) is also tested.
  - Source: Main 3 x 8192 and 2 x 32768: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.20904v3#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2509.20904v3#S4.T11; collision post-processing: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.20904v3#S3.SS1.SSS3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2509.20904v3#S4.SS1.SSS4.p3; RQ-VAE config: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.20904v3#A1.T15.
- **Inference budget**: Beam search producing 1,200 candidate SIDs; generators T5-Base (0.2B), Qwen2.5-0.5B, and Qwen2.5-3B. Training uses 16 (T5) or 32 (Qwen2.5-0.5B) PPU-ZW810E GPUs; inference hardware, batch size, and latency: not reported.
  - Source: Beam candidates: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.20904v3#S3.SS4.p1; models and GPUs (training): https://arxiv.org/html/2509.20904v3#A1.SS2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2509.20904v3#A1.T14.
- **Results from**: Table 3 (AL-GR SID configurations across stages S1-S3); Table 4 (Amazon); Table 5 (relation sources); Table 9 (encoding methods including RQ-Kmeans); Table 11 (generative search); Table 12 (architectures and model sizes); Figures 3-4 (Embedding HitRate, Gini, and other SID metrics).
  - Source: Results: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.20904v3#S4.T3, https://arxiv.org/html/2509.20904v3#S4.T4, https://arxiv.org/html/2509.20904v3#S4.T5, https://arxiv.org/html/2509.20904v3#S4.T11, https://arxiv.org/html/2509.20904v3#S4.T12; encoding comparison: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.20904v3#S4.SS1.SSS6.p1.

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: predecessor; note: TIGER introduced RQ-VAE semantic IDs for recommendation; FORGE benchmarks how modality, encoding, and collision post-processing choices for such SIDs affect retrieval at industrial scale.; where: FORGE v3, Section 2.2 cites Rajput et al. (2023) as the SID adopted in recommendation: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.20904v3#S2.SS2.p1; Section 3.1.2 RQ-VAE encoding: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.20904v3#S3.SS1.SSS2.p1.

(2025) for RQ-Kmeans and compares it in Table 9: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.20904v3#S4.SS1.SSS6.p1.

### Notes

## 旧卡片说明

迁自 `d61aa6c:papers/forge.md`。保留方法说明、实验叙述与局限；本轮只对照现有记录处理明确冲突，未重新逐句核查原论文。分类和规格以页面上方由记录生成的表格为准。

### FORGE：工业数据集语义标识构建

> FORGE 面向大规模工业交互数据，融合多模态内容和协同关系构造、清洗并评估生成式检索所需的语义标识。

### 研究动机与问题定义

小规模公开数据集难以反映工业生成式检索中的多模态、长尾和标识碰撞问题。FORGE 提供大规模数据、SID 构建流程、碰撞后处理和生成式检索评估，重点考察标识质量对推荐的影响。

### TL;DR（核心摘要）

`多模态内容与协同关系 → RQ-VAE SID → 碰撞消解 → 生成式检索 → 推荐物品`

文本和图像编码器提取内容表示，并以最相关的物品关系补充协同信息；RQ-VAE 生成多级 SID，随后使用碰撞处理和质量指标筛选。下游生成式检索模型直接生成 SID，SID 再映射到物品。

### 输入与使用场景

| 方面 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| 使用信息 | 文本、图像、物品关系和用户交互 |
| 信息融入位置 | SID 构建与生成式检索训练 |
| 语义标识结构 | 多级离散序列 |
| 适用场景 | 大规模工业生成式检索 |

### 方法设计

#### 3.1 SID 生成（SID Generation）
FORGE 使用文本和图像语言模型提取物品多模态内容，并结合最具协同关系的物品信息。融合表示经过 RQ-VAE 量化为多级 SID，既保留内容语义，也纳入工业交互中的相似关系。

#### 3.2 标识碰撞缓解（Alleviating ID Collisions）
论文分析多个物品获得相同 SID 的情况，并通过碰撞后处理、码本分配和质量指标评估标识可用性。相关指标包括碰撞、分布均衡、生成命中和代码升级收敛等。

#### 3.3 生成式检索（Generative Retrieval）
SID 被作为生成式检索的目标序列，推荐模型直接预测 SID。论文同时讨论训练阶段和动态推理阶段，考察大规模工业交互下生成结果的有效性与泛化。

#### 3.4 评估与工业分析
实验把 SID 直接指标和下游推荐指标结合，并分析数据规模、模态组合、代码本升级和线上可用性。FORGE 的重点也包括工业数据资源与评估基准。

### 实验结论

- FORGE 的工业数据规模和交互密度显著高于常见公开基准。
- SID 质量指标与生成式检索效果存在关联，碰撞处理能改善可用性。

### 局限性与研究定位

#### 局限性
- 工业数据和线上结果的可复现程度受数据开放范围限制。
- 具体下游模型与完整线上延迟比较未统一报告。

#### 研究定位
FORGE 的价值在于把 SID 学习从小规模基准推进到工业数据工程与评估。它适合放在“工业生成式检索与语义标识质量”章节。

### 相关资源

- [项目与数据资源](https://huggingface.co/AL-GR)

### 标签

`工业数据` · `多模态` · `SID优化` · `生成式检索`

## GEM-Rec

- Page: pages/papers/gem-rec.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: IV. Utility
- Stage: Training
- Representation: Text; Tokenization: RQ-VAE; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP; Inference: Bid-Aware Beam
- TL;DR: GEM-Rec adds control tokens that decide whether to show an ad and bid-aware decoding that injects real-time bids, so one generator serves both semantic relevance and ad revenue.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 2

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Synthetic marketplaces built on Steam and Amazon Beauty, Sports, and Toys, each with 5-core filtering. A random 20% of items is designated sponsored and given log-normal bids (mu=0, sigma=0.2, clipped and normalized to [0.1, 1.0]); ads are injected into organic histories by a prefix-match relevance filter (depth 2, relaxed to 1), softmax bid selection (tau=0.1), and frequency capping (p=0.4, r=0.05; high-density ablation p=1.0, r=0.5). Main ad density about 3-6%; ablation about 10-20%. Retained corpus sizes: not reported.
  - Source: Base datasets and sponsored subset: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.22231v1#S5.SS1.p3; 5-core filtering: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.22231v1#A2.SS1.p1; bids and ad-injection policy: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.22231v1#A4.SS1.p1, https://arxiv.org/html/2603.22231v1#A4.SS2.p2, https://arxiv.org/html/2603.22231v1#A4.SS2.p3, https://arxiv.org/html/2603.22231v1#A4.SS2.p4.
- **Split**: not reported (the model is evaluated on test-set trajectories generated by the simulated policy; the train/validation/test construction is not described).
  - Source: Evaluation protocols name only test-set trajectories, not the split rule: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.22231v1#S5.SS2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2603.22231v1#S5.I2.i1.p1.
- **Candidates**: not reported (full catalog versus sampled evaluation candidates); ads are generated by beam search under a sampled slot flag.
  - Source: Metrics only: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.22231v1#S5.I2.i1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2603.22231v1#S5.I2.i2.p1.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined.
  - Source: No unseen-item protocol; synthetic logs from the same item universe: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.22231v1#S5.SS1.p3.
- **SID**: 3-level RQ-VAE x 256 codewords over Sentence-T5 item embeddings, plus a leading organic/sponsored flag token. Collision handling: not reported; the theoretical analysis assumes a one-to-one item-SID mapping.
  - Source: RQ-VAE depth 3 x 256 on Sentence-T5 embeddings: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.22231v1#A2.SS2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2603.22231v1#A6.p2; one-to-one item-SID mapping is an assumption of the proofs: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.22231v1#A3.p2.
- **Inference budget**: Hierarchical decoding: the organic/ad flag is sampled from modulated logits, then beam search of width K generates the SID; numerical K not reported. Bid modulation strength swept over lambda in [0, 10]. One NVIDIA A100 for all experiments; inference batch size and latency: not reported. Generated ad sequences are 100% valid (Table 4).
  - Source: Flag sampling then width-K content beam search: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.22231v1#S4.I2.i1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2603.22231v1#S4.I2.i2.p1; hardware: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.22231v1#A2.SS2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2603.22231v1#A6.p3; validity: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.22231v1#A7.T4.
- **Results from**: Table 1 (marketplace performance versus TIGER; full version in Appendix G, Table 3); Table 2 and Appendix H, Tables 5-8 (bid-shock response); Figures 2-7 (Pareto frontiers, steerability, organic integrity, high-ad-rate ablations); Table 4 (generative validity).
  - Source: Main: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.22231v1#S5.T1; full results: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.22231v1#A7.T3; volatility: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.22231v1#S5.T2, https://arxiv.org/html/2603.22231v1#A8.T5, https://arxiv.org/html/2603.22231v1#A8.T6, https://arxiv.org/html/2603.22231v1#A8.T7, https://arxiv.org/html/2603.22231v1#A8.T8.

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: competitor; note: TIGER is the pure-utility generative baseline without sponsored slots; GEM-Rec adds an organic/ad flag token and inference-time bid modulation of the logits.; where: GEM-Rec v1, Section 5.3: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.22231v1#S5.SS3.p1; Table 1 and Appendix Table 3: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.22231v1#S5.T1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2603.22231v1#A7.T3.
- id: liger; relation: predecessor; note: GEM-Rec builds on LIGER's reproduction of the TIGER architecture and 5-core preprocessing, without LIGER's own training objectives.; where: GEM-Rec v1, Section 5.4 adopts the codebase of Yang et al. (2024): https://arxiv.org/html/2603.22231v1#S5.SS4.p1; Appendix B.1 follows its 5-core filtering: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.22231v1#A2.SS1.p1; Appendix F matches its model scale: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.22231v1#A6.p1.

## GenCDR

- Page: pages/papers/gencdr.md
- Venue: AAAI’26
- Problem: VI. Generalization
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Cross-Dom; Tokenization: RQ+LoRA; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP; Inference: C-Beam
- TL;DR: GenCDR generates domain-disentangled Semantic IDs by routing between a universal encoder and domain adapters, and decodes over a domain-aware prefix tree, instead of relying on shared user or item IDs.
- [Code](https://github.com/hupeiyu21/GenCDR)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Three cross-domain pairs: Amazon Sports-Clothing (35,598 / 39,387 users; 18,357 / 23,033 items; item overlap 1.73%, 704), Amazon Phones-Electronics (27,879 / 192,403 users; 10,429 / 63,001 items; overlap 0.55%, 404), and Douban Books-Movies (1,713 / 2,628 users; 8,601 / 20,964 items; overlap 7.48%, 2,058). Filtering rules: not reported.
  - Source: Domain pairs: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.08006v2#Sx5.SSx1.p1; statistics and overlap after merging: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.08006v2#Sx5.T1; no filtering rule found in Section 5.1.
- **Split**: Chronological leave-last-out per user: last item for test, second-to-last for validation; checkpoint chosen by validation Recall@10.
  - Source: Chronological leave-last-out allocation: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.08006v2#Sx5.SSx1.p2; checkpoint selection: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.08006v2#Sx5.SSx1.p6.
- **Candidates**: not reported (full catalog versus sampled evaluation candidates); generation is restricted to the target domain's prefix tree.
  - Source: Metrics only: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.08006v2#Sx5.SSx1.p6.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. The RQ-VAE is pre-trained on the textual features of all items.
  - Source: Standard split with no cold-start experiment: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.08006v2#Sx5.SSx1.p2; RQ-VAE is pre-trained on all items: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.08006v2#Sx4.SSx1.SSSx1.p1.
- **SID**: Universal RQ-VAE with M codebooks over item text embeddings, plus domain-specific LoRA adapters and an item-level router; numerical M and codebook size: not reported. Collision handling: not reported.
  - Source: M codebooks, no numerical M or codebook size: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.08006v2#Sx4.SSx1.SSSx1.p1; adapters and router: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.08006v2#Sx5.SSx1.p7.
- **Inference budget**: Qwen2.5-7B with LoRA experts; decoding constrained by a per-domain prefix tree with masked softmax; beam width not reported. Training on NVIDIA H200 GPUs; inference batch size not reported. Figure 6 (Qwen2.5-0.5B) reports runtime memory and inference time versus item-pool size against TriCDR and TIGER, stating constant cost; numerical latencies are only in the figure.
  - Source: Domain-aware prefix tree: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.08006v2#Sx4.SSx2.SSSx4.p1; backbone and GPUs: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.08006v2#Sx5.SSx1.p7; scalability figure: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.08006v2#Sx5.SSx6.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2511.08006v2#Sx5.F6.
- **Results from**: Table 2 (six domains across three pairs versus single-domain, generative, and cross-domain baselines); Table 3 (ablations); Figures 3-6 (t-SNE, sensitivity, training efficiency, inference scalability).
  - Source: Main: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.08006v2#Sx5.T2; ablation: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.08006v2#Sx5.T3; efficiency: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.08006v2#Sx5.F5 and https://arxiv.org/html/2511.08006v2#Sx5.F6.

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: competitor; note: TIGER tokenizes one domain with a single RQ-VAE; GenCDR adds domain-specific tokenizer adapters with item-level routing and an LLM with universal and domain LoRA experts.; where: GenCDR v2, baselines: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.08006v2#Sx5.SSx1.p4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2511.08006v2#Sx5.I3.i2.I1.i2.p1; Table 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.08006v2#Sx5.T2; inference scalability in Figure 6: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.08006v2#Sx5.F6.
- id: vq-rec; relation: competitor; note: VQ-Rec transfers across domains with discrete codes in a discriminative model; GenCDR generates domain-adapted semantic IDs autoregressively.; where: GenCDR v2, baselines: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.08006v2#Sx5.I3.i2.I1.i1.p1; Table 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.08006v2#Sx5.T2.
- id: utgrec; relation: alternative; note: UTGRec is cited for item tokenization in generative recommendation that GenCDR describes as developed for single domains; GenCDR targets multi-domain tokenization with domain adapters.; where: GenCDR v2, Related Work cites Zheng et al. (2025): https://arxiv.org/html/2511.08006v2#Sx2.p2; not a baseline in Table 2.

### Notes

## 旧卡片说明

迁自 `d61aa6c:papers/gencdr.md`。保留方法说明、实验叙述与局限；本轮只对照现有记录处理明确冲突，未重新逐句核查原论文。分类和规格以页面上方由记录生成的表格为准。

### GenCDR：带自适应语义分词的跨域生成推荐

> GenCDR 用共享语义空间和域特定适配器构造统一 SID，并以动态路由适配不同领域的推荐偏好。

### 研究动机与问题定义

跨域推荐既需要共享知识，也需要保留领域特征；固定的物品标识和静态融合容易造成负迁移。GenCDR 研究如何让 SID 和生成器同时具备跨域共享与域内适应能力。

### TL;DR（核心摘要）

`多域物品文本 → 通用SID → 域适配量化 → 统一生成器 → 域路由 → 推荐物品`

第一阶段用共享编码器和 RQ-VAE 学习通用 SID；第二阶段通过 LoRA 适配器学习域特定表示，并用 item-level 动态路由融合通用与域内表示。统一生成器先学习跨域兴趣，再进行域特定微调，使用前缀树约束生成完整 SID，直接得到物品。

### 输入与使用场景

| 方面 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| 使用信息 | 多域物品文本与用户交互 |
| 信息融入位置 | SID 构建、LoRA 适配和生成输入 |
| 语义标识结构 | 跨域共享的层次化序列 |
| 适用场景 | 跨域序列推荐 |

### 方法设计

#### 3.1 问题定义与总体流程
GenCDR 面向多个领域的跨域序列推荐，目标是使用共享 SID 建立可迁移的物品和用户兴趣空间。系统分为域自适应分词、跨域自回归推荐和域特定微调三部分。

#### 3.2 域自适应分词
通用编码器和 RQ-VAE 先从多域文本学习共享语义基础；每个领域再通过 LoRA 适配器补充领域特征。item-level 动态路由器以物品为单位融合通用表示和域特定表示，融合结果再量化为 SID。

#### 3.3 跨域自回归推荐
统一生成器把跨域历史 SID 作为输入，先学习域无关的兴趣模式。域特定适配阶段加入各领域 LoRA，使模型保留共享知识并适应领域差异。

#### 3.4 训练与推理
训练采用通用阶段和领域微调阶段。在线生成时使用前缀树约束，确保输出完整 SID 能对应目标领域中的真实物品。

### 实验结论

- GenCDR 在跨域推荐设置中改善了域内和迁移表现。
- 动态路由和域特定 LoRA 有助于缓解负迁移。

### 局限性与研究定位

#### 局限性
- 多适配器和路由网络增加部署管理成本。
- 前缀树与域特定 SID 更新流程仍需更多工业验证。

#### 研究定位
GenCDR 的贡献是把域适配从推荐器参数扩展到 SID 表示和路由，适合放在“跨域语义标识生成”章节。

### 相关资源

- [论文原文](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.08006)

### 标签

`跨域推荐` · `自适应分词` · `动态路由` · `LoRA`

## GenRec-JD

- Page: pages/papers/genrec-jd.md
- Venue: SIGIR’26
- Problem: IV. Utility
- Stage: Training
- Representation: Text+Img+CF; Tokenization: RQ-VAE; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP → RL; Inference: Beam
- TL;DR: GenRec-JD trains a decoder-only generator with page-wise next-token prediction, compresses prompt Semantic IDs with a Token Merger, and aligns outputs with GRPO-SR under hybrid rewards.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: JD.com large-scale recommender platform: about 560 million user interaction sequences over one month. Filtering rules and catalog size: not reported.
  - Source: JD.com data scope: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.14878v1#S3.SS1.p1.
- **Split**: Temporal: the last day for testing, the remaining days for training; a validation split is not reported. Online: 10% of traffic per variant for one month on JD's homepage feed.
  - Source: Last-day test split: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.14878v1#S3.SS1.p1; online test: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.14878v1#S3.SS3.p1.
- **Candidates**: not reported (full catalog versus sampled evaluation candidates); HR and NDCG at K=1, 10, 50 over beam-search outputs, plus the share of invalid SIDs.
  - Source: Metrics only, including the hallucination rate: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.14878v1#S3.SS1.p1.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Online results report long-tail item gains without a visibility definition.
  - Source: Next-day temporal test with no unseen-item protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.14878v1#S3.SS1.p1; long-tail items are analyzed online only: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.14878v1#S3.SS3.p1.
- **SID**: 3-level RQ K-means over Qwen2.5-VL multimodal embeddings fine-tuned on domain collaborative pairs; codebook size per level: not reported. A linear token merger compresses each SID triplet into one input vector in the prompt. Collision handling: not reported; generated invalid SIDs are measured (HaR 4.96% for GenRec).
  - Source: Qwen2.5-VL embeddings fine-tuned on collaborative pairs, RQ K-means triplets: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.14878v1#S2.SS1.p2; token merger: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.14878v1#S2.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.
- **Inference budget**: Point-wise beam search returning beam-width items per query; numerical beam width not reported. Qwen2.5 decoder-only backbones of 1.5B, 3B, and 7B; training on 8 NVIDIA H100 GPUs; inference hardware, batch size, and latency: not reported.
  - Source: Point-wise beam search at serving: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.14878v1#S2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1; hardware: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.14878v1#S3.SS1.p1.
- **Results from**: Table 1 (page-wise SFT versus BERT4Rec, SASRec, TIGER, LC-Rec, with hallucination rate); Table 2 (model scaling); Table 3 (GRPO-SR and reward variants); Table 4 (one-month online A/B test).
  - Source: SFT table: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.14878v1#S3.T1; scaling: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.14878v1#S3.T2; RL: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.14878v1#S3.T3; online: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.14878v1#S3.T4.

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: competitor; note: TIGER is trained with point-wise next-item prediction; GenRec trains on page-wise target lists with a decoder-only LLM and aligns it with GRPO-SR.; where: GenRec v1, Section 3.1 baselines: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.14878v1#S3.SS1.p1; Table 1: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.14878v1#S3.T1.
- id: lc-rec; relation: competitor; note: LC-Rec also fine-tunes an LLM on SIDs but with point-wise NTP; GenRec adds page-wise supervision, a token merger, and RL alignment.; where: GenRec v1, Section 3.1 baselines: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.14878v1#S3.SS1.p1; Table 1: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.14878v1#S3.T1.
- id: letter; relation: alternative; note: LETTER improves the tokenizer, whereas GenRec keeps RQ K-means SIDs and changes the supervision and alignment of the generator.; where: GenRec v1, Section 4 cites Wang et al. (2025), LETTER: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.14878v1#S4.p1; not a baseline in Table 1.

## GenSAR

- Page: pages/papers/gensar.md
- Venue: RecSys’25
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text+CF; Tokenization: Shared/Spec. RQ; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: Multi-task NTP; Inference: C-Beam
- TL;DR: GenSAR unifies search and recommendation in one generator with dual-purpose identifiers carrying semantic and collaborative signals and task-specific training, to reduce the trade-off between the two tasks.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Semi-synthetic Amazon Electronics search/recommendation data; Commercial Chinese-app data, 10,000 users over two weeks. Filtering rules: not reported in paper.
  - Source: Section 4.1.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2504.05730v2#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1
- **Split**: not reported in paper; data-processing and train/validation/test details are delegated to code.
  - Source: Section 4.1.1 directs split details to code: https://arxiv.org/html/2504.05730v2#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1
- **Candidates**: Recommendation sampled: 99 random negatives excluding user-interacted items, plus the target. Search sampled: 99 BM25-retrieved hard negatives, plus the target; search history exclusion: not reported.
  - Source: Tables 3 and 4 captions: https://arxiv.org/html/2504.05730v2#S4.T3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2504.05730v2#S4.T4
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Collaborative-encoder exposure to test items: not reported.
  - Source: Sections 3.2.1 and 4.1 define no unseen-item protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2504.05730v2#S3.SS2.SSS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2504.05730v2#S4.SS1
- **SID**: Shared/task-specific RQ-VAE; sensitivity favors 2 shared + 2 task-specific codes. Numerical codebook size and collision handling: not reported; semantic/collaborative collision rates 0.18%/0.39%.
  - Source: Sections 3.2.2 and 4.4.2-4.4.3: https://arxiv.org/html/2504.05730v2#S3.SS2.SSS2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2504.05730v2#S4.SS4.SSS2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2504.05730v2#S4.SS4.SSS3.p2
- **Inference budget**: Constrained beam search; HR/NDCG@1/5/10. Beam width, hardware, inference batch size, latency: not reported in paper.
  - Source: Sections 3.4.2 and 4.1.3: https://arxiv.org/html/2504.05730v2#S3.SS4.SSS2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2504.05730v2#S4.SS1.SSS3.p1
- **Results from**: Original Tables 3/4: recommendation/search; Table 5: task ablations; Figures 4-7: identifier analyses.
  - Source: Tables 3-5 and Figures 4-7: https://arxiv.org/html/2504.05730v2#S4.T3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2504.05730v2#S4.T4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2504.05730v2#S4.T5 and https://arxiv.org/html/2504.05730v2#S4.F4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2504.05730v2#S4.F7

## GeoGR

- Page: pages/papers/geogr.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Representation
- Representation: Text+Geo+CF; Tokenization: R-KM+EM; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Altern.†; Objective: Multi-task NTP; Inference: Beam
- TL;DR: GeoGR builds geo-aware POI Semantic IDs from geographically constrained co-visited pairs, contrastive learning, and iterative refinement, then aligns an LLM to them through continued pre-training and fine-tuning.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 4

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Foursquare NYC and TKY (11 months of check-ins; POIs with fewer than 10 interactions and users with fewer than 10 check-ins removed, following GNPR-SID; 2,083 users / 5,135 POIs and 2,293 / 7,873), and AMAP industrial data: AMAP (one day of platform-wide traffic with users' traced histories; 7,536K users / 34,119K POIs) and AMAP-SH (one month in Shanghai; 4,820K users / 910K POIs). Industrial filtering rules: not reported.
  - Source: Datasets and filtering: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.10411v2#S5.SS1.SSS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.10411v2#S5.SS1.SSS1.p2; statistics: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.10411v2#S5.T1.
- **Split**: NYC and TKY: records sorted by time and split 80% / 10% / 10% into training, validation, and test. AMAP: one day for training and 1 million records randomly sampled from the following day for testing. AMAP-SH: last day held out for testing. Online: three-month A/B test against the legacy multi-stage retrieval.
  - Source: Splits: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.10411v2#S5.SS1.SSS1.p2; online test: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.10411v2#S5.SS9.p2.
- **Candidates**: not reported (full catalog versus sampled evaluation candidates); top-k SIDs come from beam search.
  - Source: Metrics only: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.10411v2#S5.SS1.SSS2.p1.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined.
  - Source: Temporal splits with no unseen-POI protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.10411v2#S5.SS1.SSS1.p2.
- **SID**: 3 RQ-Kmeans layers over Qwen-4B POI embeddings with geographic co-visitation alignment; codebook size stated as 32 and 64 for NYC and TKY, respectively, and 4,096 for AMAP and AMAP-SH. SIDs are refined by an EM-style loop with the LLM, using a 20-candidate dynamic beam to prevent SID collisions; a final collision-resolution rule is not reported.
  - Source: Three RQ-Kmeans layers and codebook sizes: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.10411v2#S5.SS1.SSS4.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.10411v2#S4.SS1.SSS2.p2; RQ-Kmeans following OneRec: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.10411v2#S4.SS1.p1; EM refinement with 20-candidate beam to avoid collisions: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.10411v2#S4.SS1.SSS3.p1.
- **Inference budget**: Offline: beam search for the top-k SIDs; numerical beam width not reported. Online: dynamic beam search generating 50 candidate SIDs per request; GeoGR-0.6B averages 50 ms per request on NVIDIA H20 GPUs versus 90 ms for GeoGR-4B; inference batch size not reported. Training on 16 H20 GPUs with per-GPU batch 16.
  - Source: Beam search for top-k: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.10411v2#S4.SS2.SSS2.p4; deployment budget and latency: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.10411v2#S5.SS9.p1; training hardware: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.10411v2#S5.SS1.SSS4.p1.
- **Results from**: Table 2 (NYC, TKY versus traditional, POI, and generative baselines); Table 3 (AMAP, AMAP-SH); Table 4 (ablation); Table 5 (SID quality); Table 6 (CPT effect); Section 5.6 (model scaling); Table 7 and Section 5.9 (three-month online A/B test).
  - Source: Public: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.10411v2#S5.T2; industrial: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.10411v2#S5.T3; ablation: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.10411v2#S5.T4; SID evaluation: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.10411v2#S5.T5; CPT: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.10411v2#S5.T6; scaling: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.10411v2#S5.SS6.p2; online: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.10411v2#S5.SS9.p2.

- id: oneloc; relation: competitor; note: OneLoc injects geography into the SID input embedding and adds geographic rewards; GeoGR builds geo-aware SIDs from geographically constrained co-visitation and refines them with an EM loop tied to the LLM.; where: GeoGR v2, Table 2 (POI baseline) and Table 3 (strongest industrial baseline): https://arxiv.org/html/2602.10411v2#S5.T2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.10411v2#S5.T3; discussion in Section 5.2.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.10411v2#S5.SS2.SSS2.p3.

## 旧卡片说明

迁自 `d61aa6c:papers/geogr.md`。保留方法说明、实验叙述与局限；本轮只对照现有记录处理明确冲突，未重新逐句核查原论文。分类和规格以页面上方由记录生成的表格为准。

### GeoGR：面向工业规模生成式 POI 推荐的时空感知框架

> GeoGR 通过地理约束共访关系构造时空协同 SID，并用持续预训练和监督微调使 LLM 直接生成可服务的 POI 标识。

### 研究动机与问题定义

工业 POI 推荐同时面对稀疏行为、复杂地理关系和 LLM 不理解非原生 SID token 的问题。GeoGR 面向导航类本地服务，目标是在保留用户时空状态变化的同时，建立可生成、可扩展并能在线服务的 POI 标识。

### TL;DR（核心摘要）

`POI描述/地理/共访关系 → 对比表示学习 → RQ-KMeans SID → CPT → SFT生成 → 在线POI`

GeoGR 先利用地理约束的共访 POI 对学习时空协同表示，再通过层次化 RQ-KMeans 生成 SID，并用 EM 风格优化减少标识质量问题。推荐模型经过多模板持续预训练和监督微调，使 LLM 学会 SID、POI 描述与下一位置预测之间的对应关系。

### 输入与使用场景

| 方面 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| 使用信息 | POI 描述、经纬度、地理约束共访关系和用户轨迹 |
| 信息融入位置 | SID 表示、量化优化、持续预训练和生成输入 |
| 语义标识结构 | 多级定长离散序列 |
| 适用场景 | 导航、本地生活和工业规模服务 |

### 方法设计

#### 4.1 地理感知 POI SID 构建
GeoGR 将 POI 文本、经纬度、地址和类别输入 LLM，构造初始语义表示。为避免只依赖文本相似性，作者从用户轨迹中挖掘地理接近且具有共访关系的 POI 对，并加入正负样本进行对比学习。

#### 4.1.1 时空协同语义表示
正样本来自轨迹中频繁共现且空间相近的 POI，负样本通过采样获得。对比目标使表示同时靠近行为相关和地理合理的 POI，减少“文本相似但行为无关”的错误关联。

#### 4.1.2 语义表示量化
模型使用层次化 RQ-KMeans 逐级量化 POI 表示。每层对当前残差聚类并生成 code，所有 code 拼成 POI SID；层次结构让前缀承载较粗粒度的时空语义。

#### 4.1.3 EM 风格 SID 优化
作者让 LLM 根据生成 SID 相关任务反向评估标识质量，再用 EM 风格过程交替细化 SID 和模型参数，改善 SID 与 POI 语义、地理关系的一致性。

#### 4.2 生成式 POI 推荐
在推荐训练前，GeoGR 用包含 SID 描述、用户轨迹和 POI 问答的多任务语料进行持续预训练，使 LLM 适应新增的非原生 token。之后使用下一 POI 监督模板进行 SFT，模型根据历史和当前上下文自回归生成目标 SID。

### 实验结论

- 公共数据集和工业数据集实验均报告 GeoGR 优于比较方法。
- 在线部署三个月的实验报告 WINRATE 提升 2.91%、PV_CTR 提升 5.55%，说明该框架具备生产可用性。
- 消融与表示可视化支持地理协同 SID、CPT 和 SFT 对效果的贡献；模型规模影响也被单独分析。

### 局限性与研究定位

#### 局限性

- SID 构建、EM 风格优化和多阶段 LLM 训练流程较复杂，复现实验需要较多工业数据与资源。
- 论文对动态新增 POI、标识碰撞在线修复和生成失败回退的细节报告有限。

#### 研究定位

GeoGR 适合放在“工业级地理生成式推荐”章节，体现时空协同 SID 与 LLM 任务对齐、线上部署相结合的路线。

### 相关资源

- [论文原文](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.10411)

### 标签

`工业规模` · `时空协同` · `RQ-KMeans` · `在线部署`

## GFlowGR

- Page: pages/papers/gflowgr.md
- Venue: SIGIR’26
- Problem: IV. Utility
- Stage: Training
- Representation: Text / Text+CF; Tokenization: RQ-VAE / Learn. RQ; Backbone: Enc-Dec†; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP + Aux.; Inference: Beam† / C-Beam†
- TL;DR: GFlowGR fine-tunes generative recommenders as multi-step generation with GFlowNets, using a collaborative trajectory sampler and reward model to explore unobserved positives, instead of next-token or DPO fine-tuning.
- [Code](https://github.com/Applied-Machine-Learning-Lab/SIGIR26_GFlowGR)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Yelp, Amazon Beauty, and Amazon Instruments, preprocessed following LETTER (filter thresholds not restated); 30,431 / 20,032, 22,362 / 12,101, and 24,772 / 9,922 users / items. Production: Taobao search advertising data with hundreds of millions of daily requests; filtering not reported.
  - Source: Datasets and LETTER preprocessing: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.16114v3#S4.SS1.p1; statistics: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.16114v3#S4.T1; production data: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.16114v3#S5.p2.
- **Split**: Per-user leave-one-out: last item for test, second-to-last for validation, the rest for training. Three random seeds. Online: 15-day A/B test on 10% of traffic (50/50).
  - Source: Leave-one-out allocation: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.16114v3#S4.SS1.p1; three seeds: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.16114v3#S4.SS1.p2; online test: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.16114v3#S5.p3.
- **Candidates**: not reported (full catalog versus sampled evaluation candidates); top-5 and top-10 lists. Training negatives for the flow objective come from a collaborative-model sampler or beam search, which is a training choice, not the evaluation candidate set.
  - Source: Metrics only: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.16114v3#S4.SS1.p2.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Online, newly listed items gain 4.0% revenue, but their tokenizer and generator visibility is not reported.
  - Source: Standard split with no unseen-item protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.16114v3#S4.SS1.p1; online newly listed items without visibility definition: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.16114v3#S5.p3.
- **SID**: Uses the TIGER and LETTER tokenizers as backbones; layer count and codebook size for the experiments: not reported (Figure 1 illustrates L=3). Collision handling: not reported; the paper notes that intermediate states do not uniquely identify items.
  - Source: Backbones TIGER and LETTER, no own SID settings: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.16114v3#S4.SS1.p2; L=3 appears in the overview figure: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.16114v3#S1.F1.
- **Inference budget**: Decoding method and beam width for evaluation: not reported. All experiments run on the same GPU (model not stated). Table 7 reports training cost on production data (GFlowGR 2.1x SFT with 80x samples); inference latency and batch size: not reported.
  - Source: Hardware statement and cost: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.16114v3#S4.SS1.p3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2506.16114v3#S4.T7.
- **Results from**: Table 2 (Beauty, Instruments, Yelp; SFT, GRPO, DPO-family baselines on TIGER and LETTER backbones); Tables 3-6 (rewards, combination, sample selection, LLM reward); Figures 3-4 (parameter study); Table 7 and Section 5 (production offline and 15-day online A/B).
  - Source: Main: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.16114v3#S4.T2; ablations and strategies: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.16114v3#S4.T3, https://arxiv.org/html/2506.16114v3#S4.T4, https://arxiv.org/html/2506.16114v3#S4.T5, https://arxiv.org/html/2506.16114v3#S4.T6; production: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.16114v3#S4.T7 and https://arxiv.org/html/2506.16114v3#S5.p3.

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: predecessor; note: TIGER is one of the two generative backbones; GFlowGR updates the LLM with the sum of the SFT loss and a GFlowNets loss over augmented generation trajectories.; where: GFlowGR v3, Section 4.1 installs GFlowGR on TIGER: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.16114v3#S4.SS1.p2; Table 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.16114v3#S4.T2; training objective: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.16114v3#S3.SS4.p1.

- id: onerec; relation: competitor; note: OneRec's IPA aligns the model by iterative SFT and DPO with reward-selected rejected samples; GFlowGR learns probabilities proportional to rewards over many trajectories.; where: GFlowGR v3, IPA baseline from OneRec, reimplemented with the same reward model: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.16114v3#S4.I2.i6.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2506.16114v3#S4.SS1.p3; Table 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.16114v3#S4.T2.

## 旧卡片说明

迁自 `d61aa6c:papers/gflowgr.md`。保留方法说明、实验叙述与局限；本轮只对照现有记录处理明确冲突，未重新逐句核查原论文。分类和规格以页面上方由记录生成的表格为准。

### GFlowGR：生成流网络生成式推荐微调

> GFlowGR 将生成流网络用于生成式推荐微调，使模型从多条可能的生成轨迹中学习更符合推荐价值的物品标识。

### 研究动机与问题定义

最大似然训练倾向于复现日志中的单一路径，难以表达推荐结果的多样性和长期价值。GFlowGR 将 SID 生成过程视为轨迹采样问题，用奖励约束生成分布。

### TL;DR（核心摘要）

`用户历史 → SID生成轨迹 → 奖励模型 → GFlowNet微调 → 推荐物品`

框架从交互日志、随机采样、协同模型或在线策略获得轨迹，并训练奖励模型评估生成结果。GFlowNet 目标在训练阶段调整生成概率；在线仍由生成器直接产生完整 SID 并映射物品。

### 输入与使用场景

| 方面 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| 使用信息 | 交互日志、协同信号和生成轨迹 |
| 信息融入位置 | 奖励模型与轨迹采样 |
| 语义标识结构 | 多 token 序列 |
| 适用场景 | 偏好对齐与多样化推荐 |

### 方法设计

#### 3.1 轨迹采样器（Trajectory Sampler）
GFlowGR 把 SID 逐 token 生成看作从根节点到完整物品标识的轨迹。轨迹可以来自交互日志、随机策略、协同模型、组合采样或当前生成策略，用于覆盖单一监督路径之外的候选空间。

#### 3.2 奖励模型（Reward Model）
奖励模型评估完整生成结果或中间轨迹的推荐价值，将点击/偏好等信号转成训练奖励。它负责提供 GFlowNet 所需的终点价值，但不作为在线独立精排器。

#### 3.3 GFN 训练目标
模型学习前向生成概率与后向流之间的平衡，使不同高价值 SID 轨迹获得合理概率。该目标鼓励多条有效生成路径共存，缓解最大似然对单一日志目标的过拟合。

#### 3.4 训练与推理
训练阶段交替采样轨迹、计算奖励和更新生成器；推理阶段仍由生成器直接产生 SID。实验还分析不同轨迹来源、参数设置和部署成本。

### 实验结论

- GFlowNet 微调改善了生成推荐的排序表现。
- 不同轨迹来源对训练效果有影响，在线策略轨迹更贴近目标。

### 局限性与研究定位

#### 局限性
- 奖励模型和轨迹采样带来额外训练成本。
- 奖励偏差、探索范围与线上稳定性仍需验证。

#### 研究定位
GFlowGR 的贡献是把生成式推荐的偏好微调改写为生成流学习问题，适合放在“生成轨迹优化与偏好学习”章节。

### 标签

`生成流网络` · `偏好优化` · `SID生成` · `序列推荐`

### 架构图来源

*图源：原论文，图2。图片使用许可待核实。*

- 使用场景：偏好对齐。

## Ghost

- Page: pages/papers/ghost.md
- Venue: NeurIPS’26
- Problem: IV. Utility
- Stage: Training
- Representation: Text; Tokenization: Skeleton R-KM; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP + Aux.; Inference: –
- TL;DR: Ghost reduces popularity bias in generative recommenders with an asymmetric unlikelihood loss and skeleton-founded tokenization, addressing token-level optimization and undifferentiated item tokenization as its causes.
- [Code](https://github.com/Esperanto-mega/Ghost)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 2

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Product Review 2018: Musical Instruments; Arts, Crafts and Sewing; Video Games. Users/items with fewer than five interactions are filtered out.
  - Source: Appendix C-A: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.16825v3#A3.SS1.p1
- **Split**: User interactions are ordered chronologically; train/validation/test allocation: not reported.
  - Source: Appendix C-A reports chronological sequences but no holdout allocation: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.16825v3#A3.SS1.p1
- **Candidates**: not reported
  - Source: Section V and Appendix C describe metrics/baselines but not Ghost's candidate protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.16825v3#S5 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.16825v3#A3
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined.
  - Source: Section V and Appendix C define no unseen-item evaluation: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.16825v3#S5 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.16825v3#A3
- **SID**: Skeleton RQ-KMeans, 256 centers/level; head length Lh, tail length Lh+Lt with inherited head prefix. Sweeps Lh=3/4/5 and Lt=1/2/3; main numerical lengths and collision handling: not reported.
  - Source: Section IV-A, Section V-C, Appendix C-D: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.16825v3#S4.SS1.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.16825v3#S5.SS3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.16825v3#A3.SS4.p2
- **Inference budget**: Metrics at K=5/10; decoding algorithm, beam width, inference batch size, latency: not reported. General experimental machine: 8 NVIDIA A100 80GB GPUs; inference-specific allocation: not reported.
  - Source: Table I and Appendix C-D: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.16825v3#S5.T1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.16825v3#A3.SS4.p2
- **Results from**: Original Table I: main comparison; Table II: ablations; Table III: backbone scaling. Main and ablation experiments use Qwen2.5-3B; scaling uses Qwen3 0.6B-8B.
  - Source: Tables I-III and Appendix C-D: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.16825v3#S5.T1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.16825v3#S5.T2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.16825v3#S5.T3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.16825v3#A3.SS4.p1

## GMC

- Page: pages/papers/gmc.md
- Venue: arXiv’25
- Problem: VI. Generalization
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Cross-Dom; Tokenization: Unified RQ; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP; Inference: C-Beam
- TL;DR: GMC assigns domain-shared Semantic IDs with a domain-aware contrastive loss and trains one sequence-to-sequence generator across domains, instead of relying on users or items shared between domains.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 4

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Multi-target cross-domain task on five Amazon 2018 Reviews subsets: Scientific, Pantry, Instruments, Arts, Office. Items without titles are removed and 5-core filtering is applied to users and items; sequences capped at 20 items. Sizes (users / items): 8,317 / 4,344; 13,073 / 4,897; 24,772 / 9,922; 45,141 / 20,956; 86,554 / 25,847.
  - Source: Five Amazon subsets, title filter, 5-core, length 20: https://arxiv.org/html/2507.12871v3#S5.SS1.SSS1.p1; statistics: https://arxiv.org/html/2507.12871v3#S5.T2.
- **Split**: Per-user leave-one-out: last item for test, second latest for validation, the rest for training; results reported per domain and as a user-weighted average.
  - Source: Leave-one-out allocation: https://arxiv.org/html/2507.12871v3#S5.SS1.SSS3.p1.
- **Candidates**: full catalog (the target item is ranked over the entire item set).
  - Source: Ranking over the entire item set: https://arxiv.org/html/2507.12871v3#S5.SS1.SSS3.p1.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined.
  - Source: Standard split with no unseen-item protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2507.12871v3#S5.SS1.SSS3.p1.
- **SID**: 4-level RQ-VAE x 256 codewords (dimension 32) over LLaMA-3.1-8B text embeddings (D=4,096), with a codebook shared across domains and a domain-aware contrastive loss; first-level codes separate domains and deeper levels are shared. Collision handling: not reported.
  - Source: L=4 x N=256, d=32, LLaMA-3.1 4,096-dimensional embeddings, shared codebook across domains: https://arxiv.org/html/2507.12871v3#S5.SS1.SSS4.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2507.12871v3#S5.SS4.SSS1.p2; no collision rule found.
- **Inference budget**: Beam size 20 for item generation; T5-small backbone with domain-specific LoRA. Recall and NDCG at K=5 and 10. Hardware, inference batch size, and latency: not reported.
  - Source: Beam size 20: https://arxiv.org/html/2507.12871v3#S5.SS1.SSS4.p2; T5-small backbone: https://arxiv.org/html/2507.12871v3#S5.SS1.SSS4.p2.
- **Results from**: Table 3 (five domains and user-weighted average versus ID, ID-text, pre-training, and generative baselines); Table 4 (ablations); Figures 3-5 (code sharing, code similarity, multi-domain settings).
  - Source: Main: https://arxiv.org/html/2507.12871v3#S5.T3; ablation: https://arxiv.org/html/2507.12871v3#S5.T4; code analysis: https://arxiv.org/html/2507.12871v3#S5.F3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2507.12871v3#S5.F4; domain settings: https://arxiv.org/html/2507.12871v3#S5.F5.

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: competitor; note: TIGER learns one-domain RQ-VAE identifiers; GMC learns a domain-shared codebook with a domain-aware contrastive loss and adds domain-specific LoRA tuning to a unified generator.; where: GMC v3, generative baselines: https://arxiv.org/html/2507.12871v3#S5.I1.i4.I1.i2.p1; Table 1 comparison: https://arxiv.org/html/2507.12871v3#S3.T1; Table 3: https://arxiv.org/html/2507.12871v3#S5.T3.

- id: idgenrec; relation: competitor; note: IDGenRec learns textual IDs with an ID generator; GMC quantizes LLM embeddings into codebook IDs shared across domains.; where: GMC v3, generative baselines: https://arxiv.org/html/2507.12871v3#S5.I1.i4.I1.i3.p1; Table 3: https://arxiv.org/html/2507.12871v3#S5.T3.

## 旧卡片说明

迁自 `d61aa6c:papers/gmc.md`。保留方法说明、实验叙述与局限；本轮只对照现有记录处理明确冲突，未重新逐句核查原论文。分类和规格以页面上方由记录生成的表格为准。

### GMC：生成式多目标跨域推荐

> GMC 以共享语义标识连接多个推荐领域，并通过领域对比学习和域特定 LoRA 同时生成不同领域的推荐结果。

### 研究动机与问题定义

多目标跨域推荐需要从多个领域的行为中迁移知识，但领域间物品通常不重叠，传统 ID 难以建立共享空间。GMC 将物品文本转为跨域共享的语义 token，并统一训练生成器。

### TL;DR（核心摘要）

`多域文本 → 共享RQ-VAE SID → 统一生成器 → 域特定LoRA → 多域推荐物品`

GMC 使用 LLM 文本表示和 RQ-VAE 构造共享语义标识，并以领域对比损失拉近域内物品、区分跨域物品。统一推荐器在所有领域上训练，再为各领域加入 LoRA 适配器，直接自回归生成目标 SID。

### 输入与使用场景

| 方面 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| 使用信息 | 多域物品文本和用户交互 |
| 信息融入位置 | SID 量化、领域对比目标和生成训练 |
| 语义标识结构 | 跨域共享定长序列 |
| 适用场景 | 多目标跨域推荐 |

### 方法设计

#### 3.1 任务定义与总体流程
GMC 研究多个领域同时存在多个推荐目标的场景。方法分为语义标识学习、统一推荐器训练和领域特定微调三个步骤，核心是让不同领域共享可生成的 SID。

#### 3.2 语义标识学习
LLM 将物品文本编码为语义向量，统一 RQ-VAE 生成跨域共享的多级标识。领域对比损失拉近同领域物品表示并区分跨领域表示，同时保持 codeword 可共享。

#### 3.3 统一推荐器训练
所有领域的交互序列先替换为 SID，再用 Transformer 统一训练 next-item 生成。共享 SID 使不同领域的推荐模式可以在同一生成词表中迁移。

#### 3.4 领域特定微调
冻结统一推荐器后，为各领域加入 LoRA，并通过域内拉近、域间区分的目标适配领域偏好。最终生成器直接预测各领域目标 SID，完成多目标推荐。

### 实验结论

- GMC 在多目标跨域设置中优于论文列出的传统、预训练和生成式基线。
- 共享 SID、领域对比损失和域特定适配均有贡献。

### 局限性与研究定位

#### 局限性
- 多领域适配器和统一词表增加管理成本。
- 论文主要依赖离线文本表示，动态内容和开放物品验证有限。

#### 研究定位
GMC 的核心贡献是用共享 SID 作为多目标跨域知识桥梁，适合放在“跨域生成式推荐”章节。

### 相关资源

### 标签

`多目标跨域` · `共享SID` · `领域对比学习` · `LoRA`

- 使用场景：多目标跨域。

## GNPR-SID

- Page: pages/papers/gnpr-sid.md
- Venue: KDD’25
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Attr+Geo+CF; Tokenization: RQ-VAE; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP; Inference: –
- TL;DR: GNPR-SID replaces random numeric POI IDs with RQ-VAE Semantic IDs built from semantic and collaborative features under a diversity loss, and fine-tunes an LLM to generate the next POI.
- [Code](https://github.com/wds1996/GNPR-SID)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Foursquare NYC and TKY, Gowalla CA. POIs with fewer than 10 interactions and users with fewer than 10 check-ins are removed (following Yan et al. 2023). Sizes (users / POIs): NYC 1,083 / 5,135; TKY 2,293 / 7,873; CA 6,592 / 14,027.
  - Source: Datasets, filters, splits: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.01375v2#S5.SS1.p1; statistics: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.01375v2#S5.T1.
- **Split**: Records sorted by time and split 80% / 10% / 10% into training, validation, and test; within each user's test sequence the last visited POI is the target. Separate cross-city test: train on one city and test on the others (Table 5).
  - Source: Temporal 80/10/10 split and last-visit target: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.01375v2#S5.SS1.p1; out-of-domain transfer: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.01375v2#S6.T5.
- **Candidates**: not reported (full catalog versus sampled candidates); the metric is top-1 accuracy (Acc@1) of the generated POI.
  - Source: Top-1 accuracy only: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.01375v2#S5.SS3.p1.
- **Visibility**: warm; users and POIs that do not appear in the training set are removed from the test set. The cross-city test in Table 5 uses POIs from another city, but their tokenizer visibility is not reported.
  - Source: Test users and POIs absent from training are removed: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.01375v2#S5.SS1.p1.
- **SID**: 3-level RQ-VAE with 32 (NYC) or 64 (TKY, CA) codewords of dimension 64, k-means-initialized, plus diversity and compactness losses. Remaining collisions get an appended fourth token that makes each POI's SID unique (e.g. <d_0>, <d_1>). Table 4 reports unique SIDs and collisions before the suffix (e.g. NYC 590 collisions at lambda=0.25).
  - Source: 3 layers x 32 (NYC) or 64 (TKY, CA), dimension 64, k-means initialization: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.01375v2#S5.SS2.p1; collision suffix: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.01375v2#S4.SS1.SSS2.p6; diversity loss and collision counts: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.01375v2#S4.SS1.SSS3.Px3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2506.01375v2#S6.T4.
- **Inference budget**: LLaMA3-8B with LoRA; decoding method not reported beyond top-1 prediction. Fine-tuning on 4 NVIDIA L40 GPUs (batch 2 per GPU); inference batch size not reported. Table 6 (NYC): total test time 110.62 s versus 230.36 s for LLM4POI.
  - Source: Hardware for fine-tuning: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.01375v2#S5.SS2.p1; efficiency table: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.01375v2#S6.T6; decoding not specified in Section 5.
- **Results from**: Table 2 (Acc@1 on NYC, TKY, CA versus traditional, Transformer, GCN, time-aware, and LLM-based baselines); Table 3 (ablations); Table 4 (diversity-loss weight and SID collisions); Table 5 (cross-city generalization); Table 6 (efficiency).
  - Source: Main: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.01375v2#S6.T2; ablation: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.01375v2#S6.T3; diversity loss: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.01375v2#S6.T4; cross-city: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.01375v2#S6.T5; efficiency: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.01375v2#S6.T6.

### Related

- id: lc-rec; relation: predecessor; note: GNPR-SID follows LC-Rec in aligning an LLM to SID tokens through language-task prompts, and adds POI-specific quantization with time-aware prompts.; where: GNPR-SID v2, Section 4.2 builds its prompts inspired by Zheng et al. (2024): https://arxiv.org/html/2506.01375v2#S4.SS2.p2.
- id: tiger; relation: alternative; note: TIGER is cited as generative recommendation with semantic IDs for products; GNPR-SID adapts RQ-VAE SIDs to POIs with diversity and compactness losses and an LLM generator.; where: GNPR-SID v2, Section 2 cites Rajput et al. (2023): https://arxiv.org/html/2506.01375v2#S2.p2; not a baseline in Table 2.
- id: geogr; relation: alternative; note: GeoGR later builds geo-aware SIDs from geographic co-visitation and an EM refinement loop, and reports gains over GNPR-SID's SIDs.; where: Evidence is from the later GeoGR paper: it follows GNPR-SID preprocessing and compares against it in Tables 2, 3, and 5: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.10411v2#S5.SS1.SSS1.p2, https://arxiv.org/html/2602.10411v2#S5.T2, https://arxiv.org/html/2602.10411v2#S5.T3, https://arxiv.org/html/2602.10411v2#S5.T5.

## 旧卡片说明

迁自 `d61aa6c:papers/gnprsid.md`。保留方法说明、实验叙述与局限；本轮只对照现有记录处理明确冲突，未重新逐句核查原论文。分类和规格以页面上方由记录生成的表格为准。

### GNPR-SID：基于语义标识的生成式下一兴趣点推荐

> GNPR-SID 将 POI 的语义、地理、时间和协同信息构造成层次化 SID，再由大语言模型直接生成下一 POI 的完整标识。

### 研究动机与问题定义

传统下一 POI 推荐常使用随机数值 ID，模型难以从相近地点的标识之间迁移语义和地理关系。GNPR-SID 研究如何把 POI 描述与用户协同信息编码为可生成的语义标识，并根据用户历史访问记录和目标时间预测下一访问地点。

### TL;DR（核心摘要）

`POI内容/地理/时间/协同信息 → RQ-VAE量化 → POI SID → LLM生成 → 下一POI`

模型先用 POI 类别、区域、营业时间和协同关系构成语义向量，再用带多样性约束的残差量化得到层次化 SID；随后将用户历史 SID 与时间组织为提示，微调 LLM 自回归生成目标 SID。生成的 SID 通过标识表直接解析为 POI，不需要独立排序模型。

### 输入与使用场景

| 方面 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| 使用信息 | POI 类别、区域、营业时间、用户协同信号和历史访问时间 |
| 信息融入位置 | SID 构建阶段及 LLM 的序列生成输入 |
| 语义标识结构 | 定长、多级离散序列 |
| 适用场景 | 下一 POI 推荐、跨域泛化和冷启动分析 |

### 方法设计

#### 4.1 语义标识构建
作者将 POI 的类别、区域、时间信号以及用户协同关系拼接为统一语义表示。协同部分依据用户共同访问 POI 的关系构造，使表示同时包含内容相似性和行为关联。

#### 4.1.1 POI 语义表示
每个 POI 的基本属性被转换为 one-hot 特征，并与区域、营业时间和协同用户信息拼接。这样构造出的向量既描述 POI 本身，也保留其在交互网络中的位置。

#### 4.1.2 POI 量化
模型使用 RQ-VAE 的编码器、残差量化器和解码器，将连续 POI 表示映射到多级 codebook。每一级量化当前残差，多个 code 组成层次化 SID；相近 POI 可共享前缀，从而为生成模型提供可迁移的语义结构。

#### 4.1.3 模型优化
除重构和量化目标外，方法加入 diversity loss，使 code 在离散空间中更均匀分布，减少大量 POI 使用相同 code 或形成碰撞。附录还给出了裁剪、填空式训练等数据增强方式。

#### 4.2 生成式 POI 推荐
用户历史被序列化为带时间的 SID 序列，模型在指定时间条件下生成下一 POI SID。训练阶段采用语言模型微调目标；推理时直接生成完整 SID 并通过映射确定 POI。论文还比较了移除 SID、时间信息和多样性损失后的效果。

### 实验结论

- 在三个 POI 数据集上，GNPR-SID 相比比较方法取得更好的下一地点预测效果，论文报告最高约 16% 的准确率提升。
- SID 的语义相关性分析表明，相似 POI 更倾向共享前缀；多样性损失有助于缓解离散标识分布不均。
- 论文报告了跨域、效率和序列长度分析，说明语义标识输入能减少部分生成负担，但具体线上服务收益未报告。

### 局限性与研究定位

#### 局限性

- SID 仍依赖离线量化和固定 POI 标识表，动态新增 POI 的处理方式未充分展开。
- 多级自回归生成的在线延迟和无效 SID 的容错机制仍需更系统的工程评估。

#### 研究定位

GNPR-SID 是较早将 Semantic ID 直接用于下一 POI 生成的工作，适合放在“地理场景生成式推荐”章节，重点体现内容-协同融合量化与时间条件生成。

### 相关资源

- [论文原文](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.01375)
- [开源代码](https://github.com/wds1996/GNPR-SID)

`下一兴趣点推荐` · `残差量化` · `多样性损失` · `大语言模型`

## GR-Generalize

- Page: pages/papers/gr-generalize.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: Paradigms, Systems and Benchmarks
- Stage: No single stage
- Representation: Text+SID; Tokenization: RQ-VAE; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed†; Objective: NTP†; Inference: Hybrid
- TL;DR: GR-Generalize is an analysis, not a new recommender: it labels test instances as memorization or generalization, compares generative and item ID models on each, and combines both per instance.
- [Code](https://github.com/Jamesding000/MemGen-GR)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 4

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Seven public datasets: Amazon 2014 Sports and Beauty; Amazon 2023 Industrial and Scientific, Musical Instruments, Office Products; Steam; Yelp. Sizes (users / items): Sports 35,599 / 18,358; Beauty 22,364 / 12,102; Science 50,986 / 25,849; Music 57,440 / 24,588; Office 223,309 / 77,552; Steam 47,762 / 10,972; Yelp 30,432 / 20,034. Filtering rules: not reported.
  - Source: Seven datasets and split: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.19809v1#S3.SS1.p1; statistics: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.19809v1#S3.T2; filtering rules not stated.
- **Split**: Standard leave-last-out: last item for test, second-to-last for validation. Test instances are then partitioned into memorization, generalization (with hop counts up to 4), and uncategorized subsets.
  - Source: Leave-last-out: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.19809v1#S3.SS1.p1; categorization of test instances: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.19809v1#S3.SS1.p4.
- **Candidates**: not reported (full catalog versus sampled evaluation candidates). SASRec is trained with cross-entropy over all items rather than one sampled negative.
  - Source: SASRec trained against all items, evaluation set not stated: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.19809v1#S3.SS1.p2.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. The uncategorized subset may include items unseen during training, but they are not separated.
  - Source: No unseen-item protocol; uncategorized instances may include unseen items: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.19809v1#S2.SS5.p1.
- **SID**: Analysis of TIGER SIDs: the mechanism study varies SID length L in {2, 3, 4, 5} (including identifier tokens) with two codebook sizes V per length (e.g. L=2 with V=1,024 or 4,096; L=3 with V=256 and a second size), at matched training compute. The default configuration for Table 1 and collision handling: not reported.
  - Source: SID length and codebook variations: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.19809v1#S4.SS4.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2603.19809v1#S4.T3; default TIGER configuration not stated.
- **Inference budget**: Decoding method and beam width: not reported. Table 3 gives matched training compute per SID length (e.g. 5.00e15 FLOPs for L=2); hardware, inference batch size, and latency: not reported. NDCG@10 is the main metric.
  - Source: Compute budgets in Table 3: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.19809v1#S4.T3; no decoding settings found.
- **Results from**: Table 1 (NDCG@10 of TIGER and SASRec on memorization and generalization subsets); Figures 4-7 and Table 3 (token-level memorization analysis and codebook-size study); Table 4 (memorization-aware adaptive ensemble).
  - Source: Breakdown: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.19809v1#S2.T1; SID configurations: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.19809v1#S4.T3; ensemble: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.19809v1#S5.T4.

## GR4AD-X

- Page: pages/papers/gr4ad-x.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: III. SID–Model Alignment
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: –; Tokenization: Multi-Path R-KM+Hash; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP + PV-RSPO + Rank + Aux.; Inference: PV-Beam+Rerank
- TL;DR: GR4AD-X extends GR4AD for advertising with multi-path Semantic ID assignment, capacity scaling beyond wider or deeper backbones, and value-guided generation with beam pruning and discriminative reranking.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Kuaishou production advertising; 7.556M advertisement embeddings in the SID analysis. Dates and filtering rules not reported.
  - Source: Section 4.2 and Appendix A: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.38378v1#S4.SS2.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.38378v1#A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1
- **Split**: Offline train/validation/test split not reported; each online variant receives a random 5% traffic share for seven days.
  - Source: Appendix A: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.38378v1#A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1
- **Candidates**: not reported; value-alignment analysis uses final-ranking candidates from sampled online requests, without a full-catalog or sampled-negative protocol.
  - Source: Section 4.4: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.38378v1#S4.SS4.p1
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined.
  - Source: Section 4 and Appendix A define no item holdout: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.38378v1#S4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.38378v1#A1
- **SID**: Two paths per advertisement, each with three levels: first-level RQ-KMeans 16384 centroids, second-level RQ-KMeans size not reported, final non-semantic feature hash size not reported. Collision disambiguation not reported; repeated retrieved advertisements are deduplicated by their highest-scoring path.
  - Source: Section 3.2 and Appendix A: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.38378v1#S3.SS2.p3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.38378v1#A1.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1
- **Inference budget**: Beam 512; PV-BeamSearch expands to 1024 before pruning at SID levels >=2, followed by advertisement deduplication and reranking. Serving exceeds 500 QPS per NVIDIA L20 GPU with end-to-end latency below 100 ms; inference batch size not reported.
  - Source: Sections 3.2/3.4 and Appendix A: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.38378v1#S3.SS2.p7 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.38378v1#S3.SS4.SSS2.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.38378v1#A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.38378v1#A1.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1
- **Results from**: Original Table 1: cumulative online revenue versus deployed GR4AD; Table 2: scaling/QPS; Table 3: value alignment; Figure 3: SID analysis.
  - Source: Section 4: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.38378v1#S4.T1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.38378v1#S4.T2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.38378v1#S4.T3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.38378v1#S4.F3

## GRAM

- Page: pages/papers/gram.md
- Venue: ACL’25
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text+CF; Tokenization: H-KM; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP; Inference: C-Beam
- TL;DR: GRAM translates hierarchical and collaborative item relationships into LLM vocabulary words and encodes multi-granular prompts separately, fusing them only at decoding, to use lengthy item text efficiently.
- [Code](https://github.com/skleee/GRAM)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 5

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Beauty, Toys and Games, Sports and Outdoors, and Yelp, with 5-core filtering of users and items (following Hua et al. 2023). Sizes (users / items / interactions): Beauty 22,363 / 12,101 / 198,502; Toys 19,412 / 11,924 / 167,597; Sports 35,598 / 18,357 / 296,337; Yelp 30,431 / 20,033 / 316,354.
  - Source: Datasets and 5-core: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.01673v1#S4.p1; statistics: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.01673v1#A7.T10.
- **Split**: Per-user leave-one-out: last item for test, second last for validation, the rest for training; sequences capped at 20 items. Three seeds.
  - Source: Leave-one-out allocation and history cap: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.01673v1#S4.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2506.01673v1#S4.p4.
- **Candidates**: full catalog (full-ranking evaluation on all items rather than sampled items).
  - Source: Full ranking on all items: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.01673v1#S4.p2.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. A head/tail analysis splits test users by target-item popularity (top 20% versus bottom 80%).
  - Source: Standard split with no unseen-item protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.01673v1#S4.p2; head/tail by target popularity: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.01673v1#S5.SS3.p2.
- **SID**: Hierarchical textual IDs: recursive k-means over item text embeddings, stopping when a cluster has fewer than c items or depth reaches l; each cluster index is mapped to an existing LLM vocabulary token chosen by TF-IDF. Final (l, k, c): Beauty (7, 128, 128); Toys (5, 32, 32); Sports and Yelp (7 or 9, 32, 32). Duplicate IDs receive an appended digit for uniqueness.
  - Source: Hierarchical k-means textual IDs: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.01673v1#S3.SS2.SSS1.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2506.01673v1#S3.SS2.SSS1.p3; final settings: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.01673v1#A7.T12; duplicate-ID digit: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.01673v1#S3.SS2.SSS1.p3.
- **Inference budget**: Constrained beam search with beam size 50 and a Trie over valid IDs; T5-small on OpenP5. Table 7: average inference time per user sequence with all user sequences in a single batch on one NVIDIA A6000 GPU (Beauty 0.2008 s, Toys 0.1605 s; LC-Rec 1.8312 s and 1.8125 s).
  - Source: Constrained beam 50 with Trie: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.01673v1#S4.p4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2506.01673v1#S3.SS4.p2; timing: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.01673v1#A3.T7.
- **Results from**: Table 2 (four datasets versus six sequential and eight generative baselines; three seeds); Table 3 (ablations); Table 4 (ID types); Figures 6-8 (head/tail, ID length, similar items); Tables 6-7 (preprocessing and inference time); Tables 8-9 (baseline reproduction fixes for ELMRec and IDGenRec).
  - Source: Main: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.01673v1#S4.T2; ablation: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.01673v1#S5.T3; ID types: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.01673v1#S5.T4; reproducibility: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.01673v1#A3.T8 and https://arxiv.org/html/2506.01673v1#A4.T9.

## 旧卡片说明

迁自 `d61aa6c:papers/gram.md`。保留方法说明、实验叙述与局限；本轮只对照现有记录处理明确冲突，未重新逐句核查原论文。分类和规格以页面上方由记录生成的表格为准。

### GRAM：语义感知多粒度后融合生成推荐

> GRAM 在层次化语义与协同语义之间进行多粒度后融合，由生成模型直接输出物品标识。

### 研究动机与问题定义

早期融合容易让不同来源的信息相互干扰，单一粒度的语义标识又难以兼顾概括性和区分性。GRAM 延迟融合多层语义，以改善生成推荐的表达与决策。

### TL;DR（核心摘要）

`物品内容与交互 → 层次化语义/协同信息 → 多粒度编码 → 后融合解码 → 推荐物品`

模型构造层次化语义标识，并将协同语义 verbalize 为可被语言模型处理的 token。多粒度编码器分别建模局部和整体语义，解码端进行 late fusion，直接生成目标物品标识。

### 输入与使用场景

| 方面 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| 使用信息 | 用户行为、物品文本语义和协同语义 |
| 信息融入位置 | 多粒度编码与解码端后融合 |
| 语义标识结构 | 层次化多粒度序列 |
| 适用场景 | 语义增强序列推荐 |

### 方法设计

#### 3.1 语义到词汇的转换
GRAM 先建立层次化语义索引，将物品整体语义拆成多个粒度，再把协同表示转换为可被语言模型处理的协同语义 token。这样既保留语义结构，也让用户行为信号进入文本生成空间。

#### 3.2 多粒度编码器
多粒度编码器分别处理粗粒度类别、细粒度属性和协同语义。编码结果保留各层级的位置信息和语义差异，为后续生成提供互补条件。

#### 3.3 后融合解码器
与输入端早期融合不同，GRAM 在解码端延迟组合多源表示。解码器在生成不同 SID 位置时选择对应粒度的语义信息，从而减少模态间相互干扰。

#### 3.4 训练与推理
模型以用户历史到目标 SID 的生成损失训练，推理时自回归生成完整标识并映射到物品。实验重点比较多粒度、融合位置和语义来源。

### 实验结论

- 多粒度后融合优于单粒度或早期融合设置。
- 语义和协同信息的联合使用带来互补收益。

### 局限性与研究定位

#### 局限性
- 多路编码和融合增加模型与推理开销。
- 动态物品加入和大规模线上服务仍未充分评估。

#### 研究定位
GRAM 的关键贡献是将多粒度语义融合位置推迟到解码阶段，适合放在“多源语义融合”章节。

### 相关资源

- [论文原文](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.01673)
- 代码公开情况未报告。

### 标签

`多粒度融合` · `语义标识` · `后融合` · `生成式推荐`
