## GRC

- Page: pages/papers/grc.md
- Venue: CIKM’26
- Problem: III. SID–Model Alignment
- Stage: Inference
- Representation: –; Tokenization: RQ-VAE; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP → RL; Inference: GRC+Beam
- TL;DR: GRC extends single-pass decoding into generation, reflection, and correction in the semantic token space, trains the trajectory with GRPO, and allocates correction budget by entropy during beam search.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 2

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Arts and Musical Instruments; industrial e-commerce advertising logs spanning March-August 2025 (over 1B interactions, 19M users, 25M advertisements). Filtering rules not reported.
  - Source: Section 5.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.23639v1#S5.SS1.p1
- **Split**: Amazon: per-user last interaction test, penultimate validation, remaining interactions training. Industrial offline split not reported. Online A/B: January 2-12, 2026, with control/treatment each containing 15% randomly sampled users.
  - Source: Sections 5.1 and 6: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.23639v1#S5.SS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.23639v1#S6.p1
- **Candidates**: not reported
  - Source: Sections 5.1 and 3.2 specify metrics and beam search, not evaluation negatives: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.23639v1#S5.SS1.p3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.23639v1#S3.SS2.p3
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Tokenizer exposure to test items not reported; all GR models share a frozen dataset-specific RQ-VAE codebook.
  - Source: Section 5.1 defines no item holdout: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.23639v1#S5.SS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.23639v1#S5.SS1.p4
- **SID**: RQ-VAE: 4 levels x 300 codes, fitted to Qwen3-8B item embeddings and then frozen. Deterministic SID-to-item lookup defined; collision disambiguation not reported.
  - Source: Sections 3.1 and 5.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.23639v1#S3.SS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.23639v1#S5.SS1.p4
- **Inference budget**: Beam 200 offline/online; reflection and correction use entropy-guided pruning with alpha_e=0.2; paths judged correct skip regeneration. K=5/10, plus Recall@100/200 ablations. Online P99 latency 31 ms versus TIGER 27 ms, both using FlashAttention. Inference hardware and batch size not reported.
  - Source: Sections 4.3, 5.1 and 6: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.23639v1#S4.SS3.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.23639v1#S4.SS3.p4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.23639v1#S5.SS1.p4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.23639v1#S6.p1
- **Results from**: Original Table 1: offline comparisons; Table 2: reflection accuracy; Table 3: ablations; Section 6: online A/B against in-house TIGER.
  - Source: Section 5 Tables 1-3 and Section 6: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.23639v1#S5.T1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.23639v1#S5.T2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.23639v1#S5.T3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.23639v1#S6.p1

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: predecessor; note: GRC augments TIGER with structured reflection-correction supervision, followed by GRPO optimization.; where: GRC v1, Section 5.2 and Table 1: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.23639v1#S5.SS2.p1; https://arxiv.org/html/2602.23639v1#S5.T1.

## GREAM

- Page: pages/papers/gream.md
- Venue: arXiv’25
- Problem: III. SID–Model Alignment
- Stage: Training
- Representation: Text+CF; Tokenization: RQ-KM; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP → RL; Inference: Beam
- TL;DR: GREAM adapts an LLM into a reasoning recommender with collaborative-semantic item indices, a chain-of-thought curriculum, and SRPO post-training, and supports direct and reasoning-first inference modes.
- [Code](https://github.com/Indolent-Kawhi/GRRM)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 4

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Beauty, Sports and Outdoors, Musical Instruments, with 5-core filtering of users and items. Sizes (users / items / interactions): 22,363 / 12,101 / 198,360; 35,598 / 18,357 / 296,175; 24,733 / 9,923 / 206,153. Alignment and reasoning text is synthesized by Qwen3, GPT-5, Llama-3.1, and Gemini.
  - Source: Datasets and 5-core: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.20815v1#S6.SS1.SSS1.p1; statistics: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.20815v1#S6.T1.
- **Split**: Leave-one-out; the exact validation/test position allocation is not reported beyond the leave-one-out label.
  - Source: Leave-one-out named only: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.20815v1#S6.SS1.SSS2.p1.
- **Candidates**: not reported (full catalog versus sampled evaluation candidates); direct mode reports Recall and NDCG at 5 and 10, reasoning mode reports Pass@1, 5, 10.
  - Source: Metrics only: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.20815v1#S6.SS1.SSS2.p1.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined.
  - Source: Standard split with no unseen-item protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.20815v1#S6.SS1.SSS2.p1.
- **SID**: RQ-KMeans indices over LLM last-hidden-state embeddings of GPT-5-enriched item text; fixed length 5 with 256 values per layer, where the fifth position is a conflict-resolution slot.
  - Source: Length 5 with a conflict-resolution slot, 256 values per layer: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.20815v1#S6.SS1.SSS3.p1; RQ-KMeans over LLM embeddings of GPT-5-enriched text: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.20815v1#S3.SS1.SSS2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2510.20815v1#S4.SS1.p1.
- **Inference budget**: Direct mode: beam size 20 for all generative methods. Reasoning mode: sampling with temperature 0.7 and top-p 0.9. Backbone Qwen3-4B-Instruct; experiments on a cluster of 24 NVIDIA A100 GPUs; inference batch size and latency: not reported.
  - Source: Beam 20 and sampling settings: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.20815v1#S6.SS1.SSS2.p1; hardware: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.20815v1#S6.SS1.SSS3.p1.
- **Results from**: Table 2 (direct and reasoning modes on Beauty, Sports, Instruments versus traditional, Transformer, generative, and LLM baselines); Table 3 (alignment and RL ablations); Table 4 (data composition); Figure 3 (RL regimes on Instruments).
  - Source: Main: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.20815v1#S6.T2; ablations: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.20815v1#S6.T3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2510.20815v1#S6.T4; RL regimes: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.20815v1#S6.SS5.p2.

## 旧卡片说明

迁自 `d61aa6c:papers/gream.md`。保留方法说明、实验叙述与局限；本轮只对照现有记录处理明确冲突，未重新逐句核查原论文。分类和规格以页面上方由记录生成的表格为准。

### GREAM：基于大语言模型的生成式推理推荐

> GREAM 将协同-语义对齐、推理课程学习和稀疏反馈强化学习结合，在生成物品标识的同时提供可解释推理。

### 研究动机与问题定义

已有推理式推荐常把推理与最终物品选择分离，依赖外部检索器或黑盒评分器。GREAM 试图让模型端到端完成推理和物品标识生成，并处理推荐反馈稀疏、偏置强的问题。

### TL;DR（核心摘要）

`用户历史与物品文本 → 协同-语义对齐 → 推理课程学习 → SRPO → 完整物品标识`

模型用标题、描述和评论构造离散物品索引，并加入行为对齐任务。随后通过五阶段合成推理数据训练证据提取、偏好建模、意图推断、推荐形成和序列重写；SRPO 使用可验证奖励与稀疏正则优化。论文提供直接序列推荐和先推理后推荐两种模式，最终标识直接确定物品。

### 输入与使用场景

| 方面 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| 使用信息 | 用户交互、物品文本、评论和稀疏反馈 |
| 信息融入位置 | 索引构建、推理数据和强化学习奖励 |
| 语义标识结构 | 层次化离散序列 |
| 适用场景 | 常规序列推荐与可解释推荐 |

### 方法设计

#### 3.1 生成式推荐与知识丰富索引
GREAM 将目标物品表示为层次化索引序列。物品标题、描述和评论经语言模型编码，再通过 RQ-KMeans 残差量化获得具有前缀共享的离散索引；索引 token 被映射到 LLM 词表。

#### 3.2 可验证奖励强化学习
论文先构造协同-语义对齐任务，让 LLM 学习行为和语言之间的关系；再通过反向推理生成五阶段结构化推理数据，包括行为证据、潜在偏好、意图、购买目标和推荐形成。

#### 3.3 混合 SFT 与课程学习
模型在对齐数据和推理数据上进行混合监督微调，按课程逐步提高推理难度。直接序列模式服务高吞吐推荐，推理模式先生成可解释链再生成目标索引。

#### 3.4 SRPO
Sparse-Regularized Group Policy Optimization 结合残差敏感可验证奖励和校准组优势，针对点击/购买反馈稀疏的问题稳定策略更新。最终生成完整索引并映射物品。

### 实验结论

- GREAM 在三个公开数据集的直接推荐和推理指标上优于比较基线。
- 推理课程学习和 SRPO 均有增益。
- 推理性能随训练计算量增加仍有提升趋势。

### 局限性与研究定位

#### 局限性
- 推理链会增加生成长度和计算成本。
- 推荐反馈的反事实偏差和稀疏性仍难完全消除。
- 论文未充分报告大规模线上服务结果。

#### 研究定位
GREAM 的贡献是把显式推理与直接 SID 生成放进同一推荐模型，适合放在“推理增强与强化学习”章节。

### 相关资源

- [论文原文](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.20815)

### 标签

`生成式推理` · `协同语义对齐` · `强化学习` · `稀疏反馈`

### 架构图来源

*图源：原论文，图2。图片使用许可待核实。*

来源：`d61aa6c:tables/all-methods.md`。

- 核心贡献：将显式推理与可验证强化学习结合。
- 使用场景：可解释推荐。

## GRID

- Page: pages/papers/grid.md
- Venue: CIKM’25
- Problem: Paradigms, Systems and Benchmarks
- Stage: No single stage
- Representation: Text; Tokenization: R-KM; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP; Inference: Beam
- TL;DR: GRID is an open-source modular framework, not a new recommender: it makes components of Semantic ID generative recommenders swappable and ablates them on public benchmarks.
- [Code](https://github.com/snap-research/GRID)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 2

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: 5-core filtered Amazon Beauty, Sports, and Toys; item text from Title, Categories, Description, and Price. Retained corpus sizes: not reported in the body.
  - Source: 5-core Amazon datasets and text features: https://arxiv.org/html/2507.22224v1#S4.p2.
- **Split**: Per-user leave-last-out: last item for test, second-to-last for validation, the rest for training; sliding-window training samples; averages over 5 seeds.
  - Source: Leave-last-out allocation and 5 seeds: https://arxiv.org/html/2507.22224v1#S4.p2.
- **Candidates**: not reported (full catalog versus sampled evaluation candidates); top-K lists from beam search.
  - Source: Metrics only: https://arxiv.org/html/2507.22224v1#S4.p2.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined.
  - Source: Standard split with no unseen-item protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2507.22224v1#S4.p2.
- **SID**: Benchmark default: RK-Means with 3 levels x 256 tokens over mean-pooled Flan-T5-XL embeddings; also R-VQ and RQ-VAE, and L x W variants (e.g. 3 x 128, 3 x 512, 2 x 256). Collisions: Table 7 compares TIGER-style appended-digit de-duplication with randomly selecting one item when SIDs conflict; which one is the default setting is not stated.
  - Source: Default RK-Means (3, 256) with Flan-T5-XL: https://arxiv.org/html/2507.22224v1#S4.SS1.p1; dimension study: https://arxiv.org/html/2507.22224v1#S3.T3; de-duplication strategies: https://arxiv.org/html/2507.22224v1#S4.SS2.p5 and https://arxiv.org/html/2507.22224v1#S4.T7.
- **Inference budget**: Beam search with KV cache; constrained and unconstrained beam compared (Table 8), with unconstrained stated to be cheaper; numerical beam width not reported. Tokenizers trained on 8 GPUs (per-device batch 2,048); generator training batch 256; inference hardware, batch size, and latency: not reported.
  - Source: Beam search with KV cache: https://arxiv.org/html/2507.22224v1#S3.SS1.p3; constrained versus free-form beam: https://arxiv.org/html/2507.22224v1#S4.SS2.p6 and https://arxiv.org/html/2507.22224v1#S4.T8; tokenizer GPUs: https://arxiv.org/html/2507.22224v1#S4.p2.
- **Results from**: Tables 1-3 (tokenizer algorithm, encoder size, codebook dimensions); Tables 4-8 (user tokens, encoder-decoder versus decoder-only, augmentation, SID de-duplication, constrained versus free-form beam). Tables 3 and 4 cover Beauty only; the other tables cover Beauty, Sports, and Toys; results average 5 seeds.
  - Source: Tables 1-8: https://arxiv.org/html/2507.22224v1#S3.T1, https://arxiv.org/html/2507.22224v1#S3.T2, https://arxiv.org/html/2507.22224v1#S3.T3, https://arxiv.org/html/2507.22224v1#S4.T4, https://arxiv.org/html/2507.22224v1#S4.T5, https://arxiv.org/html/2507.22224v1#S4.T6, https://arxiv.org/html/2507.22224v1#S4.T7, https://arxiv.org/html/2507.22224v1#S4.T8.

## 旧卡片说明

迁自 `d61aa6c:papers/grid.md`。保留方法说明、实验叙述与局限；本轮只对照现有记录处理明确冲突，未重新逐句核查原论文。分类和规格以页面上方由记录生成的表格为准。

### GRID：语义标识生成式推荐实践框架

> GRID 将物品分词、生成模型训练、约束解码和评估组织为可复用的 Semantic ID 生成式推荐流程。

### 研究动机与问题定义

语义标识生成式推荐涉及标识学习、数据处理、模型训练和解码部署多个环节，实践中缺少统一流程。GRID 以工程视角整理这些组件，并讨论不同设计的选择。

### TL;DR（核心摘要）

`物品内容/交互 → SID分词器 → 生成模型 → 约束解码 → 推荐物品`

框架先用内容或协同信息学习物品 SID，再把用户历史转为标识序列输入生成模型。模型生成完整 SID 后通过词表或索引映射到物品；手册同时覆盖训练、评估、开放物品和部署注意事项。

### 输入与使用场景

| 方面 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| 使用信息 | 交互、文本、图像和协同信息，依配置而定 |
| 信息融入位置 | SID 构建、模型输入和评估流程 |
| 语义标识结构 | 多级离散序列 |
| 适用场景 | 生成式推荐研究与工程实践 |

### 方法设计

#### 3.1 先分词后生成（Tokenization-then-Generation）
GRID 将 Semantic ID 生成式推荐拆成物品分词和推荐生成两个相对独立的阶段。物品分词器把文本、图像或协同表示转换为离散标识；生成器再根据用户历史标识预测下一标识。

#### 3.2 物品分词实践
手册比较 RQ-VAE、码本设计、标识长度、碰撞、语义一致性和新物品更新等选择。不同分词策略会改变词表规模、前缀共享和生成合法率，因此需要结合数据与服务目标选择。

#### 3.3 生成、评估与部署
生成模型可以使用编码器-解码器或其他自回归骨干，推理通常配合前缀树、束搜索和合法 SID 过滤。GRID 还讨论数据处理、评价协议、开放物品和系统部署，重点是形成可复用实践流程，而非提出单一新模型。

### 实验结论

- 手册系统比较了 SID 构建与生成流程中的常见选择。
- 结果强调标识质量、生成有效性和系统效率需要联合考虑。

### 局限性与研究定位

#### 局限性
- GRID 是实践框架与总结性工作，并非单一新模型。
- 具体性能取决于所选分词器、生成骨干和数据设置。

#### 研究定位
GRID 适合放在“方法全景与工程实践”章节，作为理解 Semantic ID 生成式推荐完整流程的入口。

### 标签

`实践框架` · `Semantic ID` · `生成式推荐` · `工程流程`

### 架构图来源

*图源：原论文，图1（a、b）。图片使用许可待核实。*

来源：`d61aa6c:tables/all-methods.md`。

- 核心贡献：统一SID生成推荐实践流程。
- 使用场景：研究与工程实践。

## GrIS (RecDMoN / RQ-GAE)

- Page: pages/papers/gris-recdmon-rq-gae.md
- Venue: CIKM’26
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text+CF; Tokenization: RecDMoN / RQ-VAE; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: –; Inference: –
- TL;DR: GrIS (RecDMoN / RQ-GAE) treats Semantic ID construction as hierarchical partition of an item graph with collaborative edges, recovering RQ-VAE and RQ-KMeans as the empty-graph case.
- [Code](https://github.com/hirc-airecs/graph-informed-sids)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Reviews 2014 Beauty, Toys, Sports, Books; MIND-Small; Yelp 2018. Iterative 5-core filtering on all datasets.
  - Source: Section 5.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.01533v1#S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.01533v1#S5.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1
- **Split**: Per-user leave-one-out: last interaction test, second-to-last validation; maximum sequence length 20.
  - Source: Section 5.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.01533v1#S5.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1
- **Candidates**: not reported
  - Source: Evaluation protocol in Section 5.1 does not specify candidate enumeration or negative sampling: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.01533v1#S5.SS1
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. RQ-GAE item-graph edges use adjacent co-occurrences from training sequences.
  - Source: Section 5.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.01533v1#S5.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.01533v1#S5.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p3
- **SID**: RQ-GAE: 4 x 256 codebooks; collision handling not reported. RecDMoN: four recursive levels with branching factor 6 in Table 6, plus a fifth deduplication codebook; Appendix A reports five levels. Deduplication assignment rule not reported.
  - Source: Section 5.1, Section 5.2.4, Table 6, and Appendix A Table 8: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.01533v1#S5.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.01533v1#S5.SS2.SSS4.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.01533v1#S5.T6 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.01533v1#A1.T8
- **Inference budget**: Hit/NDCG@5/10; decoding beam, hardware, inference batch size, latency not reported.
  - Source: Section 5.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.01533v1#S5.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.01533v1#S5.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p2
- **Results from**: Original Table 3: six-dataset comparison, averages over three seeds. RecDMoN Books unavailable due to GPU memory limits.
  - Source: Table 3 and Section 5.2.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.01533v1#S5.T3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.01533v1#S5.SS2.SSS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.01533v1#S5.SS2.SSS1.p2

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: predecessor; note: Uses TIGER's T5 backbone to isolate improvements from graph-informed SID construction.; where: GrIS v1, Section 5.2.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.01533v1#S5.SS2.SSS1.p1.

## GRLM

- Page: pages/papers/grlm.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: III. SID–Model Alignment
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text; Tokenization: Term-ID; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: Multi-task NTP; Inference: Beam
- TL;DR: GRLM identifies items by Term IDs, standardized textual keywords generated from metadata, and fine-tunes an LLM on them, avoiding free-text hallucination and the vocabulary expansion of Semantic IDs.
- [Code](https://github.com/ZY0025/GRLM)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 4

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: In-domain: Amazon Beauty, Sports, Toys (5-core, following TIGER and OneRec-Think; 22,363 / 12,101, 35,598 / 18,357, 19,412 / 11,924 users / items). Cross-domain pairs Sports-Clothing and Phones-Electronics, built per GenCDR by merging overlapping users' interactions chronologically. Appendix: ten Amazon 2014 categories merged.
  - Source: In-domain and cross-domain datasets: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.06798v1#S4.p3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2601.06798v1#S4.p4; statistics: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.06798v1#S4.T1; ten-dataset appendix: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.06798v1#A1.T6.
- **Split**: Leave-one-out (allocation not restated beyond the label); in the cross-domain setting the last interaction in each domain of the pair is predicted separately.
  - Source: Leave-one-out and cross-domain evaluation: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.06798v1#S4.p3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2601.06798v1#S4.p4.
- **Candidates**: not reported (full catalog versus sampled evaluation candidates); validity of generated Term IDs is measured separately (Table 5).
  - Source: Metrics only: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.06798v1#S4.p5.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined.
  - Source: Standard split with no unseen-item protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.06798v1#S4.p3.
- **SID**: Term IDs: 5 natural-language terms per item from Qwen3-4B's native vocabulary, produced by context-aware term generation (7 and 10 terms tested). Collision handling: not reported beyond relying on a large term space; an optional K-means compression maps 54,255 raw terms to K core terms (3,000-8,000).
  - Source: Term IDs of length 5 from the LLM vocabulary: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.06798v1#S4.p5; length study: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.06798v1#A2.T8; collision discussion and compression: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.06798v1#A2.p1, https://arxiv.org/html/2601.06798v1#A4.p4, https://arxiv.org/html/2601.06798v1#A4.T9.
- **Inference budget**: Beam search with generation max length 30 tokens; beam width not reported. Qwen3-4B backbone; hardware, inference batch size, and latency: not reported. Valid rate at 10 is 0.989-0.998 (Table 5).
  - Source: Beam search, max length 30: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.06798v1#S4.p5; training batch: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.06798v1#A1.p2; validity: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.06798v1#S5.T5.
- **Results from**: Table 2 (in-domain), Table 3 (cross-domain), Table 4 (ablations), Table 5 (Term ID validity), Appendix Tables 7-9 (ten-dataset results, Term ID length, vocabulary compression).
  - Source: Results: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.06798v1#S5.T2, https://arxiv.org/html/2601.06798v1#S5.T3, https://arxiv.org/html/2601.06798v1#S5.T4, https://arxiv.org/html/2601.06798v1#S5.T5, https://arxiv.org/html/2601.06798v1#A1.T7, https://arxiv.org/html/2601.06798v1#A2.T8, https://arxiv.org/html/2601.06798v1#A4.T9.

## 旧卡片说明

迁自 `d61aa6c:papers/grlm.md`。保留方法说明、实验叙述与局限；本轮只对照现有记录处理明确冲突，未重新逐句核查原论文。分类和规格以页面上方由记录生成的表格为准。

### GRLM：基于结构化术语标识的原生 LLM 生成推荐

> GRLM 用原生语言词表构造结构化 Term IDs，使 LLM 直接生成语义丰富的物品术语标识。

### 研究动机与问题定义

数值 SID 通常需要扩展词表和额外对齐，文本标识又容易出现同义词分裂和幻觉。GRLM 以原生 LLM token 构造 Term IDs，并通过邻域上下文提升一致性与区分性。

### TL;DR（核心摘要）

`物品元信息与相似邻域 → 上下文术语生成 → IIFT → Term ID生成 → EIG落地物品`

上下文术语生成从相似物品邻域中抽取标准化且有区分度的关键词。IIFT 联合训练术语内化和用户行为预测；推理时生成 Term ID。若无法精确匹配，EIG 会对候选库进行结构化匹配评分，因此最终物品仍依赖外部标识落地机制。

### 输入与使用场景

| 方面 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| 使用信息 | 物品元信息、相似邻域和用户交互 |
| 信息融入位置 | 术语生成、LLM 训练和候选落地 |
| 语义标识结构 | 变长术语序列 |
| 适用场景 | 跨域、长尾和文本信息丰富的推荐 |

### 方法设计

#### 3.1 上下文术语生成（CTG）
GRLM 先用嵌入模型检索与目标物品相似的邻域，再把目标元信息和邻域元信息一起交给 LLM。提示要求共享属性使用一致术语，同时保留能区分相似物品的细粒度关键词，得到 Term ID。

#### 3.2 综合指令微调（IIFT）
IIFT 联合训练术语内化和用户行为序列预测。术语内化要求模型从元信息恢复标准 Term ID，行为任务则使用历史 Term ID 与标题预测后续物品，从而让 LLM 同时理解标识结构和用户偏好。

#### 3.3 弹性标识落地（EIG）
推理时先尝试 Term ID 的精确字符串匹配；若失败，再按术语位置和衰减权重对候选库进行结构化匹配评分。该后置步骤负责将生成的术语标识落到候选物品。

#### 3.4 实验分析
论文分别评估域内、跨域、消融、规模扩展和术语幻觉，分析上下文邻域对一致性、区分性和可落地性的影响。

### 实验结论

- GRLM 在域内和跨域设置中报告了较强推荐效果。
- 上下文术语生成降低了标识碎片化与幻觉。
- 论文报告了随模型规模扩大而提升的趋势。

### 局限性与研究定位

#### 局限性
- EIG 的结构化匹配依赖候选库和后置评分，不是纯 SID 直达。
- 术语生成、候选库更新和多级匹配增加工程复杂度。
- 代码公开状态未报告。

#### 研究定位
GRLM 的主要贡献是利用 LLM 原生词表构造可解释 Term ID；它适合放在“文本标识与生成推荐”章节。

### 相关资源

- [论文原文](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.06798)

### 标签

`术语标识` · `上下文术语生成` · `LLM推荐` · `标识落地`

Term ID 无法精确匹配时，仍通过候选库结构化评分完成物品落地。

## Gryphon

- Page: pages/papers/gryphon.md
- Venue: CIKM’26 Short
- Problem: IV. Utility
- Stage: Backbone
- Representation: –; Tokenization: R-KM; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP + Rank; Inference: Hybrid
- TL;DR: Gryphon adds a jointly trained item-level scoring component to an encoder-decoder generator, resolving each generated Semantic ID to its items and re-scoring them, instead of ranking by token likelihood.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: One week of industrial music-platform logs; tens of millions of active users and items. Filtering not reported.
  - Source: Section 4.1.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2606.08604v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1
- **Split**: not reported
  - Source: Section 4.1.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2606.08604v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1
- **Candidates**: not reported
  - Source: Offline evaluation in Sections 4.1.1/4.1.4 does not specify full-catalog versus sampled-negative evaluation: https://arxiv.org/html/2606.08604v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2606.08604v1#S4.SS1.SSS4.p1
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. All items are quantized into SIDs; tokenizer fitting exposure not reported.
  - Source: Sections 4.1.1/4.1.3: https://arxiv.org/html/2606.08604v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2606.08604v1#S4.SS1.SSS3.p1
- **SID**: Residual K-Means: 3 x 32000; collisions retained, generated SIDs expanded to all matching items and rescored by ILSM.
  - Source: Sections 3.4/4.1.3: https://arxiv.org/html/2606.08604v1#S3.SS4.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2606.08604v1#S4.SS1.SSS3.p1

  - Source: Sections 4.1.3/4.1.4/4.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2606.08604v1#S4.SS1.SSS3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2606.08604v1#S4.SS1.SSS4.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2606.08604v1#S4.SS2.p1
- **Results from**: Original Table 1: offline comparison; Table 2: same-pool scoring ablation; Table 3: seven-day online A/B test.
  - Source: Tables 1-3: https://arxiv.org/html/2606.08604v1#S4.T1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2606.08604v1#S4.T2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2606.08604v1#S4.T3

## GTI

- Page: pages/papers/gti.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: III. SID–Model Alignment
- Stage: Training
- Representation: Text+CF / Text; Tokenization: RQ-VAE; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: Multi-task NTP; Inference: –
- TL;DR: GTI maps new Semantic ID tokens to distinct locations in the pretrained embedding space with paired linguistic supervision before fine-tuning, instead of initializing them as the mean of existing embeddings.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 2

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Industrial recruitment pairs (good matches for SFT; profiles require at least one listed attribute); Vibrent rentals; other filtering not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.02324v1#S7.SS1
- **Split**: Vibrent: leave-one-out; validation details not reported. Industry: 200 evaluation jobs; train/test separation not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.02324v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1
- **Candidates**: not reported; 200 retrieved candidates per industrial query does not specify the evaluation universe.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.02324v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1 (200 retrieved candidates is an output count, not a negative-sampling protocol).
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Industrial Mistral-E5 uses engagement supervision; test-candidate exposure not reported.

- **SID**: RQ-VAE SIDs from 1024-d embeddings. Industry: engagement-tuned Mistral-E5 embeddings, 3 x 8192. Vibrent: Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B embeddings, 4 x 256 with 32-d codes and the Wang et al. (2024) diversity regularizer for balanced codebook use. The appendix's 4 x 256 configuration additionally uses final-layer Sinkhorn-Knopp balancing to reduce collisions; residual collision resolution is not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.02324v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p2 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2604.02324v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p3 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2604.02324v1#S7.SS3.p2
- **Inference budget**: K=5/10/20/50/100. Experiments use four H100s; inference-specific hardware, beam width, batch size and latency not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.02324v1#S4.T1 ; #S4.T3 ; #S4.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1
- **Results from**: Original experiments: Tables 1-2 industrial relative gains; Table 3 Vibrent relative gains; Table 4 absolute metrics.

## Gwhere

- Page: pages/papers/gwhere.md
- Venue: RecSys’26
- Problem: II. Uniqueness and Validity
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text+Img+Geo+CF; Tokenization: Contr. RQ; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP → DPO; Inference: –
- TL;DR: Gwhere learns POI Semantic IDs with a contrastive residual-quantization tokenizer over text, image, spatial, and collaborative signals, then adapts an LLM through continued pretraining, fine-tuning, and exposure-aware KTO.
- [Code](https://github.com/alibaba/SimCIT)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 2

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Foursquare NYC and TKY, Gowalla CA (POIs with fewer than 10 interactions and users with fewer than 10 check-ins removed, following GNPR-SID; 1,083 / 5,135, 2,293 / 7,873, 6,592 / 14,027 users / POIs), and a proprietary AMAP dataset of sampled desensitized users (10,000K users / 83,100K POIs / 380,000K interactions); AMAP filtering not reported.
  - Source: Datasets and GNPR-SID preprocessing: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.26073v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2607.26073v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p2; statistics: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.26073v1#S4.T2.
- **Split**: Public: time-sorted 80% / 10% / 10% train/validation/test; within each user's test sequence the last visited POI is the target. AMAP offline split: not reported. Online: one-week and one-month A/B tests on the 'Guess Where You Go' card.
  - Source: Public split: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.26073v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p2; AMAP split not stated; online tests: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.26073v1#S4.SS4.SSS3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2607.26073v1#S4.SS4.SSS3.p3.
- **Candidates**: not reported (full catalog versus sampled candidates); the metric is top-1 accuracy (Acc@1).
  - Source: Top-1 accuracy only: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.26073v1#S4.T3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2607.26073v1#S4.T4.
- **Visibility**: warm; users and POIs absent from the training set are removed from the test set.
  - Source: Test users and POIs absent from training are removed: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.26073v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p2.
- **SID**: 3-layer residual quantizer over a 96-dimensional fused latent from text, ALS collaborative, image, and spatial GraphSAGE views, trained contrastively with Gumbel-softmax assignment; 48 codewords per layer on public data, larger (not specified) on AMAP. Collision handling: not reported beyond the contrastive objective that aims to reduce code collision.
  - Source: 3-layer residual quantizer, 96-dimensional latent, 48 codewords on public data: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.26073v1#S4.SS1.SSS2.p2; four modality views: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.26073v1#S4.SS1.SSS2.p1; contrastive Gumbel-softmax quantization: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.26073v1#S3.SS2.SSS2.Px1.p1.
- **Inference budget**: Decoding method and beam width: not reported. Online load test at 50 QPS on 2 NVIDIA H20 GPUs: deployed Gwhere-0.5B at about 30 ms p99 versus about 20 ms for the cascade-ranking system (Figure 4). Training on 200 H20 GPUs with batch 16 per GPU; inputs are the 50 most recent check-ins.
  - Source: Load test: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.26073v1#S4.SS4.SSS2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2607.26073v1#S4.SS4.SSS2.p2; training hardware: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.26073v1#S4.SS1.SSS2.p3; decoding not specified.
- **Results from**: Table 4 (Acc@1 on NYC, TKY, CA; baseline numbers borrowed from LLM4POI and GNPR-SID); Table 3 (AMAP model sizes versus the cascade-ranking system); Table 5 and Figures 2-3 (ablations, modalities, pretraining); Figure 4 (latency); Table 6 (online A/B).
  - Source: Public: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.26073v1#S4.T4; AMAP: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.26073v1#S4.T3; ablations: Table 5 and https://arxiv.org/html/2607.26073v1#S4.F2; online: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.26073v1#S4.T6.

### Related

- id: gnpr-sid; relation: competitor; note: GNPR-SID quantizes POIs with an RQ-VAE plus diversity losses; Gwhere fuses four modalities with a contrastive Gumbel-softmax quantizer and adds continued pretraining and exposure-aware preference alignment.; where: Gwhere v1, follows GNPR-SID preprocessing and baselines: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.26073v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2607.26073v1#S4.SS1.SSS3.p1; Table 4: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.26073v1#S4.T4.

### Notes

## 旧卡片说明

迁自 `d61aa6c:papers/gwhere.md`。保留方法说明、实验叙述与局限；本轮只对照现有记录处理明确冲突，未重新逐句核查原论文。分类和规格以页面上方由记录生成的表格为准。

### Gwhere：高德生成式下一兴趣点推荐

> Gwhere 融合文本、图像、空间和协同信号学习 POI SID，再通过时空语料、监督微调和暴露感知偏好优化服务高德下一 POI 推荐。

### 研究动机与问题定义

工业下一 POI 推荐需要处理异构 POI 信息、用户移动规律和高并发低延迟服务。随机或碰撞严重的标识会削弱生成模型的泛化，单纯监督训练也难以利用曝光数据中的偏好信号。Gwhere 以端到端 SID 生成和线上服务为目标。

### TL;DR（核心摘要）

`文本/图像/空间/协同 → 对比残差量化 → POI SID → CPT/SFT/EAKTO → 生成下一POI`

Gwhere 先用对比学习残差量化器让多模态和协同表示形成区分度更高的 SID；再用 SID-地点描述语料和时空行为语料持续预训练 LLM，随后进行 SFT 与 Exposure-Aware Kahneman-Tversky Optimization（EAKTO，暴露感知卡尼曼-特沃斯基优化）。线上数据服务将实时上下文转为提示，模型直接生成 SID。

### 输入与使用场景

| 方面 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| 使用信息 | POI 文本、图像、空间、协同、用户轨迹和曝光反馈 |
| 信息融入位置 | SID 量化、持续预训练、监督微调和偏好优化 |
| 语义标识结构 | 多级离散 POI SID |
| 适用场景 | 高德工业级下一 POI 推荐 |

### 方法设计

#### 3.2 对比物品分词
Gwhere 为每个 POI 编码文本、图片和空间信息，并结合协同关系。残差量化器逐层选择 code；对比目标拉近真实相关 POI、分离难负样本，以减少异构信息融合后的标识碰撞。

#### 3.3 时空 LLM 后训练
持续预训练语料包含 SID-地点描述、用户时空行为和 POI 问答，使 LLM 学会非原生 SID token 与地理语义之间的对应。SFT 再把用户画像、近期轨迹、当前时间和位置组织为下一 POI 预测任务。

#### 3.4 EAKTO 偏好对齐
EAKTO 使用曝光数据中的点击/未点击或行为反馈构造偏好信号，并以 Kahneman-Tversky 风格的价值函数处理正负反馈的不对称性。它在生成式目标之外补充行为偏好，使模型不只拟合历史点击。

#### 4.5 工业部署
线上服务通过模型存储引擎和数据服务引擎生成实时提示，模型输出 SID 后映射回可读 POI，并返回客户端。图1同时展示离线构建、训练与在线 serving 的完整链路。

### 实验结论

- 公共数据集和高德工业数据集实验均支持 Gwhere 的有效性。
- 长期线上 A/B 测试相较生产基线报告 P-CTR 提升 5.83%、U-CTR 提升 6.20%。
- 多模态协同、偏好对齐和序列长度分析表明，EAKTO 与异构信号融合是关键设计；模型缩放趋势也被报告。

### 局限性与研究定位

#### 局限性

- 多模态 tokenizer、持续预训练和 EAKTO 组成较长的工程链路，复现成本较高。
- 论文对动态 POI、跨城市迁移和生成无效 SID 的统一处理仍缺少细节。

#### 研究定位

Gwhere 适合放在“工业级 POI 生成推荐与行为偏好对齐”章节，突出从 SID 学习到线上 serving 的完整闭环。

### 相关资源

- [论文原文](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.26073)
- [开源代码](https://github.com/alibaba/SimCIT)

### 标签

`下一兴趣点推荐` · `多模态SID` · `暴露感知优化` · `工业部署`

## HASTE

- Page: pages/papers/haste.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: IV. Utility
- Stage: Training
- Representation: Text / MM; Tokenization: RQ-VAE; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP + Aux.; Inference: –
- TL;DR: HASTE adds a loss at each Semantic ID level and attribute-specific losses to generator training, to speed convergence and improve tail items beyond a standard causal cross-entropy objective.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon-2014 Sports/Beauty/Toys: P5 5-core; Fashion-140k: 5-core, minimum sequence length 3, cap 100; internal-fashion: six deliberate engagement types, deduplication, length 3-100, resolved location, single profile; consecutive events with gaps of at least 30 days are discarded.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.17368v1#S9.SS1.SSS1.Px1.p1 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2610.17368v1#S9.SS1.SSS2.Px1.p1 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2610.17368v1#S9.SS1.SSS3.Px1.p1 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2610.17368v1#S9.SS1.SSS3.Px1.p2 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2610.17368v1#S9.SS1.SSS3.Px2.p1
- **Split**: Public sequences: last test, penultimate validation. Amazon conversational examples: shuffled 92/5/3%. Internal-fashion: Section 9.1.3 reports 6255087/339950/203971 train/validation/test conversations; Section 9.1.5 separately reports 368482/19482 training/validation conversations for the attribute-loss SFT corpus. The relationship between these internal corpus counts is not explained.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.17368v1#S9.SS1.SSS1.Px2.p1 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2610.17368v1#S9.SS1.SSS2.Px2.p1 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2610.17368v1#S9.SS1.SSS3.Px3.p1 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2610.17368v1#S9.SS1.SSS5.Px2.p4

  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.17368v1#S9.SS1.SSS4.p1
- **SID**: TIGER-style RQ-VAE: 3 x 256 plus a fourth collision-disambiguation token. Sports/Beauty/Toys use 1024-d text representations; Internal-fashion uses 1024-d multimodal Qwen3-VL embeddings. Section 6 also describes four 256-entry codebooks, inconsistently.

- **Inference budget**: K=5/10; prefix tree from up to 100K training sequences, per-position fallback. Experiments: RTX6000 96GB; beam, inference batch/latency not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.17368v1#S6.p1 ; #S6.p4 ; #S9.SS2.SSS1.Px6.p2
- **Results from**: Original Tables 1-2: sequential/attribute results; Table 3: convergence; Tables 4-5: ablations.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.17368v1#S6.SS1

## HCGRec

## HF-SID

- Page: pages/papers/hf-sid.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Representation
- Representation: Text+Attr+Geo; Tokenization: R-KM; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP; Inference: C-Beam
- TL;DR: HF-SID restores geographic, numerical, and structural detail in POI representations before quantization, through Cartesian coordinates, unit-encoded numbers, and residual contrastive learning, instead of lengthening the Semantic ID.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: AMap-L (one day), AMap-S; remove POIs without interaction sequences and sessions without authenticated users. Foursquare NYC/TKY use Geo-CPT only; public-data filtering: not reported.
  - Source: Sections 4.1 and 4.5: https://arxiv.org/html/2608.30479v1#S4.SS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2608.30479v1#S4.SS5.p1

- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Tokenizer fits representations of the entire POI corpus.
  - Source: Sections 3.4 and 4.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2608.30479v1#S3.SS4.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2608.30479v1#S4.SS1
- **SID**: 3-level RQ-KMeans with last-residual contrastive refinement: 4096 codes/level on AMap-L, 512 on AMap-S. Public-data codebook sizes and collision materialization: not reported.
  - Source: Sections 3.4 and 4.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2608.30479v1#S3.SS4.p3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2608.30479v1#S4.SS1.p2
- **Inference budget**: Valid-SID trie-constrained beam 300; Hit@200/300 on AMap, @5 on NYC/TKY. General experiments: 64 A100 GPUs; inference allocation, batch size, latency: not reported.
  - Source: Sections 3.4, 4.1 and Table 5: https://arxiv.org/html/2608.30479v1#S3.SS4.p4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2608.30479v1#S4.SS1.p4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2608.30479v1#S4.T5
- **Results from**: Original Tables 2/3/4/5/6: AMap comparison, ablation, numerical fidelity, public datasets, one-week online A/B.
  - Source: Tables 2-6: https://arxiv.org/html/2608.30479v1#S4.T2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2608.30479v1#S4.T3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2608.30479v1#S4.T4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2608.30479v1#S4.T5 and https://arxiv.org/html/2608.30479v1#S4.T6

## HiD-VAE

- Page: pages/papers/hid-vae.md
- Venue: arXiv’25
- Problem: II. Uniqueness and Validity
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text; Tokenization: Hier. RQ; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP; Inference: C-Beam
- TL;DR: HiD-VAE aligns each Semantic ID level with multi-level item tags through hierarchically supervised quantization and adds a uniqueness loss against ID collisions, instead of flat unsupervised tokenization.
- [Code](https://anonymous.4open.science/r/HiD-VAE-84B2)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 4

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Beauty, Sports and Outdoors, and KuaiRand-1K, with 5-core filtering of users and items. Sizes (users / items / interactions): Beauty 22,363 / 12,101 / 198,360; Sports 35,598 / 18,357 / 296,175; KuaiRand 983 / 29,983 / 953,166. KuaiRand category hierarchies are generated by an LLM from titles and raw categories.
  - Source: Datasets and 5-core: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.04618v2#S4.SS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2508.04618v2#S4.I2.i2.p1; LLM-built hierarchies: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.04618v2#S4.SS1.p3; statistics: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.04618v2#A4.T4.
- **Split**: Per-user leave-one-out: last item for test, second-to-last for validation, the rest for training.
  - Source: Leave-one-out allocation: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.04618v2#S4.SS1.p5.
- **Candidates**: not reported (full catalog versus sampled evaluation candidates); generation is constrained to valid ID prefixes.
  - Source: Metrics only: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.04618v2#S4.SS1.p5.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined.
  - Source: Standard split with no unseen-item protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.04618v2#S4.SS1.p5.
- **SID**: 3-level hierarchically supervised RQ-VAE x 256 codewords (K-means initialized) over 768-dimensional SentenceTransformer embeddings; each level is aligned with a category-tag level, and a uniqueness loss pushes items apart. Measured collision rate 2.1% (Beauty), 2.8% (Sports), 1.9% (KuaiRand) versus 18.7%, 19.5%, and 17.8% for RQ-VAE. How the remaining collisions are resolved in the full model: not reported; the w/o-uniqueness variant uses TIGER's appended integer.
  - Source: L=3 x K=256, K-means initialization, SentenceTransformer input: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.04618v2#S4.SS1.p6; uniqueness loss: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.04618v2#S3.SS6.p1; collision rates: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.04618v2#S4.T3; TIGER suffix only in the w/o DUL variant: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.04618v2#S4.I4.i4.p1.
- **Inference budget**: Autoregressive generation with constrained decoding against a corpus cache; beam width not reported. 6-layer encoder-decoder (8 heads, hidden 512). Training on NVIDIA 4060 GPUs with FP16; inference batch size and latency: not reported.
  - Source: Constrained decoding: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.04618v2#S4.SS1.p6; hardware: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.04618v2#S4.SS1.p6.
- **Results from**: Table 1 (Beauty, Sports, KuaiRand versus traditional, Transformer, and generative baselines); Table 2 (ablations of tag alignment, tag prediction, uniqueness loss); Table 3 (ID collision rates).
  - Source: Main: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.04618v2#S4.T1; ablation: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.04618v2#S4.T2; collisions: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.04618v2#S4.T3.

### Notes

## 旧卡片说明

迁自 `d61aa6c:papers/hidvae.md`。保留方法说明、实验叙述与局限；本轮只对照现有记录处理明确冲突，未重新逐句核查原论文。分类和规格以页面上方由记录生成的表格为准。

### HiD-VAE：层次解耦语义标识可解释生成推荐

> HiD-VAE 通过层次标签监督和唯一性约束学习可解释、低碰撞的物品语义标识，并用于直接生成推荐。

### 研究动机与问题定义

现有 SID 往往缺乏可解释层次，且不同物品可能碰撞到相同标识。HiD-VAE 研究如何让标识的不同层级对应可理解类别，同时在潜空间中减少表示重叠。

### TL;DR（核心摘要）

`物品语义与层次标签 → HiD-VAE → 层次SID/标签ID → Transformer → 推荐物品`

离线阶段用文本表示和层次标签训练监督 VAE：标签对齐与标签预测约束各量化层的语义粒度，唯一性损失惩罚不同物品的潜表示重叠。在线阶段冻结 tokenizer，Transformer 根据用户历史自回归生成 SID，并用约束解码映射到物品。

### 输入与使用场景

| 方面 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| 使用信息 | 物品文本、类别层次和用户交互 |
| 信息融入位置 | VAE 监督目标与生成模型输入 |
| 语义标识结构 | 层次化序列，并附带标签 ID |
| 适用场景 | 可解释序列推荐与冷启动 |

### 方法设计

#### 3.3 框架总览
HiD-VAE 分为离线层次 ID 学习和在线可解释推荐两阶段。第一阶段学习冻结的物品 tokenizer，第二阶段用 Transformer 根据用户历史生成语义 ID，同时预测或展示对应的层次标签。

#### 3.4 层次标签生成
对于缺少人工类别的数据，论文先使用 LLM 从物品文本和候选标签中生成层次标签。标签从粗粒度类别逐步细化，为不同 VAE 层提供监督信号。

#### 3.5 层次表示学习
HiD-VAE 在 RQ-VAE 的多级量化基础上加入标签对齐损失和标签预测损失，使每一层承担特定语义粒度。重构和量化损失保证表示可恢复，标签监督保证层次可解释。

#### 3.6 解耦与唯一性损失
唯一性损失直接惩罚不同物品潜表示的重叠，减少 ID collision。训练后在线生成阶段采用约束解码，只保留码本中存在且能对应真实物品的标识。

### 实验结论

- HiD-VAE 在三个公开数据集上提升了推荐效果和标识可解释性。
- 层次监督改善了语义层次，唯一性损失降低了 ID 碰撞。
- 对缺少类别标签的数据，论文使用 LLM 生成层次标签。

### 局限性与研究定位

#### 局限性
- 依赖离线标签生成和 tokenizer 更新。
- 约束自回归解码仍存在延迟。
- 真实动态目录和线上效果未充分验证。

#### 研究定位
HiD-VAE 将“可解释层次”和“低碰撞”作为 SID 的联合目标，适合放在“可解释语义标识学习”章节。

### 相关资源

- [论文原文](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.04618)

### 标签

`层次监督` · `解耦表示` · `唯一性损失` · `可解释推荐`

### 架构图来源

*图源：原论文，图2。图片使用许可待核实。*

来源：`d61aa6c:tables/all-methods.md`。

- 核心贡献：学习可解释且低碰撞的SID。
- 使用场景：可解释推荐。

## HoloRec

- Page: pages/papers/holorec.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: III. SID–Model Alignment
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: –; Tokenization: Nested RQ; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP + Aux.; Inference: –
- TL;DR: HoloRec builds hierarchical Semantic IDs by nested residual quantization with a reconstruction loss over all granularities and generates chain-of-thought steps inside decoding, instead of using external annotated rationales.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Beauty and Instruments; user/item five-core filtering.
  - Source: Section 4.1.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2606.15331v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1
- **Split**: Leave-one-out; exact validation/test allocation not reported.
  - Source: Section 4.1.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2606.15331v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1
- **Candidates**: not reported
  - Source: Section 4.1 gives metrics but no evaluation candidate protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2606.15331v1#S4.SS1.SSS2.p1
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined.
  - Source: Section 4 defines no item holdout: https://arxiv.org/html/2606.15331v1#S4.SS1
- **SID**: Three nested granularities (8/16/32 dimensions), each with 4 residual levels x 256 codes; codebooks shared across granularities. Collision handling not reported.
  - Source: Sections 3.1 and 4.1.4: https://arxiv.org/html/2606.15331v1#S3.SS1.SSS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2606.15331v1#S4.SS1.SSS4.p1
- **Inference budget**: K=5/10; non-thinking and interleaved-thinking modes. Beam width, inference hardware/batch size, and measured latency not reported; A100 and batch 1024 describe training.
  - Source: Sections 4.1.2/4.1.4 and 4.7: https://arxiv.org/html/2606.15331v1#S4.SS1.SSS2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2606.15331v1#S4.SS1.SSS4.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2606.15331v1#S4.SS7.p1
- **Results from**: Original Table 2: overall comparisons; Table 3: ablations.
  - Source: Tables 2-3: https://arxiv.org/html/2606.15331v1#S4.T2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2606.15331v1#S4.T3

## IBA

- Page: pages/papers/iba.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: V. Efficiency
- Stage: Backbone
- Representation: Text; Tokenization: RQ-VAE; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP → (NTP + Aux.); Inference: C-Beam
- TL;DR: IBA allocates latent reasoning steps across Semantic ID positions by information gain, giving more refinement to the informative early positions, instead of a fixed number of steps per token.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Instruments and Beauty; MicroLens. Users with fewer than 5 interactions removed; training histories capped at 20 items.
  - Source: Section IV-A1: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.12425v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1
- **Split**: Leave-one-out, one test target per user; exact validation/test allocation not reported.
  - Source: Sections IV-A1/IV-A3: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.12425v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2607.12425v1#S4.SS1.SSS3.p1
- **Candidates**: not reported
  - Source: Section IV-A describes metrics and catalog-valid trie decoding, not evaluation negatives: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.12425v1#S4.SS1.SSS3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2607.12425v1#S4.SS1.SSS4.p2
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Information-gain prior estimated from training interactions only; tokenizer exposure to test items not reported.
  - Source: Sections IV-A1/III-A define no item holdout: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.12425v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2607.12425v1#S3.SS1.p1
- **SID**: RQ-VAE on Sentence-T5 text embeddings: 4 tokens; codebook sizes and collision handling not reported.
  - Source: Sections II-A and IV-A: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.12425v1#S2.SS1.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2607.12425v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2607.12425v1#S4.SS1.SSS4.p1
- **Inference budget**: Trie-constrained beam 20, maximum 10 generated tokens; 6 latent refinement steps with prior (3,2,1,0). NVIDIA RTX 4090 24GB; Instruments generation time 24.61 ms/user (TIGER 20.99, uniform 8-step refinement 25.78). Inference batch size not reported.
  - Source: Sections IV-A4/IV-F and Table V: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.12425v1#S4.SS1.SSS4.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2607.12425v1#S4.SS1.SSS4.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2607.12425v1#S4.T5
- **Results from**: Original Table II: TIGER/LETTER plus IBA and baselines; Tables III/IV: schedules/ablations; Table V: generation efficiency.
  - Source: Tables II-V: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.12425v1#S4.T2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2607.12425v1#S4.T3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2607.12425v1#S4.T4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2607.12425v1#S4.T5

## IDGenRec

- Page: pages/papers/idgenrec.md
- Venue: SIGIR’24
- Problem: III. SID–Model Alignment
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text; Tokenization: LLM-Vocab; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Altern.; Objective: NTP; Inference: C-Beam
- TL;DR: IDGenRec trains a textual ID generator alongside an LLM recommender, so each item receives a concise ID made of natural-language tokens, and tests zero-shot transfer to unseen platforms.
- [Code](https://github.com/agiresearch/IDGenRec)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 4

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Standard: Amazon Sports, Beauty, Toys and Yelp, filtering users and items with fewer than 5 interactions (following P5 and Hua et al. 2023). Zero-shot: a Fusion pre-training corpus from 19 other Amazon categories, each downsampled to at most 30,000 users (183,918 users / 233,323 items), tested on Sports, Beauty, Toys, Music, Instruments, and Yelp.
  - Source: Standard datasets and 5-interaction filter: https://arxiv.org/html/2403.19021v2#S3.SS1.p1; zero-shot data rules: https://arxiv.org/html/2403.19021v2#S3.SS1.p3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2403.19021v2#S3.SS1.p4; statistics: https://arxiv.org/html/2403.19021v2#S3.T3.
- **Split**: Leave-one-out for testing (validation allocation not restated). Zero-shot: train once on Fusion and test directly on held-out datasets.
  - Source: Leave-one-out: https://arxiv.org/html/2403.19021v2#S3.SS3.p1; zero-shot setting: https://arxiv.org/html/2403.19021v2#S3.SS5.p1.
- **Candidates**: full catalog (no negative sampling; ranking over all items).
  - Source: Ranking over all items without negative sampling: https://arxiv.org/html/2403.19021v2#S3.SS3.p1.
- **Visibility**: Standard: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Zero-shot: users and items of the test datasets are not seen in training; the ID generator is also trained only on the Fusion corpus, so test items are unseen by tokenizer too and receive IDs generated from their text.
  - Source: Zero-shot: users and items unseen in training: https://arxiv.org/html/2403.19021v2#S3.SS5.p1; the ID generator is trained with the recommender on the training data: https://arxiv.org/html/2403.19021v2#S3.SS2.p3.
- **SID**: Textual IDs generated from item text by a T5-small ID generator with diverse beam search (k=10 groups, diversity penalty raised from 1 to 10), length initially in [1, 10) tokens and extended to [10, 20) when needed; uniqueness is enforced at generation time by rejecting duplicates. SentencePiece vocabulary of 32,128.
  - Source: Diverse beam search for unique textual IDs, length ranges: https://arxiv.org/html/2403.19021v2#S2.SS3.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2403.19021v2#S3.SS2.p2; T5-small ID generator: from Section 2.
- **Inference budget**: Constrained decoding over a prefix tree of all generated item IDs; beam width, hardware, inference batch size, and latency: not reported. HR and NDCG at 5 and 10.
  - Source: Constrained decoding with a prefix tree over generated IDs: Section 2 inference; no beam width or hardware found.
- **Results from**: Table 4 (standard evaluation versus traditional and P5-variant baselines); Table 5 (training strategies); Table 6 (user and item IDs); Table 7 (zero-shot intra- and inter-platform).
  - Source: Standard: https://arxiv.org/html/2403.19021v2#S3.T4; training strategies: https://arxiv.org/html/2403.19021v2#S3.T5; user/item IDs: https://arxiv.org/html/2403.19021v2#S3.T6; zero-shot: https://arxiv.org/html/2403.19021v2#S3.T7.

- id: cid; relation: competitor; note: P5-SID, P5-CID, and P5-SemID assign sequential, collaborative, or category IDs; IDGenRec learns a textual ID generator jointly with the recommender.; where: IDGenRec v2, baselines: https://arxiv.org/html/2403.19021v2#S3.I1.i2.p1; Table 4: https://arxiv.org/html/2403.19021v2#S3.T4.
- id: gram; relation: alternative; note: GRAM later builds hierarchical textual IDs by clustering and reports that IDGenRec's user IDs concatenate validation and test items; it reruns IDGenRec without user IDs.; where: Evidence is from the later GRAM paper: Table 9 and Appendix E: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.01673v1#A4.T9 and https://arxiv.org/html/2506.01673v1#A5.p3; Table 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.01673v1#S4.T2.
- id: grlm; relation: alternative; note: GRLM later replaces free textual IDs with a fixed number of standardized vocabulary terms to reduce synonym ambiguity.; where: Evidence is from the later GRLM paper: baselines and Table 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.06798v1#S4.I1.i3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2601.06798v1#S5.T2; case study: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.06798v1#A3.p1.

### Notes

## 旧卡片说明

迁自 `d61aa6c:papers/idgenrec.md`。保留方法说明、实验叙述与局限；本轮只对照现有记录处理明确冲突，未重新逐句核查原论文。分类和规格以页面上方由记录生成的表格为准。

### IDGenRec：文本 ID 学习的 LLM-推荐系统对齐

> IDGenRec 同时学习物品文本 ID 和推荐生成器，使 LLM 能直接生成可识别的目标物品 ID。

### 研究动机与问题定义

随机 ID 难以利用 LLM 的语言知识，直接使用长文本又会造成冗余和幻觉。IDGenRec 将物品元信息压缩为文本 ID，并让这些 ID 与推荐器共同适配。

### TL;DR（核心摘要）

`物品元信息 → ID生成器 → 文本ID → 推荐提示 → 基础推荐器 → 目标ID`

ID 生成器从标题、类别、价格等元信息生成简短 token 序列，并用多样束搜索减少重复。基础推荐器接收用户历史中的文本 ID，通过前缀树约束直接生成目标 ID；两者交替训练，生成结果可映射到物品。

### 输入与使用场景

| 方面 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| 使用信息 | 物品元信息、用户交互和推荐目标 |
| 信息融入位置 | ID 生成、提示输入和交替训练目标 |
| 语义标识结构 | 变长文本 token 序列 |
| 适用场景 | 序列推荐和零样本扩展 |

### 方法设计

#### 2.1 生成过程
旧卡片的速览将 ID 生成器和基础推荐器都记为 T5 编码器-解码器。IDGenRec 把物品元信息转成简短文本 ID，再将用户历史中的物品替换为这些 ID，填入推荐提示。基础推荐器以提示和历史 ID 为条件，逐 token 生成目标物品 ID。

#### 2.2 ID 生成器
ID 生成器读取标题、类别、价格、描述等 plain text，输出短而具有区分性的 token 序列。它使用语言模型的文本知识进行压缩，不要求扩展为独立数值词表。

#### 2.3 多样 ID 生成
为减少不同物品获得相同 ID，论文使用多样束搜索，逐步提高多样性惩罚；必要时增加 ID 长度。生成过程维护已分配 ID 集合，直到获得可区分标识。

#### 2.4 基础推荐器与交替训练
基础推荐器使用前缀树进行约束解码，确保目标 ID 对应真实物品。ID 生成器和推荐器交替更新：前者学习可被推荐器使用的 ID，后者学习根据当前 ID 预测下一物品。

### 实验结论

- IDGenRec 在标准序列推荐和零样本设置中均展示了生成能力。
- 交替训练改善了文本 ID 与推荐器之间的可用性。

### 局限性与研究定位

#### 局限性
- ID 生成器和基础推荐器构成双模型流程，训练成本更高。
- 前缀树与多样束搜索需要维护候选 ID 库。
- 最终泛化受元信息质量影响。

#### 研究定位
IDGenRec 的贡献是以文本 ID 作为 LLM 与推荐系统之间的接口，适合放在“文本化物品标识与 LLM 对齐”章节。

### 相关资源

- [论文原文](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.19021)

`文本ID` · `交替训练` · `LLM对齐` · `生成式推荐`

## IDM/CMM

- Page: pages/papers/idm-cmm.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: IV. Utility
- Stage: Training
- Representation: Text; Tokenization: Subspace RQ; Backbone: Non-AR; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: MTP + Aux.; Inference: Scoring
- TL;DR: IDM/CMM distills a sequential recommender into a parallel Semantic ID generator by matching a reconstructed item distribution or per-position code marginals, instead of training on hard next-item labels alone.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Reviews 2014 Beauty, Toys and Games, Sports and Outdoors; existing 5-core data verified without further filtering or deduplication.
  - Source: Section 4.1 and Appendix A.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.32943v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.32943v1#A1.SS1.p1
- **Split**: Per-user chronological last/penultimate interactions are test/validation; earlier events train. Histories capped at 50; test histories include validation interaction.
  - Source: Appendix A.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.32943v1#A1.SS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.32943v1#A1.SS1.p2
- **Candidates**: full catalog; no historical-item masking
  - Source: Section 4.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.32943v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined.
  - Source: Section 4.1 and Appendix A.1 define standard chronological holdouts, without an unseen-item experiment: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.32943v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.32943v1#A1.SS1
- **SID**: 16 subspaces x 3 residual levels x 256 codes; 48 fixed heads. Collisions retained with identical scores; each item remains a distinct catalog entry.
  - Source: Section 4.1 and Appendix A.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.32943v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.32943v1#A1.SS1.p3
- **Inference budget**: Single parallel student, no teacher; Recall/NDCG@5/10; evaluation batch 32, FP32. Beam n/a; evaluation hardware and latency not reported. RTX 5880 Ada is specified for training.
  - Source: Figure 1 and Appendix A.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.32943v1#S3.F1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.32943v1#A1.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p2
- **Results from**: Table 2: IDM/CMM, AsymRec and RPG reproduced, averaged over three runs; other baseline scores copied from RPG Table 2.
  - Source: Table 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.32943v1#S4.T2

### Related

- id: rpg; relation: competitor; note: Reproduced parallel baseline with graph-guided decoding; IDM/CMM add soft teacher supervision.; where: IDM/CMM v1, Section 4.1 and Table 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.32943v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2; https://arxiv.org/html/2610.32943v1#S4.T2.
- id: tiger; relation: competitor; note: Autoregressive baseline; its comparison scores are taken from RPG.; where: IDM/CMM v1, Sections 2.2/4.1 and Table 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.32943v1#S2.SS2.p2; https://arxiv.org/html/2610.32943v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1; https://arxiv.org/html/2610.32943v1#S4.T2.
- id: llada-rec; relation: alternative; note: Iterative diffusion contrasts with the single-pass parallel predictor.; where: IDM/CMM v1, Section 2.3: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.32943v1#S2.SS3.p1.

## Intent-Driven-News

- Page: pages/papers/intent-driven-news.md
- Venue: ACL’26 Industry
- Problem: III. SID–Model Alignment
- Stage: Training
- Representation: Text; Tokenization: RQ-VAE; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: Multi-task NTP; Inference: CoT+Fuzzy Match
- TL;DR: Intent-Driven-News trains an LLM to map implicit conversational intents to hierarchical Semantic ID prefixes and fuzzy-matches them to the current news pool, instead of retrieving articles first.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Industrial Chinese news: 163560 articles, 50000 profiles, 9982 test samples across six tasks. Filtering not reported.
  - Source: Section 4.1 and Table 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.07613v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.07613v1#S4.T2
- **Split**: Temporal: training articles before cutoff, test articles after; zero item overlap. Matching tolerance selected on 1000 validation samples without test temporal overlap; cutoff date not reported.
  - Source: Section 4.1 and Appendix A.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.07613v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.07613v1#A1.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1
- **Candidates**: Open generation (76%): full 152K SID space, grounded to current news pool. Selection (24%): sampled: 5 including target; Rand has 4 random negatives, Align has 2 same-category + 2 random negatives. Historical-item exclusion not reported.
  - Source: Section 4.1 and Appendix I: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.07613v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.07613v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.07613v1#A9.p1
- **Visibility**: Items unseen by generator; whether unseen by tokenizer too: not reported. Cold users have zero recent clicks but may retain pre-cutoff behavioral profile summaries.
  - Source: Section 4.1 and Appendices L/T: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.07613v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.07613v1#A12.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.07613v1#A20.p2
- **SID**: RQ-VAE codebooks [32,64,128,1024]; generate first 3 layers only. Exact L1/L2, L3 tolerance 5; full-SID collision handling not reported.
  - Source: Section 3.2 and Appendix A.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.07613v1#S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.07613v1#S3.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.07613v1#A1.SS1.p3
- **Inference budget**: Caches 10 SID prefixes; beam width, inference hardware and batch size not reported. Warm cached response: mean 85ms, P95 150ms; cold initial delay 3.7s.
  - Source: Section 4.3 and Appendix C.4: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.07613v1#S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.07613v1#A3.SS4.p1
- **Results from**: Original Tables 3/5/6: overall, task/user-cold-start and generative-baseline comparisons; Figure 2: latency.
  - Source: Tables 3/5/6 and Figure 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.07613v1#S4.T3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.07613v1#S4.T5 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.07613v1#S4.T6 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.07613v1#S4.F2

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: competitor; note: Compared on cold-start news users; the proposed method generates conversational SID prefixes.; where: Intent-Driven News v1, Section 4.5 and Table 6: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.07613v1#S4.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1; https://arxiv.org/html/2605.07613v1#S4.T6.

## ISD

- Page: pages/papers/isd.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: IV. Utility
- Stage: Inference
- Representation: Text†; Tokenization: RQ-VAE†; Backbone: Enc-Dec†; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP†; Inference: ISD Beam
- TL;DR: ISD lets a user-specific item ranking support Semantic ID prefixes before beam search discards them, at inference time and without retraining, after showing that Semantic IDs lose local item structure.
- [Code](https://anonymous.4open.science/r/ISD-CF7C)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Reviews: Baby, Office, Scientific; filtering rules not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.24995v1#S6.SS1.SSS1.p1 ; #A1.T6
- **Split**: Per-user chronological leave-one-out: final interaction test, preceding interaction validation, remainder training.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.24995v1#S6.SS1.SSS1.p1 ; #A1.SS4.SSS1.p1
- **Candidates**: full catalog of eligible items, with the same consumed-item mask for all methods.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.24995v1#S6.SS1.SSS3.p1 ; #A1.SS4.SSS1.p1 ; #A1.SS4.SSS2.p1
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Separate item scorer and transition/co-consumption statistics use training interactions; tokenizer exposure to test items not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.24995v1#S6.SS1 ; #A1.SS2.SSS1.p1 ; #S5.SS1.SSS1.p1
- **SID**: TIGER/LIGER assignments remain fixed: three semantic positions plus a collision-resolution suffix. Codebook sizes and suffix-assignment rule not reported; primary filtering diagnostic uses RQ-VAE.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.24995v1#S3.SS3.p1 ; #A1.SS2.p1 ; #A1.SS3.SSS1.p1 ; #S6.SS4.p1
- **Inference budget**: Beam 50; one decoder pass; top-50 item-support ranking constructed once per history; reciprocal-rank fusion kappa=60; at most 50 output items, evaluated at K=10/20. Ranker construction is excluded from decoding complexity. Hardware, inference batch size and latency not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.24995v1#A1.SS3.SSS1.p1 ; #S5.SS2.SSS2.p1 ; #S5.SS3.p1 ; #A1.SS4.SSS2.p1
- **Results from**: Original Table 3: matched recommendation comparisons, means across three seeds; Table 4: SID reassignment; Table 5: filtering/ordering ablations. Tables 1-2: encoder/SID representation diagnostics.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.24995v1#S5.T3 ; #S6.T4 ; #S6.T5 ; #A1.SS4.SSS2.p1

- id: tiger; relation: predecessor; note: ISD augments a frozen TIGER decoder with item-supported prefix selection and final ordering, without changing its SIDs or retraining.; where: ISD v1, Sections 5.2/6.1.2 and Table 3: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.24995v1#S5.SS2; https://arxiv.org/html/2607.24995v1#S6.SS1.SSS2.p1; https://arxiv.org/html/2607.24995v1#S5.T3.

## JevRec

- Page: pages/papers/jevrec.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: V. Efficiency
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text; Tokenization: Freq. R-KM; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP + Aux.; Inference: Length-Quota Beam
- TL;DR: JevRec gives frequent items shorter Semantic IDs and long-tail items longer ones, and predicts length and content with separate heads, instead of one ID length for all items.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 4

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Reviews 2023: Musical Instruments, Industrial & Scientific, Video Games; exclude users/items with fewer than five interactions; maximum history 20 items.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.36937v1#S4.SS1.p1
- **Split**: Per-user chronological leave-one-out: latest interaction test, penultimate validation, earlier interactions training.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.36937v1#S4.SS1.p2
- **Candidates**: full catalog; no negative sampling.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.36937v1#S4.SS1.p2
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Frequency-based length assignment uses training interactions only; tokenizer fitting exposure to test items not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.36937v1#S4.SS1.p1 ; #A2.p1 ; #S3.SS3.p2
- **SID**: Shared residual quantizer: 4 x 256; retain 2/3/4 semantic codes by training-frequency group and append one collision token, giving complete SID lengths 3/4/5. Within each group/prefix bucket collision tokens distinguish items; collision vocabulary capacity not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.36937v1#S3.SS3.p2 ; #S3.SS3.p3 ; #S3.SS3.p4 ; #A3.SS1.p1
- **Inference budget**: Beam 10 per length branch; total recommendation budget 10, with K=5 from the same ranked list; length-probability quotas and joint-score merging, without a catalog-prefix trie. Baseline beam 50. Figure 4 reports total test-set inference speedups over TIGER of 1.05x/1.16x/1.04x on Instrument/Scientific/Game. Inference hardware, batch size and per-request latency not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.36937v1#S3.SS6 ; #A3.SS1.p1 ; #S4.F4 ; #S4.SS5.p1
- **Results from**: Table 2: main three-dataset comparison; most baseline results adopted from Zhong et al. (2025a), as stated in Appendix C. Table 3: JevRec ablations; Figure 4: runtime/convergence.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.36937v1#S4.T2 ; #S4.T3 ; #S4.F4 ; #A3.p1

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: competitor; note: TIGER uses fixed-length RQ-VAE SIDs; JevRec truncates shared residual-quantizer prefixes by item frequency and explicitly predicts target length.; where: JevRec v1, Sections 3.3/4.1 and Table 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.36937v1#S3.SS3; https://arxiv.org/html/2610.36937v1#S4.SS1.p4; https://arxiv.org/html/2610.36937v1#S4.T2.
- id: letter; relation: competitor; note: LETTER adds collaborative information and diversity constraints to learned tokenization; JevRec allocates SID length by interaction frequency.; where: JevRec v1, Sections 3.3/4.1 and Table 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.36937v1#S3.SS3; https://arxiv.org/html/2610.36937v1#S4.SS1.p4; https://arxiv.org/html/2610.36937v1#S4.T2.
- id: actionpiece; relation: competitor; note: ActionPiece merges contextually co-occurring action features; JevRec uses shared semantic codebooks with frequency-dependent prefix lengths.; where: JevRec v1, Sections 3.3/4.1 and Table 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.36937v1#S3.SS3; https://arxiv.org/html/2610.36937v1#S4.SS1.p4; https://arxiv.org/html/2610.36937v1#S4.T2.
- id: pctx; relation: alternative; note: Pctx personalizes tokenization using user history; JevRec assigns context-invariant SID lengths from global training frequencies.; where: JevRec v1, Sections 2/3.2/3.3: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.36937v1#S2.p1; https://arxiv.org/html/2610.36937v1#S3.SS2.p1; https://arxiv.org/html/2610.36937v1#S3.SS3.p1.

## KGTB

- Page: pages/papers/kgtb.md
- Venue: arXiv’25
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Attr+Geo+CF; Tokenization: KG-RQ; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: Multi-task NTP; Inference: –
- TL;DR: KGTB organizes POI data as a knowledge graph, quantizes each node into a structural ID under graph supervision, and fine-tunes an LLM on POI, category, and region visit tasks.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 1

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Foursquare Boston/Paris; Gowalla Austin/San Francisco. No filtering strategies applied.

## KL-MOPD

- Page: pages/papers/kl-mopd.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: IV. Utility
- Stage: Training
- Representation: CF; Tokenization: R-KM; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed†; Objective: (NTP† / (NTP + Aux.)†) → KL-weighted OPD; Inference: C-Beam
- TL;DR: KL-MOPD distills click and conversion teachers into a student generator token by token, weighting each teacher by its initial KL divergence from the student, instead of vanilla on-policy distillation.
- [Code](https://github.com/Yandorn/KL-MOPD)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 1

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: TencentGR (CTR/CVR), YooChoose (CTR/GMV), Taobao (CTR/CVR), industrial advertising (CTR/eCPM). Filtering: not reported.
  - Source: Section 4.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.36973v1#S4.SS1.p1
- **Split**: Public: chronological 70% student pretraining, 20% teacher tuning/student distillation, 10% evaluation. Industry: penultimate day tuning, final day evaluation, >11M requests/day; pretraining allocation not reported. Sliding windows; history caps 100 public/128 Industry.
  - Source: Section 4.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.36973v1#S4.SS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.36973v1#S4.SS1.p4
- **Candidates**: not reported
  - Source: Section 4.1 states decoding and cutoffs without specifying candidate sampling: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.36973v1#S4.SS1.p5
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Two-tower CF embedding exposure to test items: not reported.
  - Source: Section 4.1 defines no unseen-item evaluation: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.36973v1#S4.SS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.36973v1#S4.SS1.p2
- **SID**: RQ-KMeans of two-tower CF embeddings: TencentGR 5x64, YooChoose 5x128, Taobao 8x64, Industry 8x310. Collision handling: not reported.
  - Source: Section 4.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.36973v1#S4.SS1.p2
- **Inference budget**: Constrained beam 50, K=10/20 public; beam 200, K=100/200 Industry. Inference hardware, batch size, latency: not reported.
  - Source: Section 4.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.36973v1#S4.SS1.p5
- **Results from**: This study's adapted/tuned baselines: Table 3 public TIGER/REG4Rec, Table 4 ablations, Table 5 industrial TIGER, Table 6 five-day online A/B (10% control, 10% treatment).
  - Source: Tables 3-6 and baseline setup: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.36973v1#S2.T3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.36973v1#S4.T4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.36973v1#S4.T5 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.36973v1#S4.T6 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.36973v1#S4.SS1.p3

## Latte

- Page: pages/papers/latte.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: III. SID–Model Alignment
- Stage: Backbone
- Representation: Text+CF; Tokenization: RQ-VAE; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP; Inference: C-Beam
- TL;DR: Latte inserts a latent token before each Semantic ID, turning one decoding tree into several latent-conditioned trees, to relax the probability coupling between items that are close in the tree.
- [Code](https://github.com/hyp1231/Latte)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 5

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Reviews 2023: Instruments, Scientific, Games (57,439 / 24,587, 50,985 / 25,848, 94,762 / 25,612 users / items; filtering not restated beyond following ETEGRec and Zheng et al. 2025). Separate modality-order study on the Million Playlist Dataset: songs without tags or metadata and playlists with fewer than six songs removed.
  - Source: Amazon 2023 categories and split: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.06331v1#S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1; statistics: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.06331v1#A1.T7; MPD: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.06331v1#S6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.
- **Split**: Amazon: chronological leave-one-out, most recent interaction for test, second most recent for validation, the rest for training. MPD: 8:1:1 split.
  - Source: Leave-one-out allocation: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.06331v1#S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1; MPD 8:1:1: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.06331v1#S6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.
- **Candidates**: not reported (full catalog versus sampled evaluation candidates); top-K lists from beam search with beam size 500.
  - Source: Metrics only: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.06331v1#A4.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined.
  - Source: Standard split with no unseen-item protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.06331v1#S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.
- **SID**: Base PSID semantic IDs from RQ K-Means: 3 positions x 256 tokens, with PSID's ESM algorithm to prevent SID conflicts; Latte prepends one of M' learned latent tokens (2, 4, or 8; best 4 or 8) chosen freely at inference. RQ-VAE and OPQ tokenizers are also tested (Table 3).
  - Source: RQ K-Means m=3 x 256 with ESM conflict resolution, latent tokens: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.06331v1#A4.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2; tokenizer variants: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.06331v1#S5.T3.
- **Inference budget**: Beam size 500 for PSID and Latte; generation starts with an unconstrained latent token followed by SID tokens, and item scores are aggregated over latent tokens with max. Hardware, inference batch size, and latency: not reported.
  - Source: Beam size 500: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.06331v1#A3.T8 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.06331v1#A3.T9; aggregation over latent tokens: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.06331v1#S4.SS2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.06331v1#A4.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.
- **Results from**: Table 1 (Instruments, Scientific, Games; most baseline numbers copied from prior work, PSID rerun from its released code); Table 2 (tree-distance correlations); Tables 3-4 and Figure 4 (tokenizers, aggregation, number of latent tokens); Table 5 (MPD modality order).
  - Source: Main: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.06331v1#S5.T1; constraint analysis: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.06331v1#S5.T2; tokenizers: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.06331v1#S5.T3; aggregation: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.06331v1#S5.T4; latent count: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.06331v1#S5.F4; MPD: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.06331v1#S6.T5; copied baselines: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.06331v1#A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.

### Related

- id: psi; relation: predecessor; note: PSID is the base model and supplies the ESM conflict resolution; Latte only adds a freely chosen latent token before the semantic ID.; where: Latte v1, base model and implementation: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.06331v1#S5.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.06331v1#A4.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2; Table 1: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.06331v1#S5.T1.

## LC-Rec

- Page: pages/papers/lc-rec.md
- Venue: ICDE’24
- Problem: III. SID–Model Alignment
- Stage: Training
- Representation: Text; Tokenization: RQ-VAE; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: Multi-task NTP; Inference: Beam
- TL;DR: LC-Rec assigns non-conflicting item indices by vector quantization with uniform semantic mapping and tunes an LLM with alignment tasks, so it generates items from the whole catalog without candidate lists.
- [Code](https://github.com/RUCAIBox/LC-Rec/)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 4

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Reviews (May 1996-October 2018): Musical Instruments, Arts Crafts and Sewing, Video Games; users and items with fewer than 5 interactions are filtered; sequences capped at 20 items. Sizes (users / items / interactions): Instruments 24,773 / 9,923 / 206,153; Arts 45,142 / 20,957 / 390,832; Games 50,547 / 16,860 / 452,989.
  - Source: Amazon 2018 subsets, 5-interaction filter, length 20: https://arxiv.org/html/2311.09049v4#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1; statistics: https://arxiv.org/html/2311.09049v4#S4.T2.
- **Split**: Per-user leave-one-out: most recent item for test, second most recent for validation, the rest for training.
  - Source: Leave-one-out allocation: https://arxiv.org/html/2311.09049v4#S4.SS1.SSS3.p1.
- **Candidates**: full catalog (full ranking over the entire item set instead of sampled evaluation). Separate analysis (Table 5): choose between the target and one negative that is language-similar, collaborative-similar (by SASRec embeddings), or random; history exclusion for these negatives not reported.
  - Source: Full ranking over the entire item set: https://arxiv.org/html/2311.09049v4#S4.SS1.SSS3.p1; separate pairwise test with one negative: https://arxiv.org/html/2311.09049v4#S4.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined.
  - Source: Standard split with no unseen-item protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2311.09049v4#S4.SS1.SSS3.p1.
- **SID**: 4-level RQ-VAE x 256 codewords (dimension 32) over mean-pooled LLaMA embeddings of title and description, added to the LLaMA tokenizer as new tokens. Conflicts are resolved without an extra suffix level: the last-level codewords of each conflicting group are redistributed under a uniform-distribution constraint.
  - Source: 4 levels x 256 x 32 over LLaMA text embeddings: https://arxiv.org/html/2311.09049v4#S4.SS1.SSS4.p1; uniform last-level redistribution for conflicts: https://arxiv.org/html/2311.09049v4#S3.SS2.SSS2.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2311.09049v4#S3.SS2.SSS2.p3.
- **Inference budget**: Beam search with beam size 20 for all generative methods; tokens leading to invalid item indices get zero probability. LLaMA backbone with DeepSpeed; hardware, inference batch size, and latency: not reported. HR and NDCG at 1, 5, 10.
  - Source: Beam size 20 and invalid-token masking: https://arxiv.org/html/2311.09049v4#S4.SS1.SSS3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2311.09049v4#S3.SS4.SSS2.p1.
- **Results from**: Table 3 (Instruments, Arts, Games; LC-Rec averaged over instruction templates); Table 4 (alignment-task ablation); Table 5 (similar-negative ranking accuracy).
  - Source: Main: https://arxiv.org/html/2311.09049v4#S4.T3; ablation: https://arxiv.org/html/2311.09049v4#S4.T4; negative-item analysis: https://arxiv.org/html/2311.09049v4#S4.T5.

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: competitor; note: TIGER resolves leaf conflicts with an extra index level and uses a small seq2seq model; LC-Rec redistributes conflicting last-level codes uniformly and tunes LLaMA with language-collaborative alignment tasks.; where: LC-Rec v4, conflict discussion: https://arxiv.org/html/2311.09049v4#S3.SS2.SSS2.p1; baselines and Table 3: https://arxiv.org/html/2311.09049v4#S4.I1.i10.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2311.09049v4#S4.T3.

### Notes

## 旧卡片说明

迁自 `d61aa6c:papers/lcrec.md`。保留方法说明、实验叙述与局限；本轮只对照现有记录处理明确冲突，未重新逐句核查原论文。分类和规格以页面上方由记录生成的表格为准。

### LC-Rec：协同语义融合的语言模型推荐

> LC-Rec 将语言语义与协同语义共同编码为物品索引，并通过多任务对齐使语言模型直接生成推荐物品标识。

### 研究动机与问题定义

纯文本 LLM 推荐难以表达用户-物品协同关系，纯 ID 建模又缺乏语义。LC-Rec 试图在有限增加词表的前提下，把两类信息纳入统一的生成式推荐模型。

### TL;DR（核心摘要）

`物品文本与交互 → 向量量化/统一映射 → LLM 对齐 → 生成物品索引 → 推荐物品`

模型利用文本编码器构造层次化物品索引，将索引 token 接入 LLM，再通过对齐任务引入协同信号。训练包含序列物品预测、显式索引-语言映射以及推荐对齐任务；在线生成的索引直接对应物品。

### 输入与使用场景

| 方面 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| 使用信息 | 物品标题/描述、用户交互和协同表示 |
| 信息融入位置 | 索引构建、词表扩展和对齐目标 |
| 语义标识结构 | 层次化序列索引 |
| 适用场景 | 序列推荐、意图预测和物品索引 |

### 方法设计

#### III-A 方法概览（Overview of the Approach）
LC-Rec 的目标是缩小语言语义与协同语义之间的差距。系统由物品索引学习和 LLM 对齐两部分组成：前者建立可生成的离散索引，后者让语言模型理解索引的推荐含义。

#### III-B 物品索引学习（Learning Item Indices）
论文使用物品文本编码器获得语义向量，再通过向量量化得到层次化 item index，并设计统一语义映射减少索引冲突。索引 token 被加入语言模型词表，作为文本语义和协同语义的共同接口。

#### III-C 语言-协同语义对齐
模型训练序列物品预测、显式索引生成、物品意图预测和协同/语言语义对齐等任务。不同任务分别从物品、用户历史和推荐目标施加约束，使 LLM 能在生成索引的同时利用协同结构。

#### III-D 训练与推理
论文采用分阶段对齐与推荐训练。推理时模型生成目标 item index，标识直接对应物品；索引构建和模型输入中的信息来源被明确区分。

### 实验结论

- 语言-协同联合对齐提升了物品预测和索引相关任务表现。
- 推荐对齐任务有助于缩小语言语义与协同语义之间的差距。

### 局限性与研究定位

#### 局限性
- 依赖离线物品索引构建，动态物品更新成本未充分讨论。
- 多任务对齐增加了训练和词表管理复杂度。

#### 研究定位
LC-Rec 的核心价值是把协同语义显式注入 LLM 的物品索引体系。它适合放在“LLM 推荐的协同语义对齐”章节。

### 相关资源

- [论文原文](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.09049)

### 标签

`协同语义` · `多任务对齐` · `层次化量化` · `LLM推荐`

*图源：原论文，图1。图片使用许可待核实。*

## LESSRec

- Page: pages/papers/lessrec.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: III. SID–Model Alignment
- Stage: Backbone
- Representation: Text / Text+CF; Tokenization: RQ-VAE / R-KM / LETTER; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP; Inference: C-Beam
- TL;DR: LESSRec encodes the history separately at each Semantic ID level and restricts attention to the target token's level, adding an item-level semantic sequence, instead of attending to all levels.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 4
