## MME-SID

- Page: pages/papers/mme-sid.md
- Venue: CIKM’25
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text+Img+CF; Tokenization: MM-RQ; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP; Inference: Scoring
- TL;DR: MME-SID feeds an LLM multimodal embeddings together with Semantic ID embeddings from MM-RQ-VAE, trained with maximum mean discrepancy and contrastive alignment, to reduce embedding collapse and forgetting.
- [Code](https://github.com/Applied-Machine-Learning-Lab/MME-SID)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 4

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon 2014 5-core: Beauty (22,332 users / 12,086 items), Toys and Games (19,121 / 11,757), Sports and Outdoors (35,092 / 18,090); items lacking a title or image are removed. Positives are ratings above 3.
  - Source: 5-core Amazon 2014 and item removal: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.02017v1#S5.SS1.SSS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2509.02017v1#A2.p1; statistics: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.02017v1#S5.T1.
- **Split**: Per user, the N-th (last) item is the test target and the (N-1)-th item the training target; a validation split is not reported. Results averaged over 3 runs.
  - Source: Last and second-last item as test and training targets: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.02017v1#S5.SS1.SSS1.p1; three runs: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.02017v1#S5.SS1.SSS4.p1.
- **Candidates**: not reported (full catalog versus sampled); items are scored by dot products between the LLM output and multimodal item embeddings, with HR and nDCG at 5, 10, 20.
  - Source: Scores over target item embeddings: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.02017v1#S4.SS3.p3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2509.02017v1#S6.SS2.p1; metrics: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.02017v1#S5.SS1.SSS2.p1.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. A frequency-aware fusion module reweights modalities by each item's training-set frequency.
  - Source: Standard split; frequency-aware fusion for cold versus warm items without an unseen-item protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.02017v1#S5.SS1.SSS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2509.02017v1#S4.SS3.p3.
- **SID**: Separate collaborative, textual, and visual SIDs from RQ-VAEs with 4 levels x 256 codes (300 for Sports), used as LLM input embeddings alongside projected modality embeddings. The paper states that MME-SID does not need to tackle collisions because multimodal data discriminate between items; no resolution rule is described.
  - Source: 4 levels x 256 (300 for Sports) per modality: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.02017v1#A1.T4; no collision handling needed by design: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.02017v1#S4.I1.i2.p1.
- **Inference budget**: No autoregressive decoding: one forward pass of Llama3-8B-instruct, then scoring against item embeddings. All experiments on A100 GPUs; inference batch size and latency: not reported.
  - Source: Scoring instead of autoregressive decoding: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.02017v1#S6.SS2.p1; hardware: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.02017v1#S5.SS1.SSS4.p1.
- **Results from**: Table 3 (Beauty, Toys, Sports versus ID, multimodal, and SID-based baselines; t-tests); Figure 3 (embedding collapse and SR performance); Appendix Table 4 (hyperparameters).
  - Source: Main: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.02017v1#S5.T3; collapse analysis: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.02017v1#S5.SS3.p1.

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: competitor; note: TIGER-MM generates per-modality RQ-VAE semantic IDs autoregressively and must resolve collisions; MME-SID feeds multimodal SIDs and embeddings to an LLM and scores items directly.; where: MME-SID v1, baseline TIGER-MM: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.02017v1#S5.I2.i7.p1; collision contrast: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.02017v1#S4.I1.i2.p1; Table 3: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.02017v1#S5.T3.
- id: letter; relation: competitor; note: LETTER regularizes the tokenizer for generative retrieval on a TIGER backbone; MME-SID avoids generation and aligns modalities with an MMD loss.; where: MME-SID v1, baseline LETTER implemented on TIGER: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.02017v1#S5.I2.i9.p1; Table 3: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.02017v1#S5.T3.
- id: lc-rec; relation: alternative; note: LC-Rec aligns an LLM to item indices but decodes autoregressively; MME-SID scores items from the LLM output for lower latency.; where: MME-SID v1, Section 6.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.02017v1#S6.SS2.p1.
- id: adc-sid; relation: alternative; note: ADC-SID later compares against MM-RQ-VAE (MME-SID's tokenizer) and adds adaptive behavior-content alignment.; where: Evidence is from the later ADC-SID paper: MM-RQ-VAE baseline and Table 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.25622v3#S4.I3.i6.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2510.25622v3#S4.T2.

### Notes

## 旧目录说明

迁自 `d61aa6c:README.md` 的条目说明，未沿用旧目录的收录分类。

SID 只作 LLM 的输入，用输出嵌入对全物品打分，不生成 SID。

## MMGRec

- Page: pages/papers/mmgrec.md
- Venue: TOMM’26
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text+Img+CF; Tokenization: Graph RQ-VAE; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP; Inference: C-Beam
- TL;DR: MMGRec assigns each item a Rec-ID with Graph RQ-VAE over multimodal and collaborative features and trains a Transformer with relation-aware self-attention to generate it, instead of embed-and-retrieve.
- [Code](https://github.com/hanliu95/MMGRec)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 1

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: MovieLens, TikTok, Kwai multimodal recommendation benchmarks; filtering: not reported.
  - Source: Section 5.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16555v4#S5.SS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16555v4#S5.SS1.p2
- **Split**: Per-user random interaction split: 80% training, 10% validation, 10% test; non-sequential CF, without temporal labels.
  - Source: Sections 5.1-5.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16555v4#S5.SS1.p3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16555v4#S5.SS2.p2
- **Candidates**: not reported
  - Source: Sections 4.4 and 5.1 specify generated top-K lists but no full-catalog/sampled evaluation declaration: https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16555v4#S4.SS4.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16555v4#S5.SS1.p3
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Graph RQ-VAE uses user-item interactions; test-interaction exposure in graph construction: not reported.
  - Source: Sections 4.2.1 and 5.1 define no unseen-item evaluation: https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16555v4#S4.SS2.SSS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16555v4#S5.SS1.p3
- **SID**: Graph RQ-VAE: 3 semantic tokens plus popularity-rank collision suffix. Codebooks tuned over 64/128/256; Kwai analysis favors 128; selected per-dataset sizes not reported.
  - Source: Sections 4.2.2, 5.3 and 6.5: https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16555v4#S4.SS2.SSS2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16555v4#S5.SS3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16555v4#S6.SS5.p4
- **Inference budget**: Constrained beam width K, default K=10. Figure 5 plots approximately 60-125 ms/user across 1/16-to-full Kwai. Hardware, inference batch size and timing scope: not reported.
  - Source: Sections 4.4-4.5, Section 6.4 and Figure 5: https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16555v4#S4.SS4.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16555v4#S4.SS5.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16555v4#S5.SS1.p3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16555v4#S6.SS4.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16555v4#S6.F5
- **Results from**: This paper's experiments using public baseline implementations: Table 2 main; Tables 3-5 ablations; Figures 4-6 hyperparameters, inference efficiency, Rec-ID design. TIGER is explicitly excluded from the benchmark.
  - Source: Tables 2-5, Figures 4-6 and baseline implementation statement: https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16555v4#S6.T2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16555v4#S6.T3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16555v4#S6.T4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16555v4#S6.T5 and https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16555v4#S6.F4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16555v4#S6.F6 and https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16555v4#S6.F5 and https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16555v4#S5.SS2.p2

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: predecessor; note: MMGRec extends TIGER's RQ-VAE idea with multimodal/CF inputs and popularity-based collision suffixes; TIGER is not evaluated.; where: MMGRec v4, Sections 1, 3 and 5.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16555v4#S1.p4; https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16555v4#S3.p1; https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16555v4#S5.SS2.p2.

## MMQ

- Page: pages/papers/mmq.md
- Venue: WSDM’26
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text+Img; Tokenization: MoE-VQ; Backbone: HeterRec; Tokenizer: Joint; Objective: MTP; Inference: –
- TL;DR: MMQ trains a multimodal tokenizer with modality-shared and modality-specific experts under orthogonal regularization, then fine-tunes its Semantic IDs on behavior objectives with a multimodal reconstruction loss.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Beauty; retrieval uses user/item 5-core filtering and histories capped at 20. Southeast Asian advertising logs, October 2024-May 2025 (30M users, 40M ads); industrial filters not reported.
  - Source: Section 4.1.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.15281v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2508.15281v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p3
- **Split**: Beauty ranking: chronological 90% train/10% test; ratings >3 positive, <=3 negative. Retrieval and industrial offline splits not reported. Online A/B: July 6-August 6, 2025; treatment 10% random user traffic.
  - Source: Sections 4.1.1 and 5: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.15281v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2508.15281v1#S5.p1
- **Candidates**: Retrieval: not reported; ranking evaluates labeled ratings, candidate retrieval n/a.
  - Source: Section 4.1.1/4.1.2 gives labels and metrics, not retrieval candidates: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.15281v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2508.15281v1#S4.SS1.SSS2.p3
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined.
  - Source: Section 4.1 defines no item holdout: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.15281v1#S4.SS1
- **SID**: 6 positions: 2 shared, 2 text-specific, 2 visual-specific; codebook size 100 (Beauty), 3000 (industrial). Collision handling not reported.
  - Source: Section 4.1.4: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.15281v1#S4.SS1.SSS4.p2
- **Inference budget**: Retrieval K=5/10 using HeterRec; ranking uses PPNet. Decoding budget, hardware, inference batch size, and latency not reported.
  - Source: Sections 4.1.2/4.1.4: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.15281v1#S4.SS1.SSS2.p3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2508.15281v1#S4.SS1.SSS4.p1
- **Results from**: Original Table 1: tokenizer comparisons under HeterRec retrieval/PPNet ranking; Section 5: online A/B versus deployed ItemID system.
  - Source: Table 1 and Section 5: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.15281v1#S4.T1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2508.15281v1#S5.p1

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: predecessor; note: MMQ replaces TIGER's separated tokenizer training with behavior-aware joint adaptation.; where: MMQ v1, Section 3.3: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.15281v1#S3.SS3.p1.
- id: onerec; relation: alternative; note: OneRec aligns modalities before quantization; MMQ separates shared and specific experts.; where: MMQ v1, Section 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.15281v1#S2.p3.
- id: lc-rec; relation: alternative; note: LC-Rec aligns indices through multitask fine-tuning; MMQ adapts multimodal tokenization directly.; where: MMQ v1, Sections 2 and 3.3: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.15281v1#S2.p2; https://arxiv.org/html/2508.15281v1#S3.SS3.p1.

## Molar

- Page: pages/papers/molar.md
- Venue: arXiv’24
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Representation
- Representation: Text+Img+CF; Tokenization: n/a; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: n/a; Objective: Discrim.; Inference: Scoring
- TL;DR: Molar builds item representations from text and images with a multimodal LLM and aligns its user representations with an ID-based model, to add collaborative signals that LLM recommenders lack.
- [Code](https://anonymous.4open.science/r/Molar-8B06/)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 0

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon clothing (993,087 users / 301,312 items / 8,813,442 interactions), PixelRec (50,000 / 82,864 / 989,476), MovieLens (6,040 / 3,706 / 1,000,209). Filtering rules: not reported.
  - Source: Datasets: https://arxiv.org/html/2412.18176v2#S4.I2.i1.p1, https://arxiv.org/html/2412.18176v2#S4.I2.i2.p1, https://arxiv.org/html/2412.18176v2#S4.I2.i3.p1; statistics: https://arxiv.org/html/2412.18176v2#S4.T1; filtering not stated.
- **Split**: Sequential leave-one-out into training, validation, and test; the exact position allocation is not reported beyond the label.
  - Source: Leave-one-out: https://arxiv.org/html/2412.18176v2#S4.SS1.SSS1.p2.
- **Candidates**: full catalog (the paper states metrics are evaluated on the full amount of data); training uses 1:1 negative sampling with BCE.
  - Source: Evaluated on the full amount of data: https://arxiv.org/html/2412.18176v2#S4.SS1.SSS1.p2; 1:1 negatives are a training choice: https://arxiv.org/html/2412.18176v2#A2.p1.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined.
  - Source: Standard split with no unseen-item protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2412.18176v2#S4.SS1.SSS1.p2.
- **SID**: n/a (items are represented by continuous embeddings from a fine-tuned multimodal LLM; no discrete SIDs are built).
  - Source: Continuous item embeddings from the MLLM, no discrete IDs: https://arxiv.org/html/2412.18176v2#S4.SS1.SSS2.p1; Table 1 judgment in facts/dash.yaml.
- **Inference budget**: Scoring with item embeddings from Qwen2-VL-2B (MIRM) and a user model (DUEG); hardware, inference batch size, and latency: not reported.
  - Source: Backbone and training: https://arxiv.org/html/2412.18176v2#S4.SS1.SSS2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2412.18176v2#S4.SS1.SSS2.p2; no inference settings found.
- **Results from**: Table 2 (Amazon, PixelRec, MovieLens versus traditional, content, and LLM-based baselines); Tables 3-5 (modalities, post-alignment model, ablations); Appendix Table 6 (MLLM backbones).
  - Source: Main: https://arxiv.org/html/2412.18176v2#S4.T2; modalities: https://arxiv.org/html/2412.18176v2#S4.T3; post-alignment: https://arxiv.org/html/2412.18176v2#S4.T4; ablation: https://arxiv.org/html/2412.18176v2#S4.T5; backbones: https://arxiv.org/html/2412.18176v2#A1.T6.

### Notes

## 旧目录说明

迁自 `d61aa6c:README.md` 的条目说明，未沿用旧目录的收录分类。

用多模态 LLM 产出用户和物品嵌入，按相似度推荐，不使用 SID。

## MQL4GRec

- Page: pages/papers/mql4grec.md
- Venue: ICLR’25
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text+Img; Tokenization: Dual RQ; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: Multi-task NTP; Inference: Beam
- TL;DR: MQL4GRec translates item text and images from several domains into a shared quantitative language and pre-trains generation tasks over it, to transfer recommendation knowledge across domains and modalities.
- [Code](https://github.com/zhaijianyang/MQL4GRec)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 5

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Reviews 2018 (May 1996-October 2018). Pre-training on six categories (Pet, Cell, Automotive, Tools, Toys, Sports); target tasks on Instruments (17,112 users / 6,250 items), Arts (22,171 / 9,416), Games (42,259 / 13,839). Users and items with fewer than 5 interactions are filtered; sequences capped at 20 items.
  - Source: Pre-training and target categories: https://arxiv.org/html/2504.05314v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2504.05314v1#A1.p1; filtering and length: https://arxiv.org/html/2504.05314v1#A1.p2; statistics: https://arxiv.org/html/2504.05314v1#A1.T6.
- **Split**: Leave-one-out (allocation not restated beyond the label). Separate zero-shot study: models pre-trained on source categories are tested on the targets without fine-tuning.
  - Source: Leave-one-out named only: https://arxiv.org/html/2504.05314v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1; zero-shot study: https://arxiv.org/html/2504.05314v1#S4.SS5.p1.
- **Candidates**: full catalog (full ranking over the entire item set instead of sample-based evaluation).
  - Source: Full ranking over the entire item set: https://arxiv.org/html/2504.05314v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.
- **Visibility**: Main: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Zero-shot: target-domain items are unseen by the pre-trained generator; whether the RQ-VAE translators saw them: not reported.
  - Source: Standard split; zero-shot uses target-domain items absent from pre-training: https://arxiv.org/html/2504.05314v1#S4.SS5.p1.
- **SID**: Separate text (LLaMA) and image (ViT-L/14) quantitative languages from RQ-VAEs with 4 levels x 256 codewords (dimension 32). Colliding items have tokens reassigned by the distances between their residuals and code vectors, instead of an appended identifier.
  - Source: 4 levels x 256 x 32 per modality: https://arxiv.org/html/2504.05314v1#A3.p1; distance-based reassignment for collisions: https://arxiv.org/html/2504.05314v1#S3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.
- **Inference budget**: Beam search with beam size 20 in each modality; the two recommendation lists are re-ranked so items in both rank higher. T5 encoder-decoder with 4 layers each. Hardware, inference batch size, and latency: not reported.
  - Source: Beam size 20 and dual-list re-ranking: https://arxiv.org/html/2504.05314v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2504.05314v1#S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1; T5 backbone: https://arxiv.org/html/2504.05314v1#A3.p2.
- **Results from**: Table 1 (Instruments, Arts, Games versus sequential, multimodal, and generative baselines); Table 2 (collision handling versus TIGER's appended index); Tables 3-4 (generation tasks and pre-training); Figures 3-4 (pre-training data and epochs); Table 5 (zero-shot).
  - Source: Main: https://arxiv.org/html/2504.05314v1#S4.T1; collisions: https://arxiv.org/html/2504.05314v1#S4.T2; tasks and pre-training: https://arxiv.org/html/2504.05314v1#S4.T3, https://arxiv.org/html/2504.05314v1#S4.T4; zero-shot: https://arxiv.org/html/2504.05314v1#S4.T5.

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: competitor; note: TIGER uses one text modality and an appended index for collisions; MQL4GRec translates text and images into separate quantitative languages and reassigns colliding tokens by distance.; where: MQL4GRec v1, Table 1 baseline TIGER: https://arxiv.org/html/2504.05314v1#S4.T1; collision comparison in Table 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2504.05314v1#S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2504.05314v1#S4.T2.
- id: lc-rec; relation: alternative; note: LC-Rec spreads items across the last level with a uniform constraint, which MQL4GRec says does not fully remove collisions.; where: MQL4GRec v1, Section 3.1 Handling Collisions cites Zheng et al. (2023): https://arxiv.org/html/2504.05314v1#S3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.
- id: cid; relation: competitor; note: P5-CID uses collaborative indexing for a T5 model; MQL4GRec uses multimodal content codes with cross-modal generation tasks.; where: MQL4GRec v1, baseline P5-CID: https://arxiv.org/html/2504.05314v1#A2.I1.i8.p1; Table 1: https://arxiv.org/html/2504.05314v1#S4.T1.
- id: vq-rec; relation: competitor; note: VQ-Rec uses product-quantized text codes in a discriminative transferable model; MQL4GRec generates multimodal codes with pre-training across categories.; where: MQL4GRec v1, Table 1 baseline VQ-Rec: https://arxiv.org/html/2504.05314v1#S4.T1.
- id: macrec; relation: successor; note: MACRec later reuses MQL4GRec's collision reassignment and dual-modality ensemble and adds cross-modal contrastive alignment during quantization.; where: Evidence is from the later MACRec paper: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.15122v2#Sx3.SSx1.SSSx3.p5 and https://arxiv.org/html/2511.15122v2#Sx3.SSx2.SSSx3.p3; MQL4GRec is its main baseline in Table 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.15122v2#Sx4.T2.

### Notes

## 旧卡片说明

迁自 `d61aa6c:papers/mql4grec.md`。保留方法说明、实验叙述与局限；本轮只对照现有记录处理明确冲突，未重新逐句核查原论文。分类和规格以页面上方由记录生成的表格为准。

### MQL4GRec：生成式推荐的多模态量化语言

> MQL4GRec 将不同领域和模态的物品内容翻译为统一的离散量化语言，并以生成任务迁移推荐知识。

### 研究动机与问题定义

文本和图像内容形式复杂，跨域推荐中的表示难以共享。MQL4GRec 把量化器视为翻译器，将多模态内容映射到共享 codebook 语言，降低跨域迁移的表示差异。

### TL;DR（核心摘要）

`文本/图像 → RQ-VAE量化语言 → 预训练生成任务 → 目标域微调 → 推荐物品`

冻结模态编码器提取文本或图像表示，RQ-VAE 将其转为带模态前缀的离散 token；通过下一物品生成、非对称生成和量化语言对齐任务进行预训练，再在目标推荐数据上微调。论文在生成候选后进行模态结果重排，重排仍属于模型内部流程。

### 输入与使用场景

| 方面 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| 使用信息 | 文本、图像、用户交互和多域数据 |
| 信息融入位置 | 量化语言、预训练任务和目标域生成 |
| 语义标识结构 | 带模态前缀的多级序列 |
| 适用场景 | 多模态、跨域推荐 |

### 方法设计

#### 3.1 量化语言
MQL4GRec 将量化器视为翻译器。冻结的 LLaMA/ViT 编码器提取文本或图像表示，RQ-VAE 为每种模态学习多级 codebook，并通过模态前缀组成统一量化语言。碰撞物品再依据残差距离重新分配 code。

#### 3.2 量化语言生成任务
除同模态下一物品生成外，论文加入非对称生成：用文本历史预测图像量化语言，或反向预测；同时加入 text-to-image 和 image-to-text 的显式量化语言对齐任务。

#### 3.3 训练与推荐
模型先在多域、多模态数据上预训练，再在目标推荐任务上微调。生成器预测目标模态的量化 token，推理阶段综合不同模态生成列表，并依据模型分数进行内部重排。

#### 3.4 零样本与分析
实验考察跨域迁移、模态组合、消融和零样本能力，重点验证量化语言是否能把模态知识和推荐知识传递到新领域。

### 实验结论

- MQL4GRec 在 ICLR 2025 论文报告的跨域设置中优于比较方法。
- 量化语言预训练和跨模态对齐带来迁移收益。

### 局限性与研究定位

#### 局限性
- 模态候选重排增加了推理链路。
- 量化语言依赖模态编码器和离线 codebook。
- 开放物品和动态领域更新仍需验证。

#### 研究定位
MQL4GRec 的主要贡献是将多模态跨域知识迁移表述为量化语言生成，适合放在“跨域与多模态生成推荐”章节。

### 标签

`量化语言` · `多模态` · `跨域迁移` · `生成式推荐`

### 架构图来源

*图源：原论文，图2。图片使用许可待核实。*

### 旧总表补充

来源：`d61aa6c:tables/all-methods.md`。

- 核心贡献：以量化语言促进跨域迁移。
- 使用场景：多模态跨域。

## MSCGRec

- Page: pages/papers/mscgrec.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text+Img+CF; Tokenization: RQ-VAE+DINO; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed†; Objective: NTP; Inference: Trie/C-Beam
- TL;DR: MSCGRec quantizes images with self-supervised DINO-based learning, adds collaborative features as a separate modality, and restricts training outputs to permissible tokens, to scale generative recommendation to large catalogs.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 5

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon 2023 Beauty and Personal Care (724,796 users / 203,843 items), Sports and Outdoors (408,287 / 151,632), and PixelRec (8,886,078 / 407,082). 5-core filtering of users and items; for Amazon, samples with empty or placeholder images are removed and items with identical images are merged into one ID; sequences capped at 20 items.
  - Source: Datasets and preprocessing: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.03713v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1; statistics: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.03713v1#S4.T1.
- **Split**: Chronological leave-one-out into training, validation, and test; for Amazon every item in a training sequence is a separate target, for PixelRec only the last item.
  - Source: Chronological leave-one-out and target construction: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.03713v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.
- **Candidates**: not reported (full catalog versus sampled evaluation candidates); top-K lists from constrained beam search.
  - Source: Metrics only: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.03713v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. The collaborative modality uses SASRec item embeddings trained on the interaction data.
  - Source: Standard split with no unseen-item protocol; SASRec embeddings as the collaborative modality: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.03713v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.03713v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.
- **SID**: Per-modality residual quantizers (image via DINO self-supervised quantization, LLAMA text, SASRec collaborative) with 3 levels x 256 entries each, applied directly in embedding space; an extra collision level per modality makes each item's code unique (TIGER style). The collaborative codes serve as generation targets.
  - Source: 3 levels x 256 per modality plus a collision level: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.03713v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.03713v1#S3.SS1.p2; DINO-based image quantization: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.03713v1#S3.SS2.p2.
- **Inference budget**: Constrained beam search with 20 beams; T5 encoder-decoder; training and evaluation on four NVIDIA A100 GPUs. Inference batch size and latency: not reported.
  - Source: Constrained beam search with 20 beams and hardware: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.03713v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p3; constrained training softmax: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.03713v1#S3.SS3.p2.
- **Results from**: Table 2 (Beauty, Sports, PixelRec versus sequential and generative baselines); Table 3 (component ablations, modality Shapley values, image-only).
  - Source: Main: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.03713v1#S4.T2; ablations and Shapley values: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.03713v1#S4.T3.

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: competitor; note: TIGER quantizes one modality; MSCGRec concatenates codes from image, text, and collaborative modalities and trains with a softmax restricted to permissible next codes, keeping TIGER's collision level.; where: MSCGRec v1, baselines TIGER_i and TIGER_t: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.03713v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1; Table 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.03713v1#S4.T2; collision level follows TIGER: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.03713v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p2.
- id: mql4grec; relation: competitor; note: MQL4GRec uses separate text and image quantitative languages with collision reassignment; MSCGRec adds a collaborative modality, DINO-based image codes, and constrained training, and found MQL4GRec's reassignment gave no gain under constrained training.; where: MSCGRec v1, follows MQL4GRec's text embeddings and tests its reassignment: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.03713v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.03713v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p2; Table 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.03713v1#S4.T2.
- id: letter; relation: competitor; note: LETTER aligns quantized codes with a sequential recommender inside one tokenizer; MSCGRec keeps collaborative information as its own code modality.; where: MSCGRec v1, LETTER-TIGER baseline: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.03713v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1; Table 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.03713v1#S4.T2.
- id: cost; relation: competitor; note: CoST aligns embeddings before and after quantization contrastively; MSCGRec changes the modalities and the training softmax instead.; where: MSCGRec v1, baselines: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.03713v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1; Table 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.03713v1#S4.T2.
- id: etegrec; relation: competitor; note: ETEGRec trains tokenizer and generator end to end; MSCGRec quantizes frozen pretrained embeddings per modality.; where: MSCGRec v1, baselines: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.03713v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1; Table 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.03713v1#S4.T2.

## 旧目录说明

迁自 `d61aa6c:README.md` 的条目说明，未沿用旧目录的收录分类。

用多模态语义码和协同码共同表示物品，以约束 softmax 训练，约束束搜索解码。

## MuSID-KD

- Page: pages/papers/musid-kd.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: IV. Utility
- Stage: Training
- Representation: –; Tokenization: RQ-VAE; Backbone: Enc-MLP; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP + Aux.; Inference: C-Beam
- TL;DR: MuSID-KD distills a generative teacher into lightweight students by aligning candidate distributions at successive Semantic ID prefix levels and weighting supervision by ranking impact, instead of uniform alignment.
- [Code](https://anonymous.4open.science/r/m7k2-review-83f9/)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 2

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Reviews 2014 Beauty/Toys, Amazon Reviews 2023 Video Games, and Steam-100K; histories capped at 20. Filtering rules not reported.
  - Source: Section 6.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.35218v1#S6.SS1.p1
- **Split**: Chronological leave-one-out; exact validation/test allocation not reported. Checkpoints selected by validation NDCG@10.
  - Source: Section 6.1 and Appendix B.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.35218v1#S6.SS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.35218v1#A2.SS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.35218v1#S6.SS1.p3
- **Candidates**: Evaluation: not reported. The 64 teacher candidates per request are training support, not sampled evaluation negatives.
  - Source: Section 6.1 separates evaluation from training candidates: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.35218v1#S6.SS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.35218v1#S6.SS1.p3
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Frozen teacher encoder/token embeddings/mapping shared with students; additional distillation caches use training requests only. Teacher/tokenizer exposure to test items not reported.
  - Source: Sections 6.1/B.1 define no item holdout: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.35218v1#S6.SS1.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.35218v1#A2.SS1.p3
- **SID**: Main RQ-VAE: 4 positions x 256 codes; frozen and shared teacher/student mapping. R-KMeans additionally tested. Unique SIDs assumed; collision handling not reported.
  - Source: Sections 6.1/6.2 and Appendix B.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.35218v1#S6.SS1.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.35218v1#S6.SS2.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.35218v1#A2.SS1.p4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.35218v1#S3.SS1.p1
- **Inference budget**: Constrained beam 50; K=5/10; student batch 32 (teacher throughput batch 64). MuSID-KD MLP/GRU/CNN: 3036/3423/3024 requests/s; GRU/CNN serving totals 0.292/0.331 ms/request. Hardware not reported.
  - Source: Section 6.1/6.5 and Appendix B.3/Table B1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.35218v1#S6.SS1.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.35218v1#S6.SS5.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.35218v1#A2.SS3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.35218v1#A2.T6
- **Results from**: Original Table 1: Amazon, mean over seeds 42-44; Table S1: Steam; Figure 6: R-KMeans. KD baselines adapted to shared teacher/students/decoding; TIGER is a teacher reference, excluded from student comparisons.
  - Source: Table 1, Figure 6 and Appendix A.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.35218v1#S6.T1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.35218v1#S6.F6 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.35218v1#A1.T3

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: predecessor; note: MuSID-KD uses TIGER as its frozen teacher and shares its history encoder.; where: MuSID-KD v1, Section 6.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.35218v1#S6.SS1.p2.
- id: sid-mlp; relation: predecessor; note: SID-MLP supplies the Base KD objective and lightweight student design.; where: MuSID-KD v1, Sections 2.3/6.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.35218v1#S2.SS3.p1; https://arxiv.org/html/2610.35218v1#S6.SS1.p2.

## NAU

- Page: pages/papers/nau.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: IV. Utility
- Stage: Training
- Representation: –; Tokenization: R-KM; Backbone: Enc-Dec†; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP + Aux.; Inference: –
- TL;DR: NAU adds explicit control over the probability mass on forgotten items' Semantic ID neighborhoods to interaction-level unlearning, because shared tokens let unlearning degrade neighboring items.
- [Code](https://github.com/pierre-lubitzsch/neighborhood-aware-unlearning)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Beauty, Sports, Toys using released five-core preprocessing. Table 24 additionally lists Food k5 SID diagnostics; its source and preprocessing details not reported.
  - Source: Section 4 and Appendix H Table 24: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.27232v1#S4.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.27232v1#A8.T24
- **Split**: Chronological train/validation/test; allocation sizes not reported. Training histories capped at 20 items; all unlearning methods start from the same original model.
  - Source: Appendix A: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.27232v1#A1.p1
- **Candidates**: not reported; no items are filtered from generated candidates during unlearning evaluation.
  - Source: Section 4 and Appendix A: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.27232v1#S4.p6 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.27232v1#A1.p1
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Users, items and SIDs remain fixed during NAU.
  - Source: Sections 2/4 study interaction deletion with existing items, without an unseen-item protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.27232v1#S2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.27232v1#S4
- **SID**: RQ-KMeans/RQ-VAE diagnostics: 3 semantic levels plus fourth deduplication level. Codebook sizes not reported; Table 24 shows 256 occupied first-level RQ-KMeans codes. LETTER and TRACER-compatible tokenizers also evaluated; their sizes not reported.
  - Source: Section 4 and Appendix H Table 24: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.27232v1#S4.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.27232v1#A8.T24
- **Inference budget**: Top-10 utility/exposure metrics; beam width, inference hardware, inference batch size and recommendation latency not reported. One H200 and NAU's 3.9s measure unlearning per request, not recommendation inference.
  - Source: Section 4 and Appendix D Table 9: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.27232v1#S4.p6 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.27232v1#A4.T9
- **Results from**: Original Tables 1/3/4: spam/unwanted-item removal; Appendices D/F: extended results. Five data seeds. RQ-KMeans selection uses validation; other-tokenizer operating-point selection uses test results.
  - Source: Section 5 and Appendix D: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.27232v1#S5.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.27232v1#S5.p8 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.27232v1#S5.p9 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.27232v1#A4.p1

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: predecessor; note: Supplies the generative backbone for the interaction-unlearning experiments.; where: NAU v1, Section 4: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.27232v1#S4.p2.
- id: letter; relation: predecessor; note: Its collaboratively regularized tokenizer is used to test NAU across SID constructions.; where: NAU v1, Section 4 and Appendix D: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.27232v1#S4.p2; https://arxiv.org/html/2610.27232v1#A4.p5.
- id: tracer; relation: competitor; note: Reassigns concept-item SIDs; NAU deletes interactions while preserving the identifiers.; where: NAU v1, Sections 4/6: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.27232v1#S4.p4; https://arxiv.org/html/2610.27232v1#S6.p2.

## NEO

- Page: pages/papers/neo.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: Paradigms, Systems and Benchmarks
- Stage: No single stage
- Representation: Text / Audio; Tokenization: R-KM; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: Multi-task NTP; Inference: C-Beam
- TL;DR: NEO adapts a decoder-only LLM to interleave natural language and typed item Semantic IDs in one sequence, with constrained decoding, to unify search, recommendation, and reasoning without tools.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Industrial media logs: >10M episodes, shows, audiobooks and artists; about 15M users; 5M grounding examples, 10M instruction-training examples, 100K test examples. Filtering not reported.
  - Source: Section 4.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.17533v1#S4.SS1.p1
- **Split**: Global temporal protocol: context through t, labels at t+k, evaluation at t+2k; k=1 day for episodes/shows, 7 days for audiobooks. Baselines share train/test windows; dates and validation allocation not reported.
  - Source: Section 4.1.5: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.17533v1#S4.SS1.SSS5.p1
- **Candidates**: not reported; NEO and baselines use the same candidate universe.
  - Source: Section 4.1.5 specifies a common candidate universe but not full-catalog versus sampled evaluation: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.17533v1#S4.SS1.SSS5.p1
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. User cold-start simulated by removing listening history and retaining user metadata.
  - Source: Section 4.1.5 and its cold-user experiment: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.17533v1#S4.SS1.SSS5.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2603.17533v1#S4.SS1.SSS5.Px1.p1
- **SID**: Separate residual K-Means vocabularies by type: 4 x 256 for audiobooks/episodes/shows, 4 x 1024 for artists. Each collision bucket resolves to one popularity-selected item.
  - Source: Section 4.1.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.17533v1#S4.SS1.SSS2.p2
- **Inference budget**: Trie-constrained beam 30; HR/NDCG@10/30. Top-p alternative: temperature 0.6, top-k 20, top-p 0.95. Inference hardware, batch size and absolute latency not reported; Table 3 latency@10 decreases 2.92% without constraints and 7.91% with sampling.
  - Source: Section 4.2.1 and Table 3: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.17533v1#S4.SS2.SSS1.Px5.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2603.17533v1#S4.T3
- **Results from**: Original Tables 5/8/9: production-baseline comparisons, cold/warm users and search breakdowns. Recommendation baseline is GNN/two-tower; search baseline dense retrieval. NEO uses about half the production baseline's historical logs.
  - Source: Original Tables 5/8/9 and Sections 4.1.1/4.2.3: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.17533v1#S4.T5 and https://arxiv.org/html/2603.17533v1#A2.T8 and https://arxiv.org/html/2603.17533v1#A2.T9 and https://arxiv.org/html/2603.17533v1#S4.SS1.SSS1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2603.17533v1#S4.SS2.SSS3.Px1.p1

### Related

- id: plum; relation: alternative; note: Concurrent SID-LLM adaptation; NEO emphasizes mixed text-ID outputs and multiple item types.; where: NEO v1, Section 2 and Table 1: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.17533v1#S2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2; https://arxiv.org/html/2603.17533v1#S2.T1.
- id: tiger; relation: predecessor; note: Prior SID-based generative retrieval informs NEO's catalog-grounded item representation.; where: NEO v1, Introduction and Section 2, citing Rajput et al. (2024): https://arxiv.org/html/2603.17533v1#S1.p4; https://arxiv.org/html/2603.17533v1#S2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.
- id: eager-llm; relation: alternative; note: Motivates testing collaborative SID signals; NEO favors content-derived SIDs in its experiments.; where: NEO v1, Section 4.2.1, citing Hong et al. (2025): https://arxiv.org/html/2603.17533v1#S4.SS2.SSS1.Px4.p1.

## Netflix-SID-Comparison

- Page: pages/papers/netflix-sid-comparison.md
- Venue: NeurIPS’26 PALM Workshop
- Problem: Paradigms, Systems and Benchmarks
- Stage: No single stage
- Representation: –; Tokenization: RQ-VAE; Backbone: Dec-Only / Non-AR; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: Multi-task NTP / (Text NTP + MTP + Rank); Lang. RL after SFT; Inference: C-Beam / Scoring
- TL;DR: Netflix-SID-Comparison is an industry comparison, not a new recommender: it compares single-head autoregressive beam search with multi-token prediction for LLM Semantic ID generation on quality and cost.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 4

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Proprietary streaming-media member histories, synthetic content QA, and open instruction-following data; >=10M examples/task. Catalog size, exact corpus sizes and filtering not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.15864v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1 ; #S4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1
- **Split**: Histories snapshotted at a fixed date-hour; internal ranking test averages future-interaction offsets +1 through +7 days. Exact cutoff and train/validation/test sizes not reported; content QA uses a stratified test set.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.15864v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1 ; #S4.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1
- **Candidates**: not reported; trie/request-eligible catalog constraints define serving validity, but the ranking test universe and evaluation negative sampling are not specified.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.15864v1#S3.SS3.SSS1.p1 ; #S3.SS3.SSS2.p1 ; #S4.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1
- **Visibility**: Cold-start cohort: titles launched after training cutoff, without training engagement. Generator exposure through content QA and tokenizer fitting exposure not reported; unseen by generator only versus unseen by tokenizer too is not established.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.15864v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1 ; #S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1 ; #S4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1
- **SID**: Frozen snapshot of RQ-VAE identifiers: 4 x 1024. For collisions (<=1% example rate), return the first entity in the SID bucket.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.15864v1#S3.SS1.p1 ; #S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1
- **Inference budget**: Single-head: vLLM constrained beam search with prefix caching; MTP: one-pass per-code distributions and eligible-entity scoring. Beam width, output K, inference batch size and latency not reported. Shared training/inference pool: up to 256 H200/A100-80GB GPUs; inference allocation not reported. MTP throughput is 75% higher on 8B.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.15864v1#S3.SS3 ; #S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1 ; #S4.T2 ; #S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1
- **Results from**: Original Tables 1-2: controlled single-head versus MTP quality/system comparison. Tables 3-4: SID recipe versus previous non-SID auxiliary-head baseline; Tables 5-7: ablations. Proprietary scores/costs reported relatively; no imported baseline result table identified.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.15864v1#S4.T1 ; #S4.T2 ; #S4.T3 ; #S4.T4 ; #S4.SS2.p1

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: predecessor; note: The single-head arm follows TIGER-style autoregressive SID generation with constrained beam search in a multitask streaming-media LLM.; where: Netflix comparison v1, Introduction and Section 3.2.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.15864v1#S1.p3; https://arxiv.org/html/2610.15864v1#S3.SS2.SSS1.p1.
- id: rpg; relation: alternative; note: RPG pairs parallel SID prediction with graph-constrained decoding; this study strengthens its MTP arm with an auxiliary item-ranking loss and tests moderate four-token SIDs.; where: Netflix comparison v1, Sections 2/3.2.2/4.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.15864v1#S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1; https://arxiv.org/html/2610.15864v1#S3.SS2.SSS2.Px1.p1; https://arxiv.org/html/2610.15864v1#S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.
- id: stamp; relation: alternative; note: STAMP uses auxiliary multi-token prediction to densify training supervision; this study compares MTP and autoregressive decoding as generation paradigms.; where: Netflix comparison v1, Section 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.15864v1#S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.
- id: nezha; relation: alternative; note: NEZHA accelerates SID beam search using self-drafting and hash-set verification; this study addresses generation quality and cost rather than only decoding acceleration.; where: Netflix comparison v1, Section 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.15864v1#S2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.

## NEZHA

- Page: pages/papers/nezha.md
- Venue: WWW’26 Industry
- Problem: V. Efficiency
- Stage: Inference
- Representation: Text; Tokenization: RQ-VAE; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP; Inference: Self-Draft+Hash
- TL;DR: NEZHA adds an autoregressive draft head inside the main model for self-drafting and checks drafts against a hash set of valid IDs, instead of separate draft models and model-based verifiers.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Yelp, Amazon Beauty, Amazon Games; filtering rules not reported. Deployment uses Taobao Search Advertising production data; size, dates and filtering not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.18793v1#S4.SS1.p1 ; #S5.p1
- **Split**: Public per-user leave-one-out: last interaction test, penultimate validation, remainder training. Production offline split not reported; online A/B lasts seven days, traffic allocation not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.18793v1#S4.SS1.p1 ; #S5.p3
- **Candidates**: not reported
  - Source: Section 4.1 specifies metrics and beam size, not an evaluation universe: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.18793v1#S4.SS1
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Tokenizer fitting exposure to test items not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.18793v1#S4.SS1.p1 ; #S4.SS1.p4
- **SID**: Public RQ-VAE: 3 x 512, using embeddings of textual item attributes. Production uses three levels with different, unreported codebook sizes. Collision handling not reported; hash-set verification filters invalid generated SIDs.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.18793v1#S4.SS1.p4 ; #S3.SS3.p6
- **Inference budget**: Public beam 10, HR/NDCG@5/10; mean prefill+decode latency on Beauty/Games/Yelp: Llama 7.00/7.52/7.41 ms, Qwen 4.41/4.80/4.46 ms. Production benchmark beam 512; 2.6x algorithm speedup, deployed total latency <30 ms including queue savings. GPU model/count and inference batch size not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.18793v1#S4.SS1.p4 ; #S3.T3 ; #S1.T1 ; #S1.p3 ; #S5.p2
- **Results from**: Original Table 3: public beam/MTP/NEZHA comparison, means over seeds 42/43/44; Table 4: Yelp ablations. Section 5: production offline hit-rate gains and seven-day online revenue test. No imported baseline results identified.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.18793v1#S3.T3 ; #S4.T4 ; #S4.SS1.p4 ; #S5.p3

### Related

- id: atspeed; relation: alternative; note: AtSpeed uses a separate draft model and target-model verification; NEZHA uses an internal autoregressive draft head and hash-set validation. AtSpeed is omitted from public comparisons.; where: NEZHA v1, Sections 2.2/4.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.18793v1#S2.SS2.p2; https://arxiv.org/html/2511.18793v1#S4.SS1.p2.
- id: specgr; relation: alternative; note: SpecGR supports out-of-vocabulary recommendation with speculative inference; NEZHA removes separate drafting and costly target-model verification for fast catalog-valid generation.; where: NEZHA v1, Sections 1/6, citing Ding et al. (2024): https://arxiv.org/html/2511.18793v1#S1.p4; https://arxiv.org/html/2511.18793v1#S6.p2; https://arxiv.org/html/2511.18793v1#S6.p6.
- id: rpg; relation: alternative; note: RPG uses long semantic IDs and graph-based parallel decoding; NEZHA retains sequential dependencies through a lightweight autoregressive draft head.; where: NEZHA v1, Sections 3.2/6: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.18793v1#S3.SS2.p7; https://arxiv.org/html/2511.18793v1#S6.p2.

## OneChord

- Page: pages/papers/onechord.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: IV. Utility
- Stage: Training
- Representation: –; Tokenization: Par. OPQ; Backbone: Non-AR; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: Next-item CE + Cons. KD + Rank KD; Inference: Scoring
- TL;DR: OneChord uses one catalog-normalized fusion of Semantic ID evidence and item-matching scores for supervision, distillation, and inference in a parallel decoder, so training targets the ranking used in serving.
- [Code](https://anonymous.4open.science/r/OneChord-D1A2/)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon 2014 5-core Sports/Beauty/Toys; Amazon 2023 5core/last_out_w_his Scientific/Instruments/Games, reconstructing each user's longest chronological sequence.
  - Source: Section 4.1 and Appendix B.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.25805v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.25805v1#A2.SS1.p1
- **Split**: Last two interactions validation/test; sliding training windows over earlier interactions, history cap 20; one validation/test target per user.
  - Source: Appendix B.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.25805v1#A2.SS1.p1
- **Candidates**: full catalog of distinct legal SIDs; identical SIDs share one entry; exact four-code match determines hits.
  - Source: Appendix B.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.25805v1#A2.SS1.p2
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Fixed OPQ mapping covers every processed item.
  - Source: Appendix B.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.25805v1#A2.SS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.25805v1#A2.SS1.p2
- **SID**: Four-code OPQ, 256 codes/position; collisions remain merged as one catalog entry.
  - Source: Appendix A.5: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.25805v1#A1.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1
- **Inference budget**: One encoder/parallel-decoder pass plus catalog scoring; no beam. Recall/NDCG@5; full-test Top-10 generation 0.23-1.24 s; test batch 256. Hardware and per-request latency: not reported.
  - Source: Section 3.6, Section 4.2 and Appendix B.3: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.25805v1#S3.SS6.SSS0.Px3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.25805v1#S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.25805v1#A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1
- **Results from**: Reported Tables 1/2/3/4: accuracy, full-test cost, ablations, sparsity groups. OneChord accuracy is five-run mean/SD; baselines use common splits, but borrowed-versus-rerun provenance is not reported.
  - Source: Tables 1-4 and Appendix B.2-B.3: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.25805v1#S3.T1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.25805v1#S3.T2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.25805v1#S4.T3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.25805v1#S4.T4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.25805v1#A2.SS2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.25805v1#A2.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1

### Related

- id: sprint; relation: competitor; note: SPRINT adds normalized SID/item evidence; OneChord learns and distills the fusion.; where: OneChord v1, Section 2 and Table 1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.25805v1#S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1; https://arxiv.org/html/2610.25805v1#S3.T1.
- id: rpg; relation: competitor; note: RPG is compared for full-catalog accuracy and complete-test generation cost.; where: OneChord v1, Tables 1-2: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.25805v1#S3.T1; https://arxiv.org/html/2610.25805v1#S3.T2.

## OneLatent

- Page: pages/papers/onelatent.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: V. Efficiency
- Stage: Training
- Representation: MM; Tokenization: R-KM; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: Multi-task NTP; Inference: Beam
- TL;DR: OneLatent compresses explicit chain-of-thought into learnable latent tokens through multi-view teacher traces, staged alignment, and curriculum post-training, instead of generating long reasoning traces at inference.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 2

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Kuaishou LLM-Rec advertising and seven-day industrial local-services logs. Deduplicate user-item interactions by strongest feedback; remove samples lacking profile/target SID and history items lacking SIDs.
  - Source: Section 4.1.1 and Appendix A.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.30675v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.30675v1#A1.SS2.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.30675v1#A1.SS2.p4
- **Split**: Allocation rule: not reported. SFT/CoT/test counts: industrial 100063/59113/20393; public 60000/30000/10000. Conversion targets use at most 50 preceding interactions.
  - Source: Table 1 and Appendix A.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.30675v1#S4.T1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.30675v1#A1.SS2.p3
- **Candidates**: not reported
  - Source: Section 4.1.3 gives generation metrics without a full-catalog/sampled candidate protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.30675v1#S4.SS1.SSS3.p1
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined.
  - Source: Sections 4.1.1 and Appendix A.2 define no unseen-item evaluation: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.30675v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.30675v1#A1.SS2
- **SID**: Multimodal Res-Kmeans, 3 levels x 1024 codes; collision handling: not reported.
  - Source: Section 3.3.1 and Table 10: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.30675v1#S3.SS3.SSS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.30675v1#A1.T10
- **Inference budget**: vLLM beam search; SID/ID Hit@1/16/32/64; three fixed latent tokens, no rationale decoding. 872-instance test: total 3.17 s, 274.29 QPS. Beam width, hardware, inference batch size: not reported.
  - Source: Sections 3.4.3, 4.1.3, 4.4.2 and Table 7: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.30675v1#S3.SS4.SSS3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.30675v1#S4.SS1.SSS3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.30675v1#S4.SS4.SSS2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.30675v1#S4.T7
- **Results from**: Reported Tables 2/3/7/9: main, matched-size scaling, efficiency, online A/B. Table 2's final gains compare matched Think-OR, not strongest baseline; baseline borrowed/rerun provenance not reported.
  - Source: Tables 2/3/7/9 and Section 4.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.30675v1#S4.T2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.30675v1#S4.T3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.30675v1#S4.T7 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.30675v1#S4.T9 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.30675v1#S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1

## OneLive

- Page: pages/papers/onelive.md
- Venue: KDD’26 ADS
- Problem: VI. Generalization
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text+Img+Audio+CF; Tokenization: R-KM; Backbone: Lazy Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP → RL; Inference: Beam
- TL;DR: OneLive adapts generative recommendation to live streaming with a dynamic residual-quantization tokenizer, time-aware gated attention, a decoder-only generator with Sequential MTP, and multi-objective alignment.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Kuaishou live-streaming logs over nearly two months: 400M users, 3M authors, billions of long-view/click interactions. Filtering rules not reported.
  - Source: Appendix B.1.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.08612v1#A2.SS1.SSS1.p1
- **Split**: Last day test, earlier dates training; validation allocation not reported. Online A/B observed nearly one month on Kuaishou/Kuaishou Lite; traffic allocation not reported.

  - Source: Introduction and Appendix C.2 specify live eligibility/generated-list metrics, not a sampled-negative protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.08612v1#S1.p5 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.08612v1#A3.SS2.p1
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Collaborative post-alignment and author SID updates use real-time signals; test-author exposure in tokenizer training not reported.
  - Source: Appendix B.1 defines no item holdout: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.08612v1#A2.SS1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.08612v1#S2.SS1.SSS1.p3
- **SID**: Res-Kmeans: 3 levels x 8192 codes. Collision rates measured; collision disambiguation not reported.
  - Source: Section 2.1.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.08612v1#S2.SS1.SSS2.p2
- **Inference budget**: HR/MRR@64/128; RL beam-top settings 64/256. L20 profiling: MTP graph latency mean/P99 2.25/3.62 ms (3 layers), 2.97/5.04 ms (6 layers); QPS gains 31.8%/62.0%. Main beam width and inference batch size not reported.
  - Source: Section 3.1.2 and Tables 4/5: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.08612v1#S3.SS1.SSS2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.08612v1#S3.T4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.08612v1#S3.T5
- **Results from**: Original Table 2: offline long-view/click comparisons on shared industrial logs; Tables 3-5: ablations/serving; Table 6: online A/B.
  - Source: Table 2 and Sections 3.1/3.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.08612v1#S2.T2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.08612v1#S3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.08612v1#S3.SS2.p1

## OneLoc

- Page: pages/papers/oneloc.md
- Venue: arXiv’25
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Representation
- Representation: Text+Img+Geo†; Tokenization: R-KM; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP → DPO; Inference: Beam
- TL;DR: OneLoc extends end-to-end generative recommendation to local-life videos by adding geographic information to tokenization, encoder attention, and a decoder prompt, and by DPO with geographic and GMV rewards.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: KuaiLLSR: eight days of uniformly sampled Kuaishou local-life-service short-video interactions, with 60 million users, 900,000 videos, and 440 million interactions; additional filtering rules not reported. Foursquare NYC: 1,042 users, 36,359 POIs, 212,347 interactions; Tokyo: 2,187 users, 59,472 POIs, 545,301 interactions. The public subsets use LibCity preprocessing to filter users and POIs; numerical filtering thresholds not reported.
  - Source: Section 4.1.1 and Table 2 identify the original industrial/public datasets and preprocessing, without numerical LibCity filter thresholds; https://arxiv.org/html/2508.14646v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2508.14646v1#S4.T2.
- **Split**: KuaiLLSR: streaming training on the first seven days and evaluation on the final day. NYC and Tokyo: each user's check-ins are sorted chronologically, with interaction sequences split 80%/10%/10% for training/validation/testing.
  - Source: Section 4.1.1 states streaming seven-day training plus next-day evaluation and the public 80/10/10 sequence split; https://arxiv.org/html/2508.14646v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1.
- **Candidates**: not reported
  - Source: Offline metrics do not disclose full-catalog versus sampled evaluation, and the online statement of identical candidate pools does not determine their size; https://arxiv.org/html/2508.14646v1#S4.SS1.SSS3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2508.14646v1#S5.p1.
- **Visibility**: not reported
  - Source: The paper claims cold-start benefits but does not define generator/tokenizer visibility for a cold-start evaluation; https://arxiv.org/html/2508.14646v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2508.14646v1#S5.p2.
- **SID**: 3 layers x 8,192 codes per layer, using geo-aware residual K-means; collision handling not reported.
  - Source: Sections 2.2 and 4.1.4 specify three residual-K-means layers of 8,192 codes, but no SID collision-resolution rule; https://arxiv.org/html/2508.14646v1#S2.SS2.p1, https://arxiv.org/html/2508.14646v1#S2.SS2.p3, and https://arxiv.org/html/2508.14646v1#S4.SS1.SSS4.p1.
- **Inference budget**: Production serving uses beam search on NVIDIA A10 GPUs, followed by SID-to-video mapping, GMV scoring, rule-based filtering, and top-K output. Beam width and output K not reported. Dynamic batching, mixed precision, KV caching, and TensorRT are used; numerical inference batch size and latency not reported.
  - Source: Section 3 gives serving hardware and optimizations but no numerical beam width, output K, batch size, or latency; the A800 hardware in Section 4.1.4 is for training; https://arxiv.org/html/2508.14646v1#S3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2508.14646v1#S4.SS1.SSS4.p1.
- **Results from**: Table 1: offline Recall/NDCG at K=5, 10, and 20 on KuaiLLSR, NYC, and Tokyo. Table 3 and Figures 4-5: module/reward ablations. Table 4 and Section 5: one-week online A/B test with 10% treatment traffic, compared with the production multi-stage system.
  - Source: Main offline comparisons and online outcomes are in Tables 1 and 4, with module ablations in Table 3 and Figures 4-5; https://arxiv.org/html/2508.14646v1#S2.T1, https://arxiv.org/html/2508.14646v1#S4.T3, https://arxiv.org/html/2508.14646v1#S4.F4, https://arxiv.org/html/2508.14646v1#S4.F5, https://arxiv.org/html/2508.14646v1#S5.p1, and https://arxiv.org/html/2508.14646v1#S5.T4.

### Related

- id: onerec; relation: predecessor; note: OneRec establishes unified generative retrieval and ranking with preference alignment, while OneLoc develops this direction for local-life video recommendation through geographic modeling and geographic/GMV rewards.; where: OneLoc v1, Section 6.2 explicitly cites Deng et al. (2025), OneRec arXiv:2502.18965, for unified generation and preference alignment: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.14646v1#S6.SS2.p1; Section 2 describes OneLoc's geographic modules and rewards: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.14646v1#S2.p1.
- id: tiger; relation: competitor; note: TIGER is an evaluated generative baseline using RQ-VAE identifiers; OneLoc uses geo-aware residual-K-means identifiers together with geographic sequence modeling and neighborhood prompts.; where: OneLoc v1, Section 4.1.2 identifies TIGER as a baseline: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.14646v1#S4.SS1.SSS2.p1; Table 1 reports its comparison with OneLoc: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.14646v1#S2.T1; Sections 2 and 2.2 describe OneLoc's added geographic mechanisms: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.14646v1#S2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2508.14646v1#S2.SS2.p1.
- id: gnpr-sid; relation: competitor; note: GNPR-SID is an evaluated next-POI baseline with geographic semantic identifiers; OneLoc extends geographic modeling into attention, neighborhood prompting, and rewards for local-life video consumption.; where: OneLoc v1, Section 1 explains the geographic-modeling difference: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.14646v1#S1.p2, https://arxiv.org/html/2508.14646v1#S1.p3, and https://arxiv.org/html/2508.14646v1#S1.p4; Table 1 directly compares GNPR-SID and OneLoc: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.14646v1#S2.T1.

### Notes

## At a Glance

Key Findings: In a one-week online A/B test on 10% of traffic, OneLoc reports GMV +21.016% and order volume +17.891% against the production multi-stage pipeline (Sec. 5, Table 4).
Limitation: The paper does not state that KuaiLLSR is released, and it does not report how SID collisions are handled (Sec. 4.1.1, Sec. 2.2).

### 1. Why This Paper Matters

In Kuaishou's local-life service, each recommended video is linked to a store location, so a recommendation must match both the user's interest and the user's real-time location (Abstract). The authors state that end-to-end generative recommenders such as OneRec had not yet been built for this setting (Abstract). OneLoc adds geographic information to the tokenizer, the encoder, and the decoder, and aligns the generator with a geographic reward and a GMV reward. LGSID and GeoGR, two other POI papers in the same matrix cell, also add geographic signals in the Representation stage (`Text+Geo+CF`).

> "The first challenge is how to make full use of geographic information. The second challenge is how to balance multiple objectives, including user interests, the distance between user and stores, and some other business objectives." (Abstract)

### 2. How It Works

#### Overview

```
Video content + location context (GeoHash block: coordinates, brand, category)
  │
  ▼  multimodal LLM → one fused item embedding
Geo-aware SID (q1, q2, q3) from 3-level residual k-means, 8,192 codes per level
  │
  ▼  encoder: watch / click / pay sequences, geo-aware self-attention (GA-Attn)
User representation
  │
  ▼  decoder: neighbor-aware prompt e^s, then the SID tokens; next-token prediction
Pre-trained generator θ0
  │
  ▼  beam search → geographic and GMV rewards → preference pairs → DPO
Aligned generator
```

#### Step 1: Geo-Aware Semantic IDs

Each video $`v`$ is assigned a location $`l`$. The location is a GeoHash block with context information such as coordinates, brand, and category (Sec. 2.1). OneLoc follows OneRec and builds SIDs with residual k-means. The input to the first level is one embedding that a multimodal large language model extracts from the video content and the location context.

> "To inject geographic information, each residual $`r^{0}_{i}`$ in the initial residual set $`\mathcal{R}^{0}`$ is represented as an embedding of video content and location context information, extracted by a multimodal large language model." (Sec. 2.2)

At each level $`i`$, k-means on the residuals builds the codebook, and each residual moves to its nearest centroid (Eq. 1–3):

```math
\mathcal{C}^{i} = \mathrm{KMeans}(\mathcal{R}^{i}, N_c), \qquad q^{i}_{j} = \arg\min_{k} \left\| c^{i}_{k} - r^{i}_{j} \right\|, \qquad r^{i+1}_{j} = r^{i}_{j} - c^{i}_{q^{i}_{j}}
```

where:
- $`\mathcal{R}^{i}`$ is the set of residuals at level $`i`$, and $`r^{i}_{j}`$ is the residual of item $`j`$;
- $`\mathcal{C}^{i} = \{c^{i}_{k}\}`$ is the level-$`i`$ codebook of $`N_c`$ centroids;
- $`q^{i}_{j}`$ is the $`i`$-th token of the SID of item $`j`$.

OneLoc uses 3 levels with 8,192 clusters each (Sec. 2.2, Sec. 4.1.4). Geographic information enters only through the fused embedding; there are no separate geographic tokens.

#### Step 2: Geo-Aware Self-Attention in the Encoder

The encoder reads the user's watch, click, and purchase sequences (Eq. 4). Each behavior $`i`$ has a fused embedding $`z_i`$, built by an MLP from its video ID, location ID, and location context embeddings, and a location context embedding $`e^{lc}_i`$ (Eq. 5–7).

> "GA-Attn module is proposed to capture relevant behaviors from the user's interaction history according to the user's real-time location." (Sec. 2.3.3)

GA-Attn adds a location context similarity to the attention scores (Eq. 11–12), then scales each output row with a gate computed from the user's real-time location (Eq. 13–14):

```math
A = \mathrm{Softmax}\left( (Z W_q)(Z W_k)^{\top} / \sqrt{d} + E^{lc} (E^{lc})^{\top} \right), \qquad \widetilde{O} = A (Z W_v) W_o
```

```math
g_i = 2 \cdot \mathrm{Sigmoid}\left( \mathrm{MLP}\left( \mathrm{Concat}(e^{lc}_u, E^{lc}_{i*}) \right) \right), \qquad O_{i*} = g_i\, \widetilde{O}_{i*}
```

where:
- $`Z`$ is the sequence of fused behavior embeddings $`z_i`$, and $`E^{lc}`$ is the sequence of location context embeddings;
- $`W_q, W_k, W_v, W_o`$ are the query, key, value, and output matrices;
- $`e^{lc}_u`$ is the context embedding of the user's real-time location $`l_u`$;
- $`g_i \in (0, 2)`$ scales the $`i`$-th output row.

Each encoder block applies GA-Attn and a feed-forward network, both with RMSNorm and residual connections (Eq. 8–10).

#### Step 3: Neighbor-Aware Prompt and Next-Token Prediction

The decoder starts from a prompt that summarizes the area around the user.

> "In local life service, it is vital to model location contexts surrounding the user, such as surrounding brands, bestselling products, etc. Thus, we use cross-attention to capture the surrounding information." (Sec. 2.4.1)

OneLoc takes the context embeddings of the 8 locations around $`l_u`$ as $`E^{s}`$ and computes one prompt embedding $`e^{s} = \mathrm{CrossAttn}(e^{lc}_u, E^{s})`$, with $`e^{lc}_u`$ as the query (Eq. 15). The decoder input is $`H^{0} = \{e^{s}, e_{q^1_t}, e_{q^2_t}, e_{q^3_t}\}`$ (Eq. 19). Each decoder block has causal self-attention, cross-attention to the encoder output, and a feed-forward network (Eq. 16–18). The output at the prompt predicts the first SID token, the output at the first token predicts the second, and so on:

```math
\hat{y}^{j} = \mathrm{Softmax}\left( \mathrm{MLP}(H^{K}_{j-1}) \right) \in \mathbb{R}^{N_c}, \qquad \mathcal{L}_{ntp} = \sum_{j=1}^{3} -\log \hat{y}^{j}_{q^{j}_{t}}
```

where $`H^{K}_{j-1}`$ is the last-layer decoder output at position $`j-1`$, and $`q^{j}_{t}`$ is the $`j`$-th token of the target SID (Eq. 20–21, Sec. 2.4.2).

#### Step 4: Geographic and GMV Rewards with DPO

Next-token prediction only fits the videos that the previous system exposed (Sec. 2.5). OneLoc therefore defines two rewards. The geographic reward is the inverse distance within a threshold (Eq. 22), and the GMV reward is the output of a GMV scoring model (Eq. 23):

```math
R^{geo}(v, l_u) = \begin{cases} 0 & \text{if } \mathrm{Dis}(v, l_u) \gt D, \\ 1 / \mathrm{Dis}(v, l_u) & \text{otherwise}, \end{cases} \qquad R^{gmv}(v, S, l_u) = \mathrm{GMV}(v, S, l_u)
```

> "The geographic reward signal is proposed to encourage generating videos nearby and thus a closer video would get a higher reward" (Sec. 2.5.1)

For each training sample, the pre-trained model generates $`N`$ videos by beam search (Eq. 24). OneLoc computes both rewards for each video and pairs the video with the highest reward (positive) and the one with the lowest reward (negative) (Sec. 2.5.2). A new model $`\theta_{i+1}`$, initialized from $`\theta_i`$, is trained on these pairs together with next-token prediction:

```math
\mathcal{L}_{dpo} = -\log \sigma\left( \beta \log \frac{p_{\theta_{i+1}}(Q_p \mid S, l_u)}{p_{\theta_{i}}(Q_p \mid S, l_u)} - \beta \log \frac{p_{\theta_{i+1}}(Q_n \mid S, l_u)}{p_{\theta_{i}}(Q_n \mid S, l_u)} \right), \qquad \mathcal{L} = \mathcal{L}_{ntp} + \lambda \mathcal{L}_{dpo}
```

where:
- $`Q_p`$ and $`Q_n`$ are the SIDs of the positive and negative videos;
- the previous iterate $`\theta_i`$ serves as the reference model;
- $`\sigma`$ is the sigmoid function, and $`\lambda = 0.05`$ (Sec. 4.1.4).

Eq. 25 in v1 is printed without $`\sigma`$; the form above follows standard DPO.

```python
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F

def ga_attn(Z, E_lc, e_u, Wq, Wk, Wv, Wo, gate_mlp):
    """
    Z:        [T, d] fused behavior embeddings z_i (Eq. 6)
    E_lc:     [T, d] location context embeddings of the behaviors (Eq. 7)
    e_u:      [d]    context embedding of the user's real-time location
    gate_mlp: maps [T, 2d] -> [T, 1]
    """
    d = Z.size(-1)
    A = torch.softmax((Z @ Wq) @ (Z @ Wk).T / d ** 0.5 + E_lc @ E_lc.T, dim=-1)        # Eq. 11, [T, T]
    O = A @ (Z @ Wv) @ Wo                                                               # Eq. 12, [T, d]
    g = 2 * torch.sigmoid(gate_mlp(torch.cat([e_u.expand_as(E_lc), E_lc], dim=-1)))     # Eq. 13, [T, 1]
    return g * O                                                                        # Eq. 14

def oneloc_loss(ntp_loss, logp_new_pos, logp_old_pos, logp_new_neg, logp_old_neg, beta, lam=0.05):
    """Sequence log-probabilities of the positive and negative SIDs; old = previous iterate theta_i."""
    margin = beta * ((logp_new_pos - logp_old_pos) - (logp_new_neg - logp_old_neg))
    return ntp_loss + lam * (-F.logsigmoid(margin).mean())                             # Eq. 25-26
```

Simplifications: The code shows one attention head and leaves out RMSNorm, the feed-forward network, and the residual connections of each block. It takes the projection matrices, the gate MLP, and the log-probabilities as inputs, and it does not build preference pairs or run beam search.

### 3. Experimental Findings

- Foursquare: OneLoc outperforms the baselines in Table 1, which include TIGER and GNPR-SID, on the NYC and Tokyo subsets (Table 1).

  > "Similarly, on the Foursquare global dataset, it attains an average performance boost of 13.18% in Recall@5 and 16.34% in NDCG@5." (Sec. 4.2)

- Online A/B test: OneLoc reports GMV +21.016%, order volume +17.891%, and new local-service buyers +23.027%, with p < 0.01 under two-tailed t-tests (Sec. 5, Table 4).

  > "In this experiment, 10% of the traffic was allocated to the treatment group using the end-to-end OneLoc system, while the control group retained the production-level multi-stage recommendation pipeline" (Sec. 5)

- Ablations: the study covers the neighbor-aware prompt, geo-aware self-attention, and the two rewards (Sec. 4.3, Fig. 4, Table 3, Fig. 5). It measures Recall and NDCG, and adds GMV for the rewards. The authors report lower scores for every ablated variant than for the full model. The paper has no ablation of the geo-aware SID.

### 4. Limitations & Critical Analysis

**Stated by the authors.** The paper states no limitations of OneLoc. The conclusion names two directions for future work: scaling laws of model size and sequence length, and RL methods adapted to local-life services (Sec. 7).

**Our analysis.**

- Location enters the SID only through the fused embedding before residual k-means (`Text+Img+Geo†`), so no SID position is tied to geography. LGSID uses geographic indexing with residual quantization (`Geo-Idx+RQ`), and LGRID uses `DSRQ`; both are in the same matrix cell.
- The paper does not state how the two rewards are combined when it ranks the candidates for a preference pair (Sec. 2.5.2).
- The paper does not state that KuaiLLSR or the GMV scoring model is released, and the online test runs on Kuaishou traffic. Only the Foursquare results can be reproduced from public data (Sec. 4.1.1, Sec. 5).
- The paper does not report SID collision handling, the beam width, or the evaluation candidate protocol (Sec. 2.2, Sec. 3, Sec. 4.1.3).
- The v1 front matter still carries template placeholders for the DOI and the conference, so the publication venue is unconfirmed.

## OneMall

- Page: pages/papers/onemall.md
- Venue: CIKM’26
- Problem: Paradigms, Systems and Benchmarks
- Stage: No single stage
- Representation: Text+Img+CF; Tokenization: R-KM+FSQ; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: (NTP + Ctr.) → RL; Inference: Beam
- TL;DR: OneMall unifies product-card, short-video, and live-streaming e-commerce in one generator, with a business-aware tokenizer, Query-Former and sparse MoE layers, and a ranking model as reinforcement learning reward.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 2

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Kuaishou product-card, short-video, and live-streaming logs; dates/sample counts not reported. Tokenizer: 70M product-product pairs (<=40 occurrences/item), 12M video-product pairs from long views 1-5 minutes before product clicks, excluding News/Comedy/Dance/Film-TV/Selfie videos and downsampling frequent products/same-user pairs.
  - Source: Sections 3.1.1 and 4: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.21770v1#S3.SS1.SSS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2601.21770v1#S4.p1
- **Split**: Offline train/validation/test allocation not reported; simulation replays online requests. Online A/B duration and traffic allocation not reported.
  - Source: Sections 4.2/4.3 describe replay and online tests, not a data split: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.21770v1#S4.SS2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2601.21770v1#S4.SS3.p1
- **Candidates**: not reported
  - Source: Section 4 evaluates generated top-K retrieval, without full-catalog/sampled-negative specification: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.21770v1#S4.p1
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Frozen codebooks can tokenize new uploads; encoder/tokenizer exposure to test items not reported.
  - Source: Sections 2.2/4 define no unseen-item evaluation protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.21770v1#S2.SS2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2601.21770v1#S4
- **SID**: Two Res-Kmeans levels plus a 4096-code FSQ final level; residual-only baseline uses 3x4096. Final variant's residual codebook sizes not separately stated. FSQ reduces collisions; residual collision resolution not reported.
  - Source: Sections 3.1.3/4.5: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.21770v1#S3.SS1.SSS3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2601.21770v1#S4.SS5.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2601.21770v1#S4.SS5.p2
- **Inference budget**: Deployed 0.5B-total/0.1B-active model; HR@50/100/500. Serving beam width, hardware, inference batch size, latency not reported; beam 768 is RL training candidate generation.
  - Source: Sections 4/4.2/4.4: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.21770v1#S4.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2601.21770v1#S4.SS2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2601.21770v1#S4.SS4.p1
- **Results from**: Original Table 1: scaling; Table 2: replay versus equally sized SASRec/TIGER with identical input features; Table 3: online A/B; Tables 4/5: RL/tokenizer ablations.
  - Source: Sections 4.2/4.3 and Tables 1-5: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.21770v1#S4.SS2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2601.21770v1#S4.T2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2601.21770v1#S4.T3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2601.21770v1#S3.T1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2601.21770v1#S4.T4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2601.21770v1#S4.T5

## OneRec

- Page: pages/papers/onerec.md
- Venue: arXiv’25
- Problem: Paradigms, Systems and Benchmarks
- Stage: No single stage
- Representation: Text+CF; Tokenization: R-KM; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP → DPO; Inference: Sess. Beam
- TL;DR: OneRec replaces the retrieve-and-rank cascade with one encoder-decoder generator using sparse MoE, generates whole sessions of videos, and aligns preferences by iterative DPO with a reward model.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Kuaishou short-video interaction logs; training sessions are built from high-quality user sessions (a session is 5-10 videos per request; the listed criteria include at least 5 videos actually watched, total watch time above a threshold whose value is not given, and interactions such as liking, collecting, or sharing). Dataset size: not reported.
  - Source: Industrial Kuaishou data and session construction: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.18965v1#S3.SS2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2502.18965v1#S4.p1; no dataset statistics found.
- **Split**: Offline: evaluation on a randomly sampled set of test cases in each iteration; the train/test construction is not reported. Online: A/B test on Kuaishou's main-page video scenarios with 1% of main traffic.
  - Source: Offline evaluation on randomly sampled test cases: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.18965v1#S5.SS1.SSS3.p1; online: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.18965v1#S5.SS5.p1.
- **Candidates**: n/a for ranking metrics: generated sessions are scored by a pre-trained reward model (session watch time, view, follow, and like probabilities), not ranked against a candidate set.
  - Source: Reward-model evaluation of generated sessions: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.18965v1#S5.SS1.SSS3.p1.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined.
  - Source: No unseen-item protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.18965v1#S5.SS1.SSS3.p1.
- **SID**: 3 levels x 8,192 codes from multi-level balanced residual K-means over multimodal video embeddings aligned with user behavior; balanced K-means equalizes cluster sizes. Collision handling: not reported.
  - Source: Balanced residual K-means, L=3 x K=8192: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.18965v1#S3.SS1.p2, https://arxiv.org/html/2502.18965v1#S3.SS1.p3, https://arxiv.org/html/2502.18965v1#S5.SS1.SSS1.p1; no collision rule found.
- **Inference budget**: Beam search with beam size 128 (also used to generate 128 responses per user for DPO); KV-cache decoding with float16 quantization; MoE with 24 experts, 2 active (about 13% of parameters active at inference). Training on NVIDIA A800 GPUs; serving hardware, batch size, and latency: not reported.
  - Source: Beam size 128 online and for DPO sampling; KV cache and float16: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.18965v1#S4.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2502.18965v1#S5.SS1.SSS1.p1.
- **Results from**: Table 1 (offline reward-model metrics versus pointwise, listwise, and preference-alignment baselines); Figure 4 (DPO sample ratio); Table 2 (online A/B: OneRec-1B+IPA +1.68% total watch time, +6.56% average view duration).
  - Source: Offline: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.18965v1#S3.T1; DPO ratio: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.18965v1#S5.F4; online: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.18965v1#S5.T2.

## 旧卡片说明

迁自 `d61aa6c:papers/onerec.md`。保留方法说明、实验叙述与局限；本轮只对照现有记录处理明确冲突，未重新逐句核查原论文。分类和规格以页面上方由记录生成的表格为准。

### OneRec：检索排序一体化生成式推荐

> OneRec 用生成模型直接产生推荐列表，并通过迭代偏好对齐替代传统的召回-排序级联。

### 研究动机与问题定义

级联系统把召回和排序拆开，模块目标不一致且存在信息损失。OneRec 将会话建模、候选选择和排序统一为列表生成，并研究如何使生成结果贴近真实偏好。

### TL;DR（核心摘要）

`会话历史 → SID列表目标 → 生成模型 → 推荐列表 → 偏好对齐`

模型以会话级物品列表作为训练目标，使用平衡聚类构造物品语义标识，并直接生成列表。训练后通过奖励反馈和迭代 DPO 逐步对齐列表质量；在线阶段生成的 SID 直接对应推荐物品。

### 输入与使用场景

| 方面 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| 使用信息 | 会话交互、物品标识和偏好反馈 |
| 信息融入位置 | 列表目标、生成输入和偏好训练 |
| 语义标识结构 | 列表中的多 token 序列 |
| 适用场景 | 工业会话推荐 |

### 方法设计

#### 3.1 会话级列表生成
OneRec 把单物品 next-item 目标扩展为 session-wise list generation。训练样本包含会话上下文和目标推荐列表，生成器按统一序列格式输出多个物品 SID，并在列表内部处理顺序与重复。

#### 3.2 生成器训练
模型采用编码器-解码器结构，以会话行为和物品标识作为条件。标识由平衡聚类构造，使不同物品在生成词表中具有较好的覆盖和可区分性。

#### 3.3 迭代偏好对齐
训练后使用奖励模型产生偏好信号，构造列表级偏好样本并进行 DPO。迭代过程不断用更新后的模型生成新样本，使生成列表逐步靠近业务偏好。

#### 3.4 系统部署
论文进一步设计线上生成、去重和服务流程，目标是用一个生成模型连接原本分离的召回与排序阶段。

### 实验结论

- OneRec 在论文报告的公开和工业设置中改善了生成式推荐效果。
- 列表级训练和偏好对齐均带来额外收益。

### 局限性与研究定位

#### 局限性
- 列表生成、去重和约束会增加推理工程复杂度。
- 动态物品、极端长尾和跨场景迁移仍需更多验证。

#### 研究定位
OneRec 的主要贡献是以生成列表统一召回与排序，适合放在“端到端工业生成式推荐”章节。

### 标签

`召回排序一体化` · `列表生成` · `偏好对齐` · `工业推荐`

### 架构图来源

*图源：原论文，图2。图片使用许可待核实。*
