- 使用场景：工业会话推荐。

## OneRec-Think

- Page: pages/papers/onerec-think.md
- Venue: arXiv’25
- Problem: III. SID–Model Alignment
- Stage: Training
- Representation: Text+Img+CF†; Tokenization: R-KM†; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP → RL; Inference: CoT
- TL;DR: OneRec-Think adds explicit in-text reasoning to OneRec-style generation through item-text alignment, reasoning scaffolding, and a recommendation reward for multiple valid targets, instead of implicit prediction alone.
- [Code](https://github.com/wangshy31/OneRec-Think)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Beauty, Toys, and Sports; users and items with fewer than 5 interactions are discarded. Industrial: Kuaishou short-video data with daily incremental training on about 20B tokens per day. Retained corpus sizes: not reported.
  - Source: Public datasets: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.11639v2#S5.SS1.p2; filtering and split: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.11639v2#A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1; industrial deployment: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.11639v2#S5.SS4.SSS2.Px1.p1.
- **Split**: Public: leave-one-out (allocation not restated beyond the label); training histories capped at 50 items. Online: one-week A/B test with a 1.29% traffic group.
  - Source: Leave-one-out and history cap: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.11639v2#A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1; online test: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.11639v2#S5.SS4.SSS2.Px1.p1.
- **Candidates**: not reported (full catalog versus sampled evaluation candidates); top-K lists from beam search with width 10.
  - Source: Metrics only: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.11639v2#S5.SS1.p2.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined.
  - Source: Standard split with no unseen-item protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.11639v2#A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.
- **SID**: Public: four-level hierarchical semantic IDs with 256 tokens per level (1,024 new tokens). Industrial: three levels x 8,192 itemic tokens (24,576 new tokens), plus item boundary tokens. The tokenizer algorithm is not restated; collision handling: not reported.
  - Source: Public 4 levels x 256; industrial 3 levels x 8,192: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.11639v2#A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2510.11639v2#S5.SS4.SSS1.p1; no collision rule found.
- **Inference budget**: Public: beam search with width 10 after the reasoning text (Qwen3-1.7B). Industrial: Think-Ahead serving generates the reasoning and the first two itemic tokens offline with Qwen-8B, then a real-time OneRec model completes the last token online; latency numbers: not reported. Daily training on a cluster of 80 GPUs.
  - Source: Beam width 10 for public evaluation: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.11639v2#A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1; Rollout-Beam reward with width K: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.11639v2#S4.SS3.p2; two-stage serving: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.11639v2#S4.SS4.p2; training cluster: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.11639v2#S5.SS4.SSS1.p1.
- **Results from**: Table 1 (Beauty, Toys, Sports versus sequential and generative baselines); Table 2 (alignment and reasoning ablation on Beauty); Table 3 (online A/B); Table 4 (user and video understanding BertScore).
  - Source: Public: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.11639v2#S4.T1; ablation: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.11639v2#S5.T2; online: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.11639v2#S5.T3; understanding benchmarks: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.11639v2#S5.T4.

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: competitor; note: TIGER generates the next itemic tokens directly; OneRec-Think first generates interleaved text-and-item reasoning and is rewarded with a beam-based signal.; where: OneRec-Think v2, baselines: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.11639v2#S5.SS1.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2510.11639v2#A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1; Table 1: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.11639v2#S4.T1.

## 旧卡片说明

迁自 `d61aa6c:papers/onerecthink.md`。保留方法说明、实验叙述与局限；本轮只对照现有记录处理明确冲突，未重新逐句核查原论文。分类和规格以页面上方由记录生成的表格为准。

### OneRec-Think：文本内推理生成式推荐

> OneRec-Think 在物品标识生成前加入用户偏好推理，并用多任务对齐和强化学习提升推荐质量与可解释性。

### 研究动机与问题定义

生成式推荐能够直接预测物品标识，但通常缺少可观察的偏好推理。OneRec-Think 试图让 LLM 在同一自回归过程中先形成理由，再生成目标 itemic token，同时兼顾工业响应速度。

### TL;DR（核心摘要）

`用户历史与itemic token → 多任务对齐 → 偏好理由 → 生成itemic token → 推荐物品`

框架包含 itemic alignment、reasoning activation 和 reasoning enhancement 三阶段。多任务预训练融合用户画像、序列偏好、物品描述生成和通用语言建模；随后从裁剪历史中引导理由生成，并用推荐奖励强化推理路径。Think-Ahead 架构将部分推理前置，最终 token 直接对应物品。

### 输入与使用场景

| 方面 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| 使用信息 | 用户行为、用户画像、物品文本和偏好反馈 |
| 信息融入位置 | itemic token 对齐、推理文本和奖励目标 |
| 语义标识结构 | 推理序列后接 itemic token 序列 |
| 适用场景 | 工业序列推荐和可解释推荐 |

### 方法设计

#### 4.1 多任务 Itemic 对齐预训练
OneRec-Think 将 itemic token 与文本 token 放进同一语言空间，训练用户画像、序列偏好、itemic dense captioning 和通用语言建模四类任务。Token warm-up 先学习 itemic embedding，再进行多任务联合整合。

#### 4.2 推理激活
为应对工业行为序列噪声，模型先从裁剪后的相关历史中生成偏好理由，再把这些理由蒸馏到原始行为上下文。推理目标不是独立解释，而是为后续 itemic token 生成提供中间偏好结构。

#### 4.3 推理增强
模型生成多条 reasoning rollout，并用推荐特定奖励比较目标一致性、路径质量和结果可靠性。强化学习进一步筛选能够导向有效 itemic token 的推理路径。

#### 4.4 Think-Ahead 部署架构
论文将部分推理工作前置或离线化，在线阶段快速读取增强后的上下文并生成目标 itemic token，从而在可解释性和工业响应时间之间折中。

### 实验结论

- OneRec-Think 在多个公开基准上报告了较强推荐表现。
- 三阶段训练分别改善语义对齐、推理激活和偏好一致性。
- Think-Ahead 在工业部署中报告了停留时长收益。

### 局限性与研究定位

#### 局限性
- 文本推理增加 token 数量和训练、推理成本。
- 推理奖励依赖用户行为代理信号，可能存在偏差。
- 复杂场景下的实时推理稳定性仍需更多公开验证。

#### 研究定位
OneRec-Think 将显式文本推理嵌入直接 itemic token 生成，适合放在“推理增强生成式推荐”章节。

### 相关资源

- [论文原文](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.11639)

### 标签

`文本内推理` · `多任务预训练` · `Think-Ahead` · `偏好强化学习`

*图源：原论文，图2。图片使用许可待核实。*

- 使用场景：工业推荐。

## OneRec-V2

- Page: pages/papers/onerec-v2.md
- Venue: arXiv’25
- Problem: V. Efficiency
- Stage: Backbone
- Representation: Text+Img+CF†; Tokenization: R-KM†; Backbone: Lazy Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP → RL; Inference: Beam
- TL;DR: OneRec-V2 replaces the OneRec encoder-decoder with a lazy decoder-only architecture that cuts sequence-encoding compute, and aligns with real user feedback through duration-aware reward shaping and adaptive ratio clipping.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 2

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Kuaishou impressions, August 10-14 2025, for streaming architecture experiments; Kuaishou and Kuaishou Lite feeds for online evaluation. Filtering and dataset sizes not reported.
  - Source: Sections 2.3/4: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20900v4#S2.SS3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20900v4#S4.p1
- **Split**: Offline holdout allocation not reported. Online: one week, 5% experimental traffic; V2 serves 25% of degraded traffic within that group (Appendix D wording). Separate 1% group disables caching and serves V2 for every request.
  - Source: Sections 2.3/4 and Appendix D: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20900v4#S2.SS3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20900v4#S4.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20900v4#A4.p1
- **Candidates**: not reported
  - Source: Sections 2.3/4 describe training loss and online tests without candidate-enumeration protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20900v4#S2.SS3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20900v4#S4
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Cold-start video-view metrics are reported, but subset criteria and tokenizer exposure are not reported.
  - Source: Sections 4/5 and Appendix D do not define a held-out unseen-item protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20900v4#S4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20900v4#A4.p2
- **SID**: 3 semantic tokens using the OneRec-V1 tokenizer; codebook sizes and collision handling not reported here.
  - Source: Section 2.2.2 Tokenizer: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20900v4#S2.SS2.SSS2.Px1.p1
- **Inference budget**: Online 1B model, context 3000, beam 512, L20 GPUs, latency 36ms, MFU 62%; inference batch size not reported.
  - Source: Section 4: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20900v4#S4.p1
- **Results from**: Original Tables 2-5: architecture/scaling; Tables 6-8: online alignment/deployment comparisons; Table 9: caching disabled. Online improvements are relative to OneRec-V1.
  - Source: Original Tables 2-8 and Appendix D Table 9: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20900v4#S2.T2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20900v4#S2.T5 and https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20900v4#S3.T6 and https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20900v4#S3.T8 and https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20900v4#A4.T9

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: alternative; note: Earlier generative retrieval contrasts with V2's lazy-decoder compute allocation.; where: OneRec-V2 v4, Introduction and Section 2.1, citing Rajput et al. (2023): https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20900v4#S1.p1; https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20900v4#S2.SS1.
- id: onerec-v2-quantized; relation: successor; note: Adds FP8 post-training quantization and an optimized inference stack.; where: Evidence from Quantized Inference for OneRec-V2 v1, Section 4.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.11486v1#S4.SS1.p1.

## OneRec-V2-Quantized

- Page: pages/papers/onerec-v2-quantized.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: V. Efficiency
- Stage: Inference
- Representation: Text+Img+CF†; Tokenization: R-KM†; Backbone: Lazy Dec-Only†; Tokenizer: Fixed†; Objective: NTP → RL†; Inference: FP8+RecoGEM
- TL;DR: OneRec-V2-Quantized applies low-precision floating-point post-training quantization and an optimized inference stack to OneRec-V2, whose weight and activation statistics resemble LLMs more than traditional recommenders.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 1

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Production single-column short-video recommendation; online evaluation on Kuaishou and Kuaishou Lite. Dataset dates, sizes and filtering not reported.
  - Source: Sections 5.1/5.3: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.11486v1#S5.SS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2603.11486v1#S5.SS3.p1
- **Split**: Offline split not reported; online A/B runs one week, traffic allocation not reported.
  - Source: Sections 5.1/5.3: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.11486v1#S5.SS1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2603.11486v1#S5.SS3.p1
- **Candidates**: not reported
  - Source: Section 5 evaluates serving performance and online engagement without a candidate protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.11486v1#S5
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined.
  - Source: Sections 4.1/5 define PTQ and serving tests, without an unseen-item protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.11486v1#S4.SS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2603.11486v1#S5
- **SID**: not reported
  - Source: Section 4.1 leaves the base model unchanged but does not specify SID construction: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.11486v1#S4.SS1.p1
- **Inference budget**: 4B fat-MoE, 0.5B active/token, batch 32. FP16 baseline versus FP8 Linear/MoE (Linear accumulation FP32): 139ms to 70ms mean latency; throughput 205 to 394, units not reported. GPU model, beam width and output K not reported.
  - Source: Sections 4.1/5.1/5.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.11486v1#S4.SS1.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2603.11486v1#S5.SS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2603.11486v1#S5.SS1.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2603.11486v1#S5.SS2.p2
- **Results from**: Original Section 5.2/Figure 3: FP16 versus combined infrastructure/FP8/operator optimization; Table 1: online quality. The full 49% latency reduction and 92% throughput gain include all three changes.
  - Source: Section 5.2/Figure 3 and Section 5.3/Table 1: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.11486v1#S5.SS2.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2603.11486v1#S5.F3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2603.11486v1#S5.T1

## PAD-Rec

- Page: pages/papers/pad-rec.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: V. Efficiency
- Stage: Inference
- Representation: Text+SID; Tokenization: RQ-VAE; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: Multi-task NTP†; Inference: Spec. Dec.
- TL;DR: PAD-Rec adds gated item-slot and draft-step position embeddings to the draft model of speculative decoding, instead of treating all Semantic ID draft tokens uniformly.
- [Code](https://github.com/Jiaju-Chen/PAD-Rec)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 4

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Beauty (12,101 items / 22,363 sequences), Instruments (9,922 / 24,772), Games (17,332 / 49,156), and Yelp (20,033 / 30,431). Users with fewer than 11 interactions are removed; each remaining user's 10 most recent items form the target list.
  - Source: Datasets and statistics: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.27747v1#S5.SS1.SSS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2604.27747v1#S5.T1; preprocessing: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.27747v1#S5.SS1.SSS1.p3.
- **Split**: User-level 8:1:1 split into training, validation, and test, so all interactions of a user fall in one partition; targets are each user's 10 most recent items.
  - Source: User-level 8:1:1 split: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.27747v1#S5.SS1.SSS1.p4.
- **Candidates**: n/a for candidate ranking: the model generates a 10-item list that is compared with the user's 10 most recent items (Recall@10, NDCG@10).
  - Source: List-wise recall against the 10-item ground-truth list: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.27747v1#S5.I4.i3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2604.27747v1#S5.I4.i4.p1.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Test users are held out from training (user-level split), while items are shared across splits.
  - Source: Test users are disjoint from training users; items are shared: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.27747v1#S5.SS1.SSS1.p4.
- **SID**: 4-level RQ-VAE semantic IDs over embeddings that integrate semantic and collaborative signals (following LETTER), with separator tokens between items; codebook size and collision handling: not reported.
  - Source: K=4 RQ-VAE codebooks following LETTER, separators between items: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.27747v1#S3.SS1.p3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2604.27747v1#S5.SS1.SSS1.p3.
- **Inference budget**: EAGLE-2-style tree speculative decoding with speculation depth 6 and tree width 10, at temperature 0 and 0.5; target LLM Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct (3B and 8B in scaling). Latency measured on NVIDIA RTX 3090 GPUs in fp16 with batch size 1 after three warm-up runs; Table 3 lists naive target-LLM latency (e.g. Beauty 693.55 at temp 0, units as in the table).
  - Source: Tree-based speculative decoding settings and timing protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.27747v1#S5.SS1.SSS4.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2604.27747v1#S5.SS1.SSS4.p3; baseline latency: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.27747v1#S5.T3.
- **Results from**: Table 2 (wall-clock speedup, accepted length, Recall@10, NDCG@10 versus EAGLE-2, HASS, FSPAD, GRIFFIN on four datasets); Table 3 (naive decoding latency); later tables and figures (ablations, model scaling, hyperparameters).
  - Source: Main: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.27747v1#S5.T2; latency: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.27747v1#S5.T3; ablations and hyperparameters in Section 5.

### Related

- id: lc-rec; relation: predecessor; note: PAD-Rec accelerates a list-wise LC-Rec target model with speculative decoding, adding item and step position embeddings to the draft head.; where: PAD-Rec v1, implementation on LC-Rec: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.27747v1#S5.SS1.SSS4.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2604.27747v1#S5.SS1.SSS1.p5.
- id: letter; relation: predecessor; note: PAD-Rec obtains its semantic IDs following LETTER's semantic-collaborative embeddings and RQ-VAE.; where: PAD-Rec v1, Section 3.1 and Section 5.1 follow reference [40], LETTER: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.27747v1#S3.SS1.p3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2604.27747v1#S5.SS1.SSS1.p3.
- id: atspeed; relation: alternative; note: AtSpeed also accelerates LLM-based generative recommendation with speculative decoding; PAD-Rec targets list-wise generation with position-aware drafts.; where: PAD-Rec v1, Sections 1 and 2.3 cite AtSpeed: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.27747v1#S1.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2604.27747v1#S2.SS3.p1; not a baseline in Table 2.
- id: specgr; relation: alternative; note: SpecGR uses speculative generation for inductive recommendation, while PAD-Rec speeds up decoding without changing the target model's outputs.; where: PAD-Rec v1, Section 2.3: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.27747v1#S2.SS3.p1.

### Notes

## 旧目录说明

迁自 `d61aa6c:README.md` 的条目说明，未沿用旧目录的收录分类。

在投机解码的草稿模型中加入 SID 位置信息，加速列表式生成。

## PCR-CA

- Page: pages/papers/pcr-ca.md
- Venue: KDD’26
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text+CF; Tokenization: PC-AE; Backbone: Disc.; Tokenizer: Joint; Objective: Discrim.; Inference: Scoring
- TL;DR: PCR-CA learns parallel codebook representations of app text, unlike hierarchical RQ-VAE, and aligns them contrastively with collaborative signals for CTR prediction on multiple-category apps.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 1

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Microsoft Store impression logs with click/install labels over several months; approximately 80K apps, click rate 6.148%; histories up to 50 interactions. Filtering rules not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.18166v1#S4.SS1.p1
- **Split**: Chronological: 340M training interactions and latest 10M validation samples. Table 2 calls evaluation the test set, but a separate test allocation is not reported. Online A/B lasts two weeks.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.18166v1#S4.SS1.p1 ; #S4.T2 ; #S4.T5
- **Candidates**: n/a for logged-impression CTR/AUC evaluation; candidate pool for top-10 diversity analysis not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.18166v1#S4.SS1.p1 ; #S4.SS1.p6 ; #S4.SS4.p2
- **Visibility**: Cold-start validation naturally includes apps/users unseen in CTR training. Unseen by CTR predictor only: PC-AE pretraining iterates over all 80K apps; no generative decoder is used.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.18166v1#S4.SS1.p1 ; #S4.SS1.p4
- **SID**: PC-AE: 4 parallel codebooks x 32 entries, 16-dimensional vectors, selecting/summing two nearest codes per book. Codebooks train jointly with CTR prediction after pretraining. Unique-ID collision resolution: n/a; codes supply predictive features.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.18166v1#S3.SS2.p3 ; #S3.SS2.p7 ; #S4.SS1.p2
- **Inference budget**: Discriminative scoring; beam n/a; top-10 lists for diversity. Simulated throughput: 120K candidate items/s versus base 150K/s on the same unspecified server. Inference hardware, batch size and request latency not reported; offline text embedding costs 22 ms/new app.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.18166v1#S4.SS4.p2 ; #S4.SS4.p3 ; #S4.SS4.p4
- **Results from**: Original Table 2: AUC by app-popularity bucket; Tables 3-4: ablations; Table 5: online A/B. SaviorRec is explicitly reimplemented; no baseline-result reuse stated.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.18166v1#S4.T2 ; #S4.T3 ; #S4.T4 ; #S4.T5 ; #S4.SS1.p2

### Related

- id: cost; relation: alternative; note: CoST uses residual vector quantization; PCR-CA replaces its hierarchy with parallel codebooks for multiple-category app features and CTR prediction.; where: PCR-CA v1, Introduction and Section 2.2, citing Yongchao Zhu et al. (2024): https://arxiv.org/html/2508.18166v1#S1.p4; https://arxiv.org/html/2508.18166v1#S2.SS2.p3.

## Pctx

- Page: pages/papers/pctx.md
- Venue: CIKM’26
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text+CF; Tokenization: RQ; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP; Inference: Beam+Agg.
- TL;DR: Pctx tokenizes each item with the user's interaction history as context, so the same item can receive different Semantic IDs for different users, instead of one static item-only mapping.
- [Code](https://github.com/YoungZ365/Pctx)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 4

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Reviews 2023: Musical Instruments, Industrial & Scientific, Video Games; exclude users/items with fewer than five interactions; chronological histories capped at 20 items.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.21276v1#S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1 ; #A3.SS1.p1
- **Split**: Per-user chronological leave-one-out: most recent item test, penultimate validation, remaining interactions training.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.21276v1#A3.SS3.p1
- **Candidates**: full catalog; full-ranking evaluation rather than negative sampling.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.21276v1#A3.SS3.p1
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Auxiliary DuoRec is pretrained on the same training data, and representative contexts come from training interactions; textual-tokenizer fitting exposure to test items not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.21276v1#S2.SS2.p1 ; #S2.SS2.SSS1.Px1.p1 ; #S2.SS2.SSS2.p1 ; #A3.SS3.p1
- **SID**: 3 x 256 residual semantic codes plus an auxiliary collision token of unreported vocabulary size; multiple context-conditioned SIDs/item. Same-item IDs differing only in collision token are merged; collision tokens distinguish different items. Main text names RQ-VAE; appendix specifies FAISS quantization.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.21276v1#S2.SS2.SSS2.Px1.p1 ; #S2.SS2.SSS2.Px2.p2 ; #A3.SS4.p1
- **Inference budget**: Beam decoding with aggregation of generated SID probabilities per item; Recall/NDCG@5/10. GR baseline beam 50; Pctx-specific beam width not separately reported. Inference hardware, batch size and latency not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.21276v1#S2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1 ; #A3.SS3.p1 ; #S3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1
- **Results from**: Table 1: Pctx experiments with most baseline rows (including TIGER/LETTER) copied from Zheng et al. (2025); other baselines reconstructed. Table 2: ablations; Table 3: ensemble comparisons; Table 6: explainability.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.21276v1#S3.T1 ; #S3.T2 ; #S3.T3 ; #A3.SS4.p1 ; #A4.T6

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: competitor; note: TIGER assigns static semantic IDs; Pctx conditions item tokenization on user context and aggregates probabilities across personalized IDs.; where: Pctx v1, Section 2.4 and Table 1; TIGER results are reused from prior work per Appendix C.4: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.21276v1#S2.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1; https://arxiv.org/html/2510.21276v1#S3.T1; https://arxiv.org/html/2510.21276v1#A3.SS4.p1.
- id: letter; relation: competitor; note: LETTER injects collaborative information and diversity constraints into item quantization; Pctx adds history-conditioned user interpretations.; where: Pctx v1, Appendix C.2 and Table 1; LETTER results are reused per Appendix C.4: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.21276v1#A3.SS2.p1; https://arxiv.org/html/2510.21276v1#S3.T1; https://arxiv.org/html/2510.21276v1#A3.SS4.p1.
- id: actionpiece; relation: competitor; note: ActionPiece uses adjacent action context; Pctx extends tokenization context to the full user interaction history.; where: Pctx v1, Section 2.4 and Table 1: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.21276v1#S2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1; https://arxiv.org/html/2510.21276v1#S3.T1.
- id: lc-rec; relation: alternative; note: LC-Rec is discussed as static tokenization under a universal item-similarity assumption; Pctx maps an item to personalized IDs under different user contexts.; where: Pctx v1, Section 2.4: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.21276v1#S2.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.

## PFA

- Page: pages/papers/pfa.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: V. Efficiency
- Stage: Inference
- Representation: –; Tokenization: –; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: –; Objective: –; Inference: Beam
- TL;DR: PFA keeps full attention at the first decoding step, then reuses a shared importance ranking across beams to shrink the attended history at later steps, accelerating long-sequence generative decoding.
- [Code](https://anonymous.4open.science/r/PFA-review-088D)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 2

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon 2023 Kindle Store (rating>=4, users>=128 positives); Tmall IJCAI-15 clicks; industrial advertising clicks. Click data retain earliest repeated user-item event; public items require >=5 training-instance occurrences, removing invalid users.
  - Source: Section 4.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.39273v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.39273v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1
- **Split**: Per-user chronological approximately 90%/5%/5% training/validation/test; rolling-history sliding windows use only behaviors preceding each target; deterministic public split sampling.
  - Source: Section 4.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.39273v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1
- **Candidates**: not reported
  - Source: Section 4.1 metrics do not specify full-catalog versus sampled evaluation: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.39273v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1
- **Visibility**: warm; retained public items have >=5 training-instance occurrences. Industrial item exposure is not separately reported.
  - Source: Section 4.1 public filtering and split: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.39273v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1
- **SID**: Four codebooks: 128 codes/position on Kindle/Tmall, 300 on Industry. Tokenizer construction and collision handling: not reported.
  - Source: Section 4.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.39273v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px5.p1
- **Inference budget**: Beam 100; 5 L20 GPUs, BF16, batch 512/GPU; k=256, retention=0.5; Recall/NDCG@5/10. Encoder+decoding latency: Kindle18/Industry62 ms/batch/GPU, excluding loading/embedding lookup; online RT11 ms.
  - Source: Section 4.1, Section 4.5 and Tables 4/7: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.39273v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px6.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.39273v1#S4.SS5 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.39273v1#S4.T4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.39273v1#S4.T7
- **Results from**: Reported Tables 3/4/5/6/7: main comparison, ablations, selection timing, token budgets, seven-day online A/B. Online control/treatment histories differ (128/512); offline comparisons hold efficient-method token budgets equal.
  - Source: Tables 3-7: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.39273v1#S4.T3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.39273v1#S4.T4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.39273v1#S4.T5 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.39273v1#S4.T6 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.39273v1#S4.T7 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.39273v1#S4.SS6.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.39273v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: competitor; note: TIGER is the standard generative full-history baseline.; where: PFA v1, Section 4.1 and Table 3: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.39273v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1; https://arxiv.org/html/2610.39273v1#S4.T3.
- id: dualgr; relation: competitor; note: DualGR retrieves coarse-SID history buckets; PFA shares and reuses an attention-derived history ranking.; where: PFA v1, Sections 4.1/5 and Table 3: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.39273v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1; https://arxiv.org/html/2610.39273v1#S5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1; https://arxiv.org/html/2610.39273v1#S4.T3.

## PinGER

- Page: pages/papers/pinger.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: V. Efficiency
- Stage: Backbone
- Representation: Text+Img+CF; Tokenization: RQ-VAE; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: –; Objective: NTP → DPO; Inference: Div. C-Beam
- TL;DR: PinGER interleaves Semantic ID and dense tokens with an asymmetric attention mask so serving uses one token per item, and steers retrieval by goal conditioning, reinforcement learning, and diversity penalties.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Pinterest session-centric UniPinRec data: historical cross-surface actions paired with target-surface session engagements; session sampling reflects traffic. Filtering rules: not reported.
  - Source: Section 5.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.33435v1#S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1
- **Split**: Evaluation uses held-out users in a later, non-overlapping window disjoint from training. Window dates, allocation ratios and validation split: not reported.
  - Source: Section 5.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.33435v1#S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1
- **Candidates**: full catalog: generated identifiers resolve against the full production corpus.
  - Source: Section 5.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.33435v1#S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Users are held out; fresh-content analysis uses Pins created within 28 days, without specified generator/tokenizer item holdouts.
  - Source: Section 5.1 and online fresh-content analysis: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.33435v1#S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.33435v1#S5.SS3.SSS1.p1
- **SID**: RQ-VAE 5x2048; content-only PinCLIP input, OmniSage engagement distillation. Index resolves shared-SID item lists; insufficient leaves fall back to coarser prefixes, with round-robin interleaving across beams.
  - Source: Sections 3.2 and 4.3: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.33435v1#S3.SS2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.33435v1#S4.SS3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.33435v1#S4.SS3.p2
- **Inference budget**: Offline beam100, Recall@10/100. Online Related Pins beam60/penalty3; notifications beam100/penalty1. Serving L40S at ~200QPS/host: e2e p50/p99 51/77ms (beam60),54/81ms (beam100); batch not reported. Attention microbenchmark: A10G,batch4,history1018.
  - Source: Sections 5.1/5.3, Table 1 and Figure 5: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.33435v1#S5.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.33435v1#S5.SS3.SSS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.33435v1#S5.SS3.SSS2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.33435v1#S4.T1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.33435v1#S4.F5
- **Results from**: Reported Tables 1/2/3/4: serving, offline PinRec/TIGER comparison, diversity, online A/B; Tables 5-8: context sweep, trie costs, segments, ablations. Borrowed-versus-rerun baseline provenance: not reported.
  - Source: Tables 1-4 and Appendix Tables 5-8: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.33435v1#S4.T1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.33435v1#S5.T2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.33435v1#S5.T3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.33435v1#S5.T4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.33435v1#A1.T5 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.33435v1#A1.T8

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: competitor; note: TIGER is compared at matched training context and serving-token budgets.; where: PinGER v1, Section 5.2.1 and Table 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.33435v1#S5.SS2.SSS1.p1; https://arxiv.org/html/2610.33435v1#S5.T2.
- id: static; relation: predecessor; note: PinGER adopts STATIC's vectorized trie for valid-SID constrained decoding.; where: PinGER v1, Section 4.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.33435v1#S4.SS2.p2.
- id: cobra; relation: predecessor; note: PinGER retains COBRA-style SID/dense interleaving during training and removes past SIDs at serving.; where: PinGER v1, Section 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.33435v1#S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.

## PLUM

- Page: pages/papers/plum.md
- Venue: WWW’26
- Problem: Paradigms, Systems and Benchmarks
- Stage: No single stage
- Representation: Text+Img+CF; Tokenization: RQ-VAE; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: Multi-task NTP; Inference: Beam
- TL;DR: PLUM adapts a pre-trained LLM to industrial recommendation through Semantic ID tokenization, continued pre-training on domain data, and fine-tuning for generative retrieval, instead of large embedding tables.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Internal YouTube LFV/Shorts engagement and video metadata; reward-based SFT downsampling. Scaling input: 1536 tokens, roughly 100 recent watches; other filtering rules not reported.
  - Source: Sections 2.2/2.3/3.1/3.4: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.07784v1#S2.SS2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2510.07784v1#S2.SS3.p3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2510.07784v1#S3.SS1.SSS1.Px1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2510.07784v1#S3.SS4.SSS1.Px2.p1
- **Split**: Scaling: shuffle seven consecutive July 2025 days for training; evaluate Day 8. CPT ablation also uses held-out next-day evaluation; main production validation/test allocation not reported.
  - Source: Sections 3.3/3.4: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.07784v1#S3.SS3.SSS2.Px1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2510.07784v1#S3.SS4.SSS1.Px2.p1
- **Candidates**: full catalog in the scaling study: billions of videos.
  - Source: Section 3.4 explicitly evaluates against the comprehensive corpus: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.07784v1#S3.SS4.SSS1.Px1.p1
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Tokenizer/CPT item exposure relative to next-day tests not reported.
  - Source: Section 3 defines no unseen-item holdout: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.07784v1#S3
- **SID**: SID-v2 RQ-VAE: level-l codebook size 2048/2^(l-1); number of levels not reported. If a SID maps to multiple videos, randomly sample one for recall evaluation.
  - Source: Sections 2.1.2/3.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.07784v1#S2.SS1.SSS2.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2510.07784v1#S3.SS2.p1
- **Inference budget**: Beam decoding, width not reported; Recall@10 in scaling/ablations; production model 900M activated parameters. Serving hardware/batch size and latency not reported; 1024 v6e TPUs (four 256-TPU trainers) describe scaling training.
  - Source: Sections 2.3/3.1/3.4: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.07784v1#S2.SS3.p4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2510.07784v1#S3.SS1.SSS1.Px1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2510.07784v1#S3.SS4.SSS1.Px2.p1
- **Results from**: Original Table 2: PLUM/production LEM ratios; Table 3: adding PLUM versus quota-matched LEM+; Tables 4/5: SID/CPT ablations.
  - Source: Tables 2-5 and live protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.07784v1#S3.T2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2510.07784v1#S3.T3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2510.07784v1#S3.T4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2510.07784v1#S3.T5 and https://arxiv.org/html/2510.07784v1#S3.SS1.SSS2.Px2.p1

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: predecessor; note: PLUM extends TIGER's SID construction and adapts pretrained LLMs.; where: PLUM v1, Sections 1.1.2/2.1.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.07784v1#S1.SS1.SSS2.p1; https://arxiv.org/html/2510.07784v1#S2.SS1.SSS2.p2.
- id: mmq; relation: alternative; note: MMQ generates modality-specific tokens; PLUM fuses embeddings before quantization.; where: PLUM v1, Section 1.1.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.07784v1#S1.SS1.SSS2.p2.
- id: liger; relation: alternative; note: LIGER mixes generated IDs with dense retrieval; PLUM emphasizes SID-LLM adaptation.; where: PLUM v1, Section 1.1.3 (Yang et al., 2024): https://arxiv.org/html/2510.07784v1#S1.SS1.SSS3.p1.

## PrefixMem

- Page: pages/papers/prefixmem.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: III. SID–Model Alignment
- Stage: Backbone
- Representation: MM; Tokenization: RQ-VAE; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: Multi-task NTP; Inference: Beam
- TL;DR: PrefixMem gives an LLM a pre-trainable Semantic ID encoder built from prefix n-gram memory tables, so each token gets a prefix-conditioned representation instead of a plain vocabulary embedding.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Pinterest: about 10M engagement subsequences (<=32 events), 240M item occurrences, tens of millions of unique items. Filtering rules not reported.
  - Source: Section 4.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2606.00324v1#S4.SS1.p1
- **Split**: Evaluation uses later dates and disjoint users; exact dates/fractions not reported. On 100K held-out examples, a random engagement position is the target and preceding events are history.
  - Source: Sections 4.1/4.3: https://arxiv.org/html/2606.00324v1#S4.SS1.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2606.00324v1#S4.SS3.p1
- **Candidates**: not reported; retrieval evaluates exact ground-truth SID membership in generated beams.
  - Source: Section 4.3 defines beam SID matching, not sampled item negatives: https://arxiv.org/html/2606.00324v1#S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. RQ-VAE codebook trained on the full billion-item catalog; evaluation users are disjoint, not explicitly evaluation items.
  - Source: Section 4.1 has user/time holdout but no unseen-item holdout: https://arxiv.org/html/2606.00324v1#S4.SS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2606.00324v1#S4.SS1.p2
- **SID**: RQ-VAE on PinCLIP multimodal embeddings: 5 levels x 2048 codes. Collisions acknowledged; full-SID recall matches codes without resolving item collisions.
  - Source: Sections 4.1/4.3: https://arxiv.org/html/2606.00324v1#S4.SS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2606.00324v1#S4.SS3.p2
- **Inference budget**: Qwen3-1.7B default; five-step SID beam search with K=20/30/50/100; TIGER extension uses beam 10. PrefixMem: 4 hash heads, 2M rows, dimension 256, active at levels 4/5. Hardware, inference batch size, measured latency not reported.
  - Source: Sections 4.2/4.3 and Table 10: https://arxiv.org/html/2606.00324v1#S4.SS2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2606.00324v1#S4.SS2.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2606.00324v1#S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2606.00324v1#S5.T10
- **Results from**: Original Tables 2/3: teacher-forcing/initialization; Table 4: full-SID recall; Tables 9/10: LLM/TIGER transfer; Table 11: SID-Transformer comparison. Same-corpus with/without-encoder experiments.
  - Source: Tables 2-4/9-11: https://arxiv.org/html/2606.00324v1#S5.T2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2606.00324v1#S5.T3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2606.00324v1#S5.T4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2606.00324v1#S5.T9 and https://arxiv.org/html/2606.00324v1#S5.T10 and https://arxiv.org/html/2606.00324v1#S5.T11

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: predecessor; note: PrefixMem augments TIGER and transfers TIGER-trained memory to an LLM.; where: PrefixMem v1, Section 5.2 and Table 10: https://arxiv.org/html/2606.00324v1#S5.SS2.p5; https://arxiv.org/html/2606.00324v1#S5.T10.
- id: plum; relation: predecessor; note: PrefixMem follows PLUM's SID-language adaptation and adds prefix-conditioned encoding.; where: PrefixMem v1, Sections 2/3.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2606.00324v1#S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1; https://arxiv.org/html/2606.00324v1#S3.SS1.p1.
- id: onerec-think; relation: predecessor; note: PrefixMem simplifies the cited multi-stage SID-language pipeline to single-stage multitask training.; where: PrefixMem v1, Section 3.1 (Liu et al., 2025b, arXiv:2510.11639): https://arxiv.org/html/2606.00324v1#S3.SS1.p2.

## ProGEO

- Page: pages/papers/progeo.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text+Geo; Tokenization: R-KM+Geo-CB; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP; Inference: Beam+Geo-Filter
- TL;DR: ProGEO builds a proximity-aware geo-codebook with a geo-centroid local coordinate system and geo-rotary position encoding, so Semantic IDs model semantics and geography jointly.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 5

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Industrial: two months of transaction records from a Chinese local-life service platform (search query, user location, merchant exposure sequence, interactions); size and filtering not reported. Public: Foursquare NYC (1,083 users / 5,135 POIs) and TKY (2,293 / 7,873), filtered as in GNPR-SID (POIs with fewer than 10 interactions, users with fewer than 10 check-ins removed), and Yelp (150,346 POIs; clustering analysis only).
  - Source: Industrial and public data: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.23156v1#A2.SS1.p1; public statistics: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.23156v1#A2.SS2.SSS2.p1.
- **Split**: Industrial: two months of records for training and additional daily data reserved for validation; the test construction is not reported. Public: preprocessing follows GNPR-SID; the split is not restated.
  - Source: Two-month training with extra daily validation data: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.23156v1#A2.SS1.p1; public split follows GNPR-SID but is not restated.
- **Candidates**: Industrial inference: for each generated semantic ID, the 10 POIs closest to the user's location form the candidate set, with beam width 20. Evaluation reports Hit@1, Hit@50, Hit@100 and NDCG@50, @100; full catalog versus sampled not otherwise stated.
  - Source: Ten location-nearest POIs per semantic ID as candidates, then beam search: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.23156v1#A2.SS2.SSS1.p1; metrics: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.23156v1#A2.SS3.p3.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined.
  - Source: No unseen-item protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.23156v1#A2.SS1.p1.
- **SID**: Residual quantization with geographic rotary encoding (Geo-RoPE) at the third layer over 128-dimensional Qwen3-Embedding-8B text embeddings. Codebooks: [512, 512, 512] industrial; [32, 32, 32] NYC/TKY; [64, 64, 64] Yelp. Conflicts: industrial uses closest-location matching among POIs sharing a SID (best in Table 3); public datasets use a TIGER-style fourth-layer code because user location is unavailable.
  - Source: Codebooks [512,512,512] industrial, [32,32,32] NYC/TKY, [64,64,64] Yelp, Geo-RoPE at layer 3: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.23156v1#A2.SS2.SSS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2604.23156v1#A2.SS2.SSS2.p1; conflict strategies: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.23156v1#S4.T3.
- **Inference budget**: Beam search with width 20 on Qwen2.5-1.5B; all experiments on 8 GPUs with 80GB memory. Inference batch size and latency: not reported.
  - Source: Beam width 20 and hardware: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.23156v1#A2.SS2.SSS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2604.23156v1#A2.SS2.SSS2.p1.
- **Results from**: Table 1 (industrial quantization and recommendation metrics versus RQ-VAE, RQ-Kmeans, HyMiRec-style RQ-Kmeans, RQ-OPQ); Table 2 (geographic attributes); Table 3 (conflict-resolution strategies); Table 6 (public datasets versus RQ-Kmeans); Figures 7-10 (sensitivity and case studies).
  - Source: Main: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.23156v1#S4.T1; geographic attributes: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.23156v1#S4.T2; conflicts: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.23156v1#S4.T3; public: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.23156v1#A2.T6; sensitivity: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.23156v1#S4.F7.

- id: oneloc; relation: alternative; note: OneLoc adds location context to the SID input embedding for local-life video; Pro-GEO rotates residuals by geography inside the quantizer.; where: Pro-GEO v1, Sections 1 and 2.1 cite Wei et al. ### Notes

## 旧卡片说明

迁自 `d61aa6c:papers/progeo.md`。保留方法说明、实验叙述与局限；本轮只对照现有记录处理明确冲突，未重新逐句核查原论文。分类和规格以页面上方由记录生成的表格为准。

### ProGEO：邻近 POI 聚类的距离感知地理码本

> ProGEO 在标准语义码本之外加入地理码本，用局部坐标和旋转位置编码把 POI 邻近关系直接写入 SID。

### 研究动机与问题定义

本地生活推荐要求结果在地理上可达，但常规语义码本只按向量相似性聚类，可能生成语义相关却跨城不可配送的商户。ProGEO 研究如何将地理约束从辅助特征提升为 SID 结构的一部分，同时保留内容语义。

### TL;DR（核心摘要）

`商户内容/地理 → 标准码本量化 → 地理中心局部坐标 → Geo-RoPE地理码本 → 生成推荐`

模型先用标准 RQ-KMeans 得到多级语义 code，再从残差表示中建立地理中心和局部坐标系。Geo-RoPE 将局部距离和方向转为高维旋转，形成特殊 geo-codebook；微调后的 LLM 生成包含地理 code 的 SID，并在结果层面排除跨城无效配送。

### 输入与使用场景

| 方面 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| 使用信息 | 商户文本、类别、价格、地理位置和用户意图 |
| 信息融入位置 | 标准量化、特殊地理码本和生成约束 |
| 语义标识结构 | 标准 code 加 geo code 的多级序列 |
| 适用场景 | 本地生活、配送和地理可达推荐 |

### 方法设计

#### 3.1 语义码本聚类
POI 文本和地理特征用于构建表示，标准码本使用残差 K-means 逐层聚类。每一层产生一个 code，前两层负责表达通用语义，剩余量化空间留给地理关系。

#### 3.2 地理中心局部坐标映射
对于语义簇内的 POI，ProGEO 计算地理中心，并把全球经纬度转换为相对该中心的距离和方向。局部坐标避免直接在全球坐标上建模，使同一语义簇中的邻近关系更容易被量化。

#### 3.3 Geo-RoPE
地理距离和方向被映射为正交旋转变换，作用于残差表示的不同维度。这样，表示内积会随相对空间关系变化，地理相近的 POI 更可能共享或接近特殊 geo code。

#### 3.4 生成推荐与无效结果过滤
用户意图和历史行为输入生成模型，模型输出 POI SID。由于 SID 中含有地理 code，系统可在生成后识别跨城配送等不可行结果；论文图示还展示了按用户位置返回可达商户的流程。

### 实验结论

- 在大规模工业数据集上，ProGEO 报告 Hit@50 提升 1.87%，平均地理聚类距离下降 45.60%。
- 消融结果支持局部坐标、Geo-RoPE 和不同地理信息注入位置对推荐效果的贡献。
- 案例和可视化显示，特殊地理码本能减少语义相关但跨城不可达的推荐。

### 局限性与研究定位

#### 局限性

- 地理码本和跨城过滤依赖业务配送边界，跨平台和跨交通场景的通用性未验证。
- 论文对动态地理边界、实时路网距离以及新增商户的 SID 更新机制报告有限。

#### 研究定位

ProGEO 适合放在“地理结构化语义标识”章节，代表通过专用码本和几何变换增强 SID 空间可行性的路线。

### 相关资源

- [论文原文](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.23156)

### 标签

`地理码本` · `局部坐标系` · `Geo-RoPE` · `本地生活`

## PROMISE

- Page: pages/papers/promise.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: III. SID–Model Alignment
- Stage: Inference
- Representation: Text; Tokenization: RQ-VAE; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed†; Objective: NTP + Aux.; Inference: PRM-Beam
- TL;DR: PROMISE adds a lightweight process reward model that scores intermediate Semantic ID steps and prunes beam branches with it, to correct early-token semantic drift and scale with inference compute.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Public: Amazon Beauty and Sports and Outdoors (May 1996-July 2014), following TIGER's preprocessing (users with fewer than 5 reviews removed). Industrial: Kuaishou online-learning logs (over 400 million daily active users, about 50 billion interactions per day, more than 100 million items).
  - Source: Public datasets and TIGER protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04674v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1; industrial logs: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04674v1#S4.SS2.SSS1.p2.
- **Split**: Public: chronological leave-one-out (last item for test, second-to-last for validation, rest for training). Industrial: online learning on real logs; the offline test construction is not reported. Online: 7-day A/B test on Kuaishou and Kuaishou Lite, with 5% of users (about 20 million) in the experimental group and another 5% in the control group for each app.
  - Source: Leave-one-out allocation: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04674v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1; industrial online learning: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04674v1#S4.SS2.SSS1.p2; online A/B groups and length: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04674v1#S4.SS3.p1.
- **Candidates**: not reported (full catalog versus sampled evaluation candidates); public Recall/NDCG at 5 and 10, industrial at 100, 500, 1000 from beam search.
  - Source: Metrics only: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04674v1#S4.SS1.SSS4.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04674v1#S4.SS2.SSS4.p1.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined.
  - Source: No unseen-item protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04674v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1.
- **SID**: Public: 3-level RQ-VAE x 256 codes. Industrial: residual K-means over multimodal representations, depth 3 x 8,192 codes. Collision handling: not reported.
  - Source: Public 3 x 256 RQ-VAE: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04674v1#S4.SS1.SSS3.p1; industrial residual K-means d=3, M=8192: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04674v1#S4.SS2.SSS1.p2; no collision rule found.
- **Inference budget**: PRM-guided beam search: expand to K+ candidate paths per step, score them with a lightweight path-level PRM, and keep K'. Industrial: K=K'=1000 with K+ of 4,000 or 6,000; 4 encoder and 4 decoder blocks plus 1 PRM block. Public beam settings, hardware, inference batch size, and latency: not reported.
  - Source: PRM-guided beam: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04674v1#S3.SS3.p3; industrial K=K'=1000 and K+ in {4000, 6000}: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04674v1#S4.SS2.SSS3.p1; public beam settings not found.
- **Results from**: Table 1 (Beauty and Sports; baseline numbers taken from the original papers or identical settings); Table 2 (Kuaishou offline versus six deployed retrievers); Table 3 (online A/B); Table 4 (PRM step ablation with hierarchical recall); Figure 4 (test-time scaling of K+).
  - Source: Public: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04674v1#S4.T1; industrial: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04674v1#S4.T2; online: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04674v1#S4.T3; ablation: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04674v1#S4.T4; test-time scaling: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04674v1#S4.SS5.p1.

### Related

- id: actionpiece; relation: competitor; note: ActionPiece is the strongest public baseline; it changes tokenization, whereas Promise keeps RQ-VAE SIDs and adds a process reward model to steer beam search.; where: Promise v1, generative baselines: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04674v1#S4.I2.i3.p1; Table 1 and Section 4.1.5: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04674v1#S4.T1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04674v1#S4.SS1.SSS5.p2.
- id: tiger; relation: competitor; note: TIGER decodes with standard fixed-width beam search, which Promise argues suffers semantic drift; Promise rescores expanded paths at each step with a PRM.; where: Promise v1, baselines and protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04674v1#S4.I2.i1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04674v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1; Table 1: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04674v1#S4.T1.
- id: onerec-v2; relation: alternative; note: OneRec-V2 introduces a lazy decoder and scales parameters; Promise argues that scaling inference compute with PRM-guided search is a cheaper way to scale.; where: Promise v1, Section 6.1 describes OneRec V2 (Zhou et al., 2025c): https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04674v1#S6.SS1.p1; Section 4.6.1 contrasts parameter scaling with test-time scaling: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04674v1#S4.SS6.SSS1.p1.

## PSI

- Page: pages/papers/psi.md
- Venue: arXiv’25
- Problem: II. Uniqueness and Validity
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text; Tokenization: Post-hoc RQ; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP; Inference: Beam
- TL;DR: PSI assigns unique, semantic-preserving IDs by relaxing nearest-centroid selection with exhaustive candidate matching or recursive residual searching, instead of appending a non-semantic token to resolve conflicts.
- [Code](https://github.com/wangshanyw/PurelySemanticIndexing)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 4

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Sequential recommendation on Amazon Beauty (12,101 items / 22,363 users), Sports (18,357 / 35,598), and Toys (11,924 items), keeping users and items with at least 5 interactions, following LMIndexer. Also Amazon Product Search (same domains) and document retrieval on NQ320k and MS MARCO-1M.
  - Source: Recommendation data and LMIndexer protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.16446v1#Sx4.SSx1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2509.16446v1#Sx4.SSx2.p2; statistics: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.16446v1#Sx4.T2; search and retrieval data: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.16446v1#Sx4.SSx3.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2509.16446v1#Sx4.T3.
- **Split**: Recommendation: per-user leave-one-out (last for test, second-to-last for validation, rest for training). Product search: the original train/test split. A cold-start test subset keeps targets that appear at most 0 or 1 time in training.
  - Source: Leave-one-out allocation: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.16446v1#Sx4.SSx2.p2; cold-start subset: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.16446v1#Sx4.SSx10.p2.
- **Candidates**: not reported (full catalog versus sampled evaluation candidates); generation over valid semantic IDs.
  - Source: Metrics and protocol follow LMIndexer; candidate set not restated: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.16446v1#Sx4.SSx1.p1.
- **Visibility**: Main: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Cold-start subset: targets appearing at most once in training, including items never seen by the generator; whether the RQ-VAE or clustering indexer was fit with these items: not reported.
  - Source: Cold-start subset with items that appear 0 or 1 time: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.16446v1#Sx4.SSx10.p2; the indexer embeds all items including test-only ones.
- **SID**: Purely semantic IDs: conflicts are removed by assigning non-nearest centroids instead of appending a conflict token, via exhaustive candidate matching (ECM, global scoring of top-k combinations) or recursive residual search (RRS, greedy). Applied to RQ-VAE and hierarchical clustering indexers. The level study on Amazon product search compares three-level purely semantic IDs with two levels plus a conflict index (codebook size 256); the conflict-proportion study uses codebook sizes 512, 256, and 192. Levels and codebook sizes for the main tables: not reported.
  - Source: ECM and RRS conflict-free assignment over RQ-VAE or hierarchical clustering: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.16446v1#Sx3.SSx1.p3, https://arxiv.org/html/2509.16446v1#Sx3.SSx2.p1, https://arxiv.org/html/2509.16446v1#Sx3.SSx3.p1; codebook size 256 in the level study: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.16446v1#Sx4.SSx7.SSSx1.p1; codebook sizes 512, 256, 192 in the conflict-proportion study: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.16446v1#Sx4.SSx9.p1.
- **Inference budget**: T5-base generator initialized from the same checkpoint for all indexers; decoding method and beam width: not reported. All experiments on 2 NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPUs; inference batch size and latency: not reported.
  - Source: T5-base, hardware, training batch: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.16446v1#Sx4.SSx1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2509.16446v1#Sx4.SSx2.p3; decoding settings not found.
- **Results from**: Table 5 (sequential recommendation on Beauty, Sports, Toys with RQ-VAE and HC indexers, 3 trials); Table 6 (product search); document-retrieval tables; Table 9 (candidate ranking ablation); Figure 5 (cold-start subset).
  - Source: Recommendation: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.16446v1#Sx4.T5; search: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.16446v1#Sx4.T6; ablation: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.16446v1#Sx4.T9; cold start: Figure 5 via https://arxiv.org/html/2509.16446v1#Sx4.SSx10.p2.

### Related

- id: lmindexer; relation: predecessor; note: PSID follows LMIndexer's tasks, datasets, and setup, and replaces conflict tokens with conflict-free semantic assignment.; where: PSID v1, Section 4.1 follows Jin et al. (2023): https://arxiv.org/html/2509.16446v1#Sx4.SSx1.p1; dataset tables: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.16446v1#Sx4.T2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2509.16446v1#Sx4.T3.
- id: tiger; relation: alternative; note: TIGER appends a non-semantic conflict token to colliding IDs and uses a heuristic quota for cold-start items; PSID reassigns colliding items to non-nearest centroids so IDs stay fully semantic.; where: PSID v1, Section 1 on fallback tokens: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.16446v1#Sx1.p2; cold-start discussion citing Rajput et al. (2023): https://arxiv.org/html/2509.16446v1#Sx4.SSx10.p1.
- id: liger; relation: alternative; note: LIGER adds dense retrieval to recover cold-start items; PSID improves cold-start generation by removing unpredictable conflict tokens.; where: PSID v1, Section 4.10 cites Yang et al. (2024): https://arxiv.org/html/2509.16446v1#Sx4.SSx10.p1.
- id: latte; relation: successor; note: Latte later uses PSID as its base model and its ESM conflict resolution, and adds latent prefix tokens.; where: Evidence is from the later Latte paper: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.06331v1#S5.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.06331v1#A4.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.

## PSRQ

- Page: pages/papers/psrq.md
- Venue: CIKM’25
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text+Img; Tokenization: Prog. RQ; Backbone: Encoder; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: Discrim.; Inference: Scoring
- TL;DR: PSRQ generates modality-specific and modality-joint Semantic IDs that preserve prefix semantic features and models music interests with multi-codebook cross-attention, to reduce semantic drift in residual quantization.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Baby (81,423 users / 33,652 items; ratings of 4 or more are positives), an industrial music-streaming dataset from one week of logs (4,926,656 users / 1,387,247 songs; collections are positives, played-but-not-collected are negatives), and Music4all (14,127 users / 99,596 songs; repeated plays are positives). Items with fewer than 30 interactions are marked cold-start. Further filtering: not reported.
  - Source: Datasets and labels: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20359v1#S5.SS1.SSS1.p1, https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20359v1#S5.I2.i1.p1, https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20359v1#S5.I2.i2.p1, https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20359v1#S5.I2.i3.p1; statistics: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20359v1#S5.T1.
- **Split**: not reported (sequences are built by timestamp and trained for one epoch, but the train/test division is not described). Online: A/B test in February 2025 on the music platform against a DLRM ranker.
  - Source: Timestamp-ordered sequences, no split rule: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20359v1#S5.I2.i1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20359v1#S5.SS1.SSS2.p1; online test: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20359v1#S5.SS3.p1.
- **Candidates**: n/a for ranking candidates: evaluation is pointwise AUC and Logloss on labeled positive and negative samples; how negatives relate to user history is defined by the labels above.
  - Source: Pointwise AUC on labeled samples: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20359v1#S5.SS1.SSS3.p1.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. 'Cold AUC' covers items with fewer than 30 interactions, which are low-frequency, not unseen.
  - Source: Cold-start = fewer than 30 interactions, not unseen: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20359v1#S5.SS1.SSS1.p1.
- **SID**: Progressive Semantic Residual Quantization (PSRQ): layer-wise K-means over modality embeddings (text, image or audio) that preserves the prefix semantic feature, producing modal-specific and modal-joint semantic IDs; clusters per layer k = 64 (Amazon Baby), 256 (Industrial), 128 (Music4all), 3 layers. Collision handling: not reported.
  - Source: Clusters k and layers l per dataset: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20359v1#S5.SS1.SSS2.p1; PSRQ name and modal-specific/modal-joint IDs: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20359v1#abstract1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20359v1#S4.SS1.p1.
- **Inference budget**: n/a for generation (SIDs feed a DIN-style ranker with cross-attention, MCCA). MLLM feature extractors run on NVIDIA A100 GPUs; ranker inference batch size and latency: not reported.
  - Source: Discriminative ranker, hardware for feature extraction: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20359v1#S5.SS1.SSS2.p1.
- **Results from**: Table 2 (All AUC, Cold AUC, Logloss versus multimodal and quantization-based rankers); Table 3 (quantizers added to DIN with text only); Table 4 (MCCA ablation); Section 5.3 (online A/B: collect +2.81%, full play +0.95%).
  - Source: Main: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20359v1#S5.T2; quantizers in DIN: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20359v1#S5.T3; ablation: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20359v1#S5.T4; online: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20359v1#S5.SS3.p1.

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: alternative; note: TIGER introduced RQ-VAE semantic IDs for generative retrieval; PSRQ quantizes multimodal embeddings with progressive semantic residual K-means and uses the IDs as ranking features for cold-start items.; where: PSRQ v1, Section 1 and Section 2.2 cite Rajput et al. (2023): https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20359v1#S1.p3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20359v1#S2.SS2.p1; RQ-VAE is a quantizer baseline in Table 3: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20359v1#S5.T3.
- id: vq-rec; relation: alternative; note: VQ-Rec framed vector quantization for transferable recommenders; PSRQ adds modal-specific and modal-joint codebooks for multimodal cold-start ranking.; where: PSRQ v1, Section 1 and Section 2.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20359v1#S1.p3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20359v1#S2.SS2.p1.
- id: onerec; relation: alternative; note: OneRec uses residual K-means SIDs inside an end-to-end generator; PSRQ keeps a discriminative ranker and feeds it multimodal SID embeddings.; where: PSRQ v1, contribution list and Section 2.2 cite OneRec: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20359v1#S1.I1.i2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20359v1#S2.SS2.p1.

## Q-BERT4Rec

- Page: pages/papers/q-bert4rec.md
- Venue: arXiv’25
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Representation
- Representation: Text+Img+CF; Tokenization: RQ-VAE; Backbone: Encoder (Non-AR); Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: Masked; Inference: Non-AR
- TL;DR: Q-BERT4Rec fuses text, image, and structural features into item embeddings, quantizes them into Semantic ID tokens by residual vector quantization, and pre-trains a bidirectional encoder with several masking strategies.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 4

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Reviews 2018: pre-training on six source domains (Pet, Cell, Automotive, Tools, Toys, Sports) and fine-tuning on Musical Instruments, Arts Crafts and Sewing, Video Games (same statistics table as MQL4GRec). Filtering rules: not restated.
  - Source: Source and target domains: https://arxiv.org/html/2512.02474v2#S4.SS1.p1, https://arxiv.org/html/2512.02474v2#S4.SS1.p2, https://arxiv.org/html/2512.02474v2#S4.SS1.p3; statistics: https://arxiv.org/html/2512.02474v2#S3.T1.
- **Split**: Leave-one-out: most recent interaction for test, second most recent for validation, the rest for training.
  - Source: Leave-one-out allocation: https://arxiv.org/html/2512.02474v2#S4.SS1.p4.
- **Candidates**: not reported explicitly; at inference the masked last position is filled with the most probable semantic ID over the item set (HR and NDCG at 1, 5, 10).
  - Source: Argmax over item semantic IDs: https://arxiv.org/html/2512.02474v2#S3.SS6.p2; metrics: https://arxiv.org/html/2512.02474v2#S4.SS1.p4.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined.
  - Source: Standard split with no unseen-item protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2512.02474v2#S4.SS1.p4.
- **SID**: 4-level RQ-VAE x 256 codewords (dimension 32) over LLaMA text and CLIP-ViT image features fused by a cross-modal semantic injection module. Collisions are resolved by MQL4GRec's distance-based token reallocation.
  - Source: 4 levels x 256 x 32, MQL4GRec reallocation for collisions: https://arxiv.org/html/2512.02474v2#S4.SS1.p6 and https://arxiv.org/html/2512.02474v2#S3.SS4.p7.
- **Inference budget**: Bidirectional masked prediction of the last position (no beam search); 4-layer Transformer encoder. NVIDIA RTX 4090 GPUs (four for pre-training, one for fine-tuning). Table 6 reports per-sample inference latency of about 2.66-2.67 ms with under 6M parameters.
  - Source: Masked prediction at inference: https://arxiv.org/html/2512.02474v2#S3.SS6.p2; hardware: https://arxiv.org/html/2512.02474v2#S4.SS1.p8; latency: https://arxiv.org/html/2512.02474v2#A2.T6.
- **Results from**: Table 2 (Instruments, Arts, Games versus traditional, Transformer, multimodal, prompt-LLM, and semantic-ID baselines); Tables 3-4 (modalities and pre-training strategies); Figures 3-5 (layers, mask ratio, dropout); Table 6 (complexity and latency).
  - Source: Main: https://arxiv.org/html/2512.02474v2#S3.T2; ablations: https://arxiv.org/html/2512.02474v2#S3.T3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2512.02474v2#S4.T4; sensitivity: https://arxiv.org/html/2512.02474v2#S4.SS4.p1; complexity: https://arxiv.org/html/2512.02474v2#A2.T6.

### Related

- id: mql4grec; relation: competitor; note: MQL4GRec generates multimodal quantitative language autoregressively; Q-BERT4Rec reuses its collision reallocation but fuses modalities before quantization and predicts masked SIDs bidirectionally.; where: Q-BERT4Rec v2, collision handling follows Zhai et al. (2025): https://arxiv.org/html/2512.02474v2#S3.SS4.p7; Table 2 baseline: https://arxiv.org/html/2512.02474v2#S3.T2.
- id: tiger; relation: competitor; note: TIGER decodes SIDs left to right with an encoder-decoder; Q-BERT4Rec uses a BERT-style encoder with multi-mask pre-training.; where: Q-BERT4Rec v2, Table 2 semantic-ID baseline: https://arxiv.org/html/2512.02474v2#S3.T2; Appendix A baselines: https://arxiv.org/html/2512.02474v2#A1.I5.i1.p1.
- id: vq-rec; relation: competitor; note: VQ-Rec uses product-quantized text codes for transfer; Q-BERT4Rec quantizes fused text-image features with RQ-VAE and pre-trains on six source domains.; where: Q-BERT4Rec v2, Table 2 VQ/multimodal baseline: https://arxiv.org/html/2512.02474v2#S3.T2.
- id: cid; relation: competitor; note: P5-CID uses collaborative IDs in a prompt-based LLM; Q-BERT4Rec uses multimodal semantic IDs in a small masked Transformer.; where: Q-BERT4Rec v2, Table 2 prompt-LLM baseline: https://arxiv.org/html/2512.02474v2#S3.T2; Appendix A: https://arxiv.org/html/2512.02474v2#A1.I4.i1.p1.

迁自 `d61aa6c:README.md` 的条目说明，未沿用旧目录的收录分类。

## QT-Mob

- Page: pages/papers/qt-mob.md
- Venue: KDD’25
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text+Geo; Tokenization: RQ-VAE; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: Multi-task NTP; Inference: C-Beam
- TL;DR: QT-Mob tokenizes locations into compact semantic tokens and fine-tunes an LLM with complementary objectives that align the tokens with its representations, for next-location prediction and mobility recovery.
- [Code](https://github.com/shadowfall09/QT-Mob)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 1

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Foursquare NYC/SG, April 2012-February 2013; Singapore cellular trajectories, November 2022, using 400m grids. Remove locations with <5 visits; group records into 24h trajectories and discard trajectories with <3 records.
  - Source: Section 5.1.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.11109v1#S5.SS1.SSS1.p1
- **Split**: Per-user chronological trajectories: first 70% train, next 10% validation, last 20% test.
  - Source: Section 5.1.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.11109v1#S5.SS1.SSS1.p1
- **Candidates**: not reported; the unseen-location experiment follows LLM-Move's zero-shot ranking setting without detailing its candidate pool.
  - Source: Section 5.1 and Appendix D.4 do not specify catalog enumeration or candidate sampling: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.11109v1#S5.SS1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2506.11109v1#A4.SS4.p1
- **Visibility**: Unseen-location probe: sample 100 test locations and remove all training trajectories containing them. Unseen by generator; whether unseen by tokenizer too: not reported.
  - Source: Appendix D.4: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.11109v1#A4.SS4.p1
- **SID**: 4 RQ-VAE levels x 256 codes, code dimension 32; collision handling not reported.
  - Source: Section 5.1.4: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.11109v1#S5.SS1.SSS4.p1
- **Inference budget**: Constrained beam 15; Hit/NDCG@1/5/10. Inference hardware, batch size and latency not reported; four V100 GPUs are specified for training.
  - Source: Sections 5.1.3/5.1.4: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.11109v1#S5.SS1.SSS3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2506.11109v1#S5.SS1.SSS4.p1
- **Results from**: Original Tables 2/3: next-location prediction/mobility recovery; Table 10: unseen locations. Five-run averages; compared baselines use their papers' default parameter settings.
  - Source: Section 5.1.3/5.1.4 and Tables 2/3/10: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.11109v1#S5.SS1.SSS3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2506.11109v1#S5.SS1.SSS4.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2506.11109v1#S5.T2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2506.11109v1#S5.T3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2506.11109v1#A4.T10

### Related

- id: lc-rec; relation: predecessor; note: Its cited RQ-VAE tokenization approach informs QT-Mob's hierarchical location tokens.; where: QT-Mob v1, Section 4.2, citing Zheng et al. (2024): https://arxiv.org/html/2506.11109v1#S4.SS2.p1; https://arxiv.org/html/2506.11109v1#S4.SS2.p4.

## QuaSID

- Page: pages/papers/quasid.md
- Venue: KDD’26 ADS
- Problem: II. Uniqueness and Validity
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text+CF; Tokenization: QA-RQ; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP; Inference: Beam†
- TL;DR: QuaSID repels only qualified conflicting Semantic ID pairs with Hamming-scaled margins, masks benign overlaps, and adds a dual-tower contrastive objective, instead of treating all collisions equally.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Reviews 2018 Beauty and Toys & Games, user/item 5-core; Kuaishou e-commerce industrial logs with multimodal item features.
  - Source: Section 5.1.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.00632v1#S5.SS1.SSS1.p1
- **Split**: Public: leave-one-out train/validation/test, exact held-out positions not reported. Online A/B: 5 days, about 5% randomized treatment traffic covering >20M users.
  - Source: Sections 5.1.1/5.4: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.00632v1#S5.SS1.SSS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2603.00632v1#S5.SS4.p1
- **Candidates**: not reported
  - Source: Sections 5.1.3/5.1.4 and Appendix A.2 do not specify candidate enumeration or sampling: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.00632v1#S5.SS1.SSS3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2603.00632v1#S5.SS1.SSS4.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2603.00632v1#A1.SS2
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Industrial cold-start subsets have <100 or <600 video views within the first 48h; strict generator/tokenizer unseen status not reported.
  - Source: Section 5.4: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.00632v1#S5.SS4.p1
- **SID**: Public: 3 x 256; industrial: 4 x 1024. HaMR repels qualified full/partial collisions; additional inference-time collision resolution not reported.
  - Source: Sections 4.2/5.1.4: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.00632v1#S4.SS2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2603.00632v1#S5.SS1.SSS4.p1
- **Inference budget**: Offline HitRate/NDCG@5/10; beam width, inference hardware, serving batch size and latency not reported. Appendix A.2 batches 256/1024 concern SID learning.
  - Source: Section 5.1.3 and Appendix A.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.00632v1#S5.SS1.SSS3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2603.00632v1#A1.SS2
- **Results from**: Original Table 2: matched-TIGER tokenizer comparison, five-seed means; Table 3: HaMR added to baselines; Table 4: online retrieval/ranking and low-view subsets.
  - Source: Tables 2/3/4 and Section 5.1.4: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.00632v1#S4.T2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2603.00632v1#S4.T3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2603.00632v1#S5.T4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2603.00632v1#S5.SS1.SSS4.p1

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: predecessor; note: Supplies the shared downstream backbone for tokenizer comparisons.; where: QuaSID v1, Section 5.1.4: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.00632v1#S5.SS1.SSS4.p1.
- id: letter; relation: alternative; note: Assignment balancing contrasts with QuaSID's qualified, severity-scaled collision repulsion.; where: QuaSID v1, Section 2.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.00632v1#S2.SS2.p2.
- id: hid-vae; relation: alternative; note: Overlap regularization is contrasted with selectively repelling qualified conflicts.; where: QuaSID v1, Section 2.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.00632v1#S2.SS2.p2.

## R3-VAE

- Page: pages/papers/r3-vae.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: II. Uniqueness and Validity
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text; Tokenization: Ref.-RQ; Backbone: –; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP; Inference: Beam
- TL;DR: R3-VAE stabilizes residual quantization with a reference vector as semantic anchor and a dot-product rating mechanism, and uses two Semantic ID quality metrics as training regularizers.
- [Code](https://github.com/wwqq/R3-VAE)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 4

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Public: Amazon Beauty, Sports, Toys, Clothing, plus LastFM and ML1M. Industrial: Toutiao interaction logs. Filtering rules and corpus sizes: not reported in the body.
  - Source: Public datasets: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.11440v3#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1; industrial Toutiao data: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.11440v3#S4.SS3.p1; no filtering rules or statistics found in the body.
- **Split**: not reported for the public datasets. Industrial: offline MRR plus online A/B tests for both the generative (OneRec framework) and CTR settings; test periods and traffic not reported.
  - Source: No split rule found; online tests: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.11440v3#S4.T3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2604.11440v3#S4.SS4.SSS3.p1.
- **Candidates**: not reported (full catalog versus sampled); Recall and NDCG at 10, 20, 30 on the generated top-K sequence; industrial generative MRR and CTR UAUC.
  - Source: Generated top-K sequences: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.11440v3#S4.SS1.SSS3.Px1.p1.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. The online CTR test reports cold-start click volume for existing and new users without defining item visibility.
  - Source: Online cold-start click volume for new users, no unseen-item protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.11440v3#S4.SS4.SSS3.p1.
- **SID**: Reference-vector-guided residual quantization VAE: inputs are projected on a learned reference vector, each layer assigns soft top-K weights over codewords, and the SID takes the top-weighted index per layer; a metric loss maximizes semantic cohesion and preference discrimination. Industrial: 3 levels x 8,192. Public: the Beauty sensitivity study fixes L=3 and K=256; codebook sizes for the other public runs: not reported. Collision handling: not reported (collision rates are measured, e.g. Table 6).
  - Source: Reference-vector projection and weighted rating residual quantization: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.11440v3#S3.SS3.SSS3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2604.11440v3#S3.SS5.SSS1.p1; industrial codebooks 8192^3: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.11440v3#S4.SS3.SSS1.p1; Beauty sensitivity study with L=3, K=256 fixed: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.11440v3#S4.SS6.SSS2.p1.
- **Inference budget**: Industrial generative setting follows OneRec: beam search generating 512 responses for DPO, on 64 NVIDIA A100 GPUs. CTR setting: SIDs replace item-ID embeddings in DIN, SIM, RankMixer (batch 2,048). Public decoding settings, inference batch size, and latency: not reported.
  - Source: OneRec framework with beam 512 responses and hardware: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.11440v3#S4.SS3.SSS1.p1; CTR setting: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.11440v3#S4.SS4.SSS1.p1.
- **Results from**: Table 1 (Beauty, Sports, Toys) and Table 2 (LastFM, ML1M, Clothing) with SC/PD metrics; Table 3 (industrial generative MRR and online A/B); Tables 4-5 (CTR UAUC and online A/B); Table 6 (Beauty SID quality including collision rate and Gini).
  - Source: Results: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.11440v3#S3.T1, https://arxiv.org/html/2604.11440v3#S4.T2, https://arxiv.org/html/2604.11440v3#S4.T3, https://arxiv.org/html/2604.11440v3#S4.T4, https://arxiv.org/html/2604.11440v3#S4.T5, https://arxiv.org/html/2604.11440v3#S4.T6.

### Related

- id: onerec; relation: competitor; note: OneRec's residual K-means is the main industrial baseline and the generation framework; R3-VAE adds a reference-vector projection, rating-weighted residual quantization, and SID-quality regularization.; where: R3-VAE v3, baselines and OneRec framework: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.11440v3#S4.SS1.SSS2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2604.11440v3#S4.SS3.SSS1.p1; Tables 1, 3, 4: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.11440v3#S3.T1, https://arxiv.org/html/2604.11440v3#S4.T3, https://arxiv.org/html/2604.11440v3#S4.T4.
- id: tokenrec; relation: competitor; note: TokenRec's masked vector-quantized tokenizer (MQ) is a baseline; R3-VAE differs by reference-guided soft residual assignment.; where: R3-VAE v3, baseline MQ [26]: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.11440v3#S4.SS1.SSS2.p1; Tables 1 and 4: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.11440v3#S3.T1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2604.11440v3#S4.T4.
- id: vq-rec; relation: competitor; note: VQ-Rec's OPQ-style codes appear as the OPQ-KMeans baseline; R3-VAE uses residual rather than product quantization.; where: R3-VAE v3, baseline OPQ-KMeans [5, 7]: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.11440v3#S4.SS1.SSS2.p1; Table 1: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.11440v3#S3.T1.
- id: forge; relation: alternative; note: FORGE proposes Embedding HitRate and Gini to evaluate SIDs without full training; R3-VAE proposes semantic cohesion and preference discrimination for the same purpose.; where: R3-VAE v3, Section 3.4 draws on FORGE [4]: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.11440v3#S3.SS4.p1; Section 1: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.11440v3#S1.p3.
