## RAGR

- Page: pages/papers/ragr.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Training
- Representation: Text; Tokenization: RQ-VAE; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP → DPO; Inference: Beam† / –
- TL;DR: RAGR interleaves item Semantic IDs and review Semantic IDs chronologically in the user sequence and uses DPO to favor item tokens at prediction positions, instead of modeling item-only sequences.
- [Code](https://github.com/Zhang-Yingyi/TKDE_RAGR)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 2

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Beauty, Sports and Outdoors, Toys and Games, with historical review text; remove users/items with fewer than five interactions; maximum history 20, truncating oldest interactions.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.17267v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1 ; #S4.SS1.SSS4.p3
- **Split**: Per-user chronological leave-one-out: last interaction test, second last validation, remaining interactions training.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.17267v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1
- **Candidates**: not reported
  - Source: Experimental settings report top-K metrics but no candidate universe: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.17267v1#S4.SS1
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Historical reviews are retained; tokenizer fitting exposure to test items not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.17267v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1 ; #S4.SS4.p4
- **SID**: RQ-VAE: 4 x 256, 32-dimensional codewords, shared item/review token space. Default tokenizer fits item text only; collision handling not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.17267v1#S4.SS1.SSS4.p2 ; #S4.SS4.p4 ; #S4.SS5.p4
- **Inference budget**: Autoregressive item-SID prediction; HIT/NDCG@5/10/20. Decoding algorithm/beam width, inference batch size and latency not reported. General experiment server: 8 RTX PRO 6000 96GB GPUs; inference-specific allocation not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.17267v1#S4.SS1.SSS3.p1 ; #S4.SS1.SSS4.p1 ; #S4.SS1.SSS4.p5
- **Results from**: Original Table II: TIGER/LETTER with and without RAGR, means over seeds 42/43/44; all baselines trained/evaluated with the common split/protocol. Table III: ablations; Tables IV-V: tokenizer efficiency/collisions. No baseline-result reuse stated.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.17267v1#S4.T2 ; #S4.T3 ; #S4.T4 ; #S4.T5 ; #S4.SS1.SSS4.p1 ; #S4.SS1.SSS4.p5

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: predecessor; note: RAGR augments TIGER with interleaved review SIDs, review-generation supervision and DPO alignment toward item generation.; where: RAGR v1, Section IV-A and Table II: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.17267v1#S4.SS1.SSS4.p1; https://arxiv.org/html/2605.17267v1#S4.T2.
- id: letter; relation: predecessor; note: LETTER is the second backbone receiving the same review augmentation and item-centric DPO alignment.; where: RAGR v1, Section IV-A and Table II: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.17267v1#S4.SS1.SSS4.p1; https://arxiv.org/html/2605.17267v1#S4.T2.

## RecBase

- Page: pages/papers/recbase.md
- Venue: EMNLP’25
- Problem: VI. Generalization
- Stage: Training
- Representation: Text; Tokenization: Curr. RQ; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP; Inference: Beam
- TL;DR: RecBase pretrains a domain-agnostic foundation model on a cross-domain corpus with a unified tokenizer of hierarchical concept identifiers, for zero-shot recommendation instead of language-centric pretraining.
- [Code](https://github.com/reczoo/RecBase)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 2

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Pre-training on 15 datasets and testing on 8 unseen datasets from RecBench (MIND, MovieLens, MicroLens, Goodreads, Yelp, Steam, H&M, HotelRec as test sets). Totals: training 4,595,003 items / 35,047,682 users; fine-tuning 1,005,745 / 5,098,084; test 623,615 / 145,975. Length-based filtering: users with fewer than 15 interactions are removed (e.g. AmazonToys) and histories over 2,500 interactions are truncated (e.g. LastFM, PixelRec); thresholds for the other datasets: not reported.
  - Source: RecBench and dataset roles: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.03131v1#S4.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2509.03131v1#S4.SS1.p1; statistics: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.03131v1#S4.T2; length filtering: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.03131v1#A2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.
- **Split**: Dataset-level: pre-train on training datasets and evaluate zero-shot on held-out datasets; a fine-tuning study adds in-domain data for five test datasets. Within-dataset split rules: not reported.
  - Source: Dataset-level split between pre-training and zero-shot test: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.03131v1#S4.p1; fine-tuning study: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.03131v1#S4.T3.
- **Candidates**: n/a for ranking candidates: user-item pairs are scored and evaluated by AUC (RecBench protocol); how negative pairs are formed is not restated.
  - Source: User-item pair scoring with AUC: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.03131v1#S4.SS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2509.03131v1#S4.SS1.p3.
- **Visibility**: Zero-shot: test datasets and their items are unseen by the generator; whether the CL-VAE tokenizer was trained on test-dataset items: not reported. Fine-tuned setting: warm.
  - Source: Test datasets are unseen in pre-training: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.03131v1#S4.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2509.03131v1#S4.SS1.p3.
- **SID**: Concept IDs from a curriculum-learning RQ-VAE (CL-VAE) with 4 levels x 2,048 codes over NV-Embed-v2 text embeddings, with codebook reinitialization against collapse. Collisions are measured as a conflict rate (Figure 2) but a resolution rule is not reported.
  - Source: CL-VAE with 4 levels x 2048 over NV-Embed-v2: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.03131v1#S4.SS2.p1; curriculum and reinitialization: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.03131v1#S3.SS2.p2; conflict rate study: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.03131v1#S5.SS2.p1.
- **Inference budget**: Scores items from the logits over concept IDs (no beam search described); Qwen2-style decoder (Base: 24 layers, hidden 1,024; Large: 28 layers, hidden 1,536; vocabulary 20,000). Hardware, inference batch size, and latency: not reported.
  - Source: Logit-based ranking of concept IDs: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.03131v1#S4.SS1.p2; model sizes: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.03131v1#S4.SS2.p2.
- **Results from**: Table 1 (zero-shot AUC on 8 datasets versus P5, RecGPT, and LLM baselines); Table 3 (zero-shot versus fine-tuned); Table 4 (ablations of CL-VAE components); Figure 2 (codebook size and levels).
  - Source: Zero-shot: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.03131v1#S3.T1; fine-tuning: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.03131v1#S4.T3; ablation: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.03131v1#S5.T4; codebook study: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.03131v1#S5.SS2.p1.

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: alternative; note: TIGER builds RQ-VAE semantic IDs per dataset for next-item generation; RecBase pre-trains a recommendation foundation model over concept IDs shared across many domains.; where: RecBase v1, Section 2.2 cites Rajput et al. (2023): https://arxiv.org/html/2509.03131v1#S2.SS2.p1.
- id: lc-rec; relation: alternative; note: LC-Rec adapts an existing LLM to one domain's item indices; RecBase pre-trains from scratch on recommendation corpora for zero-shot transfer.; where: RecBase v1, Section 2.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.03131v1#S2.SS2.p1.

## RecoChain

- Page: pages/papers/recochain.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: IV. Utility
- Stage: Backbone
- Representation: Text+Img; Tokenization: RQ; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP + Rank; Inference: Hybrid
- TL;DR: RecoChain generates candidates by hierarchical Semantic ID prediction and then ranks them with SIM-based click estimation in the same Transformer, to close the gap between generation and ranking.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 2

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: TAOBAO-MM: 8.79M users, 35.4M items, 99M interactions, histories up to 1,000 interactions, with 128-dimensional multimodal item embeddings; adapted from CTR to sequential recommendation by keeping interaction histories and discarding exposure labels. Further filtering: not reported.
  - Source: TAOBAO-MM and adaptation: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.25787v1#S3.p1.
- **Split**: The official TAOBAO-MM train/validation/test split, without further sequence-level partitioning.
  - Source: Official split: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.25787v1#S3.p1.
- **Candidates**: not reported (full catalog versus sampled); top-K comes from C beam candidates (beam size 20 by default) that are re-ranked by a click-probability head.
  - Source: Beam candidates re-ranked; metrics: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.25787v1#S3.p4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2604.25787v1#S2.SS4.p1.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined.
  - Source: Official split with no unseen-item protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.25787v1#S3.p1.
- **SID**: 3-level RQ-Kmeans over the pretrained multimodal embeddings, plus a random fourth token s4 that makes the item-SID mapping one-to-one; codebook size per level: not reported.
  - Source: 3-level RQ-Kmeans plus a random fourth token: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.25787v1#S2.SS2.p1.
- **Inference budget**: Hierarchical beam search (default beam 20; 10 to 40 in Table 1) with KV cache, then for each candidate the top-10 most similar history items are appended and a rank head scores the candidate by continuing decoding. 2-layer decoder (hidden 1,024). Hardware, inference batch size, and latency: not reported.
  - Source: Generate-retrieve-rerank with KV reuse: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.25787v1#S2.SS3.SSS2.p2, https://arxiv.org/html/2604.25787v1#S2.SS3.SSS2.p4, https://arxiv.org/html/2604.25787v1#S2.SS4.p2; defaults: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.25787v1#S3.p4; model: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.25787v1#S3.p2.
- **Results from**: Tables 1-3 (Recall and NDCG at 5 and 10 before and after re-ranking, varying beam size, input sequence length, and retrieval length on TAOBAO-MM).
  - Source: Results: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.25787v1#S2.T1, https://arxiv.org/html/2604.25787v1#S2.T2, https://arxiv.org/html/2604.25787v1#S2.T3.

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: alternative; note: TIGER stops at beam-search retrieval; RecoChain appends retrieved history items to each beam candidate and re-ranks them in the same decoder.; where: RecoChain v1, Section 1 cites TIGER and OneRec as beam-search retrievers: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.25787v1#S1.p4.
- id: onerec; relation: alternative; note: OneRec unifies retrieval and ranking with preference alignment over sessions; RecoChain chains generation and a click-probability re-rank head with KV-cache reuse.; where: RecoChain v1, Section 1: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.25787v1#S1.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2604.25787v1#S1.p4.

### Notes

## 旧目录说明

迁自 `d61aa6c:README.md` 的条目说明，未沿用旧目录的收录分类。

束搜索生成候选 SID 后，再由排序头对候选打分重排。

## REGER

- Page: pages/papers/reger.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Training
- Representation: Text; Tokenization: RQ-VAE; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP → (NTP + Aux.); Inference: Beam
- TL;DR: REGER pretrains a generator to produce semantic neighbors' Semantic IDs, combines global and ID-boundary local attention, and distills a discriminative teacher's next-token distributions along the target prefix path.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 4

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Reviews 2014 Beauty/Sports/Toys and 2023 Instruments/Scientific/Games; 5-core filtering and maximum history 20 items.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.37584v1#S5.SS1.p1 ; #A1.T6
- **Split**: Per-user chronological leave-one-out: latest interaction test, second latest validation, all earlier interactions training.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.37584v1#A1.SS1.p1
- **Candidates**: not reported
  - Source: Evaluation settings give metrics and seeds but no evaluation universe: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.37584v1#S5.SS1 ; #A1.SS1
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. GSR semantic neighbors are drawn from the item catalog; tokenizer and frozen DuoRec teacher exposure to test items/interactions not explicitly separated.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.37584v1#S5.SS1.p1 ; #S4.SS1.p3 ; #S4.SS3.SSS2.p1 ; #A1.SS3.p1
- **SID**: RQ-VAE on Sentence-T5 embeddings reduced to 128 dimensions by PCA/whitening; semantic level count and codebook sizes not reported in paper. Extra token distinguishes identical semantic codes; suffix vocabulary size/assignment not reported. Dataset-specific SID mapping shared across recommender seeds.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.37584v1#S3.SS1.p1 ; #A1.SS3.p1
- **Inference budget**: Unconstrained beam 20 for validation/test, without teacher; teacher ablation uses beam 50. Recall/NDCG@5/10. Table 4 efficiency probe on TIGER+HCPD: one L40, FP32, test batch 256, KV cache off, 16 s for full Beauty test set. REGER-specific absolute inference time and general inference batch/hardware not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.37584v1#A1.SS3.p2 ; #A1.SS3.p4 ; #A1.T7 ; #S5.T4 ; #S5.SS4.p3
- **Results from**: Table 1: 2014 comparisons with reproduced baselines, three seeds 2024/2025/2026; Table 2: training objectives on TIGER; Table 3: REGER ablations. Table 6: 2023 results, with published baseline rows from Latte, OMEGA, DECOR and TopoTok papers.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.37584v1#S4.T1 ; #S5.T2 ; #S5.T3 ; #A1.T6 ; #A1.SS3.p2

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: predecessor; note: REGER uses residual-quantized SID generation and additionally tests its HCPD training objective directly on TIGER.; where: REGER v1, Section 3.1 and Table 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.37584v1#S3.SS1.p1; https://arxiv.org/html/2610.37584v1#S5.T2.
- id: gflowgr; relation: competitor; note: GFlowGR supervises generation with collaborative rewards and flow balance; HCPD directly matches teacher conditional preferences over legal prefix branches, using the same DuoRec teacher.; where: REGER v1, Section 5.4 and Table 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.37584v1#S5.SS4.p2; https://arxiv.org/html/2610.37584v1#S5.T2.
- id: apao; relation: competitor; note: APAO-pointwise is a compared GR training objective; HCPD instead distills full conditional distributions over legal next tokens along observed target paths.; where: REGER v1, Sections 4.3.2/5.1 and Table 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.37584v1#S4.SS3.SSS2.p4; https://arxiv.org/html/2610.37584v1#S5.SS1.p3; https://arxiv.org/html/2610.37584v1#S5.T2.
- id: pctx; relation: predecessor; note: REGER follows Pctx in choosing DuoRec as its auxiliary recommender, but transfers collaborative preferences through distillation rather than personalized tokenization.; where: REGER v1, Section 4.3.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.37584v1#S4.SS3.SSS2.p1.

## ReRankID

- Page: pages/papers/rerankid.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: Paradigms, Systems and Benchmarks
- Stage: No single stage
- Representation: Text; Tokenization: R-KM†; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP → RL; Inference: CoT+Greedy
- TL;DR: ReRankID is a controlled testbed, not a new recommender: models reason over and rerank slates shown only as Semantic IDs, and the paper compares post-training methods for this task.
- [Code](https://github.com/lilv98/ReRankID)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 2

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Kuaishou OpenOneRec-RecIF short-video release, 162074 source users; evaluation requires a renderable positive and >=256 items with both SID/caption histories.
  - Source: Section 3 and Appendix A.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.22797v1#S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.22797v1#A1.SS2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.22797v1#A5.p1
- **Split**: User-disjoint SFT/post-training/development/test partitions; 400 development and 400 test users, each balanced 200 explicit-engagement/200 long-view positives; histories precede targets.
  - Source: Appendix A.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.22797v1#A1.SS2.p1
- **Candidates**: sampled: 29 negatives plus one positive at anchor; slate sizes 10/20/30/50/100. Exposure-hard negatives plus uniform catalog fill; user-engaged items excluded. Exclusion of other historical exposures: not reported.
  - Source: Appendix A.2-A.3: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.22797v1#A1.SS2.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.22797v1#A1.SS3.p1
- **Visibility**: warm; evaluation release users/items were exposed during backbone pretraining, while post-training users are disjoint. Reranking supplied slates is a new task.
  - Source: Appendix A.4: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.22797v1#A1.SS4.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.22797v1#A1.SS4.p3
- **SID**: Released OpenOneRec three-code SIDs from quantized item-text embeddings; quantizer algorithm, codebook sizes and collision handling: not reported.
  - Source: Section 3 and Appendix A.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.22797v1#S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.22797v1#A1.SS1.p1
- **Inference budget**: SID: greedy reasoning 2048 tokens, fallback structured extraction 256 tokens from <=1200 reasoning characters; top-10 indices; A100/BF16. Text APIs: 8192-32768 output-token caps. Inference batch and latency: not reported.
  - Source: Appendix B.1, Table B.2 and Appendix E: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.22797v1#A2.SS1.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.22797v1#A2.T2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.22797v1#A5.p2
- **Results from**: This testbed's paired evaluations: Table 1 initial models/references, Table 2 post-training, Table D.1 full metrics. Each post-training method compares its own initializer; invalid outputs score zero.
  - Source: Tables 1/2/D.1 and Section 5.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.22797v1#S4.T1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.22797v1#S5.T2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.22797v1#A4.T1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.22797v1#S5.SS1.p1

### Related

- id: onerec-think; relation: alternative; note: OneRec-Think reasons before catalog-item generation; ReRankID reasons over a supplied candidate slate.; where: ReRankID v1, Section 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.22797v1#S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.
- id: tiger; relation: predecessor; note: TIGER's SID-generation paradigm is the background contrasted with SID-only slate reranking.; where: ReRankID v1, Section 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.22797v1#S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.

## ReSID

- Page: pages/papers/resid.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Representation
- Representation: Attr+CF; Tokenization: GAOQ; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP; Inference: Beam
- TL;DR: ReSID learns item representations from structured features with field-aware masked autoencoding and quantizes them with globally aligned orthogonal quantization, instead of LLM embeddings and generic quantizers.
- [Code](https://github.com/FuCongResearchSquad/ReSID)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon 2023: Musical Instruments, Video Games, Industrial/Scientific, Baby Products, Arts/Crafts/Sewing, Sports/Outdoors, Toys/Games, Health/Household, Beauty/Personal Care, Books. User/item 5-core; require store and three category-level fields.
  - Source: Section 4 and Appendix C: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.02338v1#S4.p3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.02338v1#A3.p1
- **Split**: Chronological per-user last/penultimate interactions test/validation; sliding training windows, maximum length 32. Evaluation target items absent from training are added to the training set.
  - Source: Section 4 and Appendix C: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.02338v1#S4.p6 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.02338v1#A3.p1
- **Candidates**: not reported
  - Source: Section 4 and Appendix E specify ranking metrics but no candidate protocol; 128 sampled negatives are a training objective: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.02338v1#S4.p6 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.02338v1#A5.p2
- **Visibility**: warm; evaluation target items absent from training are added to the training set.
  - Source: Appendix C explicitly inserts evaluation-only items into training: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.02338v1#A3.p1
- **SID**: GAOQ, 3 levels. Branching tuples: MI(32,40,19),VG(32,64,13),IS(24,80,14),BP(32,64,18),ACS(64,96,16),SO(128,128,11),TG(192,192,5),HH(50,512,8),BPC(96,192,11),Books(256,256,8). Global anchor-vocabulary sizes and collision handling: not reported.
  - Source: Table 7 and Algorithm 1: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.02338v1#A5.T7 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.02338v1#alg1
- **Inference budget**: Beam 50; Recall/NDCG@5/10. Inference hardware, batch size, latency: not reported; batch 2048 is training.
  - Source: Section 4 and Appendix E: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.02338v1#S4.p6 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.02338v1#A5.p4
- **Results from**: Tables 1/4 aggregate/full main comparison; Tables 2/5 ablations; Table 3 quantization runtime, not inference latency. All SID methods use this study's common T5-style generator; tokenizer settings follow original methods.
  - Source: Tables 1-5 and Appendix E: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.02338v1#S5.T1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.02338v1#S5.T2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.02338v1#S5.T3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.02338v1#A0.T4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.02338v1#A0.T5 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.02338v1#A5.p4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.02338v1#A5.p3

### Related

- id: letter; relation: competitor; note: LETTER is the strongest compared SID baseline and a quantization-runtime reference.; where: ReSID v1, Sections 5.1/5.4: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.02338v1#S5.SS1.p4; https://arxiv.org/html/2602.02338v1#S5.SS4.p1.
- id: tiger; relation: competitor; note: TIGER's semantic RQ-VAE tokenizer is compared under the common downstream generator.; where: ReSID v1, Appendix D/E: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.02338v1#A4.p3; https://arxiv.org/html/2602.02338v1#A5.p4.
- id: unger; relation: competitor; note: UNGER aligns semantic/collaborative representations; ReSID uses structured-field masked prediction.; where: ReSID v1, Section 3.1 and Appendix D: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.02338v1#S3.SS1.p3; https://arxiv.org/html/2602.02338v1#A4.p3.

## Retrieval-Grounded-Credit

- Page: pages/papers/retrieval-grounded-credit.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: IV. Utility
- Stage: Training
- Representation: Text†; Tokenization: RQ-VAE; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP → RL; Inference: CoT+C-Beam
- TL;DR: Retrieval-Grounded-Credit splits each reasoning trace into interest hypotheses, runs each as a query through a frozen retriever, and rewards hypotheses that hit the target, not only the decoded Semantic ID.
- [Code](https://github.com/YuFan-Microsoft/Retrieval-Grounded-Credit-Assignment-for-Generative-Recommendation)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Video Games, Office Products, Industrial and Scientific; October 2016-November 2018 interactions, 5-core filtering, histories capped at 10 items.
  - Source: v1 Section 4.1, pp. 5-6: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.29983v1#page=5
- **Split**: Per-user chronological last interaction test, penultimate validation; earlier interactions form sliding-window training pairs.
  - Source: v1 Section 4.1, pp. 5-6: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.29983v1#page=5
- **Candidates**: full catalog; trie contains all catalog SIDs, no sampled negatives.
  - Source: v1 Section 4.1, p. 6: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.29983v1#page=6
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. SIDReasoner tokenizers/mappings reused and frozen; tokenizer exposure to test items not reported.
  - Source: v1 Sections 3.1/4.1, pp. 3/5-6 define no unseen-item holdout: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.29983v1#page=3 and https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.29983v1#page=5
- **SID**: Domain-specific RQ-VAE: 3 levels x 256 codes; collision handling not reported.
  - Source: v1 Section 3.1, p. 3: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.29983v1#page=3
- **Inference budget**: Qwen3-1.7B; constrained beam returns 10 valid SIDs, metrics @5/10. Interests average 3.8/query set, each retrieves top-50 by frozen Qwen3-Embedding-4B exact cosine search. Hardware, inference batch size, latency not reported; training samples 16 trajectories/prompt, distinct from evaluation.
  - Source: v1 Section 4.1, p. 6, Figure 5, p. 9: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.29983v1#page=6 and https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.29983v1#page=9
- **Results from**: Original Table 4 RL controls/ours; external baselines are reported SIDReasoner results. Ours and SID-plus-trace control average three training seeds. Figure 5 interest-conditioned decoding includes target-aware oracle upper bounds.
  - Source: v1 Section 4.1/Table 4, p. 6, Figure 5, p. 9: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.29983v1#page=6 and https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.29983v1#page=9

### Related

- id: sidreasoner; relation: predecessor; note: Reuses SIDReasoner's tokenizer, alignment data, and evaluator; adds retrieval-grounded trace credit.; where: Retrieval-Grounded-Credit v1, Sections 3.1/3.2 and 4.1, pp. 3/6: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.29983v1#page=3; https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.29983v1#page=6.
- id: promise; relation: alternative; note: PROMISE rewards intermediate SID paths; this method verifies language interests through retrieval.; where: Retrieval-Grounded-Credit v1, Section 2.3, p. 3: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.29983v1#page=3.
- id: sapo; relation: alternative; note: SAPO aligns reasoning blocks with SID tokens; this method attributes query hits to interest lines.; where: Retrieval-Grounded-Credit v1, Section 2.3, p. 3: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.29983v1#page=3.

## RoFiGR

- Page: pages/papers/rofigr.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text+Img+CF; Tokenization: CF-Aligned MM RQ; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP + Aux.; Inference: C-Beam
- TL;DR: RoFiGR aligns coarse Semantic ID code vectors with collaborative embeddings and distills a sequential teacher over legal branches with level-adaptive weights, to reduce early routing errors.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Instruments, Arts, Games; 5-core filtering, histories capped at 20; catalogs 6250/9416/13839 items, respectively.
  - Source: Section 4.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.39470v1#S4.SS1.p1
- **Split**: Per-user chronological last event test, penultimate validation, earlier events training; teacher fitting and student optimization use the training partition.
  - Source: Section 4.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.39470v1#S4.SS1.p1
- **Candidates**: full catalog; no sampled negatives. A target absent from the decoded stream union scores zero.
  - Source: Section 4.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.39470v1#S4.SS1.p2
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. MISSRec teacher fits training interactions; item embeddings/scores are frozen offline. Tokenizer exposure to test items not separately reported.
  - Source: Sections 3.1/4.1 define no item holdout: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.39470v1#S3.SS1.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.39470v1#S4.SS1.p1
- **SID**: Separate text/image residual trees, each [64,256,256,512], code dimension 32. Collisions repaired at L4 or L3-L4, preserving L1-L2; complete SIDs uniquely identify items.
  - Source: Sections 3.2/3.6: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.39470v1#S3.SS2.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.39470v1#S3.SS6.p1
- **Inference budget**: Four independent trie beams of 20, item union and equal-weight stream fusion; HR@1/5/10, NDCG@5/10. One L20, FP16, batch 1, history 20: four-stream mean latency 56.7/60.9/63.7 ms (Instruments/Arts/Games); two-stream 31.8/33.5/35.1 ms. Includes encoding through final sorting; no online teacher/reranker.
  - Source: Sections 3.5/4.8: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.39470v1#S3.SS5.p3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.39470v1#S4.SS8.p2
- **Results from**: Original Table 3: five-seed main comparison; MACRec/SynGR retain native two-stream inference versus RoFiGR's four. Tables 5/6 separate task exposure, stream fusion, matched beam slots and candidate caps.
  - Source: Section 4.1/4.2 and Tables 3/5/6: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.39470v1#S4.SS1.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.39470v1#S3.T3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.39470v1#S4.SS2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.39470v1#S4.T5 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.39470v1#S4.T6

### Related

- id: macrec; relation: predecessor; note: RoFiGR retains MACRec's two-tree quantizer and adds coarse collaborative alignment.; where: RoFiGR v1, Section 3.2 and Table 3: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.39470v1#S3.SS2.p1; https://arxiv.org/html/2610.39470v1#S3.T3.

## ROS

- Page: pages/papers/ros.md
- Venue: ACL’26
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text+Geo; Tokenization: Geo-Prefix+RQ-VAE; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP → RL; Inference: CoT+C-Beam
- TL;DR: ROS adds hierarchical spatial Semantic IDs, a mobility chain-of-thought with locality-informed pruning, and spatial-guided reinforcement learning to LLM-based next-POI generation.
- [Code](https://github.com/amap-cvlab/Reasoning-Over-Space)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 4

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Foursquare NYC and TKY, Gowalla CA, prepared with the LLM4POI pipeline: users and POIs with fewer than 10 check-ins removed, trajectories segmented by a 24-hour time-gap threshold, and street-level addresses added by reverse geocoding. Sizes after preprocessing (users / POIs / check-ins): NYC 1,048 / 4,981 / 103,941; TKY 2,282 / 7,833 / 405,000; CA 3,957 / 9,690 / 238,369.
  - Source: Datasets and LLM4POI pipeline: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04562v2#S3.SS1.p1; 24-hour gap and sizes: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04562v2#A1.T10.
- **Split**: Temporal 80% / 10% / 10% train/validation/test split. Separate cross-city test: train on one city and evaluate on others.
  - Source: Temporal 80/10/10 split keeping test users and POIs observed: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04562v2#S3.SS1.p1; cross-city: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04562v2#S3.T6.
- **Candidates**: n/a for candidate ranking: the model outputs exactly one POI per request and is scored by HR@1.
  - Source: One recommendation per request, HR@1: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04562v2#S3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.
- **Visibility**: warm; validation and test users and POIs are kept only if observed in training. The cross-city test (Table 6) uses POIs of another city; their tokenizer exposure is not reported.
  - Source: Test users and POIs observed in training: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04562v2#S3.SS1.p1.
- **SID**: Hierarchical spatial SID [g; s; u]: two S2-cell locality tokens (after removing the dataset-wide common prefix), two semantic tokens from a 2-level residual quantizer with 28 codes per level over Qwen-0.6B category embeddings, and a sequential suffix token within each (g, s) pair that makes IDs unique (at most 8 suffix values observed).
  - Source: HS-SID construction: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04562v2#A1.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.
- **Inference budget**: Generates a mobility chain-of-thought and then one POI SID per request (three inference runs averaged); decoding settings not reported. Qwen3-4B student on 8 NVIDIA H20 GPUs; inference batch size and latency: not reported.
  - Source: One output per request, hardware: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04562v2#S3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04562v2#S3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.
- **Results from**: Table 1 (HR@1 on NYC, TKY, CA versus traditional, neural, and LLM-based baselines); Tables 2-5 and Figure 3 (SID design, CoT stages, geographic cues, reward weights); Table 6 (cross-city generalization).
  - Source: Main: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04562v2#S3.T1; ablations: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04562v2#S3.T2, https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04562v2#S3.T3, https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04562v2#S3.T4, https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04562v2#S3.T5; RL weights: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04562v2#S3.F3; cross-city: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04562v2#S3.T6.

### Related

- id: oneloc; relation: alternative; note: OneLoc injects geography into the SID input and rewards; ROS encodes geography directly as S2-cell prefix tokens.; where: ROS v2, Section 1 cites OneLoc: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04562v2#S1.p3.
- id: lgsid; relation: alternative; note: LGSID aligns embeddings with geographic rewards before quantization; ROS separates geographic and semantic tokens inside the SID.; where: ROS v2, Section 1 cites LGSID: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04562v2#S1.p3.

### Notes

## 旧卡片说明

迁自 `d61aa6c:papers/ros.md`。保留方法说明、实验叙述与局限；本轮只对照现有记录处理明确冲突，未重新逐句核查原论文。分类和规格以页面上方由记录生成的表格为准。

### ROS：空间推理增强的生成式下一兴趣点推荐

> ROS 将地理关系显式纳入下一 POI 推理过程，通过层次化空间 SID、移动思维链和空间引导强化学习生成可行地点。

### 研究动机与问题定义

下一 POI 不是普通的物品分类：用户兴趣、时间规律和空间可达性共同决定目的地。已有 LLM 推荐方法虽能生成 SID，却常把空间信息作为文本或单步条件，缺少显式的候选构造和可行性判断。ROS 将推荐建模为带空间约束的多阶段决策。

### TL;DR（核心摘要）

`坐标/网格/类别 → 空间SID → 用户画像与候选空间 → 移动CoT剪枝 → 生成POI SID`

ROS 把 POI SID 分成地理前缀、语义锚点和区分性后缀。模型先通过双向对齐和序列预训练学习 SID 与地址/类别的对应关系，再用三步 Mobility CoT 建立用户画像、构造意图候选并进行局部性剪枝，最后用空间、SID 和格式奖励进行强化学习。

### 输入与使用场景

| 方面 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| 使用信息 | GPS、S2 网格、POI 类别、地址、用户历史和时间 |
| 信息融入位置 | SID 结构、预训练任务、思维链和强化学习奖励 |
| 语义标识结构 | 层次化、定长离散序列 |
| 适用场景 | 下一 POI、跨城市迁移和地理可行性推荐 |

### 方法设计

#### 2.1 问题形式化
给定用户历史轨迹、时间和上下文，模型需要生成下一 POI 的完整 SID。与只预测一个标签不同，ROS 将生成过程拆为画像分析、候选空间构造和局部性筛选等有顺序的决策。

#### 2.2 空间语义标识
地理前缀由 GPS 映射到 S2 网格，再转换为层次化六边形 token；语义锚点由 POI 类别等文本信息经过编码和 RQ-VAE 量化得到；后缀用于区分同一地理和语义区域内的不同 POI。三者拼接为 Hierarchical Spatial SID。

#### 2.2.2 SID 对齐预训练
模型使用双向 SID-文本/地址对齐任务，使 SID 能预测 POI 的类别和地址，也使文本能恢复 SID。另一个序列预训练任务让模型学习移动轨迹中的时间、类别重复和邻域连续性。

#### 2.3 Mobility CoT 推理
第一步从历史轨迹提炼用户移动画像；第二步根据画像和当前上下文形成候选 POI 空间；第三步依据访问频率、时间和空间邻近性对候选进行局部性剪枝，再生成目标 SID。这种流程把地理可行性变成显式推理条件。

#### 2.4 空间引导强化学习
训练时从策略模型采样推理轨迹，奖励由空间距离、SID 层次匹配和格式合法性组成，并通过 GRPO 优化。层级 SID 奖励使正确的地理前缀和语义部分获得分层反馈。

### 实验结论

- 在三个 LBSN 数据集上，ROS 相比 LLM 基线取得更高命中率，论文报告相对提升超过 10%。
- 移动 CoT 和空间奖励的消融支持显式候选构造与地理剪枝的作用。
- 跨城市实验显示模型具有较好的迁移能力，但论文指出短时间长距离移动的交通先验仍未充分建模。

### 局限性与研究定位

#### 局限性

- 当前地理可行性主要采用短时间内长距离移动不太可能的单调先验，可能低估地铁、高速等交通支持的远距离移动。
- 多阶段思维链会增加生成 token 和推理成本，在线延迟比较未充分展开。

#### 研究定位

ROS 代表把“空间推理”引入 Semantic ID 生成推荐的路线，适合放在“推理增强与地理约束生成推荐”章节。

### 相关资源

- [论文原文](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.04562)

### 标签

`空间推理` · `层次化SID` · `移动思维链` · `空间强化学习`

## RPG

- Page: pages/papers/rpg.md
- Venue: KDD’25
- Problem: V. Efficiency
- Stage: Backbone
- Representation: Text+Img; Tokenization: Par. OPQ; Backbone: Non-AR; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: MTP; Inference: Graph
- TL;DR: RPG predicts long, unordered OPQ Semantic IDs in parallel with a multi-token prediction loss and decodes over a graph of valid IDs, replacing autoregressive beam search over short IDs.
- [Code](https://github.com/facebookresearch/RPG_KDD2025)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Reviews: Sports and Outdoors, Beauty, Toys and Games, and CDs and Vinyl; filtering rules: not reported.
  - Source: The four Amazon categories and chronological protocol are stated, but 5-core or other filtering rules are not stated in the body or appendix; https://arxiv.org/html/2506.05781v1#S3.SS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2506.05781v1#S3.SS1.p2, dataset counts in https://arxiv.org/html/2506.05781v1#S2.T1.

The separate inference description builds a graph over valid catalog items and starts with b random valid nodes; this does not by itself establish the evaluation candidate protocol; https://arxiv.org/html/2506.05781v1#S2.SS3.SSS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2506.05781v1#S2.SS3.SSS2.p2.

Sports-only fixed-configuration scaling experiment reports approximately 15x faster inference and 25x lower runtime memory than TIGER; these are not total-storage reductions or per-request latency claims.
  - Source: Table 6 supplies b/k/q; Appendix B supplies hardware and separates checkpoint selection from graph-budget tuning; the batch size 256 in Section 3.1 is a training setting, not an inference setting; https://arxiv.org/html/2506.05781v1#A2.T6, https://arxiv.org/html/2506.05781v1#A2.p1, https://arxiv.org/html/2506.05781v1#S3.SS1.p6. ### Notes

## At a Glance

Key Findings: With 64-token IDs, RPG outperforms generative baselines by an average of 12.6% on NDCG@10 and also improves inference efficiency (Abstract).
Limitation: The authors assume that the tokens of an SID are conditionally independent given the input sequence, and the decoding graph built after training serves only until the model is retrained or the items are re-tokenized (Sec. 2.2.1, Sec. 2.3.1).

### 1. Why This Paper Matters

Generative recommenders such as TIGER decode a Semantic ID (SID) token by token with beam search, which needs several forward passes of the generator per recommendation. As a result, existing models keep SIDs short, often 4 tokens (Abstract). RPG instead predicts every token of a long, unordered SID in one forward pass and searches a graph of valid SIDs at inference. ACERec and SPRINT, later papers in the same matrix cell, use the same `Par. OPQ` tokenization and `Non-AR` backbone.

> "Running beam search for 32 steps would be computationally prohibitive." (Sec. 1)

### 2. How It Works

#### Overview

```
Item features → semantic encoder → item embedding
  │
  ▼  OPQ: one codebook per subvector
Unordered SID (c1, ..., cm), m up to 64
  │
  ▼  token embeddings pooled per item; Transformer decoder over the history
Sequence representation s
  │
  ▼  m MLP heads, one softmax per codebook (MTP loss in training)
Cached token log-probabilities p(1), ..., p(m)
  │
  ▼  graph-constrained decoding: sample b items, add graph neighbors, keep the best b, repeat q times
Top-K items
```

#### Step 1: Long SIDs from OPQ

RPG replaces residual quantization with optimized product quantization (OPQ), so that the tokens can be predicted in parallel rather than one after another (Sec. 2.1.1).

> "To align with parallel decoding, we tokenize each item into an unordered long semantic ID (up to 64 tokens per item) using optimized product quantization (Jégou et al., 2011; Ge et al., 2014)." (Sec. 1)

OPQ splits the item's semantic embedding into $`m`$ subvectors and quantizes each subvector with its own codebook of size $`M`$ (Sec. 2.1.1). The paper cites OPQ and does not restate its rotation or codebook training. The standard product-quantization assignment is:

```math
\mathbf{x}_i = \left[\mathbf{x}_i^{(1)}; \dots; \mathbf{x}_i^{(m)}\right], \qquad c_{i,j} = \arg\min_{c \in \mathcal{C}^{(j)}} \left\| \mathbf{x}_i^{(j)} - \mathbf{a}_c^{(j)} \right\|_2^2
```

where:
- $`\mathbf{x}_i`$ is the semantic embedding of item $`i`$ after the OPQ rotation;
- $`\mathbf{x}_i^{(j)}`$ is its $`j`$-th subvector;
- $`\mathcal{C}^{(j)}`$ is the $`j`$-th codebook with $`M`$ codewords $`\mathbf{a}_c^{(j)}`$;
- $`c_{i,j}`$ is the $`j`$-th token of the SID of item $`i`$.

"Unordered" means that no token is predicted from the tokens before it. Position $`j`$ still belongs to codebook $`j`$ (Sec. 2.1.1). Different items can share the same token set. Each item keeps its own node in the decoding graph, and the authors describe such collisions as very unlikely with 64-token IDs (Appendix C).

#### Step 2: Item-Level Input

A 64-token SID per history item would make the input sequence too long (Sec. 2.1.2). RPG gives each codebook a learnable token embedding table $`\mathbf{E}_j \in \mathbb{R}^{M \times d}`$ and pools the $`m`$ token embeddings of an item into one vector $`\mathbf{v}_i = \mathrm{Aggr}(\mathbf{e}_{1,c_{i,1}}, \dots, \mathbf{e}_{m,c_{i,m}})`$ with mean or max pooling (Sec. 2.1.2). A Transformer decoder reads the sequence $`\mathbf{v}_1, \dots, \mathbf{v}_{t-1}`$ and outputs a sequence representation $`\mathbf{s} \in \mathbb{R}^{d}`$ (Sec. 2.2.1).

#### Step 3: Parallel Prediction with the MTP Loss

RPG predicts each token of the next SID with its own head and trains all heads with a multi-token prediction (MTP) loss.

> "Since each token produced by OPQ encodes a separate subvector of the target item's semantic representation, we assume that tokens in the tuple are conditionally independent given the input sequence s." (Sec. 2.2.1)

```math
\mathcal{L} = -\sum_{j=1}^{m} \log \mathbb{P}^{(j)}(c_{t,j} \mid s) = -\sum_{j=1}^{m} \log \frac{\exp\left(\mathbf{e}_{c_{t,j}}^{\top} g_j(\mathbf{s}) / \tau\right)}{\sum_{c \in \mathcal{C}^{(j)}} \exp\left(\mathbf{e}_{c}^{\top} g_j(\mathbf{s}) / \tau\right)}
```

where:
- $`c_{t,j}`$ is the $`j`$-th token of the target item's SID;
- $`g_j`$ is an MLP projection head for codebook $`j`$;
- $`\mathbf{e}_c`$ is the token embedding of token $`c`$;
- $`\tau`$ is a temperature (Eq. 1).

#### Step 4: Cached Token Scores

For one input sequence, RPG computes each codebook's token distribution once and caches it (Eq. 2). The score of any candidate SID is then a sum of cached values (Eq. 3):

```math
\mathbf{p}^{(j)} = \mathrm{softmax}\left(\mathbf{E}_j\, g_j(\mathbf{s}) / \tau\right) \in \mathbb{R}^{M}, \qquad \mathrm{score}(c_1, \dots, c_m) = \sum_{j=1}^{m} \log p^{(j)}_{c_j}
```

where $`p^{(j)}_{c_j}`$ is the entry of $`\mathbf{p}^{(j)}`$ for token $`c_j`$ (Sec. 2.2.2).

#### Step 5: Graph-Constrained Decoding

After training, RPG builds a graph whose nodes are the SIDs of catalog items (Sec. 2.3.1). The similarity of two SIDs is the sum of the inner products of their token embeddings:

```math
\mathrm{sim}(i, i') = \sum_{j=1}^{m} \mathbf{e}_{j,c_{i,j}}^{\top}\, \mathbf{e}_{j,c_{i',j}}
```

Each node keeps its $`k`$ most similar neighbors (Sec. 2.3.1), and each node has an edge to itself (Sec. 2.3.2). The graph is reused until the model is retrained or the items are re-tokenized (Sec. 2.3.1). Decoding then runs four steps (Sec. 2.3.2):

1. Sample $`b`$ SIDs from the catalog as the initial beam.
2. Add all $`b \times k`$ graph neighbors of the beam to a candidate set.
3. Score the candidates with the cached values and keep the best $`b`$.
4. Repeat steps 2 and 3 for $`q`$ iterations and return the final beam as the top-$`K`$ items.

> "Since neighboring nodes in the graph tend to have similar logits, we expand the beam by propagating through the graph, including all b×k neighbors of the current beam into a temporary set." (Sec. 2.3.2)

```python
import torch

def rpg_decode(s, heads, token_emb, item_codes, neighbors, b=10, q=2, tau=0.05):
    """
    s:          [d] sequence representation of one user
    heads:      list of m projection heads g_j, each mapping [d] -> [d]
    token_emb:  [m, M, d] token embedding tables E_j
    item_codes: [N, m] SID of every catalog item; entry j indexes codebook j
    neighbors:  [N, k] graph neighbors of every item; the item itself is included here,
                although the paper does not state whether the self-edge counts toward k
    """
    m = item_codes.size(1)
    # Eq. 2: one softmax per codebook, cached for this user
    proj = torch.stack([g(s) for g in heads])                                         # [m, d]
    log_p = torch.log_softmax(torch.einsum("jcd,jd->jc", token_emb, proj) / tau, -1)  # [m, M]
    # Eq. 3 for the whole catalog; the paper scores only the visited nodes (Sec. 2.3)
    scores = log_p[torch.arange(m), item_codes].sum(dim=-1)                          # [N]
    # step 1: random initial beam of b valid SIDs
    beam = torch.randperm(item_codes.size(0))[:b]                                     # [b]
    for _ in range(q):
        # step 2: beam plus graph neighbors, without duplicates
        cand = torch.unique(neighbors[beam].reshape(-1))                              # [<= b*k]
        # step 3: keep the b best candidates
        beam = cand[torch.topk(scores[cand], k=min(b, cand.numel())).indices]
    return beam                                                                       # item indices
```

Simplifications: The code scores every item in the catalog (`scores` covers the whole catalog) before the graph search. It therefore does not follow Sec. 2.3.3, which scores only the nodes visited along graph edges, and it does not reproduce the paper's inference efficiency. It also takes the heads, token embeddings, and graph as inputs, and omits OPQ, the Transformer decoder, MTP training, and graph construction.

> "Compared to generative models like TIGER (Rajput et al., 2023), RPG reduces the number of sequence encoder forward passes per input instance from approximately O(bm) to just O(1), greatly improving inference efficiency (Section 3.3)." (Sec. 2.4.2)

### 3. Experimental Findings

- Overall: with 64-token IDs, RPG outperforms the generative baselines by an average of 12.6% on NDCG@10 (Abstract). Table 2 gives the full comparison.
- Efficiency: on Sports, RPG uses less runtime memory and less inference time than TIGER (Sec. 3.3, Fig. 3).

  > "Moreover, RPG reduces runtime memory consumption by nearly 25× and achieves an inference speedup of almost 15× compared to TIGER." (Sec. 3.3)

- ID length: performance does not rise with every increase in length. The best lengths are 16 on Sports, 32 on Beauty, 16 on Toys, and 64 on CDs (Sec. 3.5.1, Fig. 4).

  > "From Figure 4, we observe that, in general, longer OPQ-based semantic IDs lead to better performance. However, for smaller datasets, they may converge earlier." (Sec. 3.5.1)

- Semantic encoder: the main runs use OpenAI text-embedding-3-large, and Table 4 repeats the comparison with sentence-t5-base for parity with benchmark results (Sec. 3.1, Sec. 3.5.2).
- Long-tail items: on Sports, the authors state that RPG achieves the best overall performance across the training-frequency groups (Sec. 3.5.3, Fig. 5).

### 4. Limitations & Critical Analysis

**Stated by the authors.** The parallel heads rest on an assumption: the tokens of an SID are conditionally independent given the input sequence (Sec. 2.2.1). The authors state that different items can share the same token set (Appendix C). They also state that the efficiency study uses one fixed set of hyperparameters, and that its runtime memory covers the GPU memory for computing logits, not the storage of model parameters (Sec. 3.3).

**Our analysis.**

- The score of an SID is a sum of per-token scores (Eq. 3), so the model cannot express dependencies between tokens of one SID. In the same cell, ACERec adds contrastive and auxiliary objectives (`MTP + Ctr. + Aux.`), and SPRINT replaces the objective with `Dual-level Flow Ctr.`; both keep `Par. OPQ` and `Non-AR`.
- The decoding graph is an index outside the model. It has one node per catalog item and must be rebuilt after retraining or re-tokenization (Sec. 2.3.1).
- The evaluation covers four Amazon datasets. The paper reports no online or industrial test.

## S2GR

- Page: pages/papers/s2gr.md
- Venue: KDD’26
- Problem: III. SID–Model Alignment
- Stage: Backbone
- Representation: Text+CF; Tokenization: CoBa RQ-VAE; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP + Ctr.; Inference: Beam
- TL;DR: S2GR inserts a thinking token before each Semantic ID step, supervised contrastively with codebook cluster distributions, and builds the codebook with co-occurrence, load-balancing, and uniformity objectives.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Beauty (May 1996-September 2014; 22,363 users / 12,101 items / 198,502 interactions) and an industrial short-video dataset of long-play records from sampled active users over 2 consecutive days (37,500 users / 1,086,872 items / 3,778,562 interactions). Dataset filtering rules: not reported; a table footnote states that user sequences shorter than 10 are filtered out during testing.
  - Source: Datasets and statistics: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.18664v3#S5.SS1.SSS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2601.18664v3#S5.T1; test-time length filter: footnote 1 of https://arxiv.org/html/2601.18664v3#S5.T2.
- **Split**: not reported (the train/validation/test rule is not described). The co-occurrence graph for codebook optimization uses history sequences that precede those used for training and evaluation. Online: 7-day A/B test with 5.25% of users per group, TIGER as control.
  - Source: No split rule stated; leakage control for co-occurrence: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.18664v3#S5.SS1.SSS3.p1; online test: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.18664v3#S5.SS4.p1.
- **Candidates**: not reported (full catalog versus sampled evaluation candidates); HR and NDCG at 5 and 10 (Beauty) and at 10 and 100 (industrial).
  - Source: Metrics only: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.18664v3#S5.SS1.SSS1.p1.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined.
  - Source: No unseen-item protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.18664v3#S5.SS1.SSS1.p1.
- **SID**: 3 levels x 256 codes from a codebook-balanced RQ-VAE (CoBa RQ-VAE) over Qwen3-Embedding-4B embeddings smoothed by multi-hop co-occurrence propagation; collision handling: not reported (independent coding rate 99.30% on Beauty, 76.25% industrial).
  - Source: 3 levels x 256, behavior-aligned embeddings and balanced RQ-VAE: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.18664v3#S5.SS1.SSS3.p1, https://arxiv.org/html/2601.18664v3#S4.SS2.SSS1.p3, https://arxiv.org/html/2601.18664v3#S4.SS2.SSS2.p1; utilization and ICR: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.18664v3#S5.T3.
- **Inference budget**: Thinking tokens are generated before each SID level; T5 with 4 encoder and 4 decoder layers (same as the TIGER baseline). Beam width, hardware, inference batch size, and latency: not reported.
  - Source: T5 4+4 layers matching TIGER: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.18664v3#S5.SS1.SSS3.p1; decoding settings not found.
- **Results from**: Table 2 (Beauty and industrial versus sequential, reasoning, and TIGER baselines); Table 3 (tokenizer CUR and ICR); Table 4 and Section 5.4 (7-day online A/B against TIGER).
  - Source: Main: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.18664v3#S5.T2; tokenizers: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.18664v3#S5.T3; online: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.18664v3#S5.SS4.p1.

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: competitor; note: TIGER predicts SID codes directly; S2GR inserts thinking tokens aligned with coarse code semantics before each SID level and balances the codebook with behavior-aligned embeddings.; where: S2GR v3, baselines: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.18664v3#S5.I1.i6.p1; Table 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.18664v3#S5.T2; online control group: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.18664v3#S5.SS4.p1.

- id: plum; relation: alternative; note: PLUM feeds ID tokens to a pretrained LLM for explicit reasoning, whereas S2GR adds lightweight implicit reasoning steps.; where: S2GR v3, Section 2.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.18664v3#S2.SS2.p2.

### Notes

## 旧卡片说明

迁自 `d61aa6c:papers/s2gr.md`。保留方法说明、实验叙述与局限；本轮只对照现有记录处理明确冲突，未重新逐句核查原论文。分类和规格以页面上方由记录生成的表格为准。

### S2GR：潜空间逐步语义引导推理

> S2GR 在生成 SID 的每一步注入语义引导信号，使模型在潜空间中逐步缩小推荐候选范围。

### 研究动机与问题定义

传统生成器通常只在最终 SID 上接受监督，缺乏对中间 token 决策的细粒度引导。S2GR 研究如何利用 SID 层次结构在生成过程中表达逐步推理。

### TL;DR（核心摘要）

`交互图与物品内容 → 协同平衡RQ-VAE → 逐步语义引导 → 生成SID → 推荐物品`

模型先构造物品共现图并学习兼顾协同关系和码本均衡的 RQ-VAE。生成时把逐步思考 token 插入 SID 序列，并用语义引导对齐监督中间状态；完整 SID 直接确定物品。

### 输入与使用场景

| 方面 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| 使用信息 | 用户交互、物品内容和物品共现图 |
| 信息融入位置 | RQ-VAE、生成中间状态和对齐目标 |
| 语义标识结构 | 层次化序列，交织推理 token |
| 适用场景 | 常规和工业生成式推荐 |

### 方法设计

#### 4.1 协同与均衡 RQ-VAE
S2GR 先根据物品共现构建协同图，并在 RQ-VAE 中加入码本均衡约束。量化器得到层次化 SID，同时减少 codeword 使用偏斜，为后续逐步推理提供稳定结构。

#### 4.2 逐步语义引导推理
模型把 thinking token 交织到 SID 生成过程中。每个 thinking token 对应一个层次或候选簇，生成器据此从粗粒度语义逐步缩小到细粒度 code；中间状态接受语义对齐监督。

#### 4.3 训练与部署
训练联合 next-item 生成、语义-行为对齐、码本均衡和逐步监督。推理时按层次顺序生成 thinking token 与 SID，最终完整标识直接映射到物品。论文还报告线上测试和不同规模分析。

### 实验结论

- 逐步语义引导提升了推荐效果。
- 协同平衡量化和中间状态监督均有贡献。
- 论文报告了工业线上测试结果。

### 局限性与研究定位

#### 局限性
- 交织推理 token 增加序列长度与服务成本。
- 工业线上收益的可复现细节有限。

#### 研究定位
S2GR 的贡献是把 SID 的层次结构转化为逐步推理信号，适合放在“潜空间推理与结构化生成”章节。

### 标签

`潜空间推理` · `语义引导` · `协同量化` · `生成式推荐`

### 架构图来源

*图源：原论文，图3。图片使用许可待核实。*

- 使用场景：工业推荐。

## SAGE-SID

- Page: pages/papers/sage-sid.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: IV. Utility

- Relations: 3

## SAHL

- Page: pages/papers/sahl.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: IV. Utility
- Stage: Training
- Representation: Text; Tokenization: SRBQ; Backbone: Non-AR; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: (MTP + Masked Rec.) → MTP; Inference: Graph
- TL;DR: SAHL quantizes items with SRBQ into a balanced token-subspace-item hierarchy and reconstructs user history at those granularities, moving by curriculum to next-item prediction, instead of next-item prediction alone.
- [Code](https://github.com/CQU-MM-Intelligent-Lab/SAHL)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Reviews 2014 Beauty, Toys and Games, Sports and Outdoors, CDs and Vinyl, in this order; user/item 5-core.
  - Source: Section 5.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.25093v1#S5.SS1.p1
- **Split**: Per-user chronological leave-one-out: last interaction test, penultimate validation, earlier interactions train.
  - Source: Section 5.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.25093v1#S5.SS2.p1
- **Candidates**: not reported
  - Source: Sections 5.2/5.4 specify graph-constrained decoding but not full-catalog versus sampled-negative evaluation: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.25093v1#S5.SS2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.25093v1#S5.SS4.p2
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Low-frequency analysis is explicitly near-cold, not zero-interaction.
  - Source: Section 6.11.4: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.25093v1#S6.SS11.SSS4.p1
- **SID**: SRBQ: 4/8/8/16 subspaces x 4 residual levels x 256 codes, producing 16/32/32/64 tokens in dataset order. Colliding items remain separate, equal-scored candidates; fixed catalog indices break ties.
  - Source: Sections 4.2.2/5.4: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.25093v1#S4.SS2.SSS2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.25093v1#S5.SS4.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.25093v1#S5.SS4.p2
- **Inference budget**: Dataset order: beam 100/200/100/50, graph neighbors 100/100/200/500, propagation depths 3/5/2/4; temperature 0.03; Recall/NDCG@5/10. Inference hardware, batch size and latency not reported; A6000 timings concern training.
  - Source: Section 5.4 and Section 6.11.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.25093v1#S5.SS4.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.25093v1#S6.SS11.SSS2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.25093v1#S6.SS11.SSS2.p3
- **Results from**: Table 2: overall comparison. RPG*, MHL and SAHL use matched controlled experiments; Tlow follows its published matched protocol. Other baseline score provenance not reported.
  - Source: Sections 5.3/6.1 and Table 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.25093v1#S5.SS3.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.25093v1#S6.SS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.25093v1#S5.T2

## SAPO

- Page: pages/papers/sapo.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: IV. Utility
- Stage: Training
- Representation: Text; Tokenization: RQ-VAE; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP → RL; Inference: CoT+C-Beam
- TL;DR: SAPO computes a separate group-relative advantage for each reasoning step, one thinking block plus one Semantic ID token, instead of broadcasting one exact-match advantage to the whole response.
- [Code](https://github.com/zhengzaiyi/SAPO)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Reviews Office Products, Video Games, Industrial & Scientific; October 2016-November 2018; 5-core users/items. Further history truncation not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.17648v1#S5.SS1.p1 ; #A8.p1
- **Split**: Per-user chronological leave-one-out: last item test, second last validation, remaining prefix training; all valid sliding-window history/target pairs used for training.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.17648v1#A8.p1
- **Candidates**: not reported
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.17648v1#S5.SS1 ; #S5.SS2.p1 ; #A8
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Tokenizer fitting exposure to test items not explicitly separated.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.17648v1#A8.p1 ; #A8.p3
- **SID**: RQ-VAE: 3 x 256 over title/category/brand/description embeddings. Paper reports training until every item has a unique tuple, with no extra collision suffix; a separate collision-assignment rule is not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.17648v1#A8.p3
- **Inference budget**: Qwen3-1.7B generates three thinking blocks followed by three contiguous SID tokens, enabling trie-constrained beam decoding and KV reuse; Recall/NDCG@5/10. Test beam width, reasoning cap, hardware allocation, batch size and latency not reported. The 16 rollouts/prompt, 1024-token cap and 4 H100s are training settings.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.17648v1#A6.p2 ; #A9.SS2.p1 ; #A10.p1 ; #A11.p2
- **Results from**: Original Table 1: main comparison; SIDReasoner uses author checkpoints evaluated by this paper, all other baselines reimplemented. Table 2: SAPO component ablations; Table 7: training overhead, not inference latency.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.17648v1#S5.T1 ; #S5.T2 ; #S5.SS1.p2 ; #A12.T7

### Related

- id: sidreasoner; relation: predecessor; note: SAPO shares SIDReasoner Stage 1/2 checkpoints but replaces rollout-level Stage 3 credit with rewards and advantages for thinking-block/SID-token pairs.; where: SAPO v1, Appendix G and Section 5.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.17648v1#A7.p3; https://arxiv.org/html/2605.17648v1#S5.SS2.p2.

## SCRec

- Page: pages/papers/screc.md
- Venue: RecSys’26
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Representation
- Representation: Text+CF; Tokenization: RQ-VAE; Backbone: Non-AR / Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: MTP + Ctr.; Inference: Scoring / Beam†
- TL;DR: SCRec injects textualized collaborative signals into semantic tokenization, recalibrates semantic priors with learnable code embeddings during generation, and aligns codebook and semantic spaces, to couple the two stages.
- [Code](https://github.com/DanJiayi/SCRec)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Reviews Beauty, Sports and Outdoors, Toys and Games. Filtering and maximum history length not reported directly; preprocessing settings delegated to RPG.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2609.13678v1#S4.SS1.p1 ; #S4.SS1.p5
- **Split**: Per-user chronological leave-last-out: final interaction test, penultimate validation, remaining interactions training; shared across baselines.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2609.13678v1#S4.SS1.p1
- **Candidates**: not reported; evaluation configurations are delegated to RPG without specifying the candidate universe or negative sampling.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2609.13678v1#S4.SS1.p4 ; #S4.SS1.p5
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. SASRec for top-10 collaborative neighbors is pretrained on training data; tokenizer fitting exposure to test items not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2609.13678v1#S4.SS1.p1 ; #S4.SS1.p5
- **SID**: RQ-VAE with 256 entries/codebook and latent dimension 256, quantizing fused item-text and textualized-neighbor embeddings. Semantic level count and collision handling not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2609.13678v1#S3.SS1.p9 ; #S4.SS1.p5
- **Inference budget**: Main decoder-only backbone follows RPG, with TIGER/LIGER module variants. Exact main inference procedure, prediction-head structure and beam width not reported; Recall/NDCG@5/10. General experiment GPU: one RTX 4090; inference batch size and absolute latency not reported. Beauty module inference-time increases: TIGER 6.19%, LIGER 0.54%, averaged over ten runs.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2609.13678v1#S3.SS2.p5 ; #S4.SS1.p4 ; #S4.SS1.p5 ; #S4.SS5.p1 ; #S4.SS5.p2
- **Results from**: Original Table 1: main comparison; baselines including RPG rerun in the same environment, TIGER/LIGER evaluated through the same LIGER codebase. Table 2: ablations; Table 3: backbone extensions; Tables 4-5: alternative fusion/alignment. No imported baseline results stated.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2609.13678v1#S4.T1 ; #S4.T2 ; #S4.T3 ; #S4.T4 ; #S4.T5 ; #S4.SS1.p5

### Related

- id: rpg; relation: predecessor; note: SCRec adopts a decoder-only backbone following RPG but replaces tokenization with collaborative-enhanced RQ-VAE and adds semantic/manifold alignment modules.; where: SCRec v1, Sections 3.1/4.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2609.13678v1#S3.SS1.p9; https://arxiv.org/html/2609.13678v1#S4.SS1.p5.
- id: tiger; relation: predecessor; note: SCRec is also added to TIGER as a reusable module, improving collaborative input to tokenization and semantic guidance during generation.; where: SCRec v1, Section 4.5 and Table 3: https://arxiv.org/html/2609.13678v1#S4.SS5.p1; https://arxiv.org/html/2609.13678v1#S4.T3.
- id: liger; relation: predecessor; note: SCRec augments the hybrid LIGER backbone with the same reusable cross-stage supplementation module and measures its inference overhead.; where: SCRec v1, Section 4.5 and Table 3: https://arxiv.org/html/2609.13678v1#S4.SS5.p1; https://arxiv.org/html/2609.13678v1#S4.SS5.p2; https://arxiv.org/html/2609.13678v1#S4.T3.

## SEATER

- Page: pages/papers/seater.md
- Venue: SIGIR-AP’24
- Problem: V. Efficiency
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: CF; Tokenization: Tree-Clus.; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP + Ctr.; Inference: C-Beam
- TL;DR: SEATER builds item identifiers on a balanced k-ary tree and trains an encoder-decoder with generation, infoNCE, and triplet losses, to learn token hierarchy with equal inference cost for all items.
- [Code](https://github.com/Ethan00Si/SEATER_Generative_Retrieval)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Yelp 2018 (31,668 users / 38,048 items), Amazon Books (459,133 / 313,966), MIND-small News (50,000 / 39,865), and an industrial Micro-Video dataset of 0.75 million randomly selected users over two weeks in 2023 (6.1 million items, 85 million interactions, unfiltered). Public-dataset filtering: not reported.
  - Source: Datasets: https://arxiv.org/html/2309.13375v2#S5.SS1.SSS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2309.13375v2#S5.SS1.SSS1.p2; statistics: https://arxiv.org/html/2309.13375v2#S5.T2.
- **Split**: Users are partitioned 8:1:1 into training, validation, and test; for each evaluated user the first 80% of behaviors are context and the remaining 20% are ground truth (ComiRec protocol).
  - Source: User-level 8:1:1 split with 80/20 context/target: https://arxiv.org/html/2309.13375v2#S5.SS1.SSS2.p1.
- **Candidates**: full catalog (top-n items from the entire candidate set via constrained beam search); NDCG uses all positive items for the ideal DCG.
  - Source: Top-n from the entire candidate set: https://arxiv.org/html/2309.13375v2#S3.SS4.p1; NDCG computed against all positives: https://arxiv.org/html/2309.13375v2#S5.SS1.SSS2.p2.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Test users are held out from training (user-level split); the SASRec embeddings used to build identifiers are trained on interaction data whose user split is not restated.
  - Source: Test users disjoint from training users; items shared: https://arxiv.org/html/2309.13375v2#S5.SS1.SSS2.p1.
- **SID**: Balanced k-ary tree identifiers from recursive constrained k-means over trained SASRec item embeddings; leaf-layer tokens correspond one-to-one with items and share the item's embedding. The branch count k is searched over 2, 4, 8, 16, and 32, and the paper states that k is set to 8 or 16 in the experiments; the value per dataset: not reported.
  - Source: Balanced k-ary tree from constrained k-means over SASRec embeddings; https://arxiv.org/html/2309.13375v2#algorithm1.6; leaf tokens one-to-one with items: https://arxiv.org/html/2309.13375v2#S3.SS2.SSS2.p3; k search range: https://arxiv.org/html/2309.13375v2#S5.SS1.SSS3.p4; k set to 8 or 16: https://arxiv.org/html/2309.13375v2#S4.SS2.p2.
- **Inference budget**: Constrained beam search over the prefix tree with beam size 50 (also for TDM and RecForest); Table 1 gives asymptotic inference cost. Main SEATER uses a single encoder-decoder layer. Hardware, inference batch size, and latency: not reported.
  - Source: Beam size 50 for tree-based and generative methods: https://arxiv.org/html/2309.13375v2#S5.SS1.SSS3.p4; complexity: https://arxiv.org/html/2309.13375v2#S3.T1.
- **Results from**: Table 3 (Yelp, News, Books, Micro-Video versus dual-encoder, tree-based, and generative baselines including GPTRec and TIGER); Table 1 (time and space complexity); Section 5.5 (more encoder-decoder layers).
  - Source: Main: https://arxiv.org/html/2309.13375v2#S5.T3; complexity: https://arxiv.org/html/2309.13375v2#S3.T1.

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: competitor; note: TIGER builds identifiers by RQ-VAE over text embeddings; SEATER builds balanced tree identifiers from collaborative SASRec embeddings and adds alignment and ranking losses over the tree.; where: SEATER v2, Section 4.1 related work: https://arxiv.org/html/2309.13375v2#S4.SS1.p2; Table 3 generative baseline: https://arxiv.org/html/2309.13375v2#S5.T3.
- id: cid; relation: alternative; note: P5 with collaborative indexing uses spectral clustering of interactions for IDs; SEATER uses a balanced k-ary tree from constrained k-means.; where: SEATER v2, Section 4.1 cites Hua et al. (2023b): https://arxiv.org/html/2309.13375v2#S4.SS1.p2.
- id: eager; relation: alternative; note: EAGER, a later paper that cites SEATER among generative recommenders, builds two tree-structured codes (behavior and semantic) with hierarchical k-means instead of one collaborative tree.; where: Evidence is from the later EAGER paper, Section 1: https://arxiv.org/html/2406.14017v2#S1.p2.

## SemConv

- Page: pages/papers/semconv.md
- Venue: AAAI’25
- Problem: III. SID–Model Alignment
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text+CF; Tokenization: Align. RQ; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: Multi-task NTP; Inference: Beam
- TL;DR: SemConv converts item IDs into token sequences aligned with the LLM space through Alignment Tokenization, adds tasks linking collaborative signals and language, and pre-caches top-K results for serving.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 2

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Games, Arts and Instruments; history cap 20; exclude samples whose concatenated prompt exceeds 2048 tokens. Other filtering: not reported.
  - Source: Experiment Setup, Datasets: https://arxiv.org/html/2412.13771v1#Sx4.SSx1.SSSx1.p1
- **Split**: Evaluation uses each user's last interaction as target and preceding interactions as context. First S-1 actions form training examples; exact validation allocation: not reported.
  - Source: Experiment Setup, Baselines: https://arxiv.org/html/2412.13771v1#Sx4.SSx1.SSSx2.p2
- **Candidates**: not reported
  - Source: Experiment Setup does not specify evaluation candidate sampling; negative sampling in Alignment Task is training: https://arxiv.org/html/2412.13771v1#Sx4.SSx1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2412.13771v1#Sx3.SSx2.p4
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. DCCF embedding exposure to test items/interactions: not reported.
  - Source: Experiment Setup and Alignment Tokenization: https://arxiv.org/html/2412.13771v1#Sx4.SSx1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2412.13771v1#Sx3.SSx1.p3
- **SID**: Aligned residual codebooks: 4 levels x 256 codes; Games reports 0% collisions at four levels. Explicit collision handling: not reported.
  - Source: Alignment Tokenization and Table 5: https://arxiv.org/html/2412.13771v1#Sx3.SSx1.p10 and https://arxiv.org/html/2412.13771v1#Sx4.T5
- **Inference budget**: Beam-generated valid item codes are cached per user; online serving reads cache. HR/NDCG@1/5/10. Beam width, cache K, hardware, inference batch, numerical latency: not reported.
  - Source: Inference and Metrics: https://arxiv.org/html/2412.13771v1#Sx3.SSx3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2412.13771v1#Sx4.SSx1.SSSx3.p1
- **Results from**: Reported Table 1 main comparison and Tables 3-8 Games ablations. P5 uses the cited external implementation; other baseline borrowed-versus-rerun provenance: not reported.
  - Source: Tables 1/3-8: https://arxiv.org/html/2412.13771v1#Sx3.T1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2412.13771v1#Sx4.T3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2412.13771v1#Sx4.T8 and https://arxiv.org/html/2412.13771v1#Sx4.SSx1.SSSx2.p1

## SID-MLP

- Page: pages/papers/sid-mlp.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: V. Efficiency
- Stage: Backbone
- Representation: Text; Tokenization: RQ-VAE†; Backbone: Enc-MLP; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP + Aux.; Inference: C-Beam
- TL;DR: SID-MLP distills an autoregressive Transformer decoder into position-specific MLP heads over a single user-context computation, replacing repeated attention steps in Semantic ID decoding.
- [Code](https://github.com/ztguo715/SID-MLP.git)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 4

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Main: Amazon Reviews 2023 Musical Instruments, Industrial & Scientific and Video Games, 5-core. LC-Rec extension: Amazon Reviews 2018 Musical Instruments, Arts Crafts and Sewing and Video Games, filtering users/items with fewer than five interactions.
  - Source: Sec.4.1 and Appendix C.1/D.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.12617v1#S4.SS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.12617v1#A3.T10 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.12617v1#A4.T13
- **Split**: Main: chronological leave-last-out, history truncated to 20 items; four rolling next-item training targets per user; evaluation leave-one-out. Exact validation allocation: not reported. LC-Rec extension follows its protocol; exact allocation/history cap: not reported.
  - Source: Appendix C.1 and D.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.12617v1#A3.SS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.12617v1#A3.T10 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.12617v1#A4.SS1.p1
- **Candidates**: Evaluation over valid four-digit SIDs with a fixed item-to-SID prefix mask. Full-catalog versus sampled ranking and history-item exclusion: not reported.
  - Source: Sec.4.1 and Sec.3.4: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.12617v1#S4.SS1.p3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.12617v1#S3.SS4.p2
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Temporal-80/90 diagnostics select targets introduced after global 80%/90% timestamps while reusing existing TIGER checkpoints, tokenizer and candidates; the paper explicitly excludes a strict zero-shot insertion interpretation. Tokenizer exposure to test items: not reported.
  - Source: Appendix E.3 explicitly distinguishes temporal shift from strict zero-shot insertion: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.12617v1#A5.SS3.p1
- **SID**: Fixed teacher SID mapping: four digits, three residual-quantization codes with 256-way codebook plus a conflict-avoidance digit; main experiments use sentence-T5 SIDs. Tokenizer sensitivity tests RQ-KMeans, RQ-VAE and PSID. LC-Rec retains its four SID tokens.
  - Source: Sec.2.1, Sec.3.4, Sec.4.4 and Appendix D.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.12617v1#S2.SS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.12617v1#S3.SS4.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.12617v1#S4.SS4.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.12617v1#A4.SS2.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.12617v1#A4.SS4.p3
- **Inference budget**: Constrained beam 50, batch 32, Recall/NDCG@5/10; one context read followed by four sequential MLP heads. Main profile: one RTX A6000 48GB; timed forward passes, beam expansion, validity mask, item lookup and metrics, excluding initialization/loading/offline extraction. SID-MLP/++: 3706/4347 samples/s, 8.74x/10.25x TIGER-kv; reported 0.27/0.23 ms/sample is inverse throughput. Peak memory on Instruments: 0.09/0.43GB. LC-Rec extension reports 38.04 samples/s end-to-end and 5194 decode-only; Figure4 uses decode-only LC-Rec rates excluding prefill. Extension beam/batch: not separately reported.
  - Source: Sec.3.4/4.1, Appendix C.3, D.1 and Figure4: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.12617v1#S3.SS4.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.12617v1#S4.SS1.p3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.12617v1#A3.SS3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.12617v1#A3.SS3.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.12617v1#A3.SS3.p3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.12617v1#A3.T11 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.12617v1#A4.SS1.p5 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.12617v1#A4.F4
- **Results from**: This paper's matched-checkpoint evaluations, baseline adaptations and ablations, not quoted baseline scores. Table3 main comparisons; Tables5/14 ablations, Table11 profile, Table12 seeds 42/43/44, Table15 temporal diagnostic. AtSpeed/EARN/NEZHA are ports to TIGER; NEZHA is also reproduced on LC-Rec. LC-Rec extension uses released Amazon-2018 checkpoints and retrains TIGER at three scales; Figure4 LC-Rec throughput excludes prefill.
  - Source: Tables3/5/11/12 and Appendices D.1-D.4/E: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.12617v1#S4.T3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.12617v1#S4.T5 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.12617v1#A3.T11 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.12617v1#A3.T12 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.12617v1#A4.SS1.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.12617v1#A4.SS3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.12617v1#A4.SS4.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.12617v1#A5.T14 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.12617v1#A5.T15

## SIDReasoner

- Page: pages/papers/sidreasoner.md
- Venue: KDD’26
- Problem: III. SID–Model Alignment
- Stage: Training
- Representation: Text; Tokenization: RQ-VAE; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP → RL; Inference: C-Beam
- TL;DR: SIDReasoner strengthens Semantic ID-language alignment with multi-task training on a teacher-synthesized corpus, then improves reasoning through outcome-driven reinforcement learning, without annotated recommendation reasoning traces.
- [Code](https://github.com/HappyPointer/SIDReasoner)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 4

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Reviews 2023: Video Games (3,858 items / 61,417 interactions), Office Products (3,459 / 48,656), Industrial and Scientific (3,686 / 45,325); 5-core filtering of users and items; histories truncated by a sliding window of length 10.
  - Source: Datasets, 5-core, sliding window 10: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.23183v2#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1; statistics: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.23183v2#S3.T1.
- **Split**: Per user, interactions sorted chronologically and split 8:1:1 into training, validation, and test, with the most recent interactions for validation and test.
  - Source: Temporal 8:1:1 per user: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.23183v2#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1.
- **Candidates**: full catalog (ranking metrics over the entire item set rather than sampled negatives).
  - Source: Full-item ranking: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.23183v2#S4.SS1.SSS1.p2.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined.
  - Source: Temporal split with no unseen-item protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.23183v2#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1.
- **SID**: RQ-VAE semantic IDs with L codebooks of K codes over text-encoder embeddings, added to the Qwen3-1.7B vocabulary as new tokens; numerical L and K and collision handling: not reported.
  - Source: RQ-VAE with L codebooks of K codes over text embeddings: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.23183v2#S3.SS2.SSS1.p1; numerical L, K not found.
- **Inference budget**: Reason-then-recommend generation: the model writes a reasoning sequence and then the target SID; evaluation decoding method and width: not reported (GRPO training uses 16 rollouts). Hardware, inference batch size, and latency: not reported.
  - Source: Rollout and training settings: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.23183v2#S4.SS1.SSS3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2603.23183v2#S4.SS1.SSS3.p3; decoding for evaluation not found.
- **Results from**: Table 2 (Games, Office, Industrial versus discriminative, generative, and reasoning baselines); Table 3 (alignment strategies before and after RL); Table 4 (general-ability benchmarks); Table 5 (teacher models for corpus enrichment).
  - Source: Main: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.23183v2#S4.T2; alignment ablation: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.23183v2#S4.T3; general abilities: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.23183v2#S4.T4; teachers: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.23183v2#S4.T5.

### Notes

## 旧卡片说明

迁自 `d61aa6c:papers/sidreasoner.md`。保留方法说明、实验叙述与局限；本轮只对照现有记录处理明确冲突，未重新逐句核查原论文。分类和规格以页面上方由记录生成的表格为准。

### SIDReasoner：基于语义标识推理的生成式推荐

> SIDReasoner 让语言模型在生成最终语义标识前显式推理用户偏好，以提升跨域和冷启动推荐能力。

### 研究动机与问题定义

直接预测 SID 容易把推荐当作模式匹配，难以利用物品语义和用户偏好之间的中间关系。SIDReasoner 将推理文本或结构化思考引入 SID 生成过程。

### TL;DR（核心摘要）

`用户历史与物品信息 → 对齐语料预训练 → 偏好推理 → 生成SID → 推荐物品`

模型以语义标识为推荐目标，先通过丰富的对齐语料学习语义、行为和标识之间的关系，再使用冷启动推理激活与分组强化学习优化推理链。最终输出 SID 直接映射物品。

### 输入与使用场景

| 方面 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| 使用信息 | 用户行为、物品语义和跨域推荐数据 |
| 信息融入位置 | 对齐语料、推理过程和强化学习奖励 |
| 语义标识结构 | 推理序列后接多 token SID |
| 适用场景 | 跨域、冷启动和常规推荐 |

### 方法设计

#### 3.1 任务形式化
SIDReasoner 将推荐输出表示为语义标识，并要求模型在生成标识前形成与用户历史和物品语义相关的推理过程。推理文本和最终 SID 在同一生成任务中衔接。

#### 3.2 丰富的 SID-语言对齐
模型构造多种对齐语料，让 SID 能被翻译为物品语义、让物品内容能解释 SID，并同时学习行为序列预测。该阶段的作用是把离散标识嵌入语言模型的语义空间。

#### 3.3 推理增强强化学习
方法包含冷启动推理激活和分组强化学习。模型根据候选推理路径及最终推荐结果获得奖励，训练其生成更有依据的偏好分析，再输出目标 SID。

#### 3.4 实验与分析
论文评估跨域泛化、不同对齐策略、模型规模和强化学习设置，重点观察推理能力是否真正转化为推荐收益。

### 实验结论

- 推理增强改善了跨域推荐表现。
- 丰富对齐语料、冷启动激活和强化学习均有独立贡献。

### 局限性与研究定位

#### 局限性
- 推理文本会增加生成长度和推理成本。
- 推理质量、奖励设计与真实用户意图之间仍可能存在偏差。

#### 研究定位
SIDReasoner 的贡献是把 SID 作为推理对象而不只是输出标签，适合放在“推理增强生成式推荐”章节。

### 标签

`语义标识推理` · `强化学习` · `跨域泛化` · `生成式推荐`
