## SIDScope

- Page: pages/papers/sidscope.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: Paradigms, Systems and Benchmarks
- Stage: No single stage
- Representation: n/a; Tokenization: n/a; Backbone: n/a; Tokenizer: n/a; Objective: n/a; Inference: n/a
- TL;DR: SIDScope is a diagnostic resource, not a new recommender: it checks released Semantic ID mappings for code organization, item resolution, and model compatibility after a refresh.
- [Code](https://github.com/jdding/sidscope)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 5

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Diagnostic resource with nine named exports from seven tokenizer families: Amazon Musical, Video Games, Beauty (P5), and Instruments, plus Yelp Business; eight exports enter the executable diagnostic matrix. A separate DACT Tools case studies mapping refresh. For the compact D3 graph, duplicate user-item pairs are removed and only users with 2-50 distinct mapped items are included; users above 50 are excluded, not truncated. Upstream dataset filtering is not reported uniformly across routes.
  - Source: Table 2 defines named route coverage, Section 3.2 defines bounded-graph filtering, and Section 6 adds a separate Tools lifecycle case; https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#S3.T2, https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1, https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p2, and https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#S6.SS1.p1.
- **Split**: Protocol-dependent. Mapping profiles use declared training splits or supplied reference interactions when split labels are absent. Fixed-budget Beauty studies use explicit training/validation splits; ReSOT Instruments uses earlier events as history, the penultimate event for validation, and the final event as unused future holdout, with hashed users separating diagnostics from 2,000 validation users. GRID beam studies train outside each of two evaluation folds; DIGER uses a last-event case. DACT refresh uses the same 5,364 held-out users/targets across states, with test targets excluded from training and checkpoint selection.
  - Source: Profile, fixed-budget, beam, and lifecycle studies use distinct splits, so none is promoted to a resource-wide train/test protocol; https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p2, https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#S5.SS2.p1, https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#S5.SS5.p1, and https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#S6.SS1.p2.
- **Candidates**: Protocol-dependent: fixed-budget prefix retrieval uses exactly 100 candidate items per user, with sensitivity budgets of 50 and 200; sampled-ranking tests use the target plus 100 catalog negatives after excluding history items, using popular or uniformly sampled negatives; frozen-beam resolver comparisons use the same top-50 generated paths, with top-20 sensitivity and no candidate-budget expansion.
  - Source: Fixed-budget retrieval, sampled ranking, and beam accounting have different candidate meanings; https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#S5.SS2.p1, https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1, https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#A2.SS3.p1, and https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#A2.SS4.p2.
- **Visibility**: No single warm/cold regime. Fixed-budget studies separate diagnostic and validation users, not the upstream tokenizer's training population. The DACT refresh case includes 584 new-item targets and compares the released checkpoint with adapted checkpoints; whether these items were unseen during tokenizer fitting is not reported.
  - Source: Disjoint diagnostic users do not establish tokenizer-unseen items, and the DACT new-item handoff is not a declared tokenizer-cold-start protocol; https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#S5.SS2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#S6.SS1.p2.
- **SID**: Named exports have 3 or 4 SID levels; a single layers-by-codebook-size configuration is n/a, and nominal per-level codebook capacities are not reported uniformly across routes. Table 3's D1 counts are occupied first-level symbols, not nominal capacities. Shared full codes are measured explicitly; frozen-beam comparisons use singleton credit, uniform within-leaf expected credit, or deterministic training-popularity resolution with item-ID tie-breaking.
  - Source: Table 2 gives SID depths, Table 3 reports occupied symbols rather than codebook capacity, and Section 5.6 defines the collision-accounting/resolution alternatives; https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#S3.T2, https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#S4.T3, https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#S5.SS6.p1, and https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#S5.SS6.p2.
- **Inference budget**: DACT TIGER/T5 constraint comparison: beam width 50 on 500 fixed targets. Controlled GRID/P5 GRU runs: beam width 50 on 500 targets per evaluation fold, with a DIGER portability case under the same accounting. Three GRU exports each contain 25,000 beam rows for 500 targets. Generator inference hardware, inference batch size, and latency not reported; the stated batch size 512 is for GRU training.
  - Source: Sections 5.4-5.5 state the actual beam budgets, Appendix B.4's batch 512 is a training setting, and Section 3.2 distinguishes topology from runtime; https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#S5.SS4.p1, https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#S5.SS5.p1, https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#A2.SS4.p1, https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#A2.SS4.p2, and https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#S3.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p2.
- **Results from**: Table 3: eight-route D1-D5 profiles. Table 4: D3 calibration checks. Table 5: fixed-budget prefix retrieval. Section 5.4: released TIGER/T5 constrained versus unconstrained decoding. Table 6: controlled beam accounting. Table 7: resolution policies on identical beams. Table 8: DACT mapping refresh and generator handoff. Appendix B, Tables 11-12: measurement checks and candidate-budget sensitivity.
  - Source: The cited tables separate mapping diagnostics, candidate exposure, beam accounting, resolver outcomes, and lifecycle handoff; https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#S4.T3, https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#S5.T4, https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#S5.T5, https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#S5.T6, https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#S5.T7, https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#S6.T8, https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#S5.SS4.p1, https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#A2.T11, and https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#A2.T12.

### Related

- id: diger; relation: predecessor; note: DIGER supplies upstream checkpoint-derived SID mappings for Beauty and Yelp that SIDScope profiles separately and uses in a last-event beam-accounting portability case.; where: SIDScope v2, Tables 2 and 3 identify and profile the DIGER Beauty and Yelp exports: https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#S3.T2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#S4.T3; Section 5.5 and Table 6 identify the last-event sensitivity route: https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#S5.SS5.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#S5.T6.
- id: letter; relation: predecessor; note: LETTER supplies a released Instruments SID index that SIDScope re-audits under its common bounded diagnostic protocol as an upstream mapping source.; where: SIDScope v2, Table 2 identifies LETTER's released Instruments index: https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#S3.T2; Section 4.1 states that LETTER is recomputed under the common C3 protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#S4.SS1.p3; Table 3 reports the resulting profile: https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#S4.T3.
- id: lc-rec; relation: predecessor; note: LC-Rec supplies a released Instruments SID index that SIDScope re-audits alongside LETTER to distinguish mapping addressability from prefix behavioral alignment.; where: SIDScope v2, Table 2 identifies LC-Rec's released Instruments index: https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#S3.T2; Section 4.1 compares its mapping properties with LETTER and states the shared bounded protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#S4.SS1.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#S4.SS1.p3; Table 3 reports both profiles: https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18779v2#S4.T3.

## SIIT

- Page: pages/papers/siit.md
- Venue: arXiv’24
- Problem: III. SID–Model Alignment
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text; Tokenization: Self-Imp.; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Altern.; Objective: Multi-task NTP; Inference: C-Beam
- TL;DR: SIIT starts from item tokenizations of any external model and periodically adjusts them to the LLM's learned patterns during training, so tokenization matches the LLM's internal item understanding.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 4

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Instruments (24,772 users / 9,922 items), Amazon Beauty (22,363 / 12,101), and Yelp (30,431 / 20,033), as introduced by LETTER; users and items with fewer than 5 interactions removed.
  - Source: Datasets and preprocessing following LETTER and LC-Rec: https://arxiv.org/html/2412.17171v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1; statistics: https://arxiv.org/html/2412.17171v1#S4.T1.
- **Split**: Per-user leave-one-out (most recent item for test, second-to-last for validation, the rest for training); histories capped at the 10 most recent items.
  - Source: Leave-one-out allocation and 10-item cap: https://arxiv.org/html/2412.17171v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p2.
- **Candidates**: full catalog (rank list generated from the entire item set without predefined candidate sets).
  - Source: Rank list from the entire item set: https://arxiv.org/html/2412.17171v1#S4.SS1.SSS2.p1.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined.
  - Source: Standard split with no unseen-item protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2412.17171v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p2.
- **SID**: Identifiers are initialized with CID, TIGER, or LETTER codes and then regenerated by the LLM itself over 2-5 iterations. Collisions: each item takes the first unused identifier among its top-20 beam candidates; any remaining duplicates get an appended token.
  - Source: Self-improving identifiers initialized from CID, TIGER, or LETTER; diverse beam assignment k=20 and suffix fallback: https://arxiv.org/html/2412.17171v1#S3.SS3.p3, https://arxiv.org/html/2412.17171v1#S3.SS3.p4, https://arxiv.org/html/2412.17171v1#S4.I3.i3.p1.
- **Inference budget**: Constrained beam search over a prefix tree of all item identifiers, outputs ranked by perplexity; numerical beam width for recommendation: not reported. Flan-T5-Small backbone; experiments on 8 NVIDIA A100-40GB GPUs; inference batch size and latency: not reported.
  - Source: Constrained beam search and perplexity ranking: https://arxiv.org/html/2412.17171v1#S3.SS4.p1; hardware: https://arxiv.org/html/2412.17171v1#S4.SS1.SSS4.p1.
- **Results from**: Table 2 (Instruments, Beauty, Yelp versus traditional and LLM-based baselines with simple and advanced tokenization); Table 3 (diverse generation and collision avoidance ablation on Yelp); Table 4 (identifier similarity before and after refinement).
  - Source: Main: https://arxiv.org/html/2412.17171v1#S4.T2; ablation: https://arxiv.org/html/2412.17171v1#S4.T3; identifier similarity: https://arxiv.org/html/2412.17171v1#S4.T4.

### Related

- id: letter; relation: competitor; note: LETTER fixes its regularized RQ-VAE identifiers before generator training; SIIT starts from such identifiers and lets the LLM regenerate them iteratively with alignment tasks.; where: SIIT v1, advanced-tokenization baselines and initializer: https://arxiv.org/html/2412.17171v1#S4.I3.i3.p1; data from LETTER: https://arxiv.org/html/2412.17171v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1; Table 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2412.17171v1#S4.T2.
- id: tiger; relation: competitor; note: TIGER's RQ-VAE codes are both a baseline and one of SIIT's initializations, which SIIT then refines.; where: SIIT v1, https://arxiv.org/html/2412.17171v1#S4.I3.i3.p1; Tables 2 and 4: https://arxiv.org/html/2412.17171v1#S4.T2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2412.17171v1#S4.T4.
- id: cid; relation: competitor; note: CID's spectral-clustering IDs (and the simple TID/SID variants) are baselines and an initializer; SIIT replaces fixed IDs with model-generated ones.; where: SIIT v1, baselines: https://arxiv.org/html/2412.17171v1#S4.I3.i2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2412.17171v1#S4.I3.i3.p1; Table 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2412.17171v1#S4.T2.
- id: lc-rec; relation: predecessor; note: SIIT follows LC-Rec's preprocessing and its idea of aligning LLMs to item identifiers through auxiliary tasks.; where: SIIT v1, Section 4.1.1 follows Zheng et al. (2024): https://arxiv.org/html/2412.17171v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1; Section 5.2 related work: https://arxiv.org/html/2412.17171v1#S5.SS2.p1.

## SLIDE

- Page: pages/papers/slide.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: IV. Utility
- Stage: Training
- Representation: –; Tokenization: –; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP; Inference: Greedy
- TL;DR: SLIDE concatenates a teacher's offline beam-search candidates into list-wise Semantic ID targets, so a student generates the whole top-K list in one greedy pass instead of item-level beam search.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: FORGE Stage S3; industrial Taobao Search requests with about 12 training labels/request. Additional filtering rules not reported.
  - Source: Section 5.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.34764v1#S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1
- **Split**: FORGE: retain provided S3 train/evaluation sets. Taobao: 10 consecutive training days, immediately following day test. Validation allocation not reported.
  - Source: Section 5.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.34764v1#S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1
- **Candidates**: not reported
  - Source: Section 5.1 describes valid unique generated candidates, without evaluation negative-sampling details: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.34764v1#S5.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined.
  - Source: Section 5.1 defines no unseen-item holdout: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.34764v1#S5.SS1
- **SID**: Three tokens/item. FORGE uses provided SID vocabulary, sizes not restated; Taobao codebooks [32768,8192,8192]. Tokenizer algorithm and collision handling not reported.
  - Source: Section 5.1/Appendix A.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.34764v1#S5.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.34764v1#A1.SS2.p1
- **Inference budget**: Qwen2.5-0.5B student; single greedy rollout to EOS or 1024 tokens; HR@1/5/10/20. Beam reference [20,20,200]; offline teacher distillation uses [20,20,20], 20-item targets. Serving hardware/batch/latency not reported; 32 H20 GPUs and global batch 8192 describe training.
  - Source: Section 5.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.34764v1#S5.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1
- **Results from**: Original Table 2: direct-training greedy/beam references versus distilled greedy students; teacher sizes 0.5B/3B/7B. Tables 3-6 analyze training, target construction, and supplementary RL.
  - Source: Section 5.2 and Table 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.34764v1#S5.SS2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.34764v1#S5.T2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.34764v1#S5.T3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.34764v1#S5.T4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.34764v1#S5.T5 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.34764v1#S5.T6

### Related

- id: forge; relation: predecessor; note: SLIDE reuses FORGE's S3 split and SID vocabulary.; where: SLIDE v1, Section 5.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.34764v1#S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1; https://arxiv.org/html/2610.34764v1#S5.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.
- id: onerec; relation: alternative; note: OneRec models session dependencies; SLIDE focuses on search-to-greedy list distillation.; where: SLIDE v1, Section 2.1 (Deng et al., 2025, arXiv:2502.18965): https://arxiv.org/html/2610.34764v1#S2.SS1.p2.
- id: tiger; relation: predecessor; note: SLIDE replaces the conventional item-level search interface with a distilled list rollout.; where: SLIDE v1, Introduction and Section 2.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.34764v1#S1.p1; https://arxiv.org/html/2610.34764v1#S2.SS1.p1.

## SnapLGR

- Page: pages/papers/snaplgr.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: II. Uniqueness and Validity
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text+Img+CF; Tokenization: RQ-VAE+PPR; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: Multi-task NTP; Inference: Beam
- TL;DR: SnapLGR builds Semantic IDs from multimodal embeddings with Personalized PageRank contrastive learning, grounds them by continued pretraining before fine-tuning an LLM, and serves beam search with TensorRT-LLM.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 2

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Internal Snapchat short-video engagement logs and multimodal video corpus; dataset size and filtering rules not reported. Up to 10 future items/request supply evaluation targets.
  - Source: Sections 2.1/4.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.28895v4#S2.SS1.p3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2607.28895v4#S4.SS1.p1
- **Split**: SFT uses one day; evaluation uses the immediately following hour. CPT uses one month ending one week before SFT; validation allocation not reported.
  - Source: Section 4.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.28895v4#S4.SS1.p1
- **Candidates**: not reported; primary offline metrics match generated SID clusters before video materialization.
  - Source: Section 4.1/Appendix B.2 defines SID-level generated-set metrics, not sampled evaluation negatives: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.28895v4#S4.SS1.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2607.28895v4#A2.SS2.p1
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. PPR co-engagement graph and tokenizer exposure to test videos not reported.
  - Source: Sections 2.1/4.1 define no unseen-item holdout: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.28895v4#S2.SS1.p7 and https://arxiv.org/html/2607.28895v4#S4.SS1.p1
- **SID**: PPR-supervised RQ-VAE: [1024,512,256]. Shared SIDs represent video clusters; materialization ranks videos within each bucket by engagement value. Per-bucket retained-video cap not reported.
  - Source: Section 3.1/Appendix A.3.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.28895v4#S3.SS1.p3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2607.28895v4#A1.SS3.SSS1.p1
- **Inference budget**: Qwen3-0.6B, beam 32; daily offline generation, online candidate-index lookup. A100 single-GPU and 64-GPU inference studies; optimized per-GPU throughput 45.7x legacy pipeline. Inference batch size, absolute throughput and latency not reported.
  - Source: Sections 2.3/4.1/4.4: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.28895v4#S2.SS3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2607.28895v4#S2.SS2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2607.28895v4#S4.SS1.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2607.28895v4#S4.SS4.SSS2.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2607.28895v4#S4.SS4.SSS2.p3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2607.28895v4#S4.SS4.SSS2.p5
- **Results from**: Original Table 3: offline SID comparison with T5 retrained on identical SIDs/data; Table 5: SID/video recall. Table 8: seven-day A/B versus deployed T5 with coarser CLIP SIDs, jointly changing tokenizer/backbone/serving.
  - Source: Section 4.1/4.5 and Tables 3/5/8: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.28895v4#S4.SS1.p3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2607.28895v4#S4.T3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2607.28895v4#S4.T5 and https://arxiv.org/html/2607.28895v4#S4.SS5.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2607.28895v4#S4.T8

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: predecessor; note: SnapLGR replaces the deployed TIGER-style T5 retriever with a grounded decoder-only LLM.; where: SnapLGR v4, Sections 4.1/4.5: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.28895v4#S4.SS1.p3; https://arxiv.org/html/2607.28895v4#S4.SS5.p1.
- id: plum; relation: predecessor; note: SnapLGR follows PLUM's CPT/SFT pipeline and adds PPR supervision and serving optimizations.; where: SnapLGR v4, Sections 2.1/5: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.28895v4#S2.SS1.p6; https://arxiv.org/html/2607.28895v4#S5.p2.

## Spacetime-GR

- Page: pages/papers/spacetime-gr.md
- Venue: arXiv’25
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Backbone
- Representation: Geo; Tokenization: Geo-Idx; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP → DPO; Inference: Beam
- TL;DR: Spacetime-GR indexes POIs with a geographic hierarchy, encodes spatiotemporal context into action sequences, adds multimodal POI embeddings, and post-trains for embeddings, ranking scores, and candidates.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 2

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: One year of sampled Amap actions; predict interest-based actions, discard sequences with distinct-POI/action ratio <0.3. Public Foursquare-NYC/TKY and Gowalla-CA follow STHGCN preprocessing, not detailed here.
  - Source: Sections 3.2.1/4.2.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.16126v1#S3.SS2.SSS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2508.16126v1#S3.SS2.SSS1.Px1.SPx1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2508.16126v1#S3.SS2.SSS1.Px1.SPx2.p3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2508.16126v1#S4.SS2.SSS1.p1
- **Split**: Industrial train/validation/test counts: pretraining 578M/19794/19837; SFT-alignment 31M/611K/553K. Partition construction and public splits not reported. Alignment probe uses last 5 POI actions as targets, earlier actions as context.
  - Source: Table 3 and Section 5.1.3: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.16126v1#S4.T3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2508.16126v1#S5.SS1.SSS3.p1
- **Candidates**: Generation evaluation universe not reported. SFT/alignment test requests average 10.6 provided POIs; candidate selection and historical-item exclusion not reported.
  - Source: Table 3 and Sections 4.1.5/5.1.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.16126v1#S4.T3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2508.16126v1#S4.SS1.SSS5.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2508.16126v1#S5.SS1.SSS1.p3
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined.
  - Source: Sections 4-5 define no unseen-item holdout: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.16126v1#S4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2508.16126v1#S5
- **SID**: Industrial: two tokens, 5km x 5km block plus within-block POI index; one-to-one mapping, total vocabulary reduced from 100M to 400K. Public experiments use a single-level index; codebooks n/a.
  - Source: Sections 3.2.1/4.2.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.16126v1#S3.SS2.SSS1.Px2.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2508.16126v1#S4.SS2.SSS2.p1
- **Inference budget**: Generate 10 blocks x 10 inner IDs, rank 100 POIs. Generation hardware, batch size and latency not reported. T4 latency 10-20ms applies to SFT representation/ranking services.
  - Source: Sections 5.1.1/4.1.6: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.16126v1#S5.SS1.SSS1.p3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2508.16126v1#S4.SS1.SSS6.p1
- **Results from**: Tables 5/9: aligned industrial generation; Table 7: pretraining ablation; Table 6: public next-POI accuracy. Table 5 judges 800 requests with LLMs and seven volunteers; public-baseline score provenance not reported.
  - Source: Original Tables 5/6/7/9: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.16126v1#S4.T5 and https://arxiv.org/html/2508.16126v1#S4.T6 and https://arxiv.org/html/2508.16126v1#S5.T7 and https://arxiv.org/html/2508.16126v1#S5.T9

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: predecessor; note: Semantic-ID generation inspires the geographic two-token POI indexing design.; where: Spacetime-GR v1, Section 3.2.1, citing Rajput et al. (2023): https://arxiv.org/html/2508.16126v1#S3.SS2.SSS1.Px2.p2.

## SPAR

- Page: pages/papers/spar.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Representation
- Representation: Text+Geo; Tokenization: R-KM; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: Multi-task NTP; Inference: –
- TL;DR: SPAR fuses sinusoidal coordinate embeddings into Semantic ID construction, continually pre-trains the LLM on geospatial data, and anchors that knowledge as a frozen task vector during behavioral fine-tuning.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Public NYC/TKY; one month of AMAP logs from Beijing, Shanghai, Tianjin and Zhejiang. MG-CPT adds 25 geospatial datasets per city. Cleaning details not reported.
  - Source: Section 5.1, Table 1 and Appendix B: https://arxiv.org/html/2609.02062v2#S5.SS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2609.02062v2#S5.T1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2609.02062v2#A2.p1
- **Split**: Public: chronological 80%/10%/10% train/validation/test. Industrial: last day test, earlier interactions train; industrial validation allocation not reported. Each interaction uses its preceding history.
  - Source: Section 5.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2609.02062v2#S5.SS1.p1
- **Candidates**: not reported
  - Source: Section 5.1 reports metrics and splits without candidate enumeration or negative sampling: https://arxiv.org/html/2609.02062v2#S5.SS1
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Cold/warm users have <8/>=16 historical interactions; queries and real-time location remain available. Quantizer fits training POIs; test-POI exclusion not detailed.
  - Source: Sections 4.1.2/5.5: https://arxiv.org/html/2609.02062v2#S4.SS1.SSS2.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2609.02062v2#S5.SS5.p1
- **SID**: SI-SID: 3 residual K-Means codebooks x 32 codes for NYC/TKY or x 512 for AMAP, plus a fourth disambiguation index guaranteeing unique POI IDs.
  - Source: Sections 4.1.2/5.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2609.02062v2#S4.SS1.SSS2.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2609.02062v2#S5.SS1.p4
- **Inference budget**: Default Qwen3-4B; Recall/NDCG/MRR@5/10/20. Experiment environment: 64 A100 GPUs; beam width, inference batch size and latency not reported. Reported batch 32 is training.
  - Source: Section 5.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2609.02062v2#S5.SS1.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2609.02062v2#S5.SS1.p4
- **Results from**: Original Tables 2/3: public/industrial recommendation comparisons; Table 5: sparse-history users. Generative baselines are standardized to four-level SIDs with final disambiguation indices.
  - Source: Original Tables 2/3/5 and Section 5.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2609.02062v2#S5.T2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2609.02062v2#S5.T3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2609.02062v2#S5.T5 and https://arxiv.org/html/2609.02062v2#S5.SS1.p4

### Related

- id: gnpr-sid; relation: competitor; note: SID POI baseline; SPAR explicitly injects and preserves urban spatial knowledge.; where: SPAR v2, Section 5.1 and Tables 2/3: https://arxiv.org/html/2609.02062v2#S5.SS1.p3; https://arxiv.org/html/2609.02062v2#S5.T2; https://arxiv.org/html/2609.02062v2#S5.T3.

## SPAR-Youku

- Page: pages/papers/spar-youku.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Backbone
- Representation: –; Tokenization: RQ-PIB; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP → DPO; Inference: C-Beam
- TL;DR: SPAR-Youku guides each Semantic ID decoding step with prefix-relevant evidence from compressed user memory and balances interaction loads among sibling branches with RQ-PIB, to reduce branch errors and popularity bias.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Youku homepage production playback logs spanning several months; daily DPO uses recent request contexts. Dataset size, dates and filtering not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.27898v1#S3.SS5.SSS1.Px1.p1
- **Split**: User-disjoint train/validation/test split 90:5:5; randomization method not reported. Seven-day online A/B: control and treatment each approximately 10% of traffic.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.27898v1#S3.SS5.SSS1.Px1.p1 ; #S3.SS6.p1 ; #S4.p2
- **Candidates**: not reported; trie validity and HR cutoffs do not specify the evaluation universe.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.27898v1#S3.SS5.SSS1.Px2.p1 ; #S3.SS5.SSS1.Px3.p1
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. RQ-PIB branch weights use training-set interaction counts; tokenizer content-fitting exposure to test items not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.27898v1#S3.SS5.SSS1.Px1.p1 ; #S3.SS5.SSS1.Px3.p1
- **SID**: Three-level RQ-PIB: residual K-means centers followed by prefix-local interaction-load balancing with frozen centers. Codebook sizes and collision handling not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.27898v1#S3.SS3.p3 ; #S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1 ; #S3.SS5.SSS1.Px3.p1
- **Inference budget**: Qwen3-0.6B with trie-constrained beam search. Main HR@10/20/50/100; ablations also HR@1/5. Beam width, inference hardware, batch size and latency not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.27898v1#S3.SS5.SSS1.Px3.p1 ; #S3.T1 ; #S3.T3
- **Results from**: Original Table 1: Youku retrieval comparisons; Table 2: backbone scaling; Table 3: module/SID/DPO ablations; Table 4: online A/B. Table 3 parts (a)-(c) use SFT only; part (d) adds DPO. Baseline-result reuse not stated.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.27898v1#S3.T1 ; #S3.T2 ; #S3.T3 ; #S3.T4 ; #S3.SS5.SSS4.p1

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: competitor; note: TIGER is a residual-SID retrieval baseline; SPAR jointly changes prefix-local branch balance and prefix-conditioned user evidence.; where: SPAR-Youku v1, Section 3.5.1 and Table 1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.27898v1#S3.SS5.SSS1.Px4.p1; https://arxiv.org/html/2610.27898v1#S3.T1.

## SpecGR

- Page: pages/papers/specgr.md
- Venue: AAAI’26
- Problem: VI. Generalization
- Stage: Inference
- Representation: Text+SID; Tokenization: RQ-VAE; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP + Rank; Inference: Hybrid
- TL;DR: SpecGR uses an inductive drafter to propose existing and new items and the generative recommender as verifier, so the model can recommend items unseen in training.
- [Code](https://github.com/Jamesding000/SpecGR)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Reviews 2023 Video Games, Office Products, Cell Phones and Accessories; timestamp_w_his 5-core benchmark excludes users/items with fewer than five interactions; maximum input history 20 items.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2410.02939v2#Sx4.SSx1.SSSx1.p1 ; #Sx4.SSx1.SSSx4.p1
- **Split**: Global predefined timestamp cutoffs create train/validation/test sets; exact dates not reported in paper. Test divided into In-Sample and Unseen according to target-item occurrence in training.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2410.02939v2#Sx4.SSx1.SSSx1.p1 ; #Sx4.SSx1.SSSx3.p1
- **Candidates**: not reported; full-catalog and subset-ranking capabilities are discussed, but the main evaluation universe and negative-sampling protocol are not explicitly specified.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2410.02939v2#Sx4.SSx1.SSSx3.p1 ; #A6.SSx1.p1
- **Visibility**: Unseen targets have no training interactions and are unseen by the generator. New items are assigned SIDs for inference; tokenizer fitting exposure is not reported, so whether they are unseen by tokenizer too is not established.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2410.02939v2#Sx3.SSx1.p1 ; #Sx3.SSx1.p2 ; #Sx4.SSx1.SSSx3.p1
- **SID**: TIGER RQ-VAE tokenization; standard experiments use four-digit SIDs, including a final collision-identification token. Codebook sizes and suffix-assignment rule not reported. Verification excludes the identification token for unseen items.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2410.02939v2#Sx4.SSx1.SSSx4.p1 ; #Sx3.SSx2.SSSx2.p3 ; #A5.SSx2.p1
- **Inference budget**: Beam beta and draft size delta are 50 or output K (10/50); verification threshold tuned -1.1 to -1.8. Draft/verify with guided redrafting and early exit, then beam fallback if needed. Table A6 at draft size 50: SpecGR++ drafting/verifying 0.0003/0.0249 s versus TIGER 0.0403 s. Inference hardware, batch size and timing aggregation not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2410.02939v2#A2.SSx1.p1 ; #Sx3.SSx2.SSSx4.p1 ; #A5.T6
- **Results from**: Original Table 1: overall comparison; Table 2: seen/unseen breakdown; Table 3: ablations; Table A6: latency. Baselines reproduced/tuned; Recformer starts from a third-party reproduction checkpoint and is fine-tuned on these datasets.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2410.02939v2#Sx4.SSx2.p1 ; #Sx4.SSx2.p2 ; #Sx4.T3 ; #A2.SSx3.p1 ; #A5.T6

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: predecessor; note: SpecGR uses TIGER as its generative verifier and adds inductive drafting; SpecGR++ reuses the same encoder for self-drafting.; where: SpecGR v2, Implementation Details and Drafting Strategies: https://arxiv.org/html/2410.02939v2#Sx4.SSx1.SSSx4.p1; https://arxiv.org/html/2410.02939v2#Sx3.SSx3.SSSx2.p1.
- id: liger; relation: competitor; note: LIGER blends dense-retrieved candidates with generated items; SpecGR filters and orders inductive drafts using generative target-aware likelihoods.; where: SpecGR v2, Performance Analysis and Table 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2410.02939v2#Sx4.SSx2.p2.
- id: atspeed; relation: alternative; note: AtSpeed adapts speculative decoding to accelerate top-K generative recommendation; SpecGR uses draft-and-verify to introduce unseen-item recommendation capability.; where: SpecGR v2, Related Work, citing Lin et al. (2024), arXiv:2410.05165: https://arxiv.org/html/2410.02939v2#Sx2.p3.

## SPRIG

- Page: pages/papers/sprig.md
- Venue: CIKM’26 Short
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text / Audio; Tokenization: R-KM; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP; Inference: Div. Beam
- TL;DR: SPRIG trains a generator on knowledge-graph paths that end in content-derived Semantic IDs, combining relational grounding with shared item tokens instead of opaque tokens tied to embedding tables.
- [Code](https://github.com/justinhangoebl/semantic-id-knowledge-graph-recommender)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 2

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: KG-enriched MovieLens-1M from RecBole (2984 items); Onion (18415 tracks): LFM-2B March-May 2018 interactions plus music content and artist/genre/album/tag KG, iteratively filtered to 20-core. Additional ML-1M filtering: not reported.
  - Source: Sec.3 Datasets and Table1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.06590v1#S3.p3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.06590v1#S3.T1
- **Split**: Per-user chronological 60/20/20 train/validation/test; identical preprocessing and splits across models. History cap: not reported.
  - Source: Sec.3 Task and Protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.06590v1#S3.p6
- **Candidates**: Full catalog evaluation against held-out interactions; SPRIG/KGGLM rank terminal items from up to 50 generated paths per user, deduplicating by highest path log-likelihood. SASRec scores the catalog directly. History-item exclusion: not reported.
  - Source: Sec.3 Task and Protocol and Sec.4 comparison limits: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.06590v1#S3.p6 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.06590v1#S4.p3
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Generic KG pretraining excludes user-item edges; fine-tuning uses user-to-item paths. KG/quantizer exposure to test items or held-out interactions: not reported.
  - Source: Sec.2.2 pretraining excludes user-item edges; Sec.5 leaves cold-start splits to future work: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.06590v1#S2.SS2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.06590v1#S5.p2
- **SID**: Offline residual K-means, 3 levels x 256 codes (768 shared tokens), on T5 movie embeddings/musicnn track embeddings. Item entities in KG paths are expanded into SIDs; inverse lookup maps terminal SIDs to items. Collision handling: not reported.
  - Source: Sec.3 SID construction and Figure1 lookup: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.06590v1#S3.p4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.06590v1#S0.F1
- **Inference budget**: Deterministic diverse beam search: 60 beams, 5 groups, diversity penalty 0.4, length penalty 0; 3-hop paths, up to 50 paths/user. Rank by terminal path log-likelihood; nDCG/MRR/HR@10. Experiments use NVIDIA A40. Inference batch, numerical latency/throughput and runtime timing scope: not reported; reported FLOPs are per-step compute, not latency.
  - Source: Sec.3 implementation/protocol/metrics, Table2 and Sec.4 cost comparison: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.06590v1#S3.p5 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.06590v1#S3.p6 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.06590v1#S3.p7 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.06590v1#S4.T2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.06590v1#S4.p6
- **Results from**: This paper's Table2 experiments and quantizer/audio-feature ablations. Baselines run under original-publication best configurations and verified on shared splits; TIGER uses a GRID variant. SPRIG/KGGLM share DistilGPT-2 and decoding; SASRec is a full-catalog scoring reference. No quoted-score provenance is claimed.
  - Source: Sec.3 implementation/baselines, Table2 and Sec.4 ablation: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.06590v1#S3.p5 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.06590v1#S3.p8 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.06590v1#S4.T2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.06590v1#S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: predecessor; note: SPRIG adopts TIGER's content-derived SID formulation and evaluates its GRID variant.; where: SPRIG v1, Sec.1 and Table2: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.06590v1#S1.p2; https://arxiv.org/html/2610.06590v1#S4.T2.
- id: grid; relation: predecessor; note: GRID supplies the residual K-means quantization choice.; where: SPRIG v1, Sec.1 and Sec.3: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.06590v1#S1.p2; https://arxiv.org/html/2610.06590v1#S3.p4.

## SPRINT

- Page: pages/papers/sprint.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: V. Efficiency
- Stage: Backbone
- Representation: Text; Tokenization: Par. OPQ; Backbone: Non-AR; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: Dual-level Flow Ctr.; Inference: Scoring
- TL;DR: SPRINT predicts all Semantic ID token probabilities in one forward pass of a bidirectional Transformer, based on average probability velocity, and restores token coherence with a dual-level flow contrastive objective.
- [Code](https://github.com/iamZhuoCai/SPRINT)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Reviews 2014 Sports, Beauty and Toys; Amazon Reviews 2023 Instruments, Scientific, Games and Arts; Yelp. Filtering thresholds: not reported.
  - Source: Sec.4.1 and Appendix D.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2609.34306v1#S4.SS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2609.34306v1#A4.SS1.p1
- **Split**: Per-user timestamp-ordered leave-one-out: last interaction test, penultimate validation, remainder training; history cap 20.
  - Source: Appendix D.1 and D.3: https://arxiv.org/html/2609.34306v1#A4.SS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2609.34306v1#A4.SS3.p1
- **Candidates**: Full catalog: score valid SIDs with the sum of separately normalized token-probability and joint-SID similarity scores, returning top K. History-item exclusion: not reported. The 100/1000 sampled negative SIDs are training settings.
  - Source: Sec.4.1 and Sec.3.4 inference; sampled SIDs in Eq.9 are training negatives: https://arxiv.org/html/2609.34306v1#S4.SS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2609.34306v1#S3.SS4.p3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2609.34306v1#S3.SS3.p6 and https://arxiv.org/html/2609.34306v1#S4.SS1.p3
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Tokenizer exposure to test items: not reported.
  - Source: Sec.4.1 and Appendix D.1/D.3 define standard evaluation without unseen-item experiments: https://arxiv.org/html/2609.34306v1#S4.SS1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2609.34306v1#A4.SS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2609.34306v1#A4.SS3.p1
- **SID**: OPQ on sentence-t5-base content embeddings; four parallel codebooks x 256 codewords, four tokens/item. Collision handling: not reported.
  - Source: Sec.3.1 and Appendix D.3: https://arxiv.org/html/2609.34306v1#S3.SS1.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2609.34306v1#A4.SS3.p1
- **Inference budget**: One encoder-decoder pass from four masks, followed by all-valid-SID scoring with precomputed item-side vectors; beam n/a for SPRINT. Test batch 256/history20; efficiency baselines use beam10 where applicable, embedding256. Recall/NDCG@5/10; additional K=20/50/100/1000. Whole-test-set seconds on Sports/Beauty/Toys/Scientific/Instruments/Games: 2.65/1.52/1.28/4.08/4.62/7.55. Hardware, per-request latency, and inclusion of precomputation/data loading/metric computation in timing: not reported.
  - Source: Sec.3.4, Sec.4.1, Table3, Appendix D.3/D.11 and Algorithm2: https://arxiv.org/html/2609.34306v1#S3.SS4.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2609.34306v1#S3.SS4.p3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2609.34306v1#S4.SS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2609.34306v1#S4.T3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2609.34306v1#A4.SS3.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2609.34306v1#A4.SS11.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2609.34306v1#alg2
- **Results from**: Paper's comparisons/ablations, averaged over five random-seed runs (seed values not reported). Tables2/8 main accuracy, Table12 Yelp/Arts, Tables3/10 whole-test inference time, Table9 per-epoch training time. Efficiency configurations are shared; accuracy settings follow original papers and are tuned per dataset. Table10 accelerators use TIGER backbones. Explicit borrowed-versus-rerun score attribution: not reported.
  - Source: Sec.4.1, Tables2/3/4 and Appendix D.3/D.6/D.8: https://arxiv.org/html/2609.34306v1#S4.SS1.p3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2609.34306v1#S4.T2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2609.34306v1#S4.T3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2609.34306v1#S4.T4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2609.34306v1#A4.SS3.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2609.34306v1#A4.SS6.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2609.34306v1#A4.SS8.p1

### Related

- id: rpg; relation: competitor; note: RPG is the compared single-step baseline with longer SIDs.; where: SPRINT v1, Sec.1 and Sec.4.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2609.34306v1#S1.p2; https://arxiv.org/html/2609.34306v1#S4.SS2.p2.
- id: llada-rec; relation: competitor; note: LLaDA-Rec is compared under one-step and four-step generation.; where: SPRINT v1, Table1 and Sec.4.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2609.34306v1#S1.T1; https://arxiv.org/html/2609.34306v1#S4.SS1.p2.
- id: sid-mlp; relation: competitor; note: SID-MLP is the closest compared efficiency-oriented baseline.; where: SPRINT v1, Appendix D.6: https://arxiv.org/html/2609.34306v1#A4.SS6.p2; https://arxiv.org/html/2609.34306v1#A4.T10.

## SST

- Page: pages/papers/sst.md
- Venue: CIKM’26
- Problem: III. SID–Model Alignment
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text; Tokenization: RQ+IST; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP; Inference: C-Beam
- TL;DR: SST represents history items as variable-length subwords merged from stable adjacent Semantic ID tokens while keeping fixed-length target decoding, to reduce intra-item attention in the encoder.
- [Code](https://github.com/mxrcandy/Semantic-Subword-Tokenization)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 2

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Beauty/Instruments and Yelp; user/item 5-core filtering, chronological histories capped at 20.
  - Source: Section 3.1.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2608.22734v1#S3.SS1.SSS1.p1
- **Split**: Per-user last interaction test, penultimate validation, earlier interactions training.
  - Source: Section 3.1.3: https://arxiv.org/html/2608.22734v1#S3.SS1.SSS3.p1
- **Candidates**: full catalog; no sampled negatives.
  - Source: Section 3.1.3: https://arxiv.org/html/2608.22734v1#S3.SS1.SSS3.p1
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Tokenizer/collaborative encoder exposure to test items not reported.
  - Source: Section 3.1 defines no unseen-item holdout: https://arxiv.org/html/2608.22734v1#S3.SS1
- **SID**: Sentence-T5 text embeddings; TIGER-VAE, TIGER-KM or LETTER targets retain 4 levels x 256 codes. History-side IST adds semantic subwords (merge budget tuned 64-512). Collision handling not reported.
  - Source: Section 3.1.4: https://arxiv.org/html/2608.22734v1#S3.SS1.SSS4.p2
- **Inference budget**: Full-trie beam 20; Recall/NDCG@5/10. Hardware, inference batch size and standalone latency not reported; Table 3 wall time combines training, checkpoint loading and test evaluation.
  - Source: Sections 3.1.4/3.5: https://arxiv.org/html/2608.22734v1#S3.SS1.SSS4.p3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2608.22734v1#S3.SS5.p1
- **Results from**: Original Table 1: SST on three backbones; SARQ/VSID re-adapted to history-only variable lengths while preserving fixed target decoding. Table 6 reports all tokenizer-criterion variants.
  - Source: Table 1 and Section 3.1.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2608.22734v1#S3.T1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2608.22734v1#S3.SS1.SSS2.p5 and https://arxiv.org/html/2608.22734v1#A1.T6

### Related

## STAMP

- Page: pages/papers/stamp.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: V. Efficiency
- Stage: Backbone
- Representation: Text; Tokenization: RQ-VAE; Backbone: Enc-Dec / Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP + Aux.; Inference: C-Beam
- TL;DR: STAMP prunes redundant Semantic ID tokens adaptively in the forward pass and adds a multi-step auxiliary prediction objective, to cut training cost and densify supervision for long Semantic IDs.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Beauty (22.4K users / 12.1K items), Sports (35.6K / 18.4K), Toys (19.4K / 11.9K) with 5-core filtering; and AL-GR-Tiny, a subset of the AL-GR benchmark from a Chinese e-commerce platform (the full AL-GR has 131M users / 251M items / 14B interactions).
  - Source: Datasets: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.05329v3#S5.I2.i1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2604.05329v3#S5.I2.i2.p1; statistics: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.05329v3#S5.T1.
- **Split**: Amazon: per-user leave-one-out (final interaction for test, penultimate for validation). AL-GR-Tiny: the benchmark's Stage 1 split, four days of training behaviors and a test set from the following day. GRID results averaged over five seeds.
  - Source: Leave-one-out on Amazon; AL-GR S1 split: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.05329v3#S5.I2.i1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2604.05329v3#S5.I2.i2.p1.
- **Candidates**: not reported (full catalog versus sampled); Recall/NDCG at 5 and 10 under GRID, HitRate at 20-1000 under FORGE, as defined by those frameworks.
  - Source: Metrics inherited from GRID and FORGE: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.05329v3#S5.I4.i1.p1.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined.
  - Source: No unseen-item protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.05329v3#S5.I2.i1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2604.05329v3#S5.I2.i2.p1.
- **SID**: Uses each framework's SIDs unchanged: GRID with RK-Means over Flan-T5-XL embeddings and three codebooks (codebook size not restated); FORGE's pre-processed AL-GR SIDs. Collision handling: not reported.
  - Source: GRID RK-Means with three codebooks over Flan-T5-XL: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.05329v3#S5.SS1.SSS4.p2; FORGE SIDs from AL-GR: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.05329v3#S5.SS1.SSS4.p3.
- **Inference budget**: STAMP accelerates training (token pruning plus an auxiliary loss that is discarded at inference, so no inference overhead is claimed); inference decoding settings follow GRID and FORGE and are not restated. Training speed and VRAM reported on one A100-40GB (GRID) and two A100-80GB (FORGE).
  - Source: Training-time acceleration; MAP discarded at inference: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.05329v3#S4.SS4.p1; hardware: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.05329v3#S5.SS1.SSS4.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2604.05329v3#S5.SS1.SSS4.p3.
- **Results from**: Table 2 (GRID T5 on Beauty, Sports, Toys: accuracy, training time, VRAM versus EARN; five seeds); Table 3 (FORGE Qwen2.5-0.5B on AL-GR-Tiny); later analyses and ablations.
  - Source: Results: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.05329v3#S5.T2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2604.05329v3#S5.T3.

## STATIC

- Page: pages/papers/static.md
- Venue: KDD’26 ADS
- Problem: V. Efficiency
- Stage: Inference
- Representation: –; Tokenization: RQ-VAE; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP; Inference: Vec. C-Beam
- TL;DR: STATIC flattens the prefix tree of valid Semantic IDs into a sparse CSR matrix, turning trie traversal into vectorized operations for constrained decoding on TPUs and GPUs.
- [Code](https://github.com/youtube/static-constraint-decoding)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: YouTube corpus (100M-1B items); Amazon Beauty, Sports and Outdoors, Toys and Games (10K-20K items/domain). Filtering rules not reported.

- **Split**: Amazon cold targets: newest 2% or 5% of items by oldest-review date. Training-sequence exclusion wording is internally contradictory; exact temporal/validation split not reported. YouTube training split not reported.
  - Source: Section 6.2 and Appendix F: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.22647v3#S6.SS2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.22647v3#A6.p2
- **Candidates**: Restricted catalog: YouTube about 20M high-quality videos uploaded within 7 days; Amazon only the selected cold-item set. Unconstrained baselines can access the full catalog.
  - Source: Sections 5.2/6.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.22647v3#S5.SS2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.22647v3#S6.SS2.p1
- **Visibility**: Amazon generator exclusion is ambiguous; tokenizer cold-item exposure is not reported. Section 6.2 calls training sequences no-cold-start but says to remove sequences without cold items. Unseen by generator only versus unseen by tokenizer too cannot be established.
  - Source: Sections 6.1/6.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.22647v3#S6.SS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.22647v3#S6.SS2.p1
- **SID**: YouTube: 8 levels x 2048 codes; Amazon: separate RQ-VAE per domain, 4 levels x 256. Collision handling not reported.
  - Source: Sections 5.1/6.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.22647v3#S5.SS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.22647v3#S6.SS1.p1
- **Inference budget**: TPU v6e. YouTube: Gemini-based dense 3B, batch 2/chip, beam 70; added constraint overhead 0.033 ms/step, 0.25% of inference time. Amazon: Gemma-based dense 1B, batch 16, beam 20, Recall@1.
  - Source: Sections 5.1/5.2/6.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.22647v3#S5.SS1.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.22647v3#S5.SS2.p3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.22647v3#S6.SS1.p2

## SynGR

- Page: pages/papers/syngr.md
- Venue: ICML’26
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Training
- Representation: Text+Img; Tokenization: RQ-VAE; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP + Ctr.; Inference: C-Beam
- TL;DR: SynGR constrains reliance on dominant modalities during generation, so the generator uses synergistic cross-modal information beyond shared or modality-specific signals, instead of alignment-centric fusion.
- [Code](https://github.com/gxingyu/SynGR)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 4

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Reviews 2018 targets: Arts (22,171 users / 9,416 items), Games (42,259 / 13,839), Instruments (17,112 / 6,250), as in MQL4GRec; pre-training on six other categories (about 7.1M interactions, 884,918 users, 255,181 items). Filtering rules: not restated.
  - Source: Target datasets: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.18920v2#S5.SS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.18920v2#S4.T2; pre-training corpus: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.18920v2#A3.p1.
- **Split**: Leave-one-out (following MQL4GRec and MACRec; allocation not restated beyond the label).
  - Source: Leave-one-out following MQL4GRec and MACRec: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.18920v2#S5.SS1.p3.
- **Candidates**: full catalog (full ranking over the entire item space).
  - Source: Full ranking and beam 20: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.18920v2#S5.SS1.p3.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined.
  - Source: Standard split with no unseen-item protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.18920v2#S5.SS1.p3.
- **SID**: Separate text (LLaMA) and image (ViT-L/14) semantic IDs from RQ-VAEs with 4 levels x 256 codes, merged into a unified dictionary; collision handling: not reported.
  - Source: 4 layers x 256 per modality RQ-VAE: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.18920v2#A3.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.18920v2#S4.SS1.p2; collision handling not found.

Efficiency study on six NVIDIA RTX 4090 GPUs reports inference 6.0% (Arts) and 4.0% (Instruments) faster than MACRec; absolute latency and batch size: not reported.
  - Source: Beam size 20 for all generative models: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.18920v2#S5.SS1.p3; inference follows MQL4GRec: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.18920v2#S4.SS3.p2; hardware: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.18920v2#S5.F3.
- **Results from**: Table 1 (Arts, Games, Instruments versus sequential, multimodal, and generative baselines); Figure 3 (training time, inference speed, convergence versus MACRec); Figures 4-5 (parameters and ablations).
  - Source: Main: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.18920v2#S4.T1; efficiency: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.18920v2#S5.F3; parameters: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.18920v2#S5.F4; ablation: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.18920v2#S5.F5.

## TCBSA

- Page: pages/papers/tcbsa.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: IV. Utility
- Stage: Inference
- Representation: Text; Tokenization: R-KM; Backbone: Enc-Dec† / Dec-Only†; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP† / NTP → RL; Inference: CF-Guided C-Beam
- TL;DR: TCBSA converts a discriminative recommender's score margins into potentials on shared Semantic ID prefixes and adds them, gated by confidence, to path scores before beam pruning, without retraining.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Reviews 2023 Industrial and Scientific, Musical Instruments, Office Products: official 5-core, no extra rating thresholds/deduplication. Yelp Kaggle v2, 2019 window, all ratings implicit, iterative 5-core.
  - Source: Section 5.1 and Appendix B.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.32098v1#S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.32098v1#A2.SS1.p1
- **Split**: Per-user chronological last/penultimate interactions are test/validation; earlier interactions train. Input histories capped at 20.
  - Source: Section 5.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.32098v1#S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1
- **Candidates**: full catalog; previously interacted items remain eligible, padding masked
  - Source: Section 5.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.32098v1#S5.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Generator and discriminative checkpoints remain frozen during adaptation.
  - Source: Section 5.1 defines no unseen-item holdout: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.32098v1#S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.32098v1#S5.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1
- **SID**: Sentence-T5 text embeddings; 3 RQ-K-means levels plus fourth collision-resolution token for unique IDs. Codebook sizes not reported. Shared mapping across semantic-ID models.
  - Source: Section 5.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.32098v1#S5.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1
- **Inference budget**: Default beam 20, retrieval width 500; beam sweep 10/20/30/40/50. RTX 5880 Ada, inference batch 32. Synchronized per-user latency includes discriminative scoring/adaptation; default TCBSA costs 1.43-1.63x same-beam TIGER.
  - Source: Sections 5.1/5.6 and Appendix B.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.32098v1#S5.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.32098v1#S5.SS6.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.32098v1#S5.SS6.p3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.32098v1#A2.SS2.p1
- **Results from**: Original Table 1: full-catalog comparisons; Figure 5: accuracy/latency. Baselines instantiated using specified implementations; MiniOneRec evaluated at its final RL checkpoint.
  - Source: Original Table 1 and Figure 5, implementation details: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.32098v1#S5.T1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.32098v1#S5.F5 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.32098v1#S5.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1

## Think2Go

- Page: pages/papers/think2go.md
- Venue: KDD’26
- Problem: III. SID–Model Alignment
- Stage: Training
- Representation: Attr+Geo+CF†; Tokenization: RQ-VAE; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP → RL; Inference: CoT+Beam
- TL;DR: Think2Go unifies supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning reasoning for next-POI generation, weighting advantages by prompt epistemic uncertainty and normalized rewards, to deepen the LLM's understanding of Semantic IDs.
- [Code](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18206701)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Foursquare NYC and TKY (April 2012-February 2013) and Gowalla CA (February 2009-October 2010), preprocessed as in GNPR-SID: POIs with fewer than 10 interactions and users with fewer than 10 check-ins removed. Sizes (users / POIs): NYC 1,083 / 5,135; TKY 2,293 / 7,873; CA 6,592 / 14,027.
  - Source: Datasets and GNPR preprocessing: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.28997v1#S5.SS1.p1; statistics: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.28997v1#S5.T1.
- **Split**: Records sorted chronologically and split 80% / 10% / 10% for training, validation, and test; for each user the last check-in is the answer. Separate cross-city transfer test (Table 5).
  - Source: Temporal 80/10/10 with last check-in as answer: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.28997v1#S5.SS1.p1; cross-domain: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.28997v1#S5.T5.
- **Candidates**: not reported (full catalog versus sampled); Acc@1, 5, 10 and MRR over the predicted top-K POIs.
  - Source: Acc@K and MRR over predicted lists: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.28997v1#S5.SS3.p1.
- **Visibility**: warm; users and POIs that do not appear in training are removed from the test set. The cross-city transfer (Table 5) tests POIs of another city; their tokenizer exposure is not reported.
  - Source: Test users and POIs absent from training removed: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.28997v1#S5.SS1.p1.
- **SID**: Listwise semantic IDs built with RQ-VAE, which the paper contrasts with the pointwise semantic IDs of GNPR; numerical levels, codebook sizes, and collision handling: not reported.
  - Source: Listwise semantic IDs whose correlations are learned through RQ-VAE, contrasted with GNPR's pointwise IDs: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.28997v1#S5.SS5.p2; numerical settings not found.
- **Inference budget**: Reasoning generated with vLLM (max length 1,024, temperature 1.3, 4 rollouts, beam search width 10) before the POI SID; LLaMA3.1-8B with LoRA. Five NVIDIA L40s GPUs (four for training, one for rollout inference); latency: not reported.
  - Source: Rollout and decoding settings, hardware: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.28997v1#A1.p1.
- **Results from**: Table 2 (NYC, TKY, CA versus traditional, sequence, GCN, LLM, and reasoning baselines); Table 3 (ablations); Table 4 (SID category prediction versus GNPR); Table 5 (cross-city generalization).
  - Source: Main: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.28997v1#S5.T2; ablation: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.28997v1#S5.T3; SID understanding: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.28997v1#S5.T4; cross-domain: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.28997v1#S5.T5.

### Related

- id: gnpr-sid; relation: competitor; note: GNPR-SID trains SID knowledge by SFT alone; Think2Go adds reasoning tokens and advantage-calibrated GRPO over the same kind of POI semantic IDs and generalizes better across cities.; where: Think2Go v1, LLM-based baselines and preprocessing: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.28997v1#S5.SS2.p4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2607.28997v1#S5.SS1.p1; Tables 2, 4, 5: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.28997v1#S5.T2, https://arxiv.org/html/2607.28997v1#S5.T4, https://arxiv.org/html/2607.28997v1#S5.T5.

- id: oneloc; relation: alternative; note: OneLoc is a geo-aware generative recommender trained without explicit reasoning; Think2Go relies on reasoning to use spatial context.; where: Think2Go v1, Section 1 cites OneLoc: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.28997v1#S1.p4.

### Notes

## 旧卡片说明

迁自 `d61aa6c:papers/think2go.md`。保留方法说明、实验叙述与局限；本轮只对照现有记录处理明确冲突，未重新逐句核查原论文。分类和规格以页面上方由记录生成的表格为准。

### Think2Go：带大语言模型推理的生成式下一兴趣点推荐

> Think2Go 将监督微调和强化学习推理统一到自回归生成中，通过自纠错和自适应优势校准提升 LLM 对 POI SID 的理解。

### 研究动机与问题定义

用户移动轨迹具有稀疏、周期和多步空间规律，单步生成可能难以捕获深层意图。另一方面，独立训练的 SID 对 LLM 来说只是符号序列，模型未必理解 token 的类别和空间意义。Think2Go 研究如何让生成模型在输出下一 POI SID 前进行可控推理，并保持对行为模式的记忆。

### TL;DR（核心摘要）

`用户历史SID/时间 → Think → Self-Correct → Answer SID`

Think2Go 在一个自回归框架中同时训练推理轨迹和最终答案。监督微调先教模型生成思考与 SID，强化学习再用答案奖励更新推理过程；Prompt epistemic uncertainty（提示认知不确定性）鼓励难例探索，reward-informed advantage scaling（奖励感知优势缩放）调节不同难度样本的更新幅度。

### 输入与使用场景

| 方面 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| 使用信息 | 用户历史 SID、时间信息和 POI 生成结果 |
| 信息融入位置 | 推理提示、答案监督和奖励校准 |
| 语义标识结构 | 多级离散序列 |
| 适用场景 | 下一 POI、跨域泛化和推理增强推荐 |

### 方法设计

#### 4.1 模型架构
模型接收带时间的用户历史和目标上下文，输出 reasoning、Self-Correct 和 Answer 三类 token。Answer 是最终 POI SID，reasoning 用于表达用户偏好和时空判断，Self-Correct 连接推理阶段与监督答案阶段。

#### 4.2 自适应优势校准
作者指出只用普通优势估计可能造成不同难度样本更新幅度相同，或因估计偏差抑制探索。Think2Go 用核密度估计当前提示与用户历史的时空周期匹配程度，得到提示认知不确定性，并据此调节优势权重。

#### 4.2.2 奖励感知缩放
奖励被相对于同组样本最大值归一化，用于缩放策略梯度。高价值且难度合适的样本得到更有效更新，减少噪声奖励导致的过拟合和策略熵塌缩。

#### 4.2.3 规则奖励与训练目标
规则奖励综合答案 SID 正确性、格式合法性和时空行为匹配。模型在自回归推理轨迹上计算奖励，并用校准后的策略优化目标更新；这种设计形成隐式课程学习。

#### 附录：自纠错与零样本 SID 语义预测
附录给出 Self-Correct 提示格式和零样本类别预测任务。模型在答案错误时生成修正建议；类别预测实验用于检查微调和强化学习后，SID 是否承载可恢复的语义信息。

### 实验结论

- 三个真实数据集上的实验显示 Think2Go 能提升生成式下一 POI 推荐效果和 SID 语义理解。
- 优势校准、推理轨迹和自纠错的消融支持其对探索与训练稳定性的贡献。
- 相比基于完整文本提示的推理方法，论文报告 Think2Go 在训练时间、测试时间和显存占用上更高效。

### 局限性与研究定位

#### 局限性

- 推理轨迹增加输出长度和推理成本，效果与效率之间需要按场景权衡。
- 规则奖励和核密度不确定性估计依赖数据分布，跨城市和极少行为用户的可靠性仍需验证。

#### 研究定位

Think2Go 适合放在“推理增强的语义标识生成推荐”章节，重点体现将 SID 理解、显式推理和自适应强化学习结合起来。

### 相关资源

- [论文原文](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28997)

### 标签

`下一兴趣点推荐` · `推理增强` · `强化学习` · `自纠错`

## TIGER

- Page: pages/papers/tiger.md
- Venue: NeurIPS’23
- Problem: Paradigms, Systems and Benchmarks
- Stage: No single stage
- Representation: Text; Tokenization: RQ-VAE; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP; Inference: Beam
- TL;DR: TIGER encodes item text into RQ-VAE Semantic IDs and trains a Transformer encoder-decoder to decode the next item's ID, instead of retrieving items by approximate nearest neighbor search.
- [Code (third-party)](https://github.com/baiyimeng/TIGER)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Product Reviews (May 1996-July 2014): Beauty, Sports and Outdoors, Toys and Games. Users with fewer than 5 reviews are filtered; an item-frequency filter is not reported. Retained item counts: 12,101 / 18,357 / 11,924, respectively.
  - Source: Dataset/date range and user-only filtering: https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#A3.p1; corpus sizes: https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#A3.T6.
- **Split**: Chronological per-user leave-one-out: last interaction for test, penultimate for validation, earlier interactions for training; training histories contain at most 20 items. Separate Beauty cold-start experiment: remove 5% of test items from the training split.
  - Source: Chronological ordering, exact leave-one-out allocation, and training-history cap: https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#A3.p1. The separate Beauty cold-start manipulation removes 5% of test items from the training split: https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#S4.SS3.p3.
- **Candidates**: Main evaluation: full catalog versus sampled candidates not reported. Cold-start retrieval adds unseen items sharing the first three codes with a generated SID to the matching seen item; epsilon caps the proportion of unseen items in the returned top-K list (epsilon=0.1 in Fig. 5a).
  - Source: Full-catalog versus sampled-negative evaluation is not specified in Methods/Experiments or Appendices A-E; the evaluation description is https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#S4.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#A3.p1. Cold-start candidate construction and unseen-item quota: https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#S4.SS3.p4; epsilon=0.1 comparison: https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#S4.SS3.p5.
- **Visibility**: Main leave-one-out evaluation: per-target generator/tokenizer training visibility not reported. Beauty cold-start experiment: unseen by tokenizer too; the selected items are removed from the training split, both RQ-VAE and the generator are trained on that split, and unseen-item SIDs are produced afterward.
  - Source: Main preprocessing defines interaction holdouts without explicitly enumerating item-level training visibility: https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#A3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#S4.p4. For the cold-start experiment both RQ-VAE and the sequence-to-sequence model are trained on the reduced training split; unseen items are encoded afterward: https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#S4.SS3.p3.
- **SID**: Main configuration: 3 residual-quantization levels x 256 codewords (32-dimensional code embeddings), plus a fourth collision-disambiguation token, giving 4 tokens per item. Colliding three-code tuples receive different fourth tokens; non-colliding tuples receive 0. The generator uses 4 x 256 item-token entries.
  - Source: Main RQ levels, codebook cardinality, latent dimension, and collision suffix including zero for a unique tuple: https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#S4.p4. Four position-specific 256-token vocabularies: https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#S4.p5; one-time collision lookup: https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#S3.SS1.p8.
- **Inference budget**: Autoregressive beam search; numerical beam width not reported. Main evaluation: Recall and NDCG at K=5 and 10. Cold-start Fig. 5a varies K at epsilon=0.1; Fig. 5b evaluates Recall@10 while varying epsilon. Hardware, inference batch size, and measured latency: not reported.
  - Source: Autoregressive beam search: https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#A5.p3; main metric cutoffs: https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#S4.p2; cold-start cutoffs/quota experiment: https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#S4.F5. No numerical beam width, inference hardware, inference batch size, or latency is specified after checking Methods/Experiments and Appendices A-E; https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#S4.p4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#S4.p6 give training batches only.
- **Results from**: Original paper Table 1 (main sequential recommendation); Appendix E, Table 9 (three-seed means and standard errors); Fig. 5 (Beauty cold start). Table 1 combines the authors' TIGER results, previously published S3-Rec benchmark results for baselines other than P5, and P5 rerun with modified preprocessing.
  - Source: Original main comparison: https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#S4.T1; separate three-seed mean/standard-error table: https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#A5.T9; cold-start: https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#S4.F5. Baselines except P5 were taken from S3-Rec's published results; P5 was rerun with modified preprocessing: https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#S4.SS1.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#A4.p2.

### Related

- id: vq-rec; relation: alternative; note: VQ-Rec uses product-quantized content codes for transferable recommendation without generative retrieval; TIGER uses RQ-VAE codes for autoregressive retrieval.; where: TIGER, Section 2, Semantic IDs paragraph: https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1; Section 3.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#S3.SS2.p1.
- id: letter; relation: successor; note: LETTER extends TIGER's semantic-only tokenization with collaborative and diversity regularization, and adds a ranking-guided generation loss.; where: Evidence is from the later LETTER paper, Section 3.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2405.07314v1#S3.SS1.p6; Section 4.3.1 explicitly builds the LETTER-TIGER variants: https://arxiv.org/html/2405.07314v1#S4.SS3.SSS1.p1.
- id: rpg; relation: alternative; note: RPG predicts long OPQ IDs in parallel and uses graph-constrained decoding, while TIGER generates RQ-VAE IDs autoregressively.; where: Evidence is from the later RPG paper: Section 2 overview, https://arxiv.org/html/2506.05781v1#S2.p1; Section 2.1.1, https://arxiv.org/html/2506.05781v1#S2.SS1.SSS1.p1; its TIGER baseline description in Section 3.1, https://arxiv.org/html/2506.05781v1#S3.SS1.p4.

### Notes

## At a Glance

Key Findings: On Amazon Beauty, TIGER reports Recall@5 of 0.0454 against 0.0387 for SASRec, and RQ-VAE Semantic IDs outperform LSH and random IDs (Tables 1 and 2).
Limitation: The authors state that beam search can make TIGER more expensive than ANN-based retrieval at inference, and the paper does not report a beam width or latency (Appendix E).

### 1. Why This Paper Matters

Large-scale recommenders usually embed users and items in one space and select candidates by approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) search (Abstract). TIGER instead trains a sequence-to-sequence model to decode the Semantic ID (SID) of the next item. The authors describe it as the first Semantic ID-based generative model for recommendation (Sec. 2). Many later papers in this list keep this pipeline and change one of its stages.

> "We propose a new paradigm of building generative retrieval models for sequential recommendation." (Sec. 1)

### 2. How It Works

#### Overview

```
Item text (title, price, brand, category)
  │
  ▼  pre-trained Sentence-T5
Content embedding x (768 dimensions)
  │
  ▼  DNN encoder, 3-level RQ-VAE, collision token
SID (c1, c2, c3, c4): three codes from 256-entry codebooks plus one collision token
  │
  ▼  Transformer encoder-decoder (T5X), next-token prediction
Next-item SID, decoded by beam search
  │
  ▼  frozen lookup table
Recommended items
```

#### Step 1: Item Text to a Latent Vector

TIGER builds a sentence from each item's title, price, brand, and category, and the pre-trained Sentence-T5 model encodes it into a 768-dimensional embedding $`\mathbf{x}`$ (Sec. 4). A DNN encoder $`E`$ with intermediate layers of size 512, 256, and 128 and ReLU activations maps $`\mathbf{x}`$ to a 32-dimensional latent vector $`\mathbf{z} = E(\mathbf{x})`$ (Sec. 4).

#### Step 2: Residual Quantization into Codes

RQ-VAE quantizes the residual left by the previous level, so each level refines the code of the level before it.

> "Residual-Quantized Variational AutoEncoder (RQ-VAE) [40] is a multi-level vector quantizer that applies quantization on residuals to generate a tuple of codewords (aka Semantic IDs)." (Sec. 3.1)

TIGER uses $`M = 3`$ levels, each with a codebook of $`K = 256`$ codewords of dimension 32 (Sec. 4). At level $`m`$:

```math
\mathbf{r}_1 = \mathbf{z}, \qquad c_m = \arg\min_{k \in \{0, \dots, K-1\}} \left\| \mathbf{r}_m - \mathbf{e}_k^{(m)} \right\|_2^2, \qquad \mathbf{r}_{m+1} = \mathbf{r}_m - \mathbf{e}_{c_m}^{(m)}
```

where:
- $`\mathbf{r}_m \in \mathbb{R}^{32}`$ is the residual that enters level $`m`$;
- $`\mathbf{e}_k^{(m)}`$ is codeword $`k`$ of the level-$`m`$ codebook;
- $`c_m`$ is the code chosen at level $`m`$.

```python
import torch

def rqvae_quantize(z, codebooks, beta=0.25):
    """
    z:         [B, 32] latent vectors from the encoder E(x)
    codebooks: list of M tensors, each [K, 32] (M = 3, K = 256)
    """
    r = z
    z_hat = torch.zeros_like(z)
    codes, vq_loss = [], 0.0
    for E_m in codebooks:
        # nearest codeword at this level
        c_m = torch.cdist(r, E_m).pow(2).argmin(dim=-1)                     # [B]
        e_m = E_m[c_m]                                                       # [B, 32]
        # codebook and commitment terms of the quantization loss
        vq_loss = vq_loss + (e_m - r.detach()).pow(2).mean() + beta * (r - e_m.detach()).pow(2).mean()
        # straight-through estimate, then the residual for the next level
        z_hat = z_hat + r + (e_m - r).detach()
        r = r - e_m.detach()
        codes.append(c_m)
    return torch.stack(codes, dim=-1), z_hat, vq_loss                        # [B, M], [B, 32], scalar
```

Simplifications: The code shows only the quantization loop and the quantization loss. It omits the DNN encoder and decoder, the reconstruction loss, and the k-means codebook initialization.

#### Step 3: Tokenizer Training

A decoder $`D`$ reconstructs $`\hat{\mathbf{x}} = D(\hat{\mathbf{z}})`$ from the sum of the selected codewords $`\hat{\mathbf{z}} = \sum_{m=1}^{M} \mathbf{e}_{c_m}^{(m)}`$. RQ-VAE trains the encoder, decoder, and codebooks with a reconstruction loss and a quantization loss:

```math
\mathcal{L}(\mathbf{x}) = \|\mathbf{x} - \hat{\mathbf{x}}\|_2^2 + \sum_{m=1}^{M} \left( \left\|\mathrm{sg}[\mathbf{r}_m] - \mathbf{e}_{c_m}^{(m)}\right\|_2^2 + \beta \left\|\mathbf{r}_m - \mathrm{sg}[\mathbf{e}_{c_m}^{(m)}]\right\|_2^2 \right)
```

where:
- $`\mathrm{sg}[\cdot]`$ is the stop-gradient operator;
- $`\beta = 0.25`$ weights the commitment term (Sec. 4).

To prevent codebook collapse, TIGER runs k-means on the first training batch and uses the centroids to initialize the codebooks (Sec. 3.1).

#### Step 4: Collision Token

Several items can receive the same three codes. TIGER appends a fourth token so that every item has a unique SID: two items that share (12, 24, 52) become (12, 24, 52, 0) and (12, 24, 52, 1) (Sec. 3.1).

> "To remove the collisions, we append an extra token at the end of the ordered semantic codes to make them unique." (Sec. 3.1)

```python
from collections import defaultdict

def append_collision_token(code_tuples):
    """code_tuples: list of (c1, c2, c3), one per item."""
    seen = defaultdict(int)
    sids = []
    for t in code_tuples:
        sids.append((*t, seen[t]))   # 0 for the first item with this tuple, 1 for the second, ...
        seen[t] += 1
    return sids
```

The code assigns the fourth token in input order; the paper does not state how the order is chosen. The table that maps SIDs to items is built once after the tokenizer is trained and then frozen (Appendix E).

#### Step 5: Sequence-to-Sequence Generation

TIGER flattens a user's history into SID tokens and puts one user token in front. The raw user ID is hashed into one of 2,000 user tokens (Sec. 4). The generator is a Transformer encoder-decoder built with the T5X framework, with 4 layers each in the encoder and the decoder and 6 self-attention heads of dimension 64 (Sec. 4).

> "Given Semantic IDs for items in a user session, a Transformer-based sequence-to-sequence model is trained to predict the Semantic ID of the next item that the user will interact with." (Abstract)

The generator is trained with next-token prediction over the four tokens of the target SID:

```math
\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{NTP}} = -\sum_{m=1}^{4} \log P_\theta\left(c_{t,m} \mid \mathbf{c}_{1:t-1},\, c_{t,1:m-1}\right)
```

where:
- $`\mathbf{c}_{1:t-1}`$ is the SID token sequence of the history items;
- $`c_{t,m}`$ is the $`m`$-th token of the target item's SID.

At inference, TIGER decodes SIDs with autoregressive beam search and maps each generated SID to an item through the frozen lookup table (Appendix E).

### 3. Experimental Findings

The three entries below compare TIGER with SASRec. S3-Rec is the strongest baseline in all four Sports and Outdoors columns (Table 1). It is also the strongest in Recall@10 and NDCG@10 on Beauty and on Toys and Games.

- Beauty: TIGER reports Recall@5 = 0.0454, NDCG@5 = 0.0321, Recall@10 = 0.0648, and NDCG@10 = 0.0384, against 0.0387, 0.0249, 0.0605, and 0.0318 for SASRec (Table 1).
- Sports and Outdoors: TIGER reports Recall@5 = 0.0264, NDCG@5 = 0.0181, Recall@10 = 0.0400, and NDCG@10 = 0.0225, against 0.0233, 0.0154, 0.0350, and 0.0192 for SASRec (Table 1).
- Toys and Games: TIGER reports Recall@5 = 0.0521, NDCG@5 = 0.0371, Recall@10 = 0.0712, and NDCG@10 = 0.0432, against 0.0463, 0.0306, 0.0675, and 0.0374 for SASRec (Table 1).
- ID ablation: Table 2 compares random IDs, LSH Semantic IDs, and RQ-VAE Semantic IDs. RQ-VAE IDs score highest and random IDs lowest in all twelve metric columns (Table 2).

  > "Our results show that RQ-VAE consistently outperforms LSH." (Sec. 4.2)

- Invalid IDs: for top-10 predictions, 0.1%–1.6% of generated IDs map to no item across the three datasets (Sec. 4.5, Fig. 6).
- Cold start: the authors state that SIDs improve retrieval of items with no prior interaction history (Abstract, Fig. 5).
- Diversity: temperature-based sampling during decoding controls the diversity of predictions (Sec. 4.3).
- ID length and codebook size: the authors also tried other settings, such as 6 codewords from codebooks of size 64 (Appendix E).

  > "We noticed that the recommendation metrics for TIGER were robust to these changes." (Appendix E)

### 4. Limitations & Critical Analysis

**Stated by the authors.** The authors state that TIGER can be more expensive than ANN-based models at inference because of beam search (Appendix E).

> "we note that our model can be more computationally expensive than ANN-based models during inference due to the use of beam search for autoregressive decoding." (Appendix E)

**Our analysis.**

- TIGER's representation uses item text only (`Text`). LETTER uses text and collaborative signals (`Text+CF`) with a learnable RQ tokenizer (`Learn. RQ`).
- The tokenizer is fixed before the generator trains (`Fixed`). ETEGRec updates the tokenizer and the generator in turns (`Altern.`).
- The fourth token only separates items that share three codes; the paper derives it from the collision, not from item content (Sec. 3.1).
- Unconstrained beam search can produce IDs that map to no item (Sec. 4.5). LETTER decodes with constrained beam search (`C-Beam`).
- Beam search runs one generator step per SID token. RPG predicts all tokens of an SID in parallel (`Non-AR`) and decodes over a graph of valid IDs (`Graph`).

## Tlow

- Page: pages/papers/tlow.md
- Venue: CIKM’26 Applied
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text; Tokenization: Flow+PQ; Backbone: Non-AR; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: MTP + Rel.MSE; Inference: Scoring
- TL;DR: Tlow maps semantic embeddings with a normalizing flow into a standard normal latent space before independent quantization, and aligns codebook and token embedding spaces, unlike RQ-VAE or OPQ.
- [Code](https://github.com/wjjln/Tlow)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Reviews Sports/Beauty/Toys/CDs; processed Cloth-Sports cross-domain data. WeChat picture/article logs for online multimodal retrieval. Filtering not reported.
  - Source: Sections 3.1.1/3.6.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2608.24176v1#S3.SS1.SSS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2608.24176v1#S3.SS6.SSS1.p1
- **Split**: Public: chronological last item test, penultimate validation, earlier interactions train. Online holdout protocol and A/B duration not reported; two weeks refers to model training.
  - Source: Sections 3.1.1/3.6.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2608.24176v1#S3.SS1.SSS1.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2608.24176v1#S3.SS6.SSS2.p1
- **Candidates**: full catalog for offline ranking; historical-item exclusion not reported
  - Source: Section 3.1.3: https://arxiv.org/html/2608.24176v1#S3.SS1.SSS3.p1
- **Visibility**: Offline: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Cold analysis bins targets by training frequency. Online cold pictures are exposed on publication day; generator/tokenizer exclusion not reported. Tokenizer fits about 1M items, then encodes additional unseen items.
  - Source: Sections 3.5/3.6.2/3.6.3: https://arxiv.org/html/2608.24176v1#S3.SS5.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2608.24176v1#S3.SS6.SSS2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2608.24176v1#S3.SS6.SSS3.p1
- **SID**: Flow plus independent PQ: C in {16,32,64,96,128}, 256 codes each; selected C per offline dataset not reported. Online: 16 x 256. Collision handling not reported.
  - Source: Sections 3.1.4/3.6.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2608.24176v1#S3.SS1.SSS4.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2608.24176v1#S3.SS6.SSS2.p1
- **Inference budget**: Single-forward parallel token scoring, Recall/NDCG@5/10; temperature searched over 0.03/0.05/0.07. Recommendation hardware, batch size and latency not reported. Online tokenization of tens of millions of new items takes minutes on one unspecified GPU, not per-request serving time.
  - Source: Sections 3.1.4/3.6.1/3.6.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2608.24176v1#S3.SS1.SSS4.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2608.24176v1#S3.SS6.SSS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2608.24176v1#S3.SS6.SSS2.p1
- **Results from**: Tables 2/4/5/6: general/cross-domain/multimodal/online results. General comparison reuses RPG-paper baseline scores and reruns RPG; main semantic embeddings are sentence-t5-base.
  - Source: Section 3.1.4 and Tables 2/4/5/6: https://arxiv.org/html/2608.24176v1#S3.SS1.SSS4.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2608.24176v1#S3.T2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2608.24176v1#S3.T4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2608.24176v1#S3.T5 and https://arxiv.org/html/2608.24176v1#S3.T6

### Related

- id: rpg; relation: predecessor; note: Supplies the parallel prediction setup and the rerun controlled baseline.; where: Tlow v1, Section 3.1.4: https://arxiv.org/html/2608.24176v1#S3.SS1.SSS4.p1.
- id: tiger; relation: competitor; note: Autoregressive RQ-VAE comparator against independent flow-space tokenization.; where: Tlow v1, Introduction and Section 3.1.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2608.24176v1#S1.p2; https://arxiv.org/html/2608.24176v1#S3.SS1.SSS2.p1.
